the emptiness of the essential nature of nonentities
The real nature that is not grasped is not the real nature, on account of the emptiness of its inherent existence.

div.p:
The subsection on not fully grasping causal signs starts from, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “And why? Because it cannot be expressed as a causal sign,”
q.orig: because this [all-aspect omniscience] cannot be expressed by means of distinguishing marks
If you ask why, it is because this all-aspect omniscience cannot be expressed by means of mental images

div.p:
and goes up to Cp. khri brgyad
.

q.p: “having thus comprehended he did not fully grasp form, did not fully grasp feeling,”
q.orig: having thus comprehended did not fully grasp form. Similarly, he did not fully grasp feeling
Having entered into it in that manner, he did not…feelings
Having entered into it in that manner, he did not grasp physical forms, did not grasp feelings

div.p:
and up to Cf. khri brgyad
, which is similar. nyi khri “does not fully grasp even the very limit of reality.”

q.p: “did not fully grasp the very limit of reality.”
q.orig: do not fully grasp even the very limit of reality
nonappropriation of [unconditioned phenomena], up to and including the very limit of reality
He did not observe that knowledge inside the very limit of reality

div.p: The subsection of the passage on not fully grasping understanding is from,

q.p:
“And why? Because he did not apprehend a grasper of all dharmas that are empty of their own mark,” khri brgyad
, Ghoṣa 615, Gilgit 284.2 parigrāhakaṃ nopalabdhā.
q.orig: because he did not apprehend any thing, empty of its own defining characteristics, that could be…appropriated[2]

div.p: up to,

q.p:
“Lord, because all dharmas are not fully grasped, it is the bodhisattva great being’s perfection of wisdom.” le’u brgyad ma ga 145b4–5, reading slad du’o; cf. khri brgyad
.
q.orig: because they have not fully grasped all dharmas—is the state in which…bodhisattva great beings have gone beyond the others; it is the perfection of wisdom.
due to the fact that no phenomena can be grasped, is the perfection of wisdom of bodhisattva great beings
because all dharmas are not grasped…is indeed the perfection of bodhisattva great beings because it is the beyond that is not beyond

div.head: Not Fully Grasping Dharmas
div.p: There, first, in the subsection explaining not fully grasping dharmas, in regard to

q.p: “form is not fully grasped,”
q.orig: form is not fully grasped
physical forms cannot be appropriated
physical forms are not grasped

div.p:
because of the self, the true dharmic nature of form—whatever the cause of a descent into grasping at “I” and grasping at “mine”—is not grasped as form. Therefore, it teaches that when an enactment is practiced, it is not a practice practicing the ultimate perfection of wisdom. “And why” is form not fully grasped? It says, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “Because a form not fully grasped is not form, because of the emptiness of a basic nature.”
q.orig: Because a form not fully grasped is not form because of the emptiness of a basic nature
The nonappropriation of physical forms is not physical forms, on account of the emptiness of its inherent existence
Physical forms that are not grasped are not physical forms, on account of the emptiness of their inherent existence.

div.p: Here, take “not fully grasped” with the mark of a thoroughly established phenomenon. It is saying that the true dharmic nature of Golden 140a2 gis. form that is not fully grasped, which is the intrinsic nature of a thoroughly established phenomenon, is not a falsely imagined form’s intrinsic nature. Therefore, the true dharmic nature of form Golden 140a2, K, N; D “the dharma in true dharmic nature.” is connected with “is not fully grasped.”

“Because of the emptiness of a basic nature” means it is not the case that, having fully grasped some aspect of an attribute of form and so on earlier, later some other counteracting force will make it empty. Its basic nature is emptiness.
Construe from “feeling” and so on, up to “the very limit of reality,” like that as well.

q.p: “Lord, this meditative concentration sphere of bodhisattva great beings is called sarva­dharmāparigṛhīta; it is vast, prized, infinite, fixed, cannot be stolen, and is not shared in common with śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas”
q.orig: Lord, this meditative stabilization sphere of bodhisattva great beings is called sarva­dharmāparigṛhīta; it is vast, prized, infinite, fixed,…cannot be stolen, and is not shared in common with śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.

Blessed Lord, this is the bodhisattva great beings’ spacious, perfect, immeasurable, and indeterminate maṇḍala of meditative stability, known as the nonappropriation of all phenomena, which is not misappropriated by or shared in common with any of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas
Blessed Lord, this is the bodhisattva great beings’ spacious, perfect, immeasurable, definitely immeasurable…śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.

div.p:
teaches its dharma. The passage being explained is khri brgyad
– . The ultimate thoroughly established phenomenon is “known” by this meditative stabilization and in that sense is its dharma, which is to say it qualifies it as its attribute or quality.

q.p: “Abiding in that sphere of meditative stabilizations”
q.orig: engage in this maṇḍala of meditative stability
Bodhisattva great beings who engage in this maṇḍala of meditative stability

div.p: and so on teaches the benefit.

q.p: “And that knowledge of all aspects is not fully grasped, because of inner emptiness,”
q.orig: all-aspect omniscience cannot be appropriated, on account of the emptiness of internal phenomena
even this all-aspect omniscience…cannot be grasped, on account of the emptiness of internal phenomena

div.p: up to

q.p: “emptiness that is the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature,”
q.orig: the emptiness of the essential nature of nonentities
the emptiness of an essential nature of nonentities

div.p: is teaching that because the completion of the thoroughly cleansed transcendental knowledge of all the emptinesses when all dharmas are not apprehended is “the knowledge of all aspects,” Golden 140b1, K, N: “The completion of what has been thoroughly cleansed by all the emptinesses when all dharmas are not apprehended is ‘the knowledge of all aspects.’ ” therefore it too is “not fully grasped.”
Therefore, it says

q.p: “it cannot be expressed as a causal sign.”
q.orig: this [all-aspect omniscience] cannot be expressed by means of distinguishing marks
it is because this all-aspect omniscience cannot be expressed by means of mental images

div.p: This means that even the knowledge of all aspects is separated from the causal sign of the knowledge of all aspects because it definitely does not have a mental image of a causal sign.

q.p: “Because a causal sign is an affliction” K, N; D: “because a causal sign is not an affliction.”—
q.orig: in that afflicted mental states arise from distinguishing marks
because afflicted mental states arise from mental images

div.p: the very causal signs of the bodhisattvas’ conceptualizations afflict the mindstream, so they are taught to be “affliction.”

div.head: Not Fully Grasping Causal Signs
div.p: The subsection on not fully grasping causal signs also explains in terms of these, A conceptual mind is defined by having a causal sign as its appearing object. Here, “these” is in reference to them both, like a dream consciousness and its object, as affliction. so it says,

q.p: “What is a causal sign? Form is a causal sign,”
q.orig: What is a causal sign? Form[1] is a causal sign[2].
What, one might ask, constitute those distinguishing marks? Physical forms are distinguishing marks
And if you ask what those mental images are, physical forms are mental images

div.p: and so on. It means that they are all, ultimately, afflictions for bodhisattvas so they should be abandoned, but not like attachment and so on.

q.p: “If the perfection of wisdom were something that could be taken up through a causal sign, then the religious mendicant Śreṇika,”
q.orig: If this perfection of wisdom could be apprehended as a distinguishing mark, the wandering mendicant Śreṇika
If this perfection of wisdom could be apprehended as a mental image, the wandering mendicant Śreṇika

div.p: and so on, is an elucidation of the practice without causal signs.

q.p: “The religious mendicant Śreṇika also believed in this knowledge of a knower of all aspects.”
q.orig: The religious mendicant Śreṇika also believed in this knowledge of a knower of all.
The wandering mendicant Śreṇika indeed became a follower [of the Great Vehicle] endowed with faith, owing to the power of his resolution with respect to this omniscient knowledge
The wandering mendicant Śreṇika, too, having become a resolute believer in the knowledge of the Omniscient One

div.p: Earlier, that religious mendicant had not realized the practice without causal signs. He had generated a faith in it, This translation is based on K, N … ma rtogs pa and D de la dad pa bskyed. Aṣṭa (Wogihara p. 51) adhimukta iti veditavyo nādhigata iti; Bṭ1 na, 113a4–5, says he had faith in the absence of causal signs but did not realize simultaneously that all dharmas are without causal signs, only each (form and so on) separately (kun du rgyu ba de sngon mtshan ma med par spyod pa la dad pas dad pa’i rjes su ’brang ba zhes bya/ chos thams cad cig car mtshan ma med par ni ma rtogs kyi/ gzugs la sogs pa re re nas mtshan ma med par rtogs pa’i phyir/ nyi tse ba’i ye shes kyis zhugs zhes bya’o). and with just that faith he produced and gained knowledge free from causal signs, but because all dharmas were not its object it was not the knowledge without causal signs. K, N: “because it was with a partial knowledge without causal signs.”

q.p: “Partial knowledge”—
q.orig: ephemeral knowledge
partial knowledge

div.p: having comprehended dharmas, each individually, he did not apprehend the causal sign of form when he had fully grasped and understood form analytically. Similarly, he did not apprehend the causal sign of feeling when he had fully grasped and understood feeling analytically. Hence it says,

q.p: “Having thus comprehended [he] did not fully grasp form. Similarly, he did not fully grasp feeling, perception, volitional factors, or consciousness,”
q.orig: having thus comprehended did not fully grasp form. Similarly, he did not fully grasp feeling, perception, volitional factors,…or consciousness.
Having entered into it in that manner, he did not…feelings, perceptions, formative predispositions, or consciousness
Having entered into it in that manner, he did not grasp physical forms,

div.p: up to

q.p: “he has not fully grasped even the very limit of reality.”
q.orig: observe that knowledge to be anything other than [unconditioned phenomena], up to and including the very limit of reality
He did not observe that knowledge inside the very limit of reality

div.p:
To teach the reason for that, it explains khri brgyad
.

q.p: “because he did not apprehend a grasper of all dharmas that are empty of their own mark.”
q.orig: because he did not apprehend any thing, empty of its own defining characteristics
he did not apprehend grasping any phenomena that are empty of their own defining characteristics

div.p: By having comprehended with that signless knowledge each of them individually in the form of signlessness, he comes to understand that all dharmas are empty of their own mark. Hence “he did not apprehend” a person or knower that is “a grasper.”
Also, as a reason for that it says, khri brgyad (ka 84a1–3) lags pa in place of tshul gyis; cf. nyi khri (ka 142b3–5), which differs but has tshul gyis.

q.p: “Because he did not see that knowledge as being an inner attainment and clear realization of knowledge, and he did not see it as being an outer one. He did not see that knowledge as being an inner and outer attainment and clear realization, and he did not see that attainment and clear realization of knowledge as being some other either.” D bzhin du yang is a mistake for gzhan du yang.
q.orig: Because he did not see that knowledge as an inner attainment and clear realization, and he did not see it as an outer one. He did not see that knowledge as an inner and outer attainment and clear realization, and he did not see that knowledge as some other attainment and clear realization either

because he did not observe that knowledge as internally due to the attainment of clear realization. Nor did he observe it as externally due to the attainment of clear realization, and nor did he observe it as externally and internally due to the attainment of clear realization. Nor did he observe that knowledge as anything else due to the attainment of clear realization

because he did not observe that knowledge internally due to a realization and attainment; he did not observe that knowledge externally due to a realization and attainment; nor did he observe that knowledge externally and internally due to a realization and attainment. Nor did he observe that knowledge as anything else due to a realization and attainment

div.p:
This means that religious mendicant, having taken hold of his knowledge and fully investigated the attainment and the realization—whether with this knowledge of his he had attained special dharmas he had not attained before, or whether the dharmas he had clearly realized with this knowledge had not been clearly realized before—did not see the knowledge as located in him, located outside, located in both, or located somewhere else besides those. Hence it says Cf. khri brgyad
, nyi khri . I have not emended the citation to correspond to the explanation given immediately below.

q.p: “because he did not apprehend and did not see that with which he might know, or that which the knowledge might know.”
q.orig: Because he did not apprehend and see any dharma with which he might know, or which might know
because he did not observe anything that could engender that realization, any realization that could be engendered, or anything from which…that realization could be engendered
because he did not observe anything with which he might realize, or which might realize, or which he might realize

div.p:
There the “that with which” is teaching “that knowledge with which.” The “that which” is teaching “that which he has attained and clearly realized.” The “that which” is also teaching the dharmas he has not attained and has not clearly realized. The other editions are the same with minor variations. Cf. khri brgyad
: “any dharma with which he might know, or which he might know, or which he will come to know.”

div.head: Not Fully Grasping Understanding
div.p: Having thus taught that knowledge of attainment and clear realization does not exist as any of the four alternatives, then, in order to teach that knowledge of all dharmas—form and so on, which are objects—also does not operate as any of the four alternatives, it says

q.p: “he did not see that knowledge inside form,”
q.orig: because he did not see that knowledge inside form[1]
He did not observe that knowledge to be inside physical forms
He did not observe that knowledge inside physical forms

div.p: and so on. It means that he also did not see the knowledge of all dharmas—form and so on, which are objects—inside, outside, in both, or somewhere else.
To again elucidate just that, it says,

q.p: “The religious mendicant Śreṇika believed in this one of many explanations,”
q.orig: This formulation explains how the wandering mendicant Śreṇika, after making this resolution
The wandering mendicant Śreṇika became a believer in this discourse

div.p: and so on, up to

q.p: “because he did not pay attention to any causal signs.”
q.orig: because he was without distinguishing marks and focused no attention on them
he did not apprehend anything at all

div.p: This teaches the benefit of this comprehension of practice that does not fully grasp.

q.p: “Lord, this—… the state in which the bodhisattva great beings have gone beyond the others; it is the perfection of wisdom.” ’bum (kha 34a6), nyi khri , le’u brgyad ma ga 145b1, LSPW p. 135 “gone to a beyond which is no beyond.”
q.orig: Lord, this—namely, that he does not fully grasp form, that he does not fully grasp feeling, perception, volitional factors, or consciousness because he has not fully grasped all dharmas, up to that he has not fully grasped even the very limit of reality because he has not fully grasped all dharmas—is the state in which the bodhisattva great beings have gone beyond the others;…it is the perfection of wisdom.
This is indeed the perfection of bodhisattva great beings because it is the perfection that cannot be transcended
Blessed Lord, this‍…is indeed the perfection of bodhisattva great beings

div.p: This means it is thus a beyond that is different from all other dharmas, which has become different from all conceptualizations and all causal signs. The absence of conceptualization is the beyond in the sense that signlessness is the “beyond.”
What is that which is beyond the others? It says

q.p: “that he does not fully grasp form,”
q.orig: that he does not fully grasp form
[bodhisattvas] do not grasp physical forms
do not grasp physical forms

div.p: and so on. Because he does not fully grasp form and so on, he is therefore “beyond the others.”

q.p: “In the interim they do not pass into complete nirvāṇa.”
q.orig: they will not pass into final nirvāṇa prematurely
as long as their aspirations have not been fulfilled, they will not pass into final nirvāṇa prematurely

div.p: That religious mendicant Śreṇika is in the buddha lineage so in the interim he does not pass into nirvāṇa. K, N; D adds bar du zhes bya ba smos pa ni here, as well as at the end, suggesting a short passage has dropped out of the text at this point explaining “interim” as meaning until “prayers are completed, up to until the eighteen distinct attributes are completed.” This would then be followed by the nearly identical passage that follows, perhaps expanding on a different etymology for parāntarā. As for saying “in the interim,” it says

q.p: “those prayers are nonprayers, those powers are nonpowers, those fearlessnesses are nonfearlessnesses, those detailed and thorough knowledges are nondetailed and nonthorough knowledges, up to those eighteen distinct attributes of a buddha are nonbuddhadharmas,”
q.orig: those prayers are nonprayers, those powers are nonpowers, those fearlessnesses are nonfearlessnesses, those detailed and thorough knowledges are nondetailed and nonthorough knowledges, up to those eighteen distinct attributes of a buddha are nonbuddhadharmas

those aspirations are not aspirations, those applications of mindfulness are not applications of mindfulness; those correct exertions, supports for miraculous ability, faculties, powers, and branches of enlightenment…eighteen distinct qualities of the buddhas [and so forth]
it is because the aspirations are not aspirations…the eighteen distinct qualities of the buddhas are not eighteen distinct qualities of the buddhas

div.p: so this “in the interim” teaches they are beyond the others.

div.head:
Practice that has made a full investigation khri brgyad
– .
div.p: Having thus made fully complete the practice that does not fully grasp, next, taking the practice that has made a full investigation as its point of departure, it says,

q.p: “Furthermore, Lord, bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom should make an investigation like this,”
q.orig: Moreover, Blessed Lord, when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom, they should investigate
Moreover, Blessed Lord, when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom, they should investigate like this

div.p: and so on.
This practice that has made a full investigation is taught in four parts as well:

q.p:
“What is it… of what is it… why is it… and what is it for?” In each case, at khri brgyad
, the “it” is “the perfection of wisdom.” “What is it for” renders ci zhig na, kena; LSPW “whereby.” “Why” can be an inquiry about both cause and result. Below our author glosses it with nges par ’byin pa (nairyāṇikā), “causes an escape”—either the escape itself (what it is for) or the practice that brings it about.
q.orig: ‘Just what is the perfection of wisdom? Of what is it a perfection of wisdom? Why is it the perfection of wisdom? And what is the perfection of wisdom for?’
what is this perfection of wisdom, whose is this perfection of wisdom, how is this perfection of wisdom, and for what purpose is this perfection of wisdom
what is this perfection of wisdom, whose is this perfection of wisdom, how is this a perfection of wisdom, and why is this called a perfection of wisdom?

div.p:
From khri brgyad
–.

q.p: “if, when they investigate and ponder like that,”
q.orig: if, while making this investigation and pondering it
if they practice while wondering

div.p: up to

q.p: “thus, practicing the perfection of wisdom… are not separated from the knowledge of all aspects,”
q.orig: thus practicing the perfection of wisdom are not cowed, do not tense up, and do not experience regret—if they do not tremble, feel frightened, or become terrified—you should know that those bodhisattva great beings are not separated from the knowledge of all aspects.

practice the perfection of wisdom, if they investigate and ponder accordingly, and if, when they investigate and ponder in that manner, they are not disheartened, not intimidated, not afraid, not terrified, and will not be terrified, one should know that these bodhisattva great beings will not be separated from the perfection of wisdom

if they investigate and ponder accordingly, and if, when they investigate and ponder in that manner, they are not discouraged, not utterly discouraged, not afraid, not frightened, and not fearful, one should know that these bodhisattva great beings will not be separated from the perfection of wisdom

div.p: teaches the “what.”

From khri brgyad
.

q.p: “Venerable Śāriputra, form is separated from the intrinsic nature of form,”
q.orig: “Venerable Śāriputra,” replied Subhūti, “…form[2]
physical forms are without the inherent nature of physical forms
“Venerable Śāradvatīputra,” replied the venerable Subhūti, “physical forms are without the essential nature of physical forms

div.p: up to

q.p: “the very limit of reality is separated from the intrinsic nature of the very limit of reality,”
q.orig: the very limit of reality are all without the inherent nature of the very limit of reality
The very limit of reality is without the essential nature of the very limit of reality

div.p: teaches the “of what.”

From nyi khri , khri brgyad
has “form is separated from the defining mark of form.”

q.p: “furthermore, Venerable Śāriputra, form does not have the defining mark of form,”
q.orig: Furthermore, Venerable Śāriputra, form is separated from the defining mark of form
Moreover, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, physical forms are without the defining characteristics of physical forms
Moreover, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, physical forms are without the defining characteristics of physical forms

div.p: up to

q.p: “bodhisattva great beings who are training in this training go forth to the knowledge of all aspects,”
q.orig: Bodhisattva great beings who undertake this training will be emancipated in all-aspect omniscience
Those bodhisattva great beings who undertake this training will be emancipated in all-aspect omniscience

div.p: teaches the “why.”

From khri brgyad
–.

q.p: “all dharmas have not been produced and have not gone forth,”
q.orig: all phenomena are unborn [in cyclic existence]…and unemancipated
If you ask why, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, it is because all phenomena are unborn and unemancipated

div.p: up to

q.p: “Venerable Śāriputra, a bodhisattva great being thus practicing the perfection of wisdom is near unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening,”
q.orig: “Venerable Śāriputra, bodhisattva great beings thus practicing the perfection of wisdom are near…unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, bodhisattva great beings who practice the perfection of wisdom in that manner are approaching all-aspect omniscience
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, bodhisattva great beings who practice the perfection of wisdom in that manner are approaching all-aspect omniscience

div.p: teaches the “what it is for.”
There, “what is it” is a question about its basic nature. There the perfection of wisdom should be described as a realization.
“Of what is it” is a question about what it is connected with. There it should be described as a realization of all dharmas.
“Why is it” is a question about the reason it is the perfection of wisdom. There it should be said it is because it is a realization marked by the state of things as they really are.
“What is it for” is a question about function. byed pa; Mvy 4 karaṇīya, 14 kāraka. There it should be said it is because it causes an escape.
It says

q.p: “when they investigate and ponder”
q.orig: while making this investigation and pondering it
if they practice while wondering

div.p: the responses that have to be made to all those

q.p: “like that”—
q.orig: while
whether that

div.p: as in the response to the above question “what is it?”—

q.p:
“if… they see that the dharma that does not exist and that they do not find is the perfection of wisdom they still do not see it.” D, Golden 143a1–2. khri brgyad (ka 85a4) de legs par mthong ba lags te, “they see it well”; nyi khri
yang dag par mthong ba, “…perfectly.”
q.orig: If, when they investigate and ponder like that, they see that the dharma that does not exist and that they do not find is the perfection of wisdom, they see it well
they observe that the nonexistence and nonapprehensibility of anything at all denote the perfection of wisdom
phenomenon that does not exist and cannot be apprehended is the perfection of wisdom

div.p: If they thus see that the dharma that does not exist and is not found is the perfection of wisdom, that too is not seeing.

What does this intend? It means that at that time even the intrinsic nature of all dharmas that cannot be apprehended is like space, so, when that which has viewed it is a seeing without an intrinsic nature, it is a perfect seeing.
Therefore, it says

q.p: “because, Lord, all dharmas do not exist and are not found.”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, it is because all phenomena are nonexistent and nonapprehensible

div.p: It means during that period.

When the elder Subhūti says khri brgyad
.

q.p: “you should know”
q.orig: one should know
one should know

div.p: that those who, when they see that all dharmas, form and so on, are not real things,

q.p: “are not cowed… and do not tremble,”
q.orig: are not cowed, do not tense up, and do not experience regret—if they do not tremble, feel frightened, or become terrified
are not disheartened, not intimidated, not afraid, not terrified, and will not be terrified
they are not discouraged, not utterly discouraged, not afraid, not frightened, and not fearful

div.p: and so on, are not separated from the knowledge of all aspects, the elder Śāriputra, to teach the mark of nonseparation, asks,

q.p: “Venerable Subhūti, why should you know that they are not separated from the knowledge of all aspects?”
q.orig: Venerable Subhūti, why should you know that bodhisattva great beings…are not separated from the knowledge of all aspects?”
Venerable Subhūti, why should one know that these bodhisattva great beings will not be separated from the perfection of wisdom
“Venerable Subhūti, why should one know that these bodhisattva great beings will not be separated from the perfection of wisdom?”

div.p: At that point the elder Subhūti says that because all dharmas are separated from an intrinsic nature, therefore

q.p: “you should know”
q.orig: one should know
one should know[1]

div.p: that those who see that this is so

q.p: “are not separated from the knowledge of all aspects.”
q.orig: will not be separated from the perfection of wisdom
will not be separated from the perfection of wisdom

div.p: With, khri brgyad, nyi khri omit “because of this one of many explanations.”

q.p: “Venerable Śāriputra, because of this one of many explanations, form does not have the intrinsic nature of form,”
q.orig: “Venerable Śāriputra,” replied Subhūti, “…form[2]
Venerable Śāradvatīputra,” replied the venerable Subhūti, “physical forms are without the inherent nature of physical forms
“Venerable Śāradvatīputra,” replied the venerable Subhūti, “physical forms are without the essential nature of physical forms

div.p: and so on, he answers the question “of what” is it the perfection of wisdom? Given that all dharmas are not real things because they are separated from an intrinsic nature, what dharmas does it then realize so that it is taught to be “the perfection of wisdom”?
From,

q.p: “Furthermore, Venerable Śāriputra, form does not have the defining mark of form,”
q.orig: Furthermore, Venerable Śāriputra, form is separated from the defining mark of form
Moreover, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, physical forms are without the defining characteristics of physical forms
Moreover, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, physical forms are without the defining characteristics of physical forms

div.p: up to those

q.p: “who are training in this… go forth to the knowledge of all aspects,”
q.orig: who are training in this training go forth to the knowledge of all aspects
Bodhisattva great beings who undertake this training will be emancipated in all-aspect omniscience
Venerable Subhūti, will those bodhisattva great beings who undertake this training be emancipated in all-aspect omniscience?

div.p: teaches why it is a perfection of wisdom. It is posited as “the perfection of wisdom” because it realizes the marks of all dharmas. This is teaching that if all dharmas have no marks and are separated from marks, what are the marks it realizes? It is saying because all marks are falsely imagined, are nonexistent, therefore the true nature of dharmas is separated from the mark of form and so on.

From, khri brgyad
–.

q.p: “Venerable Subhūti, do bodhisattva great beings training in this training go forth to the knowledge of all aspects?”
q.orig: Venerable Subhūti, will bodhisattva great beings who undertake this training be emancipated in all-aspect omniscience
Those bodhisattva great beings who undertake this training will be emancipated in all-aspect omniscience.

div.p: up to,

Venerable Śāradvatīputra, bodhisattva great beings who practice the perfection of wisdom in that manner are approaching all-aspect omniscience
bodhisattva great beings who practice the perfection of wisdom in that manner are approaching all-aspect omniscience.

div.p: teaches what this perfection of wisdom is for. It is a “perfection of wisdom” because it causes an escape. That escape, furthermore, is not to all dharmas,

q.p: “because all dharmas have not been produced and have not gone forth.”
q.orig: because all phenomena are unborn [in cyclic existence]…and unemancipated [in nirvāṇa]
If you ask why, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, it is because all phenomena are unborn and unemancipated

div.p: Hence it is also teaching that it also does not cause an escape.

q.p: “Venerable Śāriputra… form is empty of form. You cannot get at its production and going forth.”
q.orig: “Venerable Śāriputra,” replied Subhūti…You cannot get at its production and going forth[1].
Venerable Śāradvatīputra,” replied Subhūti, “physical forms are empty of physical forms. In them birth is not apprehended, nor is emancipation apprehended
“Venerable Śāradvatīputra,” replied Subhūti, “physical forms are empty of physical forms, and therein birth is not apprehended nor is emancipation apprehended.

div.p: This means that because the thoroughly established true dharmic nature of form is empty of the intrinsic nature of falsely imagined form, therefore there is no production and going forth of a defiled nature during the period of saṃsāra, and no mistaken entity exists in the purified nature during the purified period. Hence a going forth plucked out of thin air does not exist, because in its intrinsic nature it is purity, and the true nature of dharmas does not change. It

q.p: “has not been produced”
q.orig: have not been produced
are unborn
are unborn

div.p: during the period when it has stains, and it

q.p: “has not gone forth”
q.orig: have not gone forth
unemancipated
unemancipated

div.p: during the period when it is stainless.

div.head: Practice of method Earlier ( ) our author calls this division “the practice of method.” Here (F.104.a) he calls this section brtson par sgrub pa, “practice as perseverance,” and (, F.105.a) brtson pa’i sgrub pa “practice of perseverance,” with the practice of method as a subset.
div.p:
Having thus taught the practice that has made a full investigation, next, to teach the practice as perseverance is the passage from where it says, khri brgyad
–.

q.p: “Lord, if bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom without skillful means practice form,”
q.orig: “Lord, if bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom without skillful means…practice form
Blessed Lord, when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom… if they engage unskillfully with physical forms
“Blessed Lord, if, when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom, they engage unskillfully with physical forms

div.p: and so on, up to the end:

q.p: “Śāriputra… they… bodhisattva great beings… are close to the knowledge of all aspects.”
q.orig: Śāradvatīputra, one should know that these bodhisattva great beings are approaching all-aspect omniscience
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, one should know that these bodhisattva great beings are approaching all-aspect omniscience

div.p: This practice as perseverance is also taught in two parts: the lack of method that has to be eliminated, and the method that has to be resorted to. The lack of method is explained in two parts as well: the practice of causal signs, and the practice of enactment. The method to be resorted to is also explained in two parts: not practicing dharmas, and not practicing the causal signs of dharmas.
Among these, the practice of causal signs because of lacking method is from

q.p: “if… without skillful means [bodhisattva great beings] practice form they practice a causal sign; they do not practice the perfection of wisdom,”
q.orig: if bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom without skillful means…practice form…they practice a causal sign; they do not practice the perfection of wisdom.
if they engage unskillfully with physical forms…then they are merely engaging with distinguishing marks and are not practicing the perfection of wisdom
if, when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom, they engage unskillfully with physical forms, they are engaging with mental images.

div.p:
up to where it says, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “You should know that this is the bodhisattva great beings’ lack of skillful means.”
q.orig: One should know this to be the lack of skillful means that bodhisattva great beings might have
One should know those bodhisattva great beings lack skillful means.

div.p:
The practice of enactment because of lacking method starts from where it says khri brgyad
–.

q.p: “possess, form a notion of, and believe in form,”
q.orig: possess, form a notion of, and believe in form[2]
they are intent on, perceive, and find sustenance in physical forms,
they are intent on, perceive, and possess physical forms

div.p: and is up to,

q.p: “Venerable Śāriputra, you should know that bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom like that are without skillful means.”
q.orig: Venerable Śāradvatīputra, if bodhisattvas practice the perfection of wisdom in that manner, one should know them to be without skill in means
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, if bodhisattvas practice the perfection of wisdom in that manner, one should know them to be without skillful means.

div.p: They “possess” because of mental error, “form a notion” because of perceptual error, and “believe” because of philosophical error. “Possess” (gnas, adhisthā), “form a notion” (kun tu shes, saṃjñā), and “believe” (mos, adhimuc). In “mental error,” the “mind” (citta) is a basic awareness or bare thought; “perception” (’du shes, saṃjñā) is the discrimination or naming of the known; and “philosophical view” (dṛṣṭi) is a belief formed about what is known.

For the practice of method, the practice without apprehending Here “practice without apprehending” (mi dmigs par), as at nyi khri (ka 151b4–152a1), is rendering PSP 1-1: 182, Ghoṣa 824, Gilgit 291.7 nopaiti (na upa-i), literally “go near”; and LSPW “approaches.” khri brgyad (ka 90a3) renders it consistently by khas len (“assert”): “If, while practicing the perfection of wisdom they assert (khas len) any dharma, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.” dharmas starts from where it says, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “Venerable Śāriputra… when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom they do not practice form,”
q.orig: “Venerable Śāriputra,” replied Subhūti, “if, when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom they do not practice form[1]
Venerable Śāradvatīputra,” replied Subhūti, “when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom, and do not engage with physical forms
“Venerable Śāradvatīputra,” replied Subhūti, “when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom they do not engage with physical forms.

div.p: and goes up to,

q.orig: then at that time one should know that those bodhisattva great beings do possess skill in means
Venerable Śāradvatīputra…do possess skillful means

div.p:
I have already explained “the emptiness of form is not form” and so on above,
–. They will be explained in more detail later ( – ). so there is no need to repeat the explanation here.
In the practice of method, practice without apprehending the causal signs of dharmas starts from where it says, khri brgyad (ka 90a2–7) has khas len (“assert”) in place of dmigs.

q.orig: If, while practicing the perfection of wisdom…they assert any dharma, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Even when they are practicing the perfection of wisdom, they do not accept that they are practicing it
do not apprehend…that they are practicing

div.p: and goes up to

q.p: “[those] bodhisattva great beings… are close to the knowledge of all aspects.”
q.orig: bodhisattva great beings thus practicing the perfection of wisdom are close to the knowledge of all aspects
these bodhisattva great beings are approaching all-aspect omniscience
these bodhisattva great beings are approaching all-aspect omniscience

div.p:
There, connect the four alternatives that khri brgyad
; cp. nyi khri .

q.p: “they apprehend… they do not apprehend… they apprehend when they apprehend and do not apprehend when they do not apprehend… and they neither apprehend nor not apprehend”
q.orig: they assert any dharma they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom…Even if they do not so assert, they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom. Even if they do assert when they so assert and do not assert when they do not so assert,…they are not practicing the perfection of wisdom. Even if they neither so assert nor do not so assert

Even when they are practicing the perfection of wisdom, they do not accept that they are practicing it…even when they are neither practicing nor not practicing it, they do not accept that they are [neither practicing nor] not practicing it
Those bodhisattva great beings…nor not practicing

with causal signs; and construe these four this way: khri brgyad
.

q.p: “ ‘I am practicing,’… ‘I am not practicing,’… ‘I am practicing when I am practicing and not practicing when I am not practicing,’ and… ‘I am neither practicing nor not practicing’ ”
q.orig: ‘I am practicing,’ do not assert ‘I am not practicing,’ do not assert ‘I am practicing when I am practicing and not practicing when I am not practicing,’ and do not assert, ‘I am neither practicing nor not practicing.’

div.p: with causal signs as well.

q.p:
“The perfection of wisdom is without an intrinsic nature and cannot be found” khri brgyad
; cf. PSP 1-1: 182, Ghoṣa 824, Gilgit 291.9.—
q.orig: this is because they do not apprehend the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom

div.p: at the thoroughly established stage all dharmas cannot be apprehended, so even the perfection of wisdom does not exist on account of the perfection of wisdom’s own intrinsic nature.

div.head: Practice for quickly fully awakening
div.p:
Having thus taught the practice of perseverance, now, with khri brgyad
–.

q.p: “furthermore… that knowledge of all aspects is not two and cannot be divided into two,”
q.orig: furthermore…because all dharmas are the same…as…things that are not real, that knowledge of all aspects is not two and cannot be divided into two.
This all-aspect omniscience indeed is without duality and cannot be divided into two
This all-aspect omniscience, furthermore, is without duality and cannot be divided into two

div.p: and so on, it teaches the practice for quickly fully awakening. This practice is also taught in four parts:

item.p: training in the meditative stabilization spheres,
training in not apprehending all dharmas,
training in the illusion-like and so on, and
training in skillful means.

div.p:
Among them, the training in meditative stabilizations starts from khri brgyad
.

q.p: “because all dharmas are things that are not real, that knowledge of all aspects is not two and cannot be divided into two,”
q.orig: because all dharmas are the same…as…things that are not real, that knowledge of all aspects is not two and cannot be divided into two.
This all-aspect omniscience indeed is without duality and cannot be divided into two
should train in the applications of mindfulness

div.p: and goes up to

q.p: “one should train in the applications of mindfulness.”
q.orig: This all-aspect omniscience, furthermore, is without duality and cannot be divided into two

div.p: Training in not apprehending all dharmas is taught in the passage starting from where it says,

q.p: “Śāriputra, when bodhisattva great beings train like that in the perfection of wisdom,”
q.orig: Śāriputra,” replied the Lord, “bodhisattva great beings training like that do train in the perfection of wisdom
Śāradvatīputra,” replied the Blessed Lord, “when bodhisattva great beings train accordingly, they do train in the perfection of wisdom
bodhisattva great beings…not apprehending anything[1]

div.p: and

q.p: “they train in the eighteen distinct attributes of a buddha, by way of not apprehending anything,”
q.orig: including the eighteen distinct attributes of the buddhas, without apprehending anything
train in the distinct qualities of the buddhas by way of not apprehending anything

div.p: and so on, up to the end:

q.p: “Śāriputra, they go forth to the knowledge of all aspects by way of not apprehending emptiness.”
q.orig: “Śāriputra,” replied the Lord, “they go forth to the knowledge of all aspects by way of not apprehending the emptiness of the knowledge of all aspects.”
You should know that they will be emancipated in all-aspect omniscience without apprehending anything with respect to the…including the emptiness of the essential nature of nonentities
they become emancipated in all-aspect omniscience by way of not apprehending anything

div.p:
Training in the illusion-like and so on is taught in the passage starting from where it says, khri brgyad
–.

q.p: “Lord, suppose someone were to ask, ‘Does this illusory being, having trained in the perfection of wisdom, go forth to the knowledge of all aspects or reach the knowledge of all aspects?’ ”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, suppose someone were to ask if this illusory…person… after training in the perfection of wisdom, will be emancipated in all-aspect omniscience, or if he or she will attain all-aspect omniscience
“Blessed Lord, suppose someone were to ask if this illusory person, after training in the perfection of wisdom, will go forth to all-aspect omniscience or attain all-aspect omniscience.

div.p: up to,

q.p: “Because, Lord, form is like an illusion, and feeling … perception… volitional factors… and consciousness is like an illusion, and what that consciousness is, the six faculties are. They are the five aggregates.”
q.orig: Because, Lord,[2] form is like an illusion, and feeling…perception…volitional factors…and consciousness is like an illusion, and what that consciousness is, the six faculties are. They are the five aggregates
physical forms are like a phantom, and feelings…perceptions, formative predispositions, and consciousness are like a phantom.

physical forms are like an illusion, feelings are like an illusion, perceptions are like an illusion, formative predispositions are like an illusion, and consciousness is like an illusion. What is true of consciousness is true of the six sense faculties, and that is true of the five aggregates.

div.p:
Skillful means is taught in the passage starting from where it says, khri brgyad
–.

q.p: “Subhūti… if they are bodhisattva great beings who have newly set out in the vehicle, and are those without skillful means who have not been taken in hand by a spiritual friend,”
q.orig: Subhūti,” replied the Blessed One, “bodhisattva great beings who newly embark on the [Great] Vehicle will be afraid, fearful, and terrified if they are unskilled in the perfection of wisdom, and if they are not taken in hand by a spiritual mentor.

“Subhūti,” replied the Blessed One, “bodhisattva great beings who newly embark in the Vehicle will be afraid, fearful, and terrified if they are unskilled in the perfection of wisdom, and if they are not taken in hand by a spiritual mentor.”

div.p: up to

q.p: “someone… Subhūti, they should know is a bad friend of a bodhisattva great being.”
q.orig: bodhisattva great beings should know these evil associates
You should know that those who do not mention and reveal the aspects of these sorts of demonic activities are the evil associates of bodhisattva great beings.

div.head: Training in the meditative stabilization spheres
div.p: Among these, training in meditative stabilizations is taught in two parts: an explanation of the names and an explanation of nonconceptualization.

Among these, in regard to the explanation of names, it first teaches meditative stabilization in the form of nonproduction with, Cf. nyi khri , khri brgyad
. The sarva­dharmānutpāda is the first in the list of meditative stabilizations.

q.p: “Furthermore, because all dharmas are things that are not real, that knowledge of all aspects is not two and cannot be divided into two,”
q.orig: Furthermore, because all dharmas are the same…as…things that are not real, that knowledge of all aspects is not two and cannot be divided into two
This all-aspect omniscience indeed is without duality and cannot be divided into two
This all-aspect omniscience, furthermore, is without duality and cannot be divided into two

div.p: and so on. Construe “knowledge of all aspects” as the stage when all dharmas are not two, because for all imaginary dharmas there is bifurcation into grasped-object and grasper-subject, exist and does not exist, real thing and unreal thing, eternal and annihilated, compounded and uncompounded, dharma and nondharma, and so on, as well as into permanent and impermanent, pleasure and suffering, having a self and selfless, calm and not calm, empty and not empty, having a sign and signless, wished for and wishless, and so on. All those pairs are falsely imagined phenomena, and because they do not exist in the knowledge of all aspects it says the “knowledge of all aspects is not two.” A real twofold thing arrived at through realization Emend rtog to rtogs. does not exist, so it says “cannot be divided into two.”

Having taught abiding in meditative stabilization by giving the names of the meditative stabilizations, then, to teach abiding in nonconceptual meditative stabilization, it says khri brgyad
.

q.p: “those… do not even see those meditative stabilizations, because they do not falsely project on account of those meditative stabilizations, ‘I have been absorbed,’ ”
q.orig: those who abide by means of those meditative stabilizations do not see even those meditative stabilizations, because they do not falsely project on account of those meditative stabilizations, ‘I have been absorbed
Bodhisattva great beings do not even observe those meditative stabilities. They will not give rise to conceits on account of those meditative stabilities, thinking, ‘I have been absorbed
They do not give rise to conceit on account of those meditative stabilities, thinking, ‘I have been absorbed in meditation. I am absorbed in meditation. I will be absorbed in meditation.’

div.p: and so on. They “do not even see meditative stabilization” because it is the meditative stabilization at the thoroughly established stage when all dharmas have become just suchness.

Because the falsely imagined “I will be in meditative equipoise” and so on ’bum , nyi khri : “I am in meditative equipoise”; “I am entering into meditative equipoise”; “I will be in meditative equipoise”; and “the meditative equipoise will have happened” (mnyam par gzhag par gyur to). are totally nonexistent, the threefold conceptualizations based on time periods of them as meditative stabilization and of oneself in meditative equipoise, and the conceptualization of entering into absorption and conceptualization do not exist. Therefore, it says,

q.p: “Those bodhisattva great beings do not conceive of those.”
q.orig: All such conceptual imaginations are absent
Those conceptual imaginations are absent and will not arise.

div.p: And just because of that it says,

q.p: “The perfection of wisdom is not one thing, the meditative stabilization another, and the bodhisattva yet another. Bodhisattvas themselves are the meditative stabilization, and the meditative stabilization itself is the bodhisattva.”
q.orig: the perfection of wisdom, the meditative stabilities, and bodhisattva great beings are not distinct from one another. Rather, the perfection of wisdom itself constitutes the meditative stabilities. The meditative stabilities themselves constitute the bodhisattvas. The bodhisattvas themselves constitute the meditative stabilities
‘the perfection of wisdom is one thing, the meditative stability another, and the bodhisattva yet another.’

div.p: It says that because all dharmas have the same nature as mere suchness. And just because of that, it says

q.p: “because all dharmas are the same.”
q.orig: owing to the sameness of all phenomena
owing to the sameness of all phenomena

q.p: “Is it possible to teach the meditative stabilization?”—
q.orig: is it then possible to teach those meditative stabilities
is it then possible to teach the meditative stability?

div.p: which is to say, is it possible to differentiate them and describe it? He asks, thinking that in that case the bodhisattvas themselves would be the meditative stabilizations. In order to explain that the mark of a meditative stabilization is not different it says,

q.p: “No indeed, Venerable Śāriputra.”
q.orig: Venerable Śāradvatīputra, it is not!
No indeed, Venerable Śāriputra

div.p: Then the elder Śāriputra, wondering why, if the names of the meditative stabilizations do not exist, their names were given, asks, nyi khri . The word saṃjñā (“notion,” “name,” and “discrimination,” “perception”) is rendered ’du shes here and in ’bum and nyi khri, and kun tu shes in khri brgyad (ka 93a7).

q.p: “Do they form a notion of those meditative stabilizations?”
q.orig: do the children of a good family form a notion of those meditative stabilizations?
do those noble children perceive these meditative stabilities
do those children of good family…perceive these meditative stabilities?”

div.p: He is asking, “Like śrāvakas do?” Then, because such mental construction does not exist, venerable Subhūti says,

q.p: “They do not form such notions.”
q.orig: they do not perceive them
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, they do not perceive them!

div.p: Then, because the explanation of the meditative stabilizations has been taught in one explanation and the activity taught in another, Śāriputra asks,

q.p: “How do they not form such notions?”
q.orig: How do they not perceive them
“How do they not perceive them?

div.p: Then, because the meditative stabilizations and their functions exist with a falsely imagined nature but cannot be apprehended when the marks of the falsely imagined have been eliminated, Subhūti therefore says,

q.p: “They do not mentally construct them.”
q.orig: They[2]…do not mentally construct them
they are without conceptual thought
Because they are without conceptual thought

div.p: Then, to eliminate the thought of “mine,” it says

q.p: “because all phenomena do not exist.” nyi khri ; Gilgit 294.6 avidya­mānatvena.
q.orig: because all phenomena are nonexistent
because all phenomena are nonexistent

div.p:
Thus, take the “conflict” in nyi khri ; cf. khri brgyad
.

q.p: “taught to be the foremost of śrāvakas at the conflict-free stage”
q.orig: are the foremost of śrāvakas at the conflict-free stage
declared to be foremost among śrāvakas practicing free from afflicted mental states
declared to be supreme among śrāvakas abiding free of conflict

div.p: as conceptualization. Freedom from all thought construction, absorption into the nonconceptual, is absorption into “the conflict-free.” Hence the Lord confers an

q.p: “excellent!”
q.orig: Well said
Excellent[1]

div.p: on the nonconceptual state.

div.head: Training in not apprehending all dharmas
div.p:
Having thus given an exposition of the training in meditative stabilization, to teach training in not apprehending it says, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “Śāriputra… training like that… up to they train in the eighteen distinct attributes of a buddha, by way of not apprehending anything,”
q.orig: “Śāriputra,” replied the Lord, “bodhisattva great beings training like that do train in the perfection of wisdom, by way of not apprehending anything. Similarly, they train in the perfection of concentration, the perfection of perseverance, the perfection of patience,…the perfection of morality, and the perfection of giving, by way of not apprehending anything. Similarly, they train in the thirty-seven dharmas on the side of awakening, by way of not apprehending anything, and similarly, up to they train in the eighteen distinct attributes of a buddha, by way of not apprehending anything.
Śāradvatīputra,” replied the Blessed Lord, “when bodhisattva great beings train accordingly, …up to and including the eighteen distinct attributes of the buddhas, without apprehending anything.
Then Venerable… And do they train in the distinct qualities of the buddhas by way of not apprehending anything?”

div.p: and so on.
To teach training in not apprehending, it gives an exposition of not apprehending persons with,

q.p: “Śāriputra, because of the state of absolute purity they do not apprehend a self,”
q.orig: “Śāriputra,” replied the Lord, “because of the state of absolute purity they do not apprehend a self
Owing to the utter purity…[of all phenomena], they do not apprehend a self
Owing to utter purity,… they do not apprehend a self

div.p: and so on. It then gives an exposition of not apprehending all dharmas, with

q.p: “aggregates, constituents, sense fields,”
q.orig: aggregates, the sense fields, the sensory elements
Owing to utter purity… they do not apprehend the six sense fields.

div.p: and so on, teaching

q.p: “they do not apprehend a stream enterer,”
q.orig: they do not apprehend those who enter the stream to nirvāṇa
Owing to utter purity, they do not apprehend those who have entered the stream.

div.p: and so on, up to

q.p: “a buddha.”
q.orig: buddhas
they do not apprehend buddhas

div.p: As for

q.p: “because of the state of absolute purity”
q.orig: Owing to the utter purity
Owing to utter purity

div.p: they all “All” means both self and dharmas. have, having taken the completion of purification to be serving as a cause, in order to inquire about its intrinsic nature he asks,

q.p: “Lord, what is purity?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, what is that purity
Blessed Lord, what is purity?

div.p: The Lord, to teach that the stainless, thoroughly established suchness is purity, says,

q.p: “Śāriputra, not being produced, not stopping, not being defilement, not being purification, not appearing, not being apprehended, and not occasioning anything is called the purity of all dharmas.”
q.orig: “Śāriputra,” replied the Lord, “not being produced, not stopping, not being defilement, not being purification, not appearing, not being apprehended, and not occasioning anything is called the purity of all dharmas.”
Purity indicates that all phenomena are nonarising, unceasing, neither afflicted nor purified, nonemerging, nonapprehensible, and unconditioned
That all phenomena are nonarising, unceasing, neither defiled nor purified, nonemerging, not apprehended, and unconditioned is called their purity

div.p: Earlier, during the period when suchness has stains, all dharmas are produced and stop, are defiled and purified as falsely imagined phenomena. The produced comes into being and, having come into being, it is apprehended like this and like that, occasioning things like this and like that. During the period when there are no stains, in each and every way, the production of all dharmas in that suchness is nonexistent. Because there is no production, there is no stopping; because there are no stains there is no defilement, no purification, and no appearing; because there is no appearing there is no apprehending; and because there is no apprehending, there is not occasioning anything. This is called “absolute purity.”

q.p: “Do not train in any dharma”—
q.orig: do not train in anything at all
do not train in anything at all

div.p: because bodhisattvas do not see all dharmas during the period when there are no stains, it says

q.p: “those dharmas do not exist “Do not exist” (yod pa ma yin, na saṃvidyante). in the way foolish, ordinary people take them to be.”
q.orig: these phenomena are nonexistent in the ways that ordinary people are fixated on them
because these phenomena do not exist in the way that foolish ordinary people are fixated…on them

div.p: To teach that marked as being falsely imagined they are nonexistent it says,

q.p: “Śāriputra, as they do not exist, so do they exist.”
q.orig: “Śāriputra,” replied the Lord, “as they do not exist, so do they exist
They exist to the extent that they do not exist
As they do not exist, so do they exist

div.p:
To teach that they exist in the inexpressible form of a falsely imagined thing that does not exist it says, khri brgyad
; nyi khri
de’i phyir med ces bya’o. Skt vid means both “know” and “exist.”

q.p: “Thus, they do not exist, so one says ignorance.”
q.orig: since they do not exist, they are said to be nonexistent
Because they thus do not exist, they are therefore said to be ‘nonexistent,’

div.p: This means that like dream consciousness it is not in its nature a state of perfect reality. Even while not there, it causes grasping at other things that do not exist. Alternatively, it does not know perfectly, which is to say, it causes imperfect knowledge and understanding, hence it is “ignorance.”
Śāriputra asks,

q.p: “Lord why are the nonexistent called ignorance?”
q.orig: “Lord, why are the nonexistent called ignorance?”
Blessed Lord,” he asked, “why are these phenomena that do not exist said to exist
“Blessed Lord,” he asked, “why are the nonexistent said to be ‘nonexistent’?”

div.p: and it says,

q.p: “Śāriputra, form does not exist,”
q.orig: “Śāriputra,” replied the Lord,…exist[1]
Śāradvatīputra…physical forms are nonexistent
Śāradvatīputra,” replied the Blessed One, “physical forms are nonexistent

div.p: and so on. Here is what it intends: even though dharmas are thus nonexistent and unreal, they are grasped as if they really exist, so they are not known perfectly, which is to say are not understood perfectly, so it is “ignorance.” To teach that, the Lord bka’ stsal identifies what is said by the Lord. says the dharmas, “form” and so on, do not exist.

To make just this meaning clear it says, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “Those foolish people [who] settle down on them because of ignorance and craving… are attached to the two extremes.”
q.orig: “Those foolish people settle down on them because of ignorance and craving, mentally constructing what does not exist. Having settled down on what does not exist, they are attached to the two extremes,

ordinary people, through their fixations on phenomena that are nonexistent, become fixated on their cravings. By imagining phenomena that are nonexistent, they become fixated on that which is nonexistent, and through their adherence to the two extremes

There, foolish ordinary people, through their fixation on the nonexistent, are fixated on their cravings. By imagining the nonexistent, they are fixated on the nonexistent…and through adherence to the two extremes of eternalism and nihilism

div.p: It means having settled down on the aspect of existence through the power of ignorance and having settled down by way of relishing the experience through the power of craving, they become “attached to the two extremes,”

q.p: “permanence and annihilation.”
q.orig: eternalism and nihilism
eternalism and nihilism

q.p: “They do not know, and they do not see”—

div.p: that is to say, they do not understand with inferential or direct perception, or else on account of the force of scripture or the force of their own personality.
This is in three parts, where it lists the dharmas in the context of explaining:

item.p: they have come about rooted in ignorance,
they have come about rooted in thought construction, and
they have come about rooted in the absence of faith.

div.p: There, the first section explains that having grasped dharmas as existing where they do not exist because of the power of ignorance, and through the power of relishing the experience because of craving, having fallen into the two extremes, fools “do not know and do not see.”

The second section explains they thus do not know and see, therefore mental constructions multiply. Mentally constructing dharmas not for what they are and settling down on them, mentally constructing them at the two extremes, they “do not know and do not see.” Because they do not know and see all dharmas khri brgyad
.

q.p: “they are, therefore, counted as fools. They will not definitely emerge.”
q.orig: they are, therefore, counted as fools.
In such ways, due to which they are counted among ‘ordinary people,’ they will not attain emancipation
This is why they come to be styled ‘foolish ordinary people.’ These people will not be emancipated

div.p:
The third section similarly explains that even though they have heard about them for what they really are, “they do not place their faith” in that reality, so, because they do not abide in serene confidence “they do not rest” in the perfections; and because they do not rest in the practice they do not attain the dharmas to be realized, such as becoming irreversible from awakening and so on. So khri brgyad
.

q.p: “they are, therefore, counted as fools,”
q.orig: That is why they are called ‘ordinary people
This is why…they are called ‘foolish

div.p: as ordinary people, because of the fault of settling down on all dharmas.

Having been taught that those like that do not train in them and do not go forth, there is the question, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “Why… do they… not train… and not go forth?”
q.orig: “Why, Lord, do those bodhisattva great beings not train in the perfection of wisdom and not go forth to the knowledge of all aspects?”
why are those bodhisattvas not training in the perfection of wisdom, and why will they not be emancipated in all-aspect omniscience
“Blessed Lord, why do those bodhisattvas not train in the perfection of wisdom, and why will they not be emancipated in all-aspect omniscience?”

div.p: And it says they “do not train” because

q.p: “without skillful means they mentally construct and settle down on”
q.orig: without skillful means mentally construct a perfection of wisdom and settle down on it
bodhisattva great beings who are unskillful have conceived of and become fixated on
who are unskillful have conceived of and become fixated

div.p: all the perfections and all the practice dharmas; and they “do not go forth” because they mentally construct and settle down on the dharmas on the side of awakening and so on, up to

q.p: “the knowledge of all aspects.”
q.orig: all-aspect omniscience
in all-aspect omniscience

div.p:
It also says khri brgyad
–. that practicing those same perfections without apprehending all dharmas is named having entered into the training, and not apprehending the knowledge of all aspects, and the dharmas, up to, the emptiness of all dharmas is going forth.

div.head: Training in the illusion-like
div.p:
Having thus explained the training in not apprehending all dharmas, to teach training in the illusion-like and so on, it says, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “Lord, suppose someone were to ask,”

div.p: and so on. Here this is what venerable Subhūti is thinking: “Lord, if they practice without apprehending anything then there are no dharmas. And were they to go forth having trained in dharmas that do not exist, well then, even a totally nonexistent illusory person acting out an illusion with illusory attention that cannot be apprehended would, having trained, go forth and accomplish the knowledge of all aspects.”

Then, in the first section explaining illusion, the Lord says: Just as there is no training in, or going forth to, illusory dharmas, similarly for bodhisattvas there is no training in the dharmas, form and so on, or going forth to them, or definitely reaching the knowledge of all aspects. To teach that they are like an illusion he asks, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “Subhūti, what do you think about this: Is illusion one thing and form another?”
q.orig: Subhūti…another[1]
Subhūti, do you think that physical forms are one thing, and that illusions are another
Subhūti, do you think that physical forms are one thing, and that illusions are another?

div.p:
and so on. And to teach that bodhisattvas skilled in the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature, who see that all dharmas cannot be apprehended, do not see falsely imagined dharmas like form and so on as existing apart from being illusions, there is the passage that ends, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “Illusion is not one thing, Lord, and the knowledge of all aspects another; the knowledge of all aspects is itself illusion, Lord, and illusion is itself the knowledge of all aspects.”
q.orig: [the attainments], up to and including enlightenment, are not one thing and illusions another. Enlightenment is itself illusion, and illusion itself is enlightenment
Blessed Lord, all-aspect omniscience is not one thing and illusions another. All-aspect omniscience is itself illusion, and illusion itself is all-aspect omniscience.”

div.p: It is saying that because all are in their intrinsic nature falsely imagined, they are, as the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature, undifferentiable from illusions.

Similarly, the second section explaining illusion says that because khri brgyad
.

q.p: “production… stopping… defilement and purification”
q.orig: no production, no stopping, no defilement,…and no purification
arising, cessation, affliction, or purification
arising, cessation, defilement, and purification

div.p: do not exist there is no training in all illusions and dharmas that absolutely do not exist, no going forth, and no reaching the knowledge of all aspects.

Then it teaches khri brgyad
–. that if the name bodhisattva is not said relative to the aggregates and so on, up to the distinct attributes, in that case, just like an illusory person, a bodhisattva does not exist; and because there is no production, stopping, and so on of the dharmas—from the aggregates and so on, up to the distinct attributes—they too, like illusions, do not exist, and names, conventional terms, and so on do not exist either, so how can totally nonexistent bodhisattvas train in totally nonexistent dharmas? How can they go forth, and how can they reach the knowledge of all aspects? Then in conclusion it says that when they

q.p: “train… like that, by way of not apprehending anything, they go forth to the knowledge of all aspects and reach the knowledge of all aspects.”
q.orig: have trained in the perfection of wisdom, by way of not apprehending anything, they will be emancipated in all-aspect omniscience. They will attain all-aspect omniscience
will train in the perfection of wisdom and then go forth to all-aspect omniscience, or attain all-aspect omniscience

div.p:
Thus, because of the nonexistence that is their intrinsic nature, those five aggregates are like a dream… an echo… an apparition… a reflection in a mirror… a magical creation… and a mirage, Cf. khri brgyad
, nyi khri . and because of just that the six sense fields are too, so a “bodhisattva” does not exist at all, because of the emptiness that is the nonexistence of its intrinsic nature.

div.head: Training in skillful means
div.p:
Having thus taught the training in the illusion-like and so on, to set the scene for training in skillful means it says, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “Lord, if bodhisattva great beings who have newly set out in the vehicle were to hear this exposition would they not tremble, feel frightened, and become terrified?”
q.orig: “Lord, if bodhisattva great beings who have newly set out in the vehicle were to hear this exposition, would they not…tremble, feel frightened, and become terrified?”
Blessed Lord, in that case, will bodhisattva great beings who have newly embarked upon the [Great] Vehicle not be afraid, fearful, and terrified when they hear this teaching
“Blessed Lord, in that case, will bodhisattva great beings who have newly embarked in the Vehicle not be afraid, fearful, and terrified when they hear this teaching?”

div.p: And then it explains that Both khri brgyad ka 100b6 and nyi khri ka 162b3 omit the last part.

q.p: “those without skillful means who have not been taken in hand by a spiritual friend, they will tremble, feel frightened, and become terrified, but those with skillful means will not tremble and become terrified.”
q.orig: those without skillful means who have not been taken in hand by a spiritual friend, …become terrified.

bodhisattva great beings who newly embark on the [Great] Vehicle will be afraid, fearful, and terrified if they are unskilled in the perfection of wisdom, and if they are not taken in hand by a spiritual mentor

“bodhisattva great beings who newly embark in the Vehicle will be afraid, fearful, and terrified if they are unskilled in the perfection of wisdom, and if they are not taken in hand by a spiritual mentor.”

div.p:
And it says, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “Lord, what skillful means do bodhisattva great beings who have newly set out in the vehicle have not to tremble, feel frightened, and become terrified when they hear this exposition?”
q.orig: “Lord, what skillful means do bodhisattva great beings who have newly set out in the vehicle have not to tremble, feel frightened, or become terrified when hearing this exposition?”

Blessed Lord, when bodhisattva great beings hear this teaching, what is the skill in means that enables them to practice the perfection of wisdom without being afraid, without being fearful, and without being terrified
“Blessed Lord, when bodhisattva great beings hear this teaching, what is the skillful means not to be afraid, not to be fearful, and not to be terrified of the perfection of wisdom?”

div.p: Thus, it gives an exposition of skillful means.
I have explained the meaning of “tremble, feel frightened” and so on before. .
Those skillful means are also explained in four parts:

item.p: skillful means of the analytic understanding of all dharmas,
skillful means of completing the six perfections,
skillful means of relying on a spiritual friend, and
skillful means of shunning a bad friend.

div.p:
Among these, starting from khri brgyad
.

q.p: “[they] analytically understand about form its impermanent aspect, but do not apprehend it,”
q.orig: here…bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom with attention connected with the knowledge of all aspects analytically understand about form its impermanent aspect, but do not apprehend it
they discern that physical forms are impermanent they do not apprehend that
they discern that physical forms are impermanent but do not apprehend that

div.p: up to

q.p: “you should know that this is the skillful means of bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom,”
q.orig: This, Subhūti, is the skill in means of bodhisattva great beings who practice the perfection of wisdom
This, Subhūti, is the skillful means of bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom.

div.p: teaches the skillful means of the analytic understanding of all dharmas.

Starting from, Cf. khri brgyad
–, nyi khri -. Our author perhaps intends that even the analytic understanding, each explanation of which is preceded and followed by these two extracts, is included in the completion of the six perfections, which are explicitly explained from this point on.

q.p: “Furthermore, Subhūti, bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom with attention connected with the knowledge of all aspects,”
q.orig: “Subhūti,” answered the Lord, “here…bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom with attention connected with the knowledge of all aspects
when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom, because their intention is directed toward all-aspect omniscience
when bodhisattva great beings practice…the perfection of wisdom with an intention connected with all-aspect omniscience

div.p: up to

q.p: “Subhūti, you should know that this is the skillful means of bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom,”
q.orig: This, Subhūti, is the skill in means of bodhisattva great beings who practice the perfection of wisdom
This, Subhūti, is the skillful means of bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom.

div.p: teaches the skillful means of completing the six perfections. Among them, giving expositions of Dharma by way of not apprehending anything is the perfection of giving; stopping śrāvaka and pratyekabuddha thoughts by way of not apprehending anything is the perfection of morality; forbearance and admiration for the deep dharmas is the perfection of patience; paying attention to not apprehending anything and not giving up analytic understanding is the perfection of perseverance; not providing an opportunity for unwholesome dharmas that are impediments to awakening is the perfection of concentration; and the analytic understanding of emptiness is the perfection of wisdom.

q.p:
“Form is not empty because of the emptiness of form” khri brgyad
.—
q.orig: Form is not empty because of the emptiness of form[2]
physical forms are not empty of the emptiness of physical forms
that physical forms are not empty of the emptiness of physical forms

div.p: the true dharmic nature of “form” does “not” become “empty” out of thin air “because of” being caused by “the emptiness of” falsely imagined “form,” because it is empty of an intrinsic nature. Therefore, it says

q.p: “form is itself emptiness, emptiness is itself form.”
q.orig: form is itself emptiness, and emptiness is itself form
physical forms is emptiness, and that emptiness is indeed physical forms
but that physical forms are emptiness, and that emptiness is indeed physical forms

div.p: This means emptiness and the true dharmic nature of form are the same intrinsic nature.

Starting from, khri brgyad
–.

q.p: “Subhūti, the spiritual friends of bodhisattva great beings,”
q.orig: Subhūti,” replied the Blessed One, “the spiritual mentors of bodhisattva great beings
“Subhūti,” replied the Blessed One, “the spiritual mentors of bodhisattva great beings

div.p: up to

q.p: “they, Subhūti, are the spiritual friends of bodhisattva great beings. If they have taken them in hand they do not tremble, feel frightened, or become terrified when they hear this exposition,”
q.orig: these, Subhūti, to be the spiritual mentors of bodhisattva great beings…These are the spiritual mentors by whom bodhisattva great beings are accepted and through whom they will not be afraid, fearful, or terrified on hearing this perfection of wisdom

“One should know that these, Subhūti, are the spiritual mentors of bodhisattva great beings, the spiritual mentors who have taken hold of bodhisattva great beings so that they will not be afraid, fearful, or terrified on hearing this teaching.”

div.p: teaches the skillful means of relying on a spiritual friend.

After that, the section of the text on false projections when apprehending things khri brgyad
(
“apprehend a perfection of wisdom while cultivating it, and falsely project it as the perfection of wisdom”), up to khri brgyad
. is included right with this, because it happens due to not having spiritual friends.

Starting from, Our author is either following a different version of the Sūtra or this is a corrupt reading. khri brgyad
, “Lord, why does a bodhisattva great being fall into the clutches of a bad friend,” makes better sense.

q.p: “How should you know you have been taken in hand by spiritual friends?”
q.orig: Lord, why does a bodhisattva great being fall into the clutches of a bad friend
how is it that bodhisattva great beings are enticed by evil associates
fall into the clutches of evil associates and are abandoned by spiritual mentors?”

div.p:
up to, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “Subhūti, they should know [that] is a bad friend of a bodhisattva great being, and knowing that, should shun them,”
q.orig: Subhūti, they should know is a bad friend of a bodhisattva great being, and knowing that, they should shun them
So it is that bodhisattva great beings should know these evil associates. Having understood them in that manner, you should abandon them
So it is that bodhisattva great beings should know these evil associates. Having understood them in that manner, they should abandon them.”

div.p: teaches the skillful means of shunning a bad friend.

div.head: Specific instruction for coming to an authoritative conclusion about this exposition
Part One: The twenty-eight [or twenty-nine] questions
div.p: Having thus differentiated and taught the passages to do with the inquiry into the endeavor’s many aspects, now the passages to do with the inquiry into specific instruction for coming to an authoritative conclusion about this exposition This is the last of the eight sections given earlier ( ), glossed ( ) as “the specific instruction for coming to an authoritative conclusion about this brief exposition in terms of the basis in reality and the characteristic marks.” will be explained.

There, the initial statement,
, citing khri brgyad
.

q.p: “Here, Śāriputra, bodhisattva great beings who want to fully awaken to all dharmas in all forms should make an effort at the perfection of wisdom,”
q.orig: “Śāradvatīputra, bodhisattva great beings … persevere in the perfection of wisdom.”

div.p:
which set the scene for the initial brief exegesis, now sets the scene here too. The specific instruction for coming to an authoritative conclusion, furthermore, is twofold: about the meaning of the words and about the characteristic marks. padārtha (“meaning of the words”) is explained more fully earlier in the notes and to . In it there are twenty-eight questions: khri brgyad
