–. The wording of some of the questions does not exactly follow the later wording found in the Sūtra. Furthermore, the first two, and possibly even the first three, are grouped together as one question in the later explanation. The statements that are not obvious questions are to be understood as rhetorical questions, repeating the words of the Lord with an implicit “You mean to say, then, that…?”

item.p: What is the meaning of the word bodhisattva?
What is the meaning of the term great being?
How are they armed with great armor?
How have they set out in the Great Vehicle?
How do they stand in the Great Vehicle?
How is it a great vehicle?
How have they come to set out in the Great Vehicle?
From where will the Great Vehicle go forth?
Where will that Great Vehicle stand?
Who will go forth in this vehicle?

It surpasses the world with its gods, humans, and asuras and goes forth. Is that why it is called a great vehicle? ; khri brgyad
.
That vehicle is equal to space?

The Great Vehicle is in harmony with the perfection of wisdom? This and all the remaining questions and responses are at khri brgyad
–. First are the statements made by Subhūti ( –) that are then queried by Śāriputra ( ), and then answered by Subhūti up to the end of the chapter ( ).
Why does one not apprehend a bodhisattva at the prior limit, the later limit, and in the middle?
Why does one have to know the limitlessness of a bodhisattva through the limitlessness of form, feeling, perception, volitional factors, and consciousness?
Why does even such an idea as “a bodhisattva is form, feeling, perception, volitional factors, and consciousness” not exist and why is it not found?
I, who thus do not see and do not find a bodhisattva great being as anyone at all in any way at all—to which bodhisattva great being will I give advice and instruction in which perfection of wisdom?
One says this, Lord, that is, “bodhisattva.” Is it just a word?
One says “self” again and again but it has absolutely not come into being?
Given that all dharmas thus have nonexistence for their intrinsic nature, what is that form, up to what is that consciousness?
Form has not come into being?
Does what has not come into being give advice and instruction in a perfection of wisdom that has not come into being?
You cannot apprehend a bodhisattva other than one who has not come into being?

One should know that when the mind of a bodhisattva great being given such instruction is not cowed, does not tense up, and does not experience regret, does not tremble, feel frightened, or become terrified, then that bodhisattva great being is practicing the perfection of wisdom?
What is a bodhisattva?
What is the perfection of wisdom?
What is it to investigate?
The nonproduction of form and so on is not form and so on?
A decrease in form and so on is not form and so on?
Anything called “form” and so on is counted as not two?

div.p:
Thus the topics that emerge from those twenty-eight questions, Here it says there are twenty-eight questions, and later ( ) it references the last in the list as the twenty-eighth question. Later ( ) it will say there is a list of twenty-nine questions. Below, the third question is introduced as the second, so the first two in the list are explained as just one question: “Why do you say bodhisattva great being?” Furthermore, because the response of Pūrṇa to why a bodhisattva is a great being incorporates the third in the list, our author incorporates it, in the body of his explanation, into a first, expanded question. and then the section of the text incorporating the hum of probing questions and responses by the two elders Śāriputra and Subhūti that goes up to the beginning of the Śakra Chapter, khri brgyad
–. should be known as the specific instruction for coming to an authoritative conclusion.

div.head: 1a. What is the meaning of the word bodhisattva?
div.p:
There, where it says, khri brgyad
and nyi khri
both differ slightly.

q.p: “Subhūti, the meaning of the word bodhisattva is an absence of a basis in reality,”
q.orig: “Subhūti, the basis in reality for bodhisattva is an absence of a basis in reality.
Subhūti, the actual entity denoted by the word bodhisattva is not an actual entity
the actual entity denoted by the word bodhisattva is not an actual entity denoted by a word.

div.p: bodhisattva has four ultimate meanings: awakening, a being, A bodhi-sattva is an “awakening-being.” the conventional bodhisattva constituted out of aggregates, and the ultimate bodhisattva. Because all four are the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature, the meaning of the word bodhisattva is “an absence of a basis in reality.” Construe “absence of a basis in reality” as an impossibility.

Were bodhisattva to have something real for its nature, the word for it would have a basis in reality and it would become a possibility, whereas awakening, a being, and both bodhisattvas do not exist, so the meaning of the word bodhisattva is the absence of a basis in reality, that is to say, an “impossibility.”
To separate the parts of this same topic it says,

q.p: “Subhūti, it is because bodhi and sattva are not produced. Awakening and a being do not have an arising or an existence. They cannot be apprehended.”
q.orig: Subhūti, it is because…they cannot be apprehended.
it is because bodhi (enlightenment) is nonarising and sattva (a being)…is nonarising
it is because bodhi (enlightenment) does not arise nor does sattva (a being) arise.

div.p: Awakening does not arise because it is an uncompounded phenomenon, and because a being does not exist it does not arise either. Therefore it should be construed as: “Subhūti, awakening does not have an arising” and “a being does not have an existence that can be apprehended.”
Then, to explain the locution “meaning of the word” it says,

q.p: “Subhūti, awakening has no basis in reality and a being has no basis in reality.”
q.orig: Subhūti[4], awakening has no basis in reality and a being has no basis in reality
Subhūti, in enlightenment there is no word, and in a being there is no word
Subhūti, in enlightenment there is no word, and in a being there is no word.

div.p: And it sums up in conclusion with,

q.p: “Therefore, a bodhisattva’s basis in reality is an absence of a basis in reality.”
q.orig: therefore a bodhisattva’s basis in reality is an absence of a basis in reality.
Therefore, the actual entity denoted by the word bodhisattva is not an actual entity
Therefore, the actual entity that is the word bodhisattva is not an actual entity that is a word.

div.p:
Then, to teach that the meaning of the word bodhisattva is an absence of a basis in reality it gives an elevenfold explanation: khri brgyad
.

q.p: “To illustrate, Subhūti, the track of a bird in space does not exist and cannot be apprehended,”
q.orig: Subhūti, just as in the sky there are no tracks left by birds
Subhūti, to illustrate, just as in the sky there are no tracks left by birds

div.p: and so on: that

item.p: awakening does not have a basis in a reality constructed in thought;

the basis of a falsely imagined “heroic being” “Heroic being” is a literal rendering of the Tib sems dpa’, a translation that in turn renders the second half of the older word bodhisatva before its Sanskritization to bodhisattva. It is elsewhere rendered into English consistently as “[bodhi]sattva.” does not exist at all;
a basis other and separate from awakening does not exist;
a basis separate from a conventional bodhisattva does not exist;
a basis of the true dharmic nature of a bodhisattva does not exist;
a basis for a heroic being does not exist in awakening;
a basis for awakening does not exist in a heroic being;
a basis in reality for “awakening” does not exist;
the meaning of the word for the falsely imagined “bodhisattva” does not exist in an unreal bodhisattva; and
a basis for an ultimate bodhisattva does not exist.

div.p: Among these, to teach that awakening does not have a basis in a reality constructed in thought it says,

q.p: “To illustrate, Subhūti, the track of a bird in space does not exist and cannot be apprehended,”
q.orig: Subhūti, just as in the sky there are no tracks left by birds
Subhūti, to illustrate, just as in the sky there are no tracks left by birds

div.p: and so on. This means that just as birds go through the sky but their tracks are not left there, similarly thought constructions move through awakening that is constituted out of suchness but do not remain there.
Then to teach that the basis of a falsely imagined bodhisattva does not exist in reality it says,

q.p: “To illustrate, Subhūti, in a dream a basis does not exist and cannot be apprehended,”
q.orig: Subhūti, in a dream a basis does not exist and cannot be apprehended
Subhūti, just as a dream is without any basis
Subhūti, just as a dream is without any basis

div.p: and so on. This means that a dream, an illusion, a mirage, an echo, an apparition, a reflection in a mirror, and a magical creation have no basis in reality because they are totally nonexistent. Similarly, bodhisattvas also have no basis in reality because they too do not exist.
Then to teach that a basis other than awakening does not exist it says,

q.p: “To illustrate further, Subhūti, in suchness a basis does not exist and cannot be apprehended,”
q.orig: Subhūti, just as the unmistaken real nature, the one and only real nature, reality, the realm of phenomena, the abiding nature of all phenomena, and the maturity of all phenomena are without any basis
Subhūti, just as the real nature is without any basis

div.p: and so on. This means that just as there is no basis other than suchness, unmistaken suchness, and so on, similarly there is no basis other than awakening.
Then to teach that a basis of a conventional bodhisattva does not exist it says,

q.p: “To illustrate further, Subhūti, in an illusory person a basis of form, feeling, perception, volitional factors, and consciousness does not exist and cannot be apprehended,”
q.orig: Subhūti, just as the physical form of an illusory … is without any basis, and just as the feelings, perceptions, formative predispositions, and consciousness [of an illusory … are without any basis
“Subhūti, just as the physical form of an illusory person is without any basis…is without any basis

div.p: and so on. This means that just as people who are illusory in nature do not have five aggregates and so on, because they are totally nonexistent, similarly conventional bodhisattvas also do not have a five-aggregate basis. phung po lnga’i gzhi med do. Probably the author intends to say there is no bodhisattva over and above the aggregates, and in that sense they are not the basis.
Then to teach that the true dharmic nature of a bodhisattva does not have five aggregates and so on it says,

q.p: “To illustrate, Subhūti, a basis of the form, feeling, perception, volitional factors, and consciousness of a tathāgata, worthy one, perfect complete buddha does not exist and cannot be apprehended.”
q.orig: To illustrate further, Subhūti, a basis of the form of a tathāgata, worthy one, perfectly complete buddha does not exist and cannot be apprehended. Similarly, Subhūti, a basis in reality for a bodhisattva when a bodhisattva great being is practicing the perfection of wisdom does not exist and cannot be apprehended
Subhūti, likewise the physical forms of a tathāgata, arhat, completely awakened buddha are without any basis

Subhūti, just as the physical form of a tathāgata, arhat, perfectly complete buddha is without any basis (if you ask why, it is because that physical form is nonexistent)…the consciousness of a tathāgata

div.p: and so on. This means that just as a dharma body tathāgata does not have five aggregates and so on, similarly an ultimate bodhisattva does not have five aggregates and so on either.

Then to teach that a basis for a heroic being K, N. D byang chub sems dpa’. does not exist in awakening it says, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “To illustrate further, Subhūti, in the uncompounded element a basis of the compounded element does not exist,”
q.orig: Subhūti, just as the presence of conditioned elements in the unconditioned expanse is without any basis
Subhūti, just as the conditioned element is without any basis in the unconditioned element

div.p: and so on. This means that just as saṃsāra does not exist in nirvāṇa, similarly a basis for a heroic being does not exist in awakening.
Then to teach that a basis for awakening does not exist in a heroic being it says

q.p: “in the compounded element a basis of the uncompounded element does not exist,”
q.orig: in the compounded element…a basis of the uncompounded element also does not exist
the presence of the unconditioned expanse in conditioned elements is without any basis
the unconditioned element is without any basis in the conditioned element

div.p: and so on. This means that just as nirvāṇa does not exist in saṃsāra, similarly a basis for a heroic being does not exist in awakening. K, N. D: “Just as a basis for nirvāṇa and saṃsāra does not exist, similarly…”

Then to teach that a meaning of the word In the earlier list padārtha was rendered gzhi’i don, “a basis in reality for.” awakening does not exist it says, khri brgyad
gzhi med; nyi khri
gnas med.

q.p: “To illustrate, Subhūti, in the absence of production… the absence of stopping, the absence of occasioning anything, the absence of appearing, the absence of being apprehended, the absence of defilement, and the absence of purification a basis in reality does not exist,”
q.orig: To illustrate further, Subhūti, in the absence of production a basis does not exist, and similarly, Subhūti, a basis in reality for a bodhisattva when a bodhisattva great being is practicing the perfection of wisdom does not exist. Subhūti, in the absence of stopping, the absence of occasioning anything, the absence of appearing, the absence of being apprehended, the absence of defilement and the absence of purification a basis does not exist
Subhūti, just as nonarising is without any basis, and just as nonceasing, nonaffliction, nonpurification, nonconditioning, nonorigination, and nonapprehensibility are without any basis
Subhūti, just as nonarising is without any basis…just as nonpurification is without any basis

div.p: and so on. This means that just as in the absence of production and so on a basis in reality does not exist, similarly a basis for a bodhisattva also does not exist in reality.

Then to teach that the meaning of the word for the true dharmic nature of a bodhisattva does not exist in a falsely imagined bodhisattva it says, khri brgyad (ka 112b2) has rnam par byang ba med pa’i gzhi in place of med pa la gzhi.

q.p: “To illustrate further, Subhūti, in form a basis in reality for the absence of production, the absence of stopping, the absence of occasioning anything, the absence of appearing, the absence of being apprehended, the absence of defilement, and the absence of purification does not exist,”
q.orig: To illustrate further, Subhūti, in form a basis in reality for the absence of production, the absence of stopping, the absence of occasioning anything, the absence of appearing, the absence of being apprehended, the absence of defilement and the absence of purification does not exist

Subhūti,” replied the Blessed One, “the nonarising of physical forms is without any basis. The nonceasing of physical forms, the nonaffliction of physical forms, the nonpurification of physical forms, the nonconditioning of physical forms, the nonorigination of physical forms, and the nonapprehensibility of physical forms are without any basis

“Subhūti,” replied the Blessed One, “the nonarising of physical forms is without any basis. The nonceasing of physical forms is without any basis. The nondefilement and the nonpurification of physical forms are without any basis. The nonconditioning of physical forms is without any basis. The nonorigination of physical forms is without any basis. The nonapprehensibility of physical forms is without any basis.

div.p: and so on. This means that just as the meanings of the words for uncompounded phenomena like nonproduction and so on do not exist in the meanings of the words for the five aggregates and so on, similarly the true dharmic nature of a bodhisattva does not exist in a falsely imagined bodhisattva constituted out of the five imaginary aggregates and so on.

Then to teach that the meaning of the word for the falsely imagined bodhisattva does not exist in an ultimate “Ultimate” renders don dam pa; in the list given earlier it’s don med pa (“unreal”). bodhisattva it says,

q.p: “To illustrate further, Subhūti, in the state of the absolute purity of form a basis for a causal sign does not exist,”
q.orig: To illustrate further, Subhūti, in the state of the absolute purity of form a basis for a causal sign does not exist
Subhūti, just as the signs that physical forms are utterly pure are without any basis

div.p:
and so on. This means: Just as the bases for the causal signs of compounded phenomena do not exist in the absolute purity of the dharma-constituent of the five aggregates, form and so on, [and of the constituents] and so on. And, nyi khri (ka 183b7–184a1) gnas in place of gzhi; khri brgyad (ka 113a3) omits mtshan ma’i; the other examples are up to khri brgyad
.

q.p: “To illustrate further, Subhūti, just as in the state of the absolute purity of the self and so on a basis for a causal sign does not exist,”
q.orig: To illustrate further, Subhūti, because of the nonexistence of self, in the state of the absolute purity of the self a basis does not exist[1]
Subhūti, just as the signs that the self is utterly pure are without any basis on account of the nonexistence of self
Subhūti, just as a mental image of the utter purity of the self is without any basis on account of the nonexistence of a self

div.p: and just as a basis for darkness does not exist in the sun, a basis for compounded phenomena does not exist in the eon conflagration, and in a tathāgata’s morality, meditative stabilization, wisdom, liberation, and knowledge and seeing of liberation, the bases for their opposing sides do not exist, similarly, “the falsely imagined bodhisattva” constituted out of the five aggregates does not exist in “the ultimate bodhisattva” constituted out of the dharma-constituent.

Then to teach that an ultimate bodhisattva constituted out of the dharma-constituent does not stand anywhere, with, nyi khri (ka 184b5) gnas for gzhi; khri brgyad (ka 113b2) incorrectly adds mun pa’i, “a basis for darkness.”

q.p: “To illustrate further, Subhūti, in the radiance of the sun and moon a basis does not exist,”
q.orig: To illustrate further, Subhūti, in the radiance of the sun and moon a basis for darkness does not exist
Subhūti, just as the light of the sun and moon is without any basis
just as the light of the sun and moon is without any basis

div.p: and so on, it teaches that a basis does not exist. Thus,

q.p:
“To illustrate further, the light of the sun, moon, planets, stars, jewels, and lightning”; khri brgyad
–.
q.orig: To illustrate further, Subhūti, a basis for the light of the planets, the stars, jewels, and lightning
just as the light of the planets, stars, gemstones, and lightning bolts
just as the light of the planets, stars, gemstones, and lightning bolts is without any basis

div.p: the light of the gods living in the desire realm, the light of the Brahmā and Śuddhāvāsa gods living in the form realm; and

q.p: “the light of a tathāgata”
q.orig: the light of the tathāgatas
the light of the tathāgatas, arhats, perfectly complete buddhas

div.p: do not stand anywhere because they are all just simply light means that similarly an ultimate bodhisattva without standing anywhere moves through states of existence.

Having thus given an elevenfold explanation that the meaning of the word bodhisattva is an absence of a basis, then it says that the reason a basis does not exist is khri brgyad
.

q.p: “because, Subhūti, all those phenomena—that which is awakening, that which is the bodhisattva, that which is the basis in reality of a bodhisattva—are not conjoined, are not disjoined,”
q.orig: Because, Subhūti, all those phenomena—that which is the awakening, that which is the bodhisattva, that which is the basis in reality of a bodhisattva—are not conjoined, are not disjoined
Subhūti, it is because what enlightenment is, what a bodhisattva and the actual entity denoted by the word bodhisattva is, and all such phenomena are neither conjoined nor disjoined
Subhūti, it is because all those phenomena—that enlightenment, that bodhisattva, and that actual entity denoted by the word bodhisattva—are neither conjoined nor disjoined,

div.p: and so on. These are in the sense of “that awakening” on account of “which” those awakening heroic beings making an effort at awakening are exerting themselves; or, alternatively, the “awakening” on account of “which” they get the name “awakening heroic beings”; or “that which is an awakening,” or “that which is the meaning of the name bodhisattva”; or those that are the form, feeling, perception, volitional factors, and consciousness and so on of a falsely imagined “bodhisattva”; or that which is the true dharmic nature of a bodhisattva, the dharma-constituent. “All those phenomena”—“the awakening” the uncompounded phenomena; “the bodhisattva” the compounded phenomena such as the aggregates, sense fields, constituents, dependent origination and so on; and “the basis in reality” that is the bodhisattva as the true nature of dharmas, the dharma-constituent—“are not conjoined” because in the true dharmic nature state they do not have the nature of defilement, and “are not disjoined” because they are also not marked by purification.
They

q.p: “cannot by analyzed” D dpyod pa med pa (Golden 158b1 spyod pa med pa is wrong) is based on the root rūp, “to investigate”; khri brgyad (ka 113b6), nyi khri (ka 185a3) “formless” (gzugs med pa).
q.orig: are formless
they are immaterial
immaterial

div.p: because without thought construction there is no analysis. This teaches that the mark of a grasper does not exist. They

q.p: “cannot be pointed out”
q.orig: impossible to indicate
impossible to indicate

div.p: because they are inexpressible and hence not suitable to be taught and understood by others through words. Both teach that the mark of a grasper does not exist and the mark of a grasped does not exist. They

q.p: “do not obstruct”
q.orig: unobstructed
unobstructed

div.p: because the mark of obstructing like the objects of the senses does not exist. Thus they

q.p: “have only one mark—that is, no mark,”
q.orig: their only defining characteristic is that they are without defining characteristics
have only one defining characteristic, which is to say, they are without defining characteristics

div.p: which means that which is separated from all marks is marked by no mark.

q.p: “Should train in nonattachment and in the nonexistence” nyi khri (185a4), le’u brgyad ma ga 181a5; khri brgyad (ka 113b7), ’bum (ga 60a7) omit chags pa; cf. Gilgit 310.10 asattāyām, Ghoṣa 1257 asaṅgatatāyām, PSP 1-2: 24 asaktatāyām asadbhūtatāyāṃ.—
q.orig: should train in the nonexistence…of all phenomena
should train in nonattachment to all phenomena and the fact that they are truly nonexistent
Subhūti, bodhisattva great beings should train in the fact that all phenomena are falsehoods

div.p: because of an attachment to awakening, or because of grasping at awakening as a real thing, they are called “awakening heroic beings.” So this means that in order to turn back those two conceptualizations they should train in all phenomena marked by nonattachment and marked as unreal things.

q.p:
“By not constructing any phenomena and not entertaining any ideas about them” khri brgyad
, likely a later “improvement” of an earlier reading like Ghoṣa 1263 akalpanāvikalpanātām upādāya. ’bum (ga 64b4) rtog pa myed cing / rnam par rtog pa myed pa; similarly, le’u brgyad ma ga 184a7. —
q.orig: they are without ideation and without conceptual thought
Since they are without ideation and without conceptual thought

div.p: if they construct them, with conceptualization as a cause, an awareness of existence arises, and if they entertain any ideas about them, with faith as a cause, attachment arises, so put it together as: by “not constructing” them they do not become existent, and by “not entertaining ideas” attachment does not arise.

q.p: “They should know all phenomena in a nondual way”
q.orig: they should comprehend all phenomena in accordance with nonduality
they should comprehend all phenomena in accordance with nonduality

div.p: means they are free from the sense of duality in subject and object, expression and thing to be expressed, production and cessation, existent thing and nonexistent thing, dharma and not dharma, compounded and uncompounded, ordinary and extraordinary, and so on.

div.head: 1b. What is the meaning of the term great being?
div.p:
Having thus taught the meaning of the word bodhisattva, to teach the meaning of the term great being it asks, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “Lord, you say ‘bodhisattva great beings.’ Why do you say ‘bodhisattva great beings’?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, why, in the term bodhisattva great beings, are bodhisattvas called great beings?
“Blessed Lord, why, when you say ‘bodhisattva great beings,’ do you call bodhisattvas ‘great beings’?”

div.p:
It means why do you say “great being” about a bodhisattva; why do you use the name “great being”? Of the fourfold intention of the Lord, and the elders Śāriputra, Subhūti, and Pūrṇa, first of all it teaches the Lord’s intention that they are called “great heroic beings” because among beings they are the great heroic beings. Just because of that it says khri brgyad
–.

q.p: “they will become the foremost of a great mass of beings, a great collection of groups of beings.”
q.orig: they are called…great category of beings whose receptivity is certain
bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom and lead the great number of beings with certainty to consummation. This is why bodhisattvas are called great beings.”

div.p:
The elder Śāriputra’s intention is that they are called “great heroic beings” because they realize the fact that all phenomena are nonexistent things, that they do not exist. Having seen that the names of all phenomena are nonexistent, they also demonstrate that Dharma to others to eliminate conceptualizations—views like khri brgyad
–.

q.p: “the view of a self”
q.orig: their view of self
view of the self

div.p: and so on; the extreme

q.p: “view of annihilation”
q.orig: their nihilist views
the nihilist view

div.p: and so on;

q.p: “the view of aggregates”
q.orig: their view of the aggregates
the view of aggregates

div.p: and so on; up to, at the end,

q.p: “the view of complete nirvāṇa.”
q.orig: their view concerning the attainment of final nirvāṇa
the view of the attainment of final nirvāṇa

div.p:
The elder Subhūti’s intention khri brgyad
–. is that these bodhisattvas called “great” If the text is emended to byang chub sems pa sems pa chen po zhes it would mean “this ‘bodhisattva great being’ is called a ‘great being.’ ” are called “great beings” because they have greater nonattachment and nonrepugnance. Just because of that he teaches that they are

q.p: “unattached even to that thought”
q.orig: unattached even to that unequaled thought
they are without attachment to such a mind
they are without attachment even to such a mind

div.p: and so on, and hence they stand without attachment to that.

The elder Pūrṇa’s intention is that they are “great beings” because they are armed with great armor, and have entered into a great practice and a great result. Just because of that it teaches that they khri brgyad
–.

q.p: “are armed with great armor… have set out in a great vehicle, and… have mounted on a great vehicle.”
q.orig: have donned the great armor. Blessed Lord, they are beings who have entered upon the Great Vehicle
who have donned the great armor. Blessed Lord, they are beings who have entered upon the Great Vehicle. Blessed Lord, they are beings who are mounted on…the Great Vehicle

div.head: The Lord’s intention
div.p: Among these, first is the Lord’s explanation.

q.p: “Great mass of beings”—
q.orig: great category of beings whose receptivity is certain
great number of beings

div.p:
it says “great mass of beings” based on the qualities of those from khri brgyad
.

q.p: “the Gotra level”
q.orig: level of the spiritual family
the level of the spiritual family

div.p: up to

q.p: “pratyekabuddhas.”

“Many groups of beings” “Many” (mang po) is a reading not attested either in khri brgyad ka 117a1 phal po che, or in nyi khri (ka 188b3) nges pa’i phul byed pa. Mvy 5075 gives phal po che as a translation of nicaya; Gilgit 313.8 niyatasya. —
q.orig: groups of beings
great category of beings whose receptivity is certain[2]
great number of beings

div.p: it says groups of bodhisattvas because they are foremost, because of their greater intention and greater practice. Their greater intention is their

q.p: “vajra-like”

div.p: production of the thought adorned with five qualities; it is (1) conquering, (2) precious, (3) faultless, (4) not split, and (5) accomplishes the aim.
Among these, conquering is conquering through the power of wisdom with eight qualities.
Because it conquers miserliness and so on, it is a thought to

q.p: “give away all my personal possessions.”
q.orig: I shall renounce all possessions
I should renounce all possessions

div.p: Because it conquers greed and hatred and so on, it is

q.p: “the same attitude of mind.”
q.orig: equanimity toward all beings
equanimity toward all beings

div.p: Because it conquers all wrong views, it is a thought to

q.p: “lead beings to nirvāṇa by means of the three vehicles.”
q.orig: lead all beings to nirvāṇa by means of the three vehicles
enable all beings to attain final nirvāṇa by means of the three vehicles
enable all beings to attain final nirvāṇa by means of the three vehicles

div.p: Because it does not perceive leading beings to nirvāṇa and has conquered all dharmas, it is the thought,

q.p: “I must understand that… all phenomena are not produced and do not stop.”
q.orig: I shall understand that since there are indeed no beings who will attain final nirvāṇa, all phenomena are nonarising and unceasing
all phenomena are nonarising and unceasing

div.p: Because it has conquered the deficient vehicle, it is

q.p: “the unmixed thought of the knowledge of all aspects.”
q.orig: a mind intent on unadulterated all-aspect omniscience
the unadulterated…mind of all-aspect omniscience

div.p: Because it has conquered all bad forms of life, it is

q.p: “the all-pervasive, thoroughly established realization of dharmas,”
q.orig: excellent pursuit of all realizations of the Dharma
train in the realization of the [ultimate] attribute that is followed everywhere by completion

div.p: which is to say, the realization of suchness in its all-pervasive sense on the first level.

Because it has conquered all thought constructions to do with the cycles of existence, it is the thought, Cf. nyi khri , khri brgyad
.

q.p: “I must awaken to finding and producing within myself all dharmas, from the aggregates, up to the perfections, in accord with one principle,”
q.orig: I must train in order to awaken to finding and producing within myself all dharmas in accord with one principle, up to in order to awaken to finding and producing within myself infinite dharmas
I shall comprehend how to accomplish the single principle of the Dharma. Starting from the aggregates
the accomplishment of the attributes in a single principle

div.p: which is to say it realizes all dharmas—the aggregates, constituents, sense fields, dependent origination, and perfections—in accord with the principle of emptiness.
And because it has conquered all thought constructions to do with purification, it is the awakening to the consummation of

q.p: “the dharmas on the side of awakening, the immeasurables,”
q.orig: the factors conducive to enlightenment, the meditative concentrations, the immeasurable attitudes

div.p: and so on, up to, at the end,

q.p: “the distinct attributes of a buddha,”
q.orig: the distinct qualities of the buddhas

div.p: which is to say it is an awakening to completing the meditation on those.

Having thus taught the eight good qualities of wisdom, to teach that the great power of compassion in that thought is precious, it says, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “I must, even for the sake of one being,”
q.orig: For the sake of each being
Even for the sake of each being, individually

div.p: and so on.

To teach that that precious thought is faultless, it says it is khri brgyad
.

q.p: “a prodigious thought,”
q.orig: the sublime mind
a[1]…mind[1]

div.p: without the faults of a

q.p: “greedy… hateful… confused… violent… [or] śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha thought.”
q.orig: will not have a greedy thought, will not have a hateful thought, will not have a confused thought, will not have a violent thought, and will not have a śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha thought
mindsets of desire, hatred, delusion, harm, śrāvakas, or indeed pratyekabuddhas

q.p: “That, Subhūti, is the bodhisattva great beings’ prodigious thought on account of which they become the foremost of all beings, but without falsely projecting anything.”
q.orig: This is the sublime mind of bodhisattva great beings. But even though they lead all beings to their consummation, they should not give rise to conceits on the basis of that sublime mind
this[2]…that[2]

div.p:
About that vajra-like thought not being split, it says khri brgyad
.

q.p: “that their attention connected with the knowledge of all aspects does not falsely project anything”
q.orig: directs its attention toward all-aspect omniscience, but it makes no assumptions on that basis
attention turned toward all-aspect omniscience without giving rise to conceit

div.p: because the opposing side, the Māras and so on, cannot split it.
In regard to its accomplishing the aim and being like a precious jewel, it says they

q.p: “should think to be of benefit and bring happiness.”
q.orig: should develop a mind intent on the [provisional] benefit and [ultimate] happiness
should set their mind on the benefit and happiness of all beings

div.p:
Having thus taught that the bodhisattvas have a greater intention, to teach that they have a greater practice in a threefold explanation it says they should stand in khri brgyad
–.

q.p: “a delight in Dharma… should stand in emptiness… and should abide in meditative stabilization.”
q.orig: delight in Dharma
should rejoice in the Dharma
enjoy…Dharma[2]

div.p: Take

q.p:
“the unbroken unity of all dharmas” khri brgyad
“unbroken unity” is the LSPW rendering of asaṃbheda (dbyer med pa).
q.orig: the indivisibility of all phenomena
the[4]…dharmas

div.p: as the dharma body, because all those bright dharmas are without difference.

div.head: Śāriputra’s intention
div.p: Now it teaches the elder Śāriputra’s intention.

q.p:
“Eliminate the view of a self,” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: abandon their view of self
abandon the view of the self

div.p: and so on, teaches the selflessness of persons.

q.p: “Eliminate the view of aggregates,”
q.orig: the view of aggregates
their view of the aggregates
abandon the view of aggregates

div.p: and so on, teaches the selflessness of dharmas.

q.p:
“Apprehend form, and by way of apprehending it produce a view about it” Golden 161a4, khri brgyad
, nyi khri . —
q.orig: apprehend form, and by way of apprehending it produce a view about it
apprehend physical forms and develop a view of them by way of apprehending
have a view[1]…concerning physical forms

div.p: apprehending the form aggregate and so on is the cause that produces conceptualization.

div.head: Subhūti’s intention
div.p:
The elder Subhūti’s confidence and readiness to explain is demonstrated with, nyi khri ; cf. Ghoṣa 1292 acittatvāt tatrāpi citte ’sakta iti; referenced at khri brgyad
.

q.p: “That thought is no thought and because it is no thought it is unattached even to that.”
q.orig: unattached even to that thought because it is no thought
no attachment to that mind because the mind is nonexistent

div.p: The ultimate, true dharmic nature of thought is “no thought” because it is separated from all the marks of falsely imagined thought. Therefore, “the thought” of awakening “is unattached to that,” the falsely imagined thought.

q.p: “Venerable Subhūti, what is the thought that is equal to the unequaled, a thought not shared in common with any śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas?”
q.orig: Venerable Subhūti, what is the thought of bodhisattva great beings that is equal to the unequaled, a thought not shared in common with any śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas
Venerable Subhūti, what is the mind of bodhisattva great beings that is equal to the unequaled, and that is not shared in common with the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas
“Venerable Subhūti, what is the mind of bodhisattva great beings that is equal to the unequaled, and that is not shared in common with the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas?”

div.p: He is asking about the mark of the thought of awakening.

q.p:
“Venerable Śāriputra, here after the production of the first thought of awakening,” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: Venerable Śāriputra,” replied Subhūti, “here after the production of the first thought of awakening
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, bodhisattva great beings…starting from the time when they first begin to set their mind on enlightenment
starting from the time when they first set their mind on enlightenment

div.p: and so on, teaches the mark of the ultimate thought. The nonconceptual mind from the Pramuditā level on up is called “the thought of awakening.”

q.p: “They do not see either the production or stopping of any dharma at all”—
q.orig: do not observe anything at all that is arising, and they do not observe anything at all that is ceasing
do not observe any phenomenon at all that is arising, and they do not observe any phenomenon at all that is ceasing

div.p: because it realizes suchness in its omnipresent sense and so on, the fundamentally transformed mind is space-like and sees all phenomena as space-like. Regarding this comparison to space, even though production and cessation appear in compounded phenomena, in walls and so on, that stand together with it, space has no production and cessation. It does not increase or decrease even when it is covered by or not separated from clouds and so on. Even though the rocks and trees that are together with it come and go, space itself does not come and go; even though fog, haze, smoke and so on are there and then not there, it does not become defiled and does not become purified either. It is the same with all phenomena. They are ultimately thoroughly established, with

q.p: “no production, no stopping, no decrease, no increase, no coming, no going, no defilement, and no purification.”
q.orig: there is nothing that arises or ceases, nothing that increases or decreases, nothing that comes or goes, nothing that is defiled or purified
do not observe any phenomenon at all that is arising, and they do not observe any phenomenon at all that is ceasing, increasing or decreasing, coming or going, defiled or purified.

div.p:
But during the falsely imagined period those phenomena that are like illusions appear as if they have production and so on. The mind that realizes that is called khri brgyad
.

q.p: “the thought equal to the unequaled, a thought not shared in common.”
q.orig: thought of bodhisattva great beings that is equal to the unequaled, a thought not shared in common
equal to the unequaled, and not shared in common
equal to the unequaled, and not shared in common

div.p: With

q.p: “Venerable Subhūti, you said,” “Venerable Subhūti, you said, ‘Even to that thought of all-knowing that is without outflows and does not belong they are unattached.’ ”
q.orig: Venerable Subhūti, with regard to your comments
Venerable Subhūti, you said,

div.p: and so on, the elder Śāriputra teaches that it is not only to just that that they are unattached, but the mark of nonattachment pervades all phenomena as well. It explains this with,

q.p: “Venerable Subhūti, would not form, then, also be unattached?”
q.orig: Venerable Subhūti, would not form, then, also be unattached?
Venerable Subhūti, it follows that they would also on that basis be without attachment to physical forms
Venerable Subhūti, that physical forms would therefore be without attachment

div.p: and so on.

q.p: “That thought… is without outflows and does not belong” nyi khri ; khri brgyad (ka 120b5) renders paryāpanna (“belong to”) khongs su gtogs pa.—
q.orig: this mind set on all-aspect omniscience is indeed free from contaminants…and excluded
They are not attached even to that mind‍—that mind set on omniscience, free from contaminants

div.p: this also teaches that all dharmas are pervaded by the mark of nonattachment.

q.p: “No-form also is unattached to form.” nyi khri .
q.orig: No-…form[2]
nonexistent physical forms would also be without attachment to physical forms
Nonexistent physical forms are without attachment to physical forms

div.p: Construe this as: Just as it said that the thoroughly established thought is “no-thought” because it is separated from the mark of falsely imagined thought, similarly the true dharmic nature of form is called “no-form” because it is separated from the mark of falsely imagined form. That intrinsic nature, the true nature of dharmas, that is “no-form” is “unattached” to falsely imagined form, and the true nature of dharmas that is not the unreal feeling is also unattached to falsely imagined feeling.

div.head: 1c. How are they armed with great armor?
Pūrṇa’s intention
div.p:
The elder Pūrṇa’s explanation is that they khri brgyad
.

q.p: “are armed with great armor”
q.orig: have donned the great armor
they are beings who have donned the great armor

div.p: and so on, teaching that from the first thought on, their intention is vast. They

q.p: “have set out in a Great Vehicle”
q.orig: have entered upon the Great Vehicle
who have entered upon the Great Vehicle

div.p: teaches the stage from the devoted course of conduct level up to the seventh level where practice operates together with effort and together with thought construction. They

q.p: “have mounted on a Great Vehicle”
q.orig: They are beings who dwell in the Great Vehicle
they are beings who are mounted on…the Great Vehicle

div.p: teaches from the eighth level on up, where it is the ultimate practice.
There, being armed with armor is explained in two parts: the vast intention to work hard for the welfare of all beings, and the vast practice that fully completes all practices in a single practice.

Among them, the vast intention is taught from where it says they khri brgyad
.

q.p: “do not practice for awakening for a partial number of beings,”
q.orig: for the sake of a small or limited number of beings
for the sake of a small or limited number of beings

div.p: and ‘I have to establish all beings in those perfections,’ up to,

q.p: “Venerable Śāriputra, they are therefore said to be ‘armed with great armor.’ ” nyi khri (ka 195a3), ’bum (ga 93a1) have de tsam gyis na, “to that extent,” in place of de phyir, “therefore”; khri brgyad (ka 122b4) omits this final statement.
q.orig: Venerable Śāradvatīputra, it is to that extent that bodhisattva great beings are said to don the great armor
they are said to have ‘donned the great armor.’

div.p:
The explanation of the vast practice is from nyi khri , ’bum , Ghoṣa 1302; cf. khri brgyad
ff.

q.p: “furthermore, Venerable Śāriputra, bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom give a gift,”
q.orig: Furthermore, Venerable Śāriputra, bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of giving give gifts
Moreover, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom, all the acts of generosity
when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom and undertake acts of generosity

div.p: and so on, up to where each of the six perfections is connected with the others so that the buddhas standing in the ten directions also

q.p:
“cry out cries of delight and proclaim the name.” nyi khri , khri brgyad
.
q.orig: cry out with cries of delight and raise their voices in praise of bodhisattva great beings thus armed with great armor, announcing their titles, saying the names
purposefully declare and proclaim their names

q.p: “Not… for a partial number of beings”
q.orig: do not practice for awakening for a partial number of beings
for the sake of a small or limited number of beings
for the sake of a small or limited number of beings

div.p: means “an object has not been carved out,” Cf. le’u brgyad ma ga 190a5 yongs su bcad pas; khri brgyad (ka 122b2), nyi khri (ka 194b4) yongs su dpag pas. so the vast intention is explained in terms of these three: an object has not been carved out, a being has not been carved out, and a practice has not been carved out.

From the vast practice, the practice of the perfection of giving khri brgyad
.

q.p: “is the perfection of giving armor.”
q.orig: is the armor of the perfection of generosity
This is the armor of the perfection of generosity

div.p: The basic rang bzhin gyis (prākṛta) means when the perfection of giving is the focus in each of the six explanations. giving of material things is the perfection of giving. It is called “perfection of giving armor” because it has been

q.p: “made… into something shared in common by all beings”
q.orig: Making common cause with all beings
making common cause with all beings

div.p: and dedicated

q.p: “to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening”
q.orig: into unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening
to unsurpassed, complete enlightenment
to unsurpassed, perfect, complete enlightenment

div.p: and the welfare of all beings.

Similarly, the giving of material things is the perfection of giving, and when it is practiced Cf. khri brgyad
.

q.p: “with attention not connected with śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas… it is perfection of morality armor”
q.orig: with attention connected with the knowledge of all aspects do not dedicate it to the level of śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas. That, Venerable Śāriputra, is the perfection of morality armor
do not dedicate it with the aim of the levels of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas. This is the armor of the perfection of ethical discipline
This is the armor of the perfection of ethical discipline

div.p: because, having produced the thought of perfect, complete awakening and taken the vow, giving it up is contrary to morality.
Similarly, the giving of material things is the perfection of giving. Working hard at that, the

q.p: “forbearance for”
q.orig: exhibit…endurance
bear

div.p: definitive meditation on

q.p: “phenomena,”

div.p: the reality of patience when paying attention to a gift, a giver, and a recipient that cannot be apprehended is

q.p: “the perfection of patience armor.”
q.orig: the armor of the perfection of tolerance
This is the armor of the perfection of tolerance

div.p: Similarly, when giving gifts, the intensification of perseverance at giving dedicated to the welfare of all beings is

q.p: “the perfection of perseverance armor.”
q.orig: the armor of the perfection of perseverance
This is the armor of the perfection of perseverance

div.p: Similarly, when giving gifts, be it during the period of giving or during the period of dedication, a mind one-pointedly focused on attention to the knowledge of all aspects is

q.p: “the perfection of concentration armor.”
q.orig: the armor of the perfection of meditative concentration
This is the armor of the perfection of meditative concentration

q.p:
“Have only that as their focus” Cf. khri brgyad
.
q.orig: focusing of their attention
th their attention thus directed toward

div.p: means it has only the knowledge of all aspects as its focus.

Similarly, when giving gifts, paying attention to not stopping attention to things being like illusions and so on, and attention to the absence of thought constructions—paying attention to not forsaking the conventional dedication to awakening and not forsaking the ultimate practice that cannot be apprehended—is

q.p: “perfection of wisdom armor.”
q.orig: the armor of the perfection of wisdom
This is the armor of the perfection of wisdom

div.p: Similarly, when giving gifts, still wanting to fulfill the six perfections through attention to the practice of not apprehending anything, also not apprehending the causal signs of giving, morality, patience, perseverance, concentration and wisdom; having set out to make that into something shared in common, not apprehending the causal sign even of that; and dedicating it to perfect, complete awakening but not apprehending the causal sign even of awakening—this attention to not apprehending the causal signs of all dharmas is

q.p:
“the six perfections armor,” Cf. khri brgyad
, nyi khri ; ’bum , Ghoṣa 1310 ayam… ṣaṭpāramitā­mahā­sannāhaḥ.
q.orig: the great armor of the six perfections
that manner retain all six perfections, therefore they are said to have ‘donned the great armor.’

div.p: because it has been aided by the six ultimate perfections. In order to teach just those six ultimate perfections each has been taught separately.

Furthermore, when bodhisattvas guard morality, and, because it will be in accord with that morality, give gifts, and with an intention in accord with that morality make it into something shared in common and dedicate it to awakening, that practice of the perfection of morality is called Cf. nyi khri .

q.p: “giving armor.”
q.orig: the armor of the perfection of generosity

div.p:
Similarly, connect “doing the giving and so on with an intention in accord with patience, and because it will be in accord with perseverance, and because it will be in accord with concentration” with them all. Connect “being in accord with eliminating such opposing-side afflictions as miserliness, immorality, animosity” and so on with all the perfections as well. This is an brief summary of khri brgyad
–.

div.head: 2. How have they set out in the Great Vehicle? Cf. .
div.p:
To pose the second question, it says, khri brgyad
. Śāriputra asks the question.

q.p: “Venerable Pūrṇa, to what extent have bodhisattva great beings set out in a great vehicle, and what is the bodhisattva great beings’ Great Vehicle?”
q.orig: Venerable Pūrṇa, by means of what is it said that bodhisattva great beings have entered upon the Great Vehicle
“Venerable…Pūrṇa, to what extent is it said that bodhisattva great beings ‘have entered upon the Great Vehicle,’ and what is the Great Vehicle of the bodhisattva great beings?”

div.p:
Having said that, elder Pūrṇa, having taught a tenfold great vehicle and setting out in a great vehicle tenfold, then says khri brgyad
.

q.p: “in that way… [they] have set out in the Great Vehicle.”
q.orig: and in that way bodhisattva great beings have set out in the Great Vehicle
the Great Vehicle[2]
“It is in this way, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that bodhisattva great beings are said to ‘have entered upon the Great Vehicle.’

div.p:
There, This is the first of the ten. having first taught that when they meditate on the four form concentrations, the four immeasurables, the four formless absorptions, and those twelve dharmas The twelve are the three sets of concentrations, immeasurables, and absorptions. and the six perfections it is a great vehicle, and when they khri brgyad
. Below ( ) our author says, “Names, designations, conventional terms and so on are ‘reasons’ [or ‘tokens’]; defining marks and behaviors are ‘signs.’ ” Both of these explain “attributes” (ākāra, rnam pa), the aspects of a particular thing that make up its identity. They pay attention to the attributes and so on of space because, like space, all the different meditative states are ultimately the same, without any intrinsic nature.

q.p: “pay attention to the attributes, tokens, and signs”
q.orig: conjoined with the aspects, modes, and signs
aspects, tokens, and signs of space

div.p:
of those, make them into something shared in common, and grow them into awakening that they have set out in the Great Vehicle, it sums up in conclusion with, khri brgyad
, nyi khri .

q.p: “That, Venerable Śāriputra, is the bodhisattva great beings’ Great Vehicle, and in that way bodhisattva great beings have set out in the Great Vehicle.”
q.orig: It is in this way, Venerable Śāradvatīputra…that bodhisattva great beings are said to have entered upon the Great Vehicle
“It is in this way, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, that bodhisattva great beings are said to ‘have entered upon the Great Vehicle.’

div.p:
Then, the second also teaches them, The difference between the first and the second is that in the first the twelve—the concentrations and so on—are the focus, and in the second the six perfections are. In both cases the giving, morality, and so on are in the form of an altruistically motivated meditation practice that accomplishes the different meditative states. in order to teach that when those same six perfections and those twelve have been made complete it is the Great Vehicle, and that those working hard at those as explained in the Sūtra are those who have set out. Thus it says, khri brgyad
; cf. nyi khri (ka 203a4) that omits drug gi.

q.p: “That, Venerable Śāriputra, is the bodhisattva great beings’ Great Vehicle that is the six perfections, and in that way bodhisattva great beings have set out in the Great Vehicle.”
q.orig: This is the perfection of wisdom possessed by bodhisattva great beings. It is in these ways that bodhisattva great beings have entered the Great Vehicle

div.p: Take the “giving” here as the gift of the dharmas, so, again, when meditated on in all their aspects, the dharmas from the applications of mindfulness, up to, at the end,

q.p: “the distinct attributes of a buddha”
q.orig: eighteen distinct attributes of a buddha
the eighteen distinct qualities of the buddhas
the distinct qualities of the buddhas

div.p:
are the Great Vehicle. And again, the third is that those working hard at meditating on them in all their aspects have set out in the Great Vehicle, thus it again says, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “That, Venerable Śāriputra, is the bodhisattva great beings’ Great Vehicle, and in that way bodhisattva great beings have set out in the Great Vehicle.”
q.orig: This, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, is the Great Vehicle of bodhisattva great beings

div.p:
Then the fourth is where it says khri brgyad
–. the two—meditation on the immeasurables and the six perfections—is the Great Vehicle and those working hard at those as explained in the Sūtra are those who have set out.

Then the fifth is where it says khri brgyad
, nyi khri
shes, (“knowledge of”) the emptinesses. the sixteen emptinesses are the Great Vehicle and those who pay attention to them without apprehending them are those who have set out.

Then the sixth is where it says khri brgyad
. unscattered meditative equipoises are the Great Vehicle and those who know them are those who have set out. This means that when abiding in apprehending scattering and meditative stabilization together with causal signs, not signlessness, abiding without thought construction is always meditative equipoise.

Then the seventh is where it says khri brgyad
. “Not without knowledge” explains “by way of not apprehending anything.” the nondual true nature of dharmas is the Great Vehicle and those who neither know nor not know that are those who have set out.

Then the eighth is where it says khri brgyad
. the sameness of the three time periods is the Great Vehicle, and those not without knowledge of them and with nonapprehending knowledge are those who have set out.

Then the ninth is where it says khri brgyad
. the sameness of the three realms is the Great Vehicle, and those not without knowledge of them and with nonapprehending knowledge are those who have set out.

And then the tenth is where it says all dharmas are the Great Vehicle and those who do not apprehend a knower of them are those who have set out. Having completed those, it sums up in conclusion with, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “That, Venerable Śāriputra, is the bodhisattva great beings’ Great Vehicle, and in that way bodhisattva great beings have set out in the Great Vehicle.”
q.orig: That is the bodhisattva great beings’ Great Vehicle, and in that way bodhisattva great beings have set out in the Great Vehicle
This, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, is the Great Vehicle of bodhisattva great beings
is the Great Vehicle of bodhisattva great beings.

div.head: 3. How do they stand in the Great Vehicle?
div.p: Now to pose the third question it says,

q.p: “Venerable Pūrṇa, to what extent does a bodhisattva great being stand in “Stand in” renders gnas. ’bum (ga 112b1), nyi khri (ka 205a3) gnas; khri brgyad (ka 130a2), ’bum (ga 112b3), nyi khri (ka 205a5) yang dag par gnas; PSP 1-2: 44, Ghoṣa 1329 samārūḍha; le’u brgyad ma ga 200a1 zhugs, ga 200a2 ’dzeg pa; Abhi­samayālaṃkāra 1.45d (Amano, p. 25) adhirohinī; mngon rtog rgyan, Degé Tengyur (shes phyin, ka), 4a6 ’dzegs. the Great Vehicle?”
q.orig: Venerable Pūrṇa, to what extent has a bodhisattva great being mounted…on the Great Vehicle
Venerable Pūrṇa, to what extent is it said of bodhisattva great beings that they dwell in the Great Vehicle
“Venerable Pūrṇa, to what extent is it said that bodhisattva great beings…‘are mounted upon the Great Vehicle’?”

div.p: The elder Pūrṇa then gives an exposition of six nonconceptual practices from the eighth level on up.

q.p: “Venerable Śāriputra, here when bodhisattva great beings are practicing the perfection of wisdom they mount up on yang dag par gnas; PSP 1-2: 44 ārohati, Gilgit 321.1 samārohati, “mount up on.” the perfection of giving,”
q.orig: Venerable Śāriputra, here bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom mount up on…the perfection of giving
“Venerable Śāradvatīputra,” replied Pūrṇa, “when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom, they also…dwell in the perfection of generosity
Venerable Śāradvatīputra,” replied Pūrṇa, “here, when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom, they are also mounted on the perfection of generosity,

div.p: and so on, teaches the first stage of nonconceptual perfection without thought construction. Nonconceptual meditation on emptiness is the second, nonconceptual meditation on all bright dharmas the third, all dharmas that cannot be apprehended the fourth, the stage of control the fifth, and complete awakening the sixth.
There, the first is they khri brgyad (ka 130a3) yang dag par gnas: “bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom mount up on.”

q.p: “stand in the perfection of giving.”
q.orig: mount up on…the perfection of giving
dwell in the perfection of generosity
mounted on the perfection of generosity,

div.p: This means they stand up on a place—a maturation without conceptualization—that is a perfection beyond the level of conceptual practice. At the eighth level they have arrived at effortless perfections that are maturation results that have come about from having earlier completed, with conceptualization and with effort, the accumulation of merits. They “They” means the nonconceptual perfections at the eighth bodhisattva level. have come about in the form of a result so they are nonconceptual. Bodhisattvas accomplish the welfare of beings through those, through the power of skillful means, and through the power of prayer that is a vow.

Second, it says they khri brgyad
. Alternatively, “because of a disintegration of meditation” or “in order to cause a disintegration.” Ghoṣa 1331, PSP 1-2: 44 bhāvanāvibhāvanārthena; le’u brgyad ma ga 200b1 bsgom pa rnam par gzhig pa’i don du; ’bum (ga 113b1), nyi khri (ka 205b1) bsgom pa rnam par bsgom pa’i don du, “in order to develop a meditation”; LSPW p. 184 “a development in the sense of annihilation.” It is noteworthy that the translators of khri brgyad consistently render vibhāvanā by bsgom par rnam par ’jig pa, “a disintegration of meditation,” and at khri brgyad (kha 206b) by bshig pa, the past tense of ’jig pa; cf. Bṭ3 explaining khri brgyad
ff. In general, bhāvanā is “meditation”; vibhava / vibhāva is a bahuvrihi (vigato bhāvo yasya), “devoid of existence”; vibhāvanā (rnam par ’jig pa), “disintegration of meditation”; and bhāva “existent thing,” all from root bhū, cognate with the English “be.”

q.p: “meditate on… emptiness… because of the investigation of the meditation.”
q.orig: cultivate the emptiness of internal phenomena in order to break down this cultivation
meditate on[1]…‘mounted on the Great Vehicle.’

div.p: Take “disintegration of the meditation” here as making it empty. What it means is by meditating on disintegration they meditate without apprehending anything. They “meditate” on this, on just this turning it into a nonexistent thing.

The rest are easy to understand. khri brgyad
–.

The elder Pūrṇa having thus demonstrated his confidence and readiness to speak, the elder Subhūti, wanting to understand the Lord’s intention, inquires, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “Lord, to what extent are bodhisattva great beings armed with great armor?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord! When it is said that they should don the great armor…what, Blessed Lord, is the extent of the great armor that bodhisattva great beings should don
What, Blessed Lord, is the extent of the great armor that bodhisattva great beings have donned?”

div.p:
Having been asked that, the Lord teaches the ninefold great armor. After that, then the elder Subhūti demonstrates his two Golden 167a2, cf. khri brgyad
and
; D gnyis pa, “second.” Even though it is clear that the section of the text our author is explaining is khri brgyad
–, it is not clear whether the eleven sections are the nine and the two sections introduced by Subhūti’s two statements with “The way I understand,” or whether the section beginning
should be understood as itself divided into eleven sections. confidences and readinesses to speak, and there is an explanation in eleven sections of the text.

From among those armed with all the armor, the section of the text on extinguishing bad forms of life with maturation-based magical power, together with the section on them being conjured up, is the first; khri brgyad
–. the six sections on the six perfections are the six that are like things that have been conjured up; khri brgyad
–. conjuring up establishing beings in the ten directions in the six perfections is the eighth; khri brgyad
–. and the vast intention is the ninth. khri brgyad
–.

Then the elder Subhūti, to demonstrate that he has generated a confidence and readiness to speak about that on account of an illusion-like cause, says, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “The way I understand what you, Lord, have said…”
q.orig: As I understand the teachings given by the Blessed Lord
As I understand the meaning of what the Blessed Lord has said

div.p: As for,

q.p: “Oh! Those bodhisattva great beings should be understood to be armed with no armor,”
q.orig: those bodhisattva great beings should be understood to be armed with no armor
bodhisattva great beings should know that they are donning armor that is a nonexistent armor
bodhisattva great beings should know that they have donned armor that is a nonexistent armor

div.p: this means that because all the armor that has been explained before is falsely imagined, bodhisattva great beings are armed with an armor that has the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature, suchness, for its intrinsic nature. Therefore, he says

q.p: “because all dharmas, given the illusory nature of dharmas, are empty of their own mark.”
q.orig: on account of the emptiness of intrinsic defining characteristics
on account of the emptiness of its intrinsic defining characteristics

div.p: To establish that they are illusory phenomena, it says

q.p: “form is empty of form”
q.orig: form[1] is empty of form[2]
physical forms are empty of physical forms
physical forms are empty of physical forms

div.p:
and so on. This connects thoroughly established form being empty of falsely imagined form, and thoroughly established feeling being empty of falsely imagined feeling, with “therefore ultimate armor is empty of falsely imagined armor.” Therefore at the end it says khri brgyad
.

q.p: “great armor is empty of great armor. I understand that bodhisattva great beings are armed with no armor, Lord, through this one of many explanations.”
q.orig: The great armor is also empty of the great armor. It is for that reason, Blessed Lord, that bodhisattva great beings should know that they are donning armor that is a nonexistent armor
The great armor is also empty of the great armor. It is for that reason, Blessed Lord, that bodhisattva great beings should know that they have donned armor that is a nonexistent armor.”

div.p:
What is the intention where it says, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “Subhūti, the knowledge of all aspects is not made, is not unmade, and does not occasion anything”?
q.orig: Subhūti, the knowledge of all aspects is not made, is not unmade, and does not occasion anything
all-aspect omniscience has neither been created, nor been developed, nor been composed
because all-aspect omniscience has neither been created, nor been developed, nor been composed.

div.p: In this world protective equipment refers to three things: Thinking, “What needs to be done?” you wear protective clothing. To illustrate, you think, “I will build a town” or “I will build a temple.” Thinking, “What should I destroy?” you put on armor. For example, you think, “I will destroy the town” or “I will destroy the temple.” Thinking, “To what should I give an occasion?” you put on protective equipment. To illustrate, you think, “I will enjoy the town” or “I will clean the town.” It is similar with the knowledge of all aspects as well. Someone may have become armed with great armor for the purpose of the knowledge of all aspects that is made, or destroyed, or given an occasion like that. But the knowledge of all aspects is not made, is not unmade, and does not occasion anything, so it is not correct to become armed with great armor for that purpose. The intention, therefore, is that they are correct to think they are

q.p: “armed with no armor.”
q.orig: donning armor that is a nonexistent armor
donned armor that is a nonexistent armor.”

div.p:
Just because of that it says, khri brgyad
and
; khri brgyad ka 139b3 gtan med in place of shin tu med.

q.p: “Subhūti, given that you cannot apprehend a maker, the knowledge of all aspects is not made, not unmade, and does not occasion anything … Because they absolutely do not exist and absolutely cannot be apprehended.”
q.orig: “Subhūti,” said the Lord, “given that you cannot apprehend a maker, the knowledge of all aspects is not made, not unmade, and does not occasion anything, and those beings for whose sake bodhisattva great beings are armed with great armor are also not made, not unmade, and do not occasion anything.
Subhūti,” replied the Blessed One, “it is because there is no creator to be apprehended that all-aspect omniscience has itself neither been created, nor been developed, nor been composed
“Subhūti,” said the Blessed One, “you should know it is because there is no agent to be apprehended that all-aspect omniscience has neither been created, nor been developed, nor been composed.

div.p:
Also, it says that about khri brgyad
.

q.p: “suchness,”
q.orig: the real nature
real nature

div.p: because when it is grasped in a falsely imagined form, as “the suchness of form, the suchness of feeling” and so on, in that form it does not exist.

Then the elder Subhūti, in order to teach what he is thinking, says, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “Lord, the way I understand what you have said, Lord,”
q.orig: “Lord,” said Subhūti, “the way I understand what you have said, Lord,
Blessed Lord, as I understand the words spoken by the Blessed One
Blessed Lord, as I understand the meaning of what the Blessed Lord has said

div.p: and so on.
What is intended where it says

q.p: “form is not bound and is not freed”?
q.orig: form is not bound and is not freed
physical forms, Blessed Lord, are neither fettered nor liberated
physical forms, Blessed Lord, are neither fettered nor liberated

div.p: Some think that because the five aggregates without outflows are bound with fetters, and so on, they are bound by afflictions and karma, going in cycles from one form of life to another again and again, and later the ones without outflows are freed, at which point they are destroyed. But because of what was intended by “not made” and “not unmade” it says they are

q.p: “not bound and are not freed”
q.orig: neither fettered nor liberated[2]
are neither fettered nor liberated

div.p:
and so on. This means both being bound and being freed happen when something exists. Thus, form and so on are totally nonexistent things so how could being bound and being freed happen to them, given that they do not exist? They are not established. Being bound and being freed are taught based on the falsely imagined, but not ultimately. Therefore, it says, khri brgyad
(ka 140b7) gzugs nyid med pa’i phyir; nyi khri (ka 217b1), le’u brgyad ma ga 214a2 gzugs med pa’i phyir. It is perhaps odd to write gzugs med nyid kyi phyir in Tib. The asattva here, like the sattva in sarve sattvāḥ and bodhisattva, means more than just a state of nonexistence; LSPW “nonbeingness.”

q.p: “Venerable Pūrṇa, because form does not exist, form is not bound and is not freed,”
q.orig: Because form does not exist,…form is not bound and is not freed
Venerable Pūrṇa, physical forms that resemble dreams are neither fettered nor liberated
Venerable Pūrṇa, physical forms are neither fettered nor liberated because physical forms are nonexistent.

div.p:
and so on. With they are khri brgyad
.

q.p: “dream-like”
q.orig: resemble dreams
like a dream[1]

div.p: and so on, it teaches that thoroughly established form is also not bound and is not freed.

q.p: “Because [they are] isolated, calm, empty”
q.orig: is isolated, calm, empty
like a dream[1]

div.p: means they abide, like space, so it is not logical that they are bound and freed.
The rest is easy to understand.

div.head: 6. How is it a great vehicle? This is the sixth of the twenty-eight or twenty-nine questions listed earlier ( ). The numbering here jumps to six, leaving out four and five, because the first three questions go together as 1a, 1b, and 1c, followed by 2 and then 3.
div.p:
Having made the great armor stable and complete, the elder Subhūti, taking as his point of departure the statement “have set out in a great vehicle,” This is in Pūrṇa’s explanation of a great being, khri brgyad
ff. has posed five questions: Subhūti’s five questions at khri brgyad
, are: “Lord, what is the Great Vehicle of bodhisattva great beings? Lord, to just what extent should bodhisattva great beings be known to have set out in the Great Vehicle? Where will the Great Vehicle have set out? Where will the Great Vehicle stand? Who will go forth in the Great Vehicle?” Below (Bṭ3 –) our author will say that the responses to them first explain the Great Vehicle in the context of setting out, and then, arising out of the response to the last question (khri brgyad
, “Who will go forth in the Great Vehicle?”) there is an explanation of the Great Vehicle in the context of the result, beginning with the statement (khri brgyad
), “Lord, you say this—‘Great Vehicle’—again and again. It surpasses the world with its gods, humans, and asuras and goes forth; that is why it is called a Great Vehicle.”

q.p: “Lord, what is the Great Vehicle of bodhisattva great beings?”
q.orig: “Blessed Lord, what is the Great Vehicle of bodhisattva great beings

div.p: and so on.
There the Lord explains “Great Vehicle” under twenty-one subdivisions. These are:

item.p: Great Vehicle of the perfections,
Great Vehicle of all the emptinesses,
Great Vehicle of all the meditative stabilizations,
Great Vehicle of the applications of mindfulness,
Great Vehicle of the right efforts, “Effort” (pradhāna) should also be understood as incorporating the Tib spong ba (prahāṇa), “abandonment.”
Great Vehicle of the legs of miraculous power,
Great Vehicle of the faculties,
Great Vehicle of the powers,
Great Vehicle of the limbs of awakening,
Great Vehicle of the path,
Great Vehicle of the liberations,
Great Vehicle of the knowledges,
Great Vehicle of the three faculties,
Great Vehicle of the three meditative stabilizations,
Great Vehicle of the mindfulnesses,

Great Vehicle of the five absorptions, In the list in the khri brgyad, insofar as the next in the list of the twenty-one Great Vehicles is “the Great Vehicle of the ten powers,” the five absorptions are a general term including (1) the four immeasurables, (2) the four concentrations, (3) the four formless absorptions, (4) the eight deliverances, and (5) the nine successive absorption stations.
Great Vehicle of the ten powers,
Great Vehicle of the four fearlessnesses,
Great Vehicle of the four detailed and thorough knowledges,
Great Vehicle of the eighteen distinct attributes of a buddha, and
Great Vehicle of the dhāraṇī gateways.

div.head: 2. Great Vehicle of all the emptinesses Our author begins with an explanation of the second Great Vehicle because he has already explained the six perfections in response to the earlier question.
div.p:
Among these, in the second section of the text, Great Vehicle of all the emptinesses, it says The section begins from khri brgyad
and goes up to . The extract is from .

q.p: “eyes are empty of eyes because they are neither unmoved nor destroyed.”
q.orig: eyes are empty of the eyes because they do not endure and they do not disintegrate
the eyes are empty of the eyes because they do not endure and they do not disintegrate

div.p: Falsely imagined eyes are empty of falsely imagined eyes. “Empty” has the sense of nonexistent so it means a real basis of eyes does not exist in the eyes. D dngos po, vastu (“real basis”); K, N mig gis dngos por med do, “they do not exist in actual fact (vastutaḥ) as eyes.” Alternatively, taking dngos po as rendering bhāva (“existent thing,” “real thing”) and dngos po med pa as rendering abhāva (“nonexistent thing,” “unreal thing”): “it means the nonexistence in eyes of eyes as a real thing.”

This means were they to be existent you can suppose they would remain there permanently unmoved, or they would be impermanent and destroyed. Thus they do not remain there unmoved and they are not destroyed, so they do not exist because “they are neither unmoved nor destroyed.”

q.p: “Because that is their basic nature”—
q.orig: because that is their very nature
because that is their nature

div.p: the absence of a real basis of eyes in the eyes is their basic nature, which is to say, their intrinsic nature. Alternatively, “that nonexistence in eyes of eyes as a real thing (dngos po med pa nyid, abhāvatā) is their basic nature (prakṛti), their intrinsic nature (svabhāva).”
The nonexistence of inner and outer dharmas, each separately, are two emptinesses.
The emptiness of inner dharmas that grasp outer dharmas, and of outer dharmas that have become objects of inner dharmas, that is, of subjects and objects is the

q.p: “emptiness of inner and outer,”
q.orig: inner and outer emptiness
external and internal phenomena[2]
emptiness of external and internal phenomena

div.p: the third emptiness.
That which has become

q.p: “the emptiness of that emptiness that is the emptiness of all dharmas is the emptiness of emptiness.”
q.orig: the emptiness[2]…all dharmas
the emptiness of emptiness, the emptiness that is the emptiness of all phenomena is empty of emptiness
the emptiness of that emptiness that is the emptiness of phenomena is an emptiness.

div.p: It is called an “emptiness of emptiness” because it is that—empty—and it is that—emptiness—as well. So, it is called an “emptiness of emptiness.” Of what is it empty? It is saying it is empty of the emptiness that is the emptiness of all dharmas. What is it teaching? It means there is no other second emptiness in emptiness; it is “empty” just from its nature.

q.p: “The eastern direction is empty of the eastern direction”;
q.orig: the eastern direction is empty of the eastern direction

div.p: it is called a

q.p: “great emptiness,”
q.orig: emptiness of great extent

div.p: in the sense that “it pervades all directions” because the emptiness of things that are huge is greater.

q.p:
“Nirvāṇa is also empty of nirvāṇa because it is neither unmoved nor destroyed.” khri brgyad
, explaining “the emptiness of ultimate reality.”
q.orig: nirvāṇa is empty of nirvāṇa because it does not endure and does not disintegrate
That nirvāṇa is also empty of nirvāṇa because it does not endure and does not disintegrate.

div.p: It is empty of the basic nature of ultimate nirvāṇa. K, N “ultimate nirvāṇa is empty of falsely imagined nirvāṇa.” But is nirvāṇa not taken to be “unmoved”? The system of some thinkers in the Śrāvaka Vehicle is like that, but in “ultimate reality” there is no dharma called “nirvāṇa.” K, N rtog pa dang bcas pa; D “The system (tshul, naya) of some in the Śrāvaka Vehicle who have realization (rtogs pa dang bcas pa) is not like that.” It does not make sense to understand rtog pa dang bcas pa as savitarka in the technical sense specific to the first concentration, as “The mode of some in the Śrāvaka Vehicle with applied thought is like that.”

q.p: “The compounded”
q.orig: conditioned
conditioned

div.p: is the three realms.
It says this because all compounded things are included in the three realms.

q.p: “What has no production, no stopping, no destruction, no lasting, and no changing into something else” This is explaining the emptiness of the uncompounded. —
q.orig: does not arise, that does not cease, and that does not change into something else
anything that does not arise, that does not cease, and that does not change into something else

div.p: the arising of dharmas is “production,” cutting the stream is “stopping,” moment by moment perishing is “destruction,” not cutting the stream of a continuum is “lasting,” and the earlier and later distinction in a continuum is “changing into something else.” The dharmas in which these are absent are the

q.p: “uncompounded,”
q.orig: unconditioned
unconditioned

div.p: which is to say space, suchness, and the two cessations. Those phenomena that are uncompounded do not exist as real bases, hence

q.p: “the emptiness of the uncompounded.”
q.orig: emptiness of unconditioned phenomena

div.p: Since it is enough just to teach “it is the extreme At khri brgyad (ka 144b7) “extreme” (mtha’, anta) is rendered “limit.” of annihilation and it is the extreme of permanence,” the extremes of an existent thing and a nonexistent thing, dharma and nondharma, existence and nonexistence, and so on are included in just that.
As for

q.p:
“that of which a beginning and an end are not found has no middle,” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: That which has neither beginning nor end is empty of that which has neither beginning nor end
that which has neither beginning nor end

div.p: and so on—in

q.p: “no beginning and end,”
q.orig: no beginning, end,
neither beginning nor end
neither beginning nor end

div.p: take “a beginning” as the past and take “an end” as the future; alternatively, take “a beginning” as former and “an end” as later. Because both extremes do not exist, a “middle” does not exist either. Hence the emptiness of no beginning, no end, and no middle is

q.p: “the emptiness of no beginning and no end.”
q.orig: emptiness of that which has neither beginning nor end

orig.distinct: the emptiness of that which has neither beginning nor end
