div.p: the world as inhabitants;

q.p:
“they eliminate the world” khri brgyad
. According to LC, sel bar byed pa renders nivartayati. le’u brgyad ma nga 5b7 gang dag ’jig rten sgrol ba yin, “they free the world.”—

div.p: the five sorts of sense objects;

q.p: “on account of them a world causes an escape” le’u brgyad ma nga 5b7 gang dag gis ’jig rten gyi rgal bar byed pa, “those which cause a crossing over the world.”—

div.p: the world as a superior person. As for

q.p: “those that are not the world” le’u brgyad ma nga 5b7–6a1 don du, “those that are not there for the purpose of the world” makes the dative clearer.—

div.p: these are thoroughly established phenomena. As for

q.p: “the world from which they will escape”—

div.p: they escape from the world of the cycle of existences. As for

q.p: “those who free from the world” le’u brgyad ma nga 6a1 gang dag’jig rten gyi sgrol byed yin pa, “those who are the emancipators of the world”—

div.p: this is from the container world; as for

q.p: “those who free in the world”—

div.p: this is in the worlds where there is Dharma.

q.p:
“Excellent, excellent, Venerable Śāriputra. I will object to Venerable Śāriputra in that Venerable Śāriputra has got at just what is meant by expressing the statement as an absolute.” Cf. khri brgyad
; nyi khri .
q.orig: “Excellent, excellent, Venerable Śāriputra,” said Subhūti. “I will object to venerable Śāriputra in that venerable Śāriputra has got at just what is meant by expressing the statement as an absolute.
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, well said! Well said!” replied Subhūti. “Venerable Śāradvatīputra, you have grasped the very point of the question and what you say is quite true

div.p: This is a statement, stated in three parts, rejoicing in what Śāriputra has said. It teaches that it is excellent, that there are logical objections to it, and that it has got at the meaning. Rongtön (rong ston shes bya kun khyab) in his sher phyin stong phrag brgya pa’i rnam ’grel, pp. 638–39, says this means that Subhūti is saying it is “excellent” because, as Śāriputra says, were bodhisattvas bodhisattvas just because they pay attention, then all beings would indeed be bodhisattvas. Subhūti says Śāriputra’s statement is open to logical objection because it could only be true when the words are taken too literally, so it forces the reader to think about what he is actually saying. To that extent what Śāriputra says has got at what he, Subhūti, means, namely that bodhisattvas have compassion for (“pay attention to”) all beings even while cultivating a state free from thought construction.

q.p: “You should know that the nonexistence of attention is because of the nonexistence of a being; you should know that the emptiness of attention is because of the emptiness of a being; you should know that the isolation of attention is because of the isolation of a being; you should know that the absence of an intrinsic nature in attention is because of the absence of an intrinsic nature in a being; and you should know that there is no full awakening of attention because there is no full awakening of a being.”
q.orig: One should know that attention is nonexistent because beings are nonexistent. One should know that attention is a nonentity because beings are nonentities. One should know that attention is without inherent existence because beings are without inherent existence. One should know that attention is emptiness because beings are emptiness. One should know that attention is void because beings are void. One should know that attention will not attain consummate buddhahood because beings will not attain consummate buddhahood

div.p: There are no other than those five D; Golden 243b1 lta “those sorts of attentions.” attentions so it is teaching that they too are not the bodhisattva. Therefore, it teaches:

q.p:
“I say bodhisattva great beings are not separated from staying in this state or from this attention.” Cf. khri brgyad
, nyi khri , Gilgit 415.11–12. The corresponding part of the Śata­sāhasrikā­prajñā­pāramitā (xiii F.144.a, cited and translated in LSPW folios 267-268, p. 201, n. 13) says explicitly this attention is a “compassionate” (mahā­karuṇā­manasīkāreṇa) state.
q.orig: bodhisattva great beings never part from focusing their attention with great compassion
“Venerable Śāradvatīputra, for this reason one should know that bodhisattva great beings are indeed inseparable from paying attention to great compassion.”

div.head: Explanation of Chapters 22 and 23
div.p:
Thus, first of all, along with a teaching of miraculous powers and along with a teaching of the results, the intermediate explanation of the perfection of wisdom has been completed. As explained,
. the Tathāgata in this perfection of wisdom K, N de bzhin gshegs pas. The reading in D, de bzhin gshegs pa, may intend, “In this tathāgata the perfection of wisdom is a threefold teaching: brief, middling, and detailed.” gives a threefold teaching: brief, middling, and detailed. Of them, the teaching in brief and middling modes based on trainees is finished.

From here on, having brought unmatured trainees to maturity by removing doubts that have arisen, a detailed teaching in two parts, divided into the conventional and ultimate modes, causes those who have been brought to maturity to realize the meaning of true reality.
Then,

q.p: “all the Four Mahārājas stationed in the great billion world systems together with many hundreds of thousands of one hundred million billion gods were assembled in that very retinue,”
q.orig: all the Four Mahārājas stationed in the great billionfold world system together with many hundreds of thousands of one hundred million billion gods were assembled in that very retinue,

as many gods of the Caturmahā­rāja­kāyika realm as there are in this world system of the great trichiliocosm all congregated there, in that same assembly, along with their gods—many thousands of millions and hundreds of billions in number

Then as many Great Kings as there are in this great billionfold world system…together with many hundreds of thousands of one hundred million billion gods, all congregated there, in that same assembly.

div.p: and so on. Why is it also teaching that they are all assembled on the occasion of a discourse powered by the Tathāgata?

You should know that this teaching of the perfection of wisdom is unprecedented, so there has to be a brief teaching about the retinue assembling, as a prior indicator that there is going to be an unprecedented teaching of the Dharma. Also, the show of light where he demonstrates emitting light rays and arraying light is done as a prior indicator that there is going to be an explanation of the Dharma.
Why does the chief of the gods not address his questions to the Tathāgata? Why does he ask the elder Subhūti?
At that time, those in the retinue are to be trained by an explanation by a śrāvaka, so, by way of asking him, they also have asked the Tathāgata.

q.p:
“How should bodhisattva great beings stand in the perfection of wisdom? What is the bodhisattva great beings’ perfection of wisdom? And how should bodhisattva great beings train in the perfection of wisdom?” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: how then should bodhisattva great beings dwell in the perfection of wisdom? What is the bodhisattva great beings’ perfection of wisdom? How should bodhisattva great beings train in the perfection of wisdom?

How then should bodhisattva great beings dwell in the perfection of wisdom? What is the bodhisattva great beings’ perfection of wisdom? How should bodhisattva great beings train in the perfection of wisdom?

div.p: The answers to these three questions are explained below.

div.head: What is the bodhisattva great beings’ perfection of wisdom?
div.p: There, previously, taking the knowledge of all aspects as the point of departure, it gave a middle-length explanation based on the nonconceptual perfection of wisdom. Here, taking the knowledge of path aspects as the point of departure, it teaches the conceptual and nonconceptual perfection of wisdom that is the practice of bodhisattvas.

q.p: “Those who have entered into flawlessness are incapable of producing the thought of unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening.” khri brgyad (ka 243b3) and nyi khri (kha 1b4) yang dag par skyon med pa, “flawlessness that is a perfect state.”
q.orig: Those who have entered into the flawlessness that is a perfect state are incapable of producing the thought of unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening.
Those who have already arrived at authentic maturity will not be able to set their minds on unsurpassed complete enlightenment
As for those who have entered into perfect maturity,…they are not able to set their minds on unsurpassed, perfect, complete enlightenment.

div.p: Take this as saying that those fixed in a state of error are, for the time being, without good fortune.

q.p: “And yet if they also produce the thought of unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening I still rejoice in them also.”
q.orig: However, if they do set their minds on unsurpassed, complete enlightenment…I will rejoice with them
However, if they do set their minds on unsurpassed, perfect, complete enlightenment, I rejoice in them as well.

div.p: If they hear this explanation it will not be in vain, because a scripture says, “On the other side of infinite, countless thousands of hundreds of one hundred million billion eons they will enter into buddhahood.”

q.p: “Kauśika, what is the bodhisattva great beings’ perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: Kauśika, in this regard, what, one might ask, is this perfection of wisdom of bodhisattva great beings

div.p: and so on. This is the middle of the three questions but is being taught here first because if it is taught thus, it is easier to understand.

Even though it is true that this perfection of wisdom is the all-knowledge side for the śrāvaka and pratyekabuddha levels and the knowledge of path aspects side for the bodhisattva levels, here in this knowledge of path aspects that has to be taught to a bodhisattva who wants to attain the knowledge of all aspects there are both.
There, in regard to the all-knowledge side, you should know that

q.p: “Kauśika, here bodhisattva great beings with a thought of awakening connected with the knowledge of all aspects should pay attention to form as impermanent, and they should pay attention to it as suffering, selfless, empty, a disease, a boil,”
q.orig: Kauśika, what is the bodhisattva great beings’ perfection of wisdom? Here bodhisattva great beings with a thought of awakening connected with the knowledge of all aspects should pay attention to form as impermanent, and they should pay attention to it as suffering, selfless, empty, a disease, a boil,

Kauśika, bodhisattva great beings who have set their minds on the enlightenment of all-aspect omniscience should, without apprehending anything, direct their attention to physical forms as being impermanent. They should direct their attention to physical forms as being suffering, without a self, at peace and void, a disease, a pustule

div.p: and so on, is an explanation teaching the fifteen attentions, The fifteen are, in addition, attention to form as “a thorn, a misfortune, dependent, by its nature headed to destruction, shaky, brittle, a hazard, persecution, and a headache.” and is teaching the seven attentions focused on the cessation of dependent origination. These seven attentions (khri brgyad Tempangma ka 346b7) are attention to cessation as selfless, calm, isolated, emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, and a nonenactment. khri brgyad (ka 244a7) incorrectly has attention to impermanence and suffering (mi rtag pa dang / bsdug sngal ba) in a list of nine.
In regard to the knowledge of path aspects side, it teaches that, with the nonapprehending attentions to the

Among these, I will explain the words “impermanent” and so on, in the way they are on the śrāvaka and pratyekabuddha levels.

They pay attention to [“form” and so on] khri brgyad

q.p: “impermanent”

div.p: because what has not come into being comes into being, and what has come into being becomes nonexistent. They are

q.p: “suffering”

div.p: because they have as their nature the three sufferings and because they become a cause for the suffering of others. They are

q.p: “selfless”

q.p: “empty”

div.p: like the trunk Emend sngon po to sdong po. of a plantain tree because they are hollow inside, and hence empty of an inner self. They are a

q.p: “disease”

div.p: because like a disease they require many conditions for a cure and are the root of physical and mental suffering. They are a

q.p: “boil”
q.orig: pustule

div.p: because like a boil they oppress with obsession, drip with the pus of the afflictions, and gradually swell up, ripen, and burst with birth, old age, and death. They are a

q.p: “thorn”
q.orig: sharp pain

div.p: because like a thorn they pierce with inner and outer trouble and are hard to treat. They are a

q.p: “misfortune”
q.orig: negativity

div.p: because like the wicked they are to be criticized and they become oppressive. They are

q.p: “dependent”

div.p: because they labor in the face of conditions and they labor in the work of ‘making it mine,’ so they have no agency except from others. They are

q.p: “headed to destruction”
q.orig: prone to decay

div.p: because

q.p: “by their nature”
q.orig: by its nature

div.p: they are thoroughly destroyed by sickness, old age, and death. They are

q.p: “shaky”
q.orig: disturbed

div.p: because they have the three marks of a compounded phenomenon and have the eight fickle worldly dharmas. They are

q.p: “brittle”

div.p: because it is in their inner nature to be destroyed and because they are destroyed by something harming them. They are

q.p: “a hazard”
q.orig: dangerous

div.p: because “the absence of hazards” “Absence of hazards” renders abhaya; alternatively, “freedom from fear,” because bhaya is “fear” in other contexts. is peace, is pleasure, and is the antidote, and they are the cause of all fears. They are

q.p: “persecution”

div.p: because even when they are not felt, they persecute in various harmful ways. They are

q.p: “a headache”
q.orig: contagious

div.p: because they hurt in many ways like a nagging demon “Nagging demon” renders ’dre ba (piśāca); alternatively, “a mix-up.” and a headache.

q.p:
“Putting one part of the picture together with the other parts,” khri brgyad
, literally, “causing dharmas to join together with a dharma.” The three parts of the picture are (1) the state of mind committed to becoming fully awakened, (2) the state of mind closer to the goal because of the good that has been done motivated by the commitment, and (3) the state of mind when rededicating to the original commitment, turning over all the good that brings the goal of full awakening closer to full awakening.

div.p: and so on—“putting together” is paying attention to the thought of awakening, the thought of the wholesome root, and the thought of dedication touching each other. They

q.p: “analyze”
q.orig: applying
contemplate

div.p: when they pay attention to all three not having the other’s intrinsic nature as its own intrinsic nature. They

q.p: “complete”
q.orig: completing
perfect

div.p:
when they pay attention to the meaning that has already been explained that all three are “inconceivable because they are not thought, not thought because they are inconceivable.” Cf. khri brgyad
, khri brgyad

“This not settling down on… any one part, even while thus making an examination of all the parts of the picture” khri brgyad
.

div.p: is the

q.orig: augment

div.p: completely. This is the fourth detailed and thorough analysis of all the dharmas as selfless.

q.p: “The bodhisattva great beings’ thought of the wholesome roots is not touched by the thought of awakening.”
q.orig: thoughts of dedication, possessed by bodhisattva great beings, are not associated with the mind of enlightenment

div.p: What does this teach?

Earlier bodhisattvas, having made a dedication in general with conventional attention—”I dedicate these wholesome roots to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening”—after having made an examination in the ultimate mode, since the thought of the wholesome root, the thought of awakening, and the thought of dedication do not touch Tib ’grogs suggests “accompany” or “befriend” or “associate with.” each other, they examine whether, since they do not touch, dedication exists or not.

Here some say the thoughts have not touched, but still a specific volitional factor produced through the force of an earlier thought, simultaneous with the later thought, does touch, so all the volitional factors become complete in the final thought of all. In this way, therefore, thoughts have touched.
To eliminate that, it says

q.p:
“the thought of the wholesome roots does not exist… in the thought of awakening,” khri brgyad
, nyi khri (kha 5a4).
q.orig: thoughts of dedication are nonexistent and nonapprehensible in the mind of enlightenment

div.p: and so on. It means that thought is not in the other thought, by way of a volitional factor left as a residual impression and so on. It says this because having thus taught that the actual thought does not exist, there is no volitional factor left as a residual impression and so on, like an entity that is the sharpness or dullness of a rabbit’s horn.
Having thus investigated and found that it does not exist in the intrinsic nature of the others, they also investigate and find that it does not exist in its own intrinsic nature:

q.p: “the thought of the wholesome roots does not exist in the thought of the wholesome roots, the thought of awakening does not exist in the thought of awakening,”

div.p: and so on. This is because when it is seen as just suchness there is no such investigation.

q.p:
“Kauśika, the thought of the wholesome roots is no thought,” This reading is not at khri brgyad
, ’bum nga 304a6, or nyi khri , which all have “the thought of dedication is no thought.”
q.orig: the thought of dedication is no thought
thoughts of dedication are not thought

div.p: and so on, teaches that it is just mere suchness. From the perspective of its own true dharmic nature, thought is free from falsely imagined thought so the intrinsic nature that is the nonexistence of thought comes to be known as the true dharmic nature of thought.

q.p: “A nonexistent thought does not touch a nonexistent thought,”

div.p: and so on. This reading is from our author’s version of the Sūtra. This is teaching that other than what comes to be known as the true dharmic nature of thought, no touching or existing or dedication comes to be known in any way at all. At that time it is a self-reflexive analytic knowledge beyond the path of the conceivable, hence it is

q.p: “inconceivable”
q.orig: inconceivable[5]
inconceivable[4]

div.p: and is

q.p: “no thought.”
q.orig: no thought[8]
not mind[2]

q.p: “Kauśika, this is the bodhisattva great beings’ perfection of wisdom”
q.orig: That, Kauśika, is the bodhisattva great beings’ perfection of wisdom
This, Kauśika, is the bodhisattva great beings’ perfection of wisdom

div.p: means it is nonconceptual wisdom that has gone to the other side.
Thus, conventionally they are “analytically investigating all phenomena,” but ultimately “not settling down on and not apprehending any phenomenon.”
What does

q.p: “I have to feel a sense of appreciation, Lord, and not feel no sense of appreciation”
q.orig: I should feel gratitude, and I should not fail to feel gratitude

div.p: teach? It teaches that earlier when our Lord was in the form of a bodhisattva, the great śrāvakas in the retinue of earlier tathāgatas taught him with advice and instruction, inspiring him to take it up, and inspiring him to perfectly practice what he had found. Having gradually accomplished their teaching he became completely awakened. Therefore, they too, by advising and instructing these bodhisattvas in this retinue, will establish them in perfect practice. When they have gradually accomplished that earlier teaching, they will become completely awakened. Therefore, I should show appreciation to the earlier śrāvakas.
What is the difference between the words

q.p: “advised and instructed”
q.orig: taught and instructed

div.p: and so on? Here there are the three periods: starting, middle, and end. At the start they have to be “advised and instructed.” In the middle there is practice, and at the end the result.
There during the starting period “advice” is saying, “Do not do this,” preventing them from doing what they should not do. “Instruction” is saying, “Do this,” connecting them with the activities.
In the middle there are four periods: not practicing, practicing incorrectly, practicing a bit, and practicing perfectly.
There, those who do not practice out of ignorance are inspired to practice when they are

q.p: “taught.”

div.p: Those who have set out incorrectly because of incorrect knowledge are connected with a perfect practice when they are

q.p: “made to take them up.”
q.orig: made you take them up

div.p: Those who, because of the fault of laziness and so on, practice a bit, become inspired to try to persevere when they are

q.p: “made… excited.”
q.orig: made you excited
induced

div.p: Having rejoiced, saying “excellent” to those who have set out perfectly with wisdom, they are connected with true reality when they are

q.p: “motivated.”
q.orig: aroused

div.p: At the end, they are

q.p: “caused… to enter into… and established”
q.orig: established

div.p: in the result. Construe them like that.

div.head: How should bodhisattva great beings stand in the perfection of wisdom?
div.p:
After that, in reference to the question, ‘How should they stand?’ it teaches khri brgyad
. that they should forsake where

q.p: “they should not stand,”
q.orig: they should not dwell

div.p: and, standing where they should stand, they

q.p: “should stand in the perfection of wisdom.”
q.orig: should dwell

q.p: “Form is empty of form,”
q.orig: form is empty of form;
physical forms are empty of physical forms

div.p: and so on, teaches that the realization of emptiness is where they stand.

q.p:
“By way of apprehending something” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: by way of apprehending

div.p: is where they should not stand. Therefore, this teaches that because these falsely imagined phenomena, form and so on, do not exist through the intrinsic nature of form and so on, bodhisattvas also do not exist through the intrinsic nature of a bodhisattva, and their emptinesses are not different, they are one. Therefore, form and so on in its true dharmic nature is a thoroughly established phenomenon, and a bodhisattva furthermore is

q.p: “not two,”

div.p: so to stand in their same true dharmic nature is to stand in the perfection of wisdom.

In the section of the text explaining where not to stand, furthermore, the teaching is in three parts. First they should not stand in the dharmas; second they should not stand in the true nature of dharmas; and third they should not stand as persons.

There, the section on the dharmas is again a teaching in two parts: teaching the dharmas and teaching the mark of the dharma. Both D and Golden 248a5–b1 have chos (“dharma”) and then chos nyid (“true nature of dharmas”) below. It is hard to know whether the first or the second reading is wrong, or, indeed, if both are correct. If the second, and chos nyid (“the true nature of dharmas”) is emended to chos (“dharma”), the word “mark” (mtshan nyid, *lakṣaṇa) here is used not in the sense of a general and specific mark of a form (impermanent, and suitable to be seen), but rather in the sense of a causal sign, the object aspect in a mental image, which gives rise to the perception of something, conveyed in Skt by the word followed by iti (“the idea of”). Alternatively, if the first chos (“dharma”) is emended to, or at least understood as, chos nyid (“the true nature of dharmas”), then the mark is in reference to a unifying ultimate nature, and the iti to the falsely imagined phenomenon. From, khri brgyad
–.

What is the elder Śāriputra thinking where it says,

q.p: “Then it occurred to [him] to think, ‘Well then, however could bodhisattva great beings stand in the perfection of wisdom?’ ”

Then the venerable Śāradvatīputra thought, “How should bodhisattva great beings dwell on the perfection of wisdom

div.p: He was thinking that it has said “they should not stand in all dharmas,” and that it has said it is not possible to stand in emptiness, hence “they should not stand” in it either. How could that be right?
Then the elder Subhūti establishes that they do not stand. The teaching that that is standing in the perfection of wisdom is

the tathāgatas do not dwell on anything at all

div.p: It is teaching that they stand in nonabiding nirvāṇa.

It has explained the achievement, standing without standing like that, and in the explanation based on those to be trained has said it is inexpressible. So those to be trained come to harbor doubts. Therefore, taking them as its point of departure, it sets the scene for another explanation with,

q.p: “O gods, is what is said incomprehensible?”

Divine princes! Physical forms are neither profound nor subtle

The meaning is that conceptual thought cannot get at it. it “is not deep and is not subtle.” So here the section of the text is in two parts: the dharma section and the intrinsic nature section.

q.orig: Gods, I would accept those listening to the doctrine to be like illusory beings.
Divine princes! The Dharma taught by me resembles a magical display

div.p: and so on, teaches that ultimately a speaker and a hearer are nonexistent.

q.p:
“Venerable monk Subhūti, who will be the recipients of this perfection of wisdom so deep, so hard to behold,” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: Blessed Subhūti, who will have confidence in this perfection of wisdom, which is so profound…so hard to discern

q.p: “hard to understand”
q.orig: hard to realize

div.p: because it is not an object of thinking-mind consciousness;

q.p: “peaceful”

div.p: because all the afflictions and secondary afflictions have calmed down;

q.p: “sublime”

div.p:
because up to Cf. khri brgyad
: “the cessation of volitional factors from the cessation of ignorance… the cessation of old age and death, pain, lamentation, suffering, mental anguish, and grief from the cessation of birth—thus the cessation of simply this great heap of suffering.” “all suffering” has calmed down;

q.p: “subtle”

div.p: because all conceptual thought constructions have calmed down;

q.p: “private”
q.orig: noble

div.p: because it is self-reflexive analytic knowledge;

q.p: “not an object of speculative thought”
q.orig: so hard to discern

div.p: because it transcends the path of thinking;

q.p: “brilliant”

div.p: because it is the cause for brilliance in the realization of all dharmas as they really are;

q.p: “absolutely noble”
q.orig: utterly sublime

div.p: because it is the supreme place for the realization of extraordinary dharmas; and

q.p: “an object to be known by the learned and wise”
q.orig: which is to be known by the learned and the wise

div.p: because it is not an object within the range of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and it is notThe negation in the Tibetan here (ma, "not") may very well be a scribal error that should be deleted. an object to be known by the irreversible bodhisattvas.
They

q.p:
“will be the recipients” khri brgyad
.—
q.orig: will have confidence in

div.p: they will be those who take it up. With

q.p: “persons who have seen the truths, or worthy ones with outflows dried up,”
q.orig: Those individuals who discern the truth, arhats who are free from contaminants

div.p:
and so on, it first teaches those who are seeking conventionally. There, in the ultimate sense, bodhisattvas are spoken of as those “who have seen the truths”; when they are awakened, they are called “worthy ones.” Having taught them conventionally, those being taught ultimately are from khri brgyad
–.

q.p: “they will not construct the idea that form is empty,”
q.orig: They will not construct the idea that form is empty,
They will not construe the notion that physical forms are empty

div.p: up to

q.p: “so too no being at all will be the recipient of it.”
q.orig: there are no beings at all who will have confidence in it

div.p: This teaches that just those who have directly realized the nonconceptual perfection of wisdom are those who are seeking. Ultimately there is nothing they will have sought for, so they are not those who are seeking.

Then venerable Śāriputra says the assertion that a talker and a hearer are nonexistent contradicts scripture: khri brgyad
.

q.p: “Venerable Subhūti, is it not the case that in this perfection of wisdom the three vehicles… are taught in detail?”
q.orig: Is it not the case that in this perfection of wisdom the three vehicles—that is, the Śrāvaka Vehicle, the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle, and the perfect, complete Buddha Vehicle—are taught in detail?

Venerable Subhūti, in this perfection of wisdom, have the three vehicles—that is to say, the vehicle of the śrāvakas, the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas, and the vehicle of the completely awakened buddhas—not been extensively presented

div.p: and so on. The explanation of the three vehicles; and the teaching about

q.p: “the ten levels… the assistance,”
q.orig: the first production of the thought up until the tenth production of the thought are taught for the assistance
as far as their tenth setting of the mind on enlightenment

div.p: and

q.p: “the bodhisattva path”
q.orig: the bodhisattva’s path
path of the bodhisattvas

div.p: of the perfections and so on; and about these dharmas: birth in the family of a tathāgata, sporting with

q.p: “the clairvoyances,”
q.orig: clairvoyances
extrasensory power

div.p: hearing, not forgetting, being without distraction, and the sevenfold

q.p: “confident readiness,”
q.orig: inspired speech

div.p: and so on—he is saying ‘We ourselves have heard about these.’

After that, the elder Subhūti, to teach that the explanation of these dharmas is by way of not apprehending anything, to teach they do not exist ultimately and hence that even talking is mere illusion, says, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “Exactly so, Venerable Śāriputra, exactly so,”
q.orig: Venerable Śāradvatīputra, it is so!” replied Subhūti. “It is just as you have said

div.p:
and so on. About the reason they are empty, it says khri brgyad
.

q.p: “because of inner emptiness,”
q.orig: owing to the emptiness of internal phenomena

div.p: up to

q.p: “because of the emptiness that is the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature,”
q.orig: because of outer emptiness, up to the emptiness that is the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature
the emptiness of the essential nature of nonentities

div.p: and so on.

It says the gods worship with flowers to teach the gods the sign of the emergence of the light of transcendental knowledge. Cf. Śrījagattalanivāsin’s Āmnayānusāriṇī, man ngag gi rjes su brang ba, Degé Tengyur (shes phyin, ba), 68a4 “in order to teach the gods the sign that the light of transcendental knowledge has been generated” (lha’i bu rnams la ye shes kyi snang ba bskyed pa’i rtags bstan pa’i don du me tog gi mchod pa bstan par byed de). This is in order to set the scene for the thought that comes next,

q.p:
“these flowers have been magically created,” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: These flowers have been conjured up

div.p: and so on.

q.p: “Kauśika… these flowers have not come about”
q.orig: Kauśika,” replied Subhūti, “you have said that these flowers have not originated

div.p: is saying that they are not marked as thoroughly established, that they have emptiness as their intrinsic nature, and are not flowers as their intrinsic nature.

q.p: “Kauśika, form also has not come about, and what has not come about is not form.”
q.orig: Kauśika, form also has not come about, and what has not come about is not form.
Kauśika, physical forms are also unoriginated, and that which is unoriginated is not physical forms

div.p: It says “form also has not come about” because an ultimate form does not have the production of a compounded form. Thus, it says “what has not come about is not form” because an uncompounded phenomenon that has not come about does not have the mark of a falsely imagined form.

q.p:
“Does not contradict designation and gives instruction in the true nature of dharmas” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: who teaches the nature of reality without contradicting such conceptualizations

div.p: means he gives instruction without contradicting the ultimate or the conventional.

div.head: How should bodhisattva great beings train in the perfection of wisdom?

q.p:
“Kauśika, bodhisattva great beings, having thus understood how all dharmas are mere designations, should train in the perfection of wisdom.” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: Kauśika, bodhisattva great beings should also know in that way that all phenomena are merely conceptualizations, and they should train in the perfection of wisdom

div.p:
This indicates the last of the three earlier questions,
, citing khri brgyad
. “How should a bodhisattva great being train in the perfection of wisdom?”

q.p:
“Do not train in form,” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: do not train in form
do not train in physical forms

div.p: and so on—this is saying they train without training, just as, to illustrate, they stand without standing.
In order to teach that “they do not train in form and so on because they see that form and so on are nonexistent things,” it says

q.p: “because they do not see the form in which they train,”
q.orig: Because they do not see the form in which they train,
because they do not observe any physical forms in which they should train

div.p: and so on.

q.p:
“Śatakratu… inquired… why do bodhisattva great beings not see form,” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: Śatakratu, head of the gods, inquired of venerable Subhūti, “Venerable monk Subhūti, why do bodhisattva great beings not see form,
Śakra, mighty lord of the gods, asked the elder Subhūti, “Blessed Subhūti, why do bodhisattva great beings not observe physical forms

div.p:
and so on, and to teach that “they do not see form because it is empty,” it says khri brgyad
, nyi khri .

q.p: “form is empty of form.”
q.orig: form is empty of form
physical forms are empty of physical forms

div.p:
It says, khri brgyad
; ’bum ca 64a5, nyi khri “does not see” in place of “does not train in.”

q.p: “Kauśika, it is because the emptiness of form does not train in the emptiness of form,”
q.orig: Kauśika, it is because the emptiness of form does not train in the emptiness of form
Kauśika, the emptiness of physical forms does not observe the emptiness of physical forms

div.p: and so on, as the reason they do not train. It means both a training and something that is trained in are nonexistent, so they do not train.
Then, This is not found with exactly the same words in khri brgyad, ’bum, or nyi khri.

q.p: “Kauśika, those who do not train in the emptiness of form… up to those who do not train in the emptiness of the knowledge of all aspects, train in the emptiness of form without making a division into two, up to train in the emptiness of the knowledge of all aspects without making a division into two,”

div.p: says that just those who do not train are the ones who train. “Without making a division into two” means they are the same as emptiness, so, when they have trained in the emptiness of a single dharma, they have trained in the emptiness of all. Hence it is explaining that the emptiness of a single dharma is the emptiness of all.

Then it says, I have not emended “train in the knowledge of all aspects” to “train in the emptiness of the knowledge of all aspects” (PSP 2-3: 24 and ŚsPK II-3: 83–88) because this is the reading at khri brgyad
–. The abbreviation is too extreme. The idea is that training in the emptiness of any one dharma is training in the emptiness of any other. Therefore, to train in the emptiness of any one dharma is to train in any other different dharma, or in all dharmas.

q.p: “Those who train in the emptiness of form without making a division into two, up to train in the knowledge of all aspects without making a division into two… train in countless, infinite buddhadharmas.”
q.orig: those who train in the emptiness of form without making a division into two, and those who train in . . . up to in the knowledge of all aspects without making a division into two
they train in the emptiness of physical forms without any dividing into two…all-aspect omniscience, without any dividing into two

div.p: This is teaching that those who thus train in the emptiness of all dharmas train in the six perfections and so on, up to train in all the buddhadharmas.
Then,

q.p: “do not train in order to increase or decrease form,”
q.orig: not train in order to increase or decrease form
do not train in order to enhance or diminish physical forms

div.p: teaches that training in the perfections and so on, up to the buddhadharmas, is not to increase or decrease form and so on. It means that training is not to increase the bright side or decrease the dark side.
Then,

q.p:
“[do] not train in order to get hold of or get rid of form” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: do not train in order to get hold of or get rid of form
not train in order to accept or negate physical forms

div.p: is teaching that where there are thus no dharmas to be increased or decreased, there are no special dharmas to be gotten hold of and no bad dharmas to be reduced.
It says that, and then with

q.p: “Venerable Subhūti, why do bodhisattva great beings not train in order to get hold of or get rid of form?”
q.orig: Venerable Subhūti, why do bodhisattva great beings not train in order to get hold of or get rid of form
Venerable Subhūti,” he asked, “why do bodhisattva great beings not train in order to accept or negate physical forms

div.p: the elder Śāriputra asks him why, given that bodhisattvas eliminate bad dharmas and obtain special dharmas, there is nothing for them to get hold of or get rid of. After he asks that, the elder Subhūti says

q.p: “form does not get hold of form,”
q.orig: form does not get hold of form
there is no acceptance of physical forms as physical forms

div.p: teaching that there are no grasped and grasper. It gives as the reason for that,

q.p: “based on… emptiness.”
q.orig: owing to the emptiness

q.p:
“Does not see the production… of form,” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: do not see the production and stopping, acceptance and rejection, defilement and purification, or decrease and increase of form
do not observe the arising of physical forms

div.p: and so on—something plucked out of thin air has no “production.” Something lasting in its nature does not change so there is no

q.p: “stopping.”
q.orig: cessation

div.p: In suchness there is no production so there is no

q.p: “acceptance”
q.orig: appropriation

div.p: of something not there before. There is no stopping so there is no

q.p: “rejection”
q.orig: rejection

div.p: of something gotten hold of. There is nothing to get hold of so there is no

q.p: “purification”

div.p: of something not there before. There is nothing to reject so there is no

q.p: “defilement”
q.orig: affliction

div.p: to eliminate. Since there is no purification there is no

q.p: “increase,”

div.p: and since there is no defilement there is no

q.p: “decrease.”

“Venerable monk… where should you look for the perfection of wisdom?” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: Venerable Śāradvatīputra, where should one search for the bodhisattva great beings’ perfection of wisdom

div.p: He asks about the perfection of wisdom to teach, in regard to the perfection of wisdom itself, the knowledge of path aspects and the knowledge of all aspects.

q.p: “In Subhūti’s chapter”—
q.orig: in the discourse of Subhūti

div.p: “Subhūti’s chapter” is all of the intermediate exegesis of the perfection of wisdom. See – . This is saying that the knowledge of all aspects has originated based on the perfection of wisdom, so you should grasp the explanation of it also from there.

div.head: The sustaining power of the tathāgata
div.p:
Given that the exegesis of the deep dharmas is within the range of a tathāgata, the chief of the gods does not accept that it is Subhūti’s explanation, so, setting the scene for the noble Subhūti to have given such an exegesis, he asks, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “Is it through your noble might, is it through your sustaining power…?”
q.orig: Is this through your power, through your blessing

div.p: First the elder Subhūti, in conventional mode, teaches that these are

q.p: “the Tathāgata’s sustaining power,”
q.orig: It is the blessing of the tathāgatas

div.p: that is, worthy ones give explanations of doctrine through the Tathāgata’s sustaining power. Then the chief of the gods, not accepting that either, says

q.p: “Venerable monk Subhūti, given that all dharmas are without anything that sustains them, why do you say ‘this is the Tathāgata’s sustaining power, it is the Tathāgata’s might’?”
q.orig: Blessed Subhūti, if all phenomena are without blessing, how can it be said that this is the power of the tathāgatas, this is the blessing of the tathāgatas

div.p: Then the elder, having rejoiced in that statement, to teach that in ultimate mode the tathāgata is to be taken as tathatā, Here tathāgata means “knower of reality”—literally “gone” or “come thus”; tathatā means “reality”: literally, “suchness.” with

q.p: “the tathāgata cannot be apprehended in the true nature of dharmas that is without anything that sustains it,”
q.orig: The Tathāgata…cannot be apprehended in the true nature of dharmas that is without anything that sustains it,
The existence of the tathāgatas is not apprehensible apart from reality that is devoid of blessings

div.p: and so on, teaches that there is no dharma called tathāgata at all. There are no false imagined dharmas in the true nature of dharmas, so “in” that “true dharmic nature” of all dharmas “without anything that sustains it” there is no “tathāgata.” And because there are no dharmas unincluded in the true nature of dharmas,

q.p: “nor can the tathāgata be apprehended elsewhere than the true nature of dharmas that is without anything that sustains it.”

div.p: Because the true nature of dharmas does not abide in falsely imagined phenomena,

q.p: “the true nature of dharmas that is without anything that sustains it cannot be apprehended in the tathāgata.”
q.orig: Nor indeed is reality devoid of blessings apprehensible in the tathāgatas

div.p: And because there is no true nature of dharmas elsewhere than dharmas,

q.p: “nor can the true nature of dharmas that is without anything that sustains it be apprehended elsewhere than the tathāgata.”

div.p: Construe the

q.p: “suchness”
q.orig: real nature

div.p:
section like this, khri brgyad
–. and construe the

q.p: “true dharmic nature”
q.orig: reality

div.p: and

q.p: “suchness”
q.orig: suchness[3]
real nature

div.p: of

q.p: “form,”
q.orig: physical forms

div.p: and so on, ending with

q.p: “the knowledge of all aspects”
q.orig: all-aspect omniscience

div.p: section like this as well.

q.p: “The true dharmic nature of the tathāgata is not conjoined with or disjoined from the true dharmic nature of form. … It is not conjoined with or disjoined from something other than the true dharmic nature of form.”
q.orig: the true dharmic nature of the Tathāgata…It is not conjoined with or disjoined from something other than the suchness of form

that which is a tathāgata is neither conjoined with nor disjoined from the real nature of physical forms…It is neither conjoined with nor disjoined from anything other than the reality of physical forms

div.p: It says so because they are not different, they are the same. The alternatives when a basis is conjoined with something on a basis or with something else, or disjoined from them, are that they are acceptable if they are different and not acceptable if they are not. Construe

q.p: “thus, Kauśika, not being conjoined with and not being disjoined from all dharmas—this is its might, this is its sustaining power,”
q.orig: “Thus, Kauśika, not conjoined with and not disjoined from all dharmas—this is its might, this is its sustaining power, by way of no sustaining power.
Kauśika, this is the power of those who are neither conjoined with nor disjoined from all those phenomena. This is their blessing inasmuch as they are devoid of blessing

div.p: in the suchness section, in the same way. It is the “might” of emptiness, the “sustaining power” of emptiness, in the sense that the explanation has come about taking emptiness as the point of departure.

q.p:
“They also should not look for it in form” khri brgyad
, answering Kauśika’s question, “Where should bodhisattva great beings look for the perfection of wisdom?”—
q.orig: they should not look for it in form
they should not seek it in physical forms

div.p: it says this because form and so on do not exist—

q.p: “and they should not look for it elsewhere than form.”
q.orig: and they should not look for it elsewhere than form.
They should not seek it in anything other than physical forms

div.p: It says this because the perfection of wisdom is something that does not exist, so it is not something else either. Therefore, it is teaching that because something does not exist it is not something else. It says

q.p: “all dharmas… are not conjoined, are not disjoined… and have… no mark.”
q.orig: all those phenomena—be they…in that they are without defining characteristics

q.p:
“Form is not the perfection of wisdom” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: form is not the perfection of wisdom,
physical forms are not the perfection of wisdom

div.p: teaches that both form and the perfection of wisdom are things that do not exist;

q.p: “and there is no perfection of wisdom other than form”
q.orig: and there is no perfection of wisdom other than form
Nor indeed is the perfection of wisdom anything other than physical forms

div.p: means you cannot say it is different, because it is something that does not exist. And so it says,

q.p:
“Kauśika, it is because all these dharmas do not exist and cannot be apprehended.” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: it is because all phenomena do not exist and are not apprehensible

div.head: The perfection of wisdom is great, immeasurable, infinite, and limitless
div.p:
Then Śatakratu, to teach again that this exposition of the doctrine should be taken to be amazing, makes a fourfold statement that khri brgyad
.

q.p: “The perfection of wisdom… is great… the perfection of wisdom… is immeasurable… the perfection of wisdom… is infinite… [and] the perfection of wisdom… is limitless.”
q.orig: the perfection of wisdom of bodhisattva great beings—is great. Venerable monk Subhūti, this perfection—that is, the perfection of wisdom of bodhisattva great beings—is immeasurable. Venerable monk Subhūti, this perfection—that is, the perfection of wisdom of bodhisattva great beings—is infinite. Venerable monk Subhūti, this perfection—that is, the perfection of wisdom of bodhisattva great beings—is limitless.

this perfection that bodhisattva great beings have is great. Such is the perfection of wisdom! Blessed Subhūti, this perfection that bodhisattva great beings have is immeasurable. Such is the perfection of wisdom! Blessed Subhūti, this perfection that bodhisattva great beings have is infinite

div.p:
Connect khri brgyad
.

q.p: “you cannot apprehend a prior limit of form”
q.orig: you cannot apprehend a prior limit of form
the past limit of physical forms is not apprehensible

div.p: with you cannot apprehend at that time “it was there” or “was not there”;

q.p: “you cannot apprehend a later limit”
q.orig: the future limit is not apprehensible

div.p: with at that time “it will be there” or “will not be there”; and

q.p: “you cannot apprehend a middle”
q.orig: the intervening present is not apprehensible

div.p: with “it is there” or “is not there.” Thus, it is “great” because it is not divided into three time periods.

q.p:
“You cannot apprehend a measure of form” khri brgyad
.—
q.orig: you cannot apprehend a measure of form
the limits of physical forms are nonapprehensible

div.p: ultimate form is “immeasurable” because you cannot delineate it as “just this much.” It is

q.p: “infinite”

div.p: because it cannot be given a size by counting. It is

q.p: “limitless”
q.orig: unlimited
infinite

div.p: because there is no termination of instants. The “prior limit” is production, the “later limit” is cessation, and the “middle” is lasting for an instant.

Having thus at first taught that the perfections are unlimited, it then teaches the unlimited in four parts: The first three are khri brgyad
–. The “body of dharmas” (dharmakāya) is called the “objective support”: cp. ŚsPK II-3: 213 “dharmas as objective support” (dharmālambanānantatayānanta­pāramiteyaṃ) and PSP 2-3: 33 “dharma constituent as objective support” (dharma­dhātvārambaṇānantatayānanta-pāramiteyaṃ), in the sense of being the objective support of the knowledge of all aspects—both are limitless. The third is the ultimate reality of the knowledge of all aspects and the dharmas it knows. The fourth begins from khri brgyad
. the unlimited knowledge of all aspects, the unlimited body of dharmas, unlimited suchness, and unlimited beings.

Among these, what are “unlimited beings”? Their “limits” are the two extremes: the permanent extreme and the annihilation extreme. The nonexistence of those extremes is the state where the extremes are absent, so beings are “unlimited.” Suppose beings existed. In that case they would have limits. But since beings are in their intrinsic nature just nonexistent, unlimited beings with an intrinsic nature do not exist. Suppose a certain being is taught in this explanation of the doctrine. In that case unlimited beings would also be taught. But since it does not teach a being, there are no unlimited beings here either. Therefore, it says,

q.p:
“Kauśika, where there has been no explanation of anything as a being there will also be no limitlessness of a being.” Cf. khri brgyad
, nyi khri .
q.orig: Kauśika, where there has been no elucidation of a being, where will there be the limitlessness of a being
Kauśika,” said Subhūti, “beings are infinite in this context where nothing at all is explained as a ‘being

div.p: This means that because it does not teach a being it therefore also does not teach that beings are unlimited.
Then,

q.p: “Kauśika, if a tathāgata, worthy one, perfectly complete buddha remaining for as many eons as there are sand particles in the Gaṅgā River were to say the word being again and again,”
q.orig: Kauśika, if the tathāgatas, arhats, completely awakened buddhas, present in eons as numerous as the grains of sand of the river Gaṅgā, were to speak of ‘beings

div.p: and so on, teaches that a statement from the mouth does not make beings unlimited. They are unlimited in their intrinsic nature because they are nonexistent. Suppose beings were made unlimited as a statement in the mouth, that from what the Tathāgata says beings might be born or cease. It means because that is not the case, beings are not unlimited because it has been said they are.

q.p: “Kauśika, from this one of many explanations you should know this perfection of wisdom is unlimited because beings are unlimited.”
q.orig: “Kauśika,” said Subhūti, “from this one of many explanations you should know this perfection of bodhisattva great beings is unlimited because beings are unlimited.”
Kauśika, this formulation explains how one should know that the perfection of wisdom is infinite because beings are infinite

div.p: This means suppose a being is taught in this explanation, so it exists in reality. Then the two extremes would also exist. But those two are not taught so this perfection is limitless. Because a being is not taught, therefore a being does not exist. Because it does not exist the two extremes do not exist either. Therefore, because it does not teach a being this perfection is unlimited.

q.p:
“Without apprehending any dharma… still they make known the presentation of the three vehicles” khri brgyad
.—
q.orig: Without apprehending any dharma, be it form, or feeling, or perception, or volitional factors, or consciousness, up to or the knowledge of all aspects, still they make known a presentation of the three vehicles
Although nothing at all is apprehensible…there are nonetheless three vehicles set forth

div.p: ultimately and conventionally.

q.p:
“But without apprehending the tathāgata as other than the perfection of giving” khri brgyad
.—
q.orig: A tathāgata is nevertheless not apprehensible as anything other than the perfections

div.p: this means the dharma body’s tathāgata is the intrinsic nature of the buddhadharmas. When bodhisattvas train in that, because it is ultimately the intrinsic nature of the buddhadharmas there is also no difference between bodhisattvas and tathāgatas so

q.p: “you… should therefore call them… just tathāgatas.”
q.orig: you, gods, should therefore call those bodhisattva great beings, practicing without becoming separated from the perfection of wisdom, just tathāgatas.
bodhisattva great beings who practice this perfection of wisdom inseparably are said to be tathāgatas

div.p: Since bodhisattvas newly practicing the buddhadharmas are the intrinsic nature of the buddhadharmas, because he This is the brahmin student who in the future would become Śākyamuni. would teach,

q.p: “the tathāgata… Dīpaṅkara,”
q.orig: the tathāgata, worthy one, perfectly complete buddha Dīpaṃkara
the tathāgata, arhat, completely awakened Buddha Dīpaṃkara

div.p: having seen that he was inseparable from the buddhadharmas, prophesied he would be a tathāgata. Thus it gives the example of Dīpaṅkara.

q.p: “Then those gods said to the Lord” nyi khri .—
q.orig: The gods then said to the Blessed One

div.p: because the Lord had obtained the prophesy from Dīpaṅkara—

q.p: “It is amazing, Lord, this perfection of wisdom of the bodhisattva great beings, through not appropriating and rejecting form,”
q.orig: It is amazing, Lord, the extent to which this perfection of wisdom of the bodhisattva great beings is favorable to the knowledge of all aspects through not getting hold of or rejecting form

Blessed Lord, it is wonderful how the bodhisattva great beings’ perfection of wisdom favorably sustains the bodhisattva great beings’ all-aspect omniscience, without acquiring or relinquishing physical forms

div.p: up to

q.p: “is favorable to getting hold of An alternative translation: “remains consistent with.” the knowledge of all aspects.”
q.orig: not getting hold of or rejecting the knowledge of all aspects.
including all-aspect omniscience

div.p: This means it is amazing that it assists a “knowledge of all aspects” not there before, even though the two, “getting hold of and rejecting,” do not exist, because a real superior or inferior thing in the dharmas, form and so on, does not exist.

div.head: Beneficial qualities

q.p: Then the Lord, knowing the four retinues of monks, nuns,
q.orig: Then the Blessed One, knowing that all four assemblies of monks, nuns

div.p: and so on, takes as its point of departure the Perfection of Wisdom that is being explained. I have capitalized “perfection of wisdom” as an aid to the reader, not because it refers exclusively to the book as distinct from its contents or internalization. It teaches the beneficial qualities that come about in this life and in later lives from this explanation of the Dharma that up to here has constituted the meaning, and that serves as the cause for an increase of much merit.

q.p:

q.orig: emptiness of form into a good sustainable position
have been totally consecrated in [the understanding] that physical forms are emptiness

div.p: teaches just a concordant cause with emptiness as the sustainable position, which is to say, to them The children of a good family who are not hurt (“not infiltrated”) because they respect the Perfection of Wisdom and what it teaches. all ordinary things appear as empty, and the self, too, appears as empty.
Here it teaches why

q.orig: there is no opportunity for emptiness to impinge upon emptiness

div.p: That

q.p: “with which they might infiltrate”

q.orig: the situation in which it would find an opportunity to impinge

div.p: is a bodhisattva. It is because they are all nonexistent. I will not spell it out here because the scripture is easy to interpret.

div.p: Here, furthermore, it teaches four benefits: not being infiltrated, not dying an untimely death, not getting scared and so on, and being protected by the gods.
Teaching by analogy, with

and so on, it teaches the greater value. khri brgyad
says gods will amass a greater store of merit from respecting and protecting bodhisattvas practicing and teaching the perfection of wisdom than from respecting and protecting all the other types of beings.
This teaches the benefits in this life and the many benefits in future lives. There are the ten,

and so on; The others at khri brgyad

div.p:
calm those who fight and contradict them and so on; the causes of those; perfectly gaining the six perfections; the absence of being disturbed ’khrugs; dkrugs at khri brgyad (ka 277b5). and so on; the analogy of medicine; khri brgyad

. protecting and increasing

train in the correct manner

in each of the six perfections. khri brgyad
–.

bodhisattva great beings practice the mundane

nor do they apprehend

div.p: anything and this perfection of wisdom is completely guiding them, it has been made available in order to fully guide them, and been made available in order to lessen their conceit because they do not become conceited.

div.head: Merits
div.p:
Then This summarizes khri brgyad
–, chapter 27. it teaches that it protects from weapons in a battle and the reasons for that; that it protects from external harms and the reasons for that; and that it does not present an opportunity for infiltration. glags thod. thod is a non-agentive form of gtod. It teaches with the example of the site of awakening; and with khri brgyad
.

q.p: “having borne respectfully in mind this perfection of wisdom written out in book form”
q.orig: commit this perfection of wisdom to writing, keep it in the form of a book

div.p:
it teaches the qualities of the perfection of wisdom as a collection of statements and collection of letters. It teaches that places come to serve as caityas because of the perfection of wisdom, and it teaches that the worship there of the perfection of wisdom is superior to worship of a caitya filled with the physical remains of a tathāgata and the reasons for that; that there are more beings who are lacking and many fewer who are good and the reasons for that; that in the ten directions there are more beings in the deficient vehicle and the reasons for that; that it is necessary to engage constantly in listening to this explanation and so on; that worshiping it khri brgyad
ff. The merit from the worship of the perfection of wisdom. is superior to worshiping

a stūpa of the seven precious materials

div.p: that there is more merit from that than from worshiping just a

q.p: “Jambudvīpa,”

div.p: just a

div.p: or just a

div.p:
full of stūpas; and that there is more merit from worshiping the perfection of wisdom than all beings in all world systems worshiping that many stūpas. Similarly, it teaches there is more merit from worshiping it than if khri brgyad
.

div.p:
were to have made a stūpa of the seven precious things and worshiped it, and the reasons for that. It teaches that when the perfection of wisdom is present in the world the cause of the special ordinary and extraordinary good qualities comes about; the entrusting to Śatakratu; khri brgyad
: “Kauśika, you should take up the perfection of wisdom. Kauśika, you should keep in mind, you should recite, you should master, and you should properly pay attention to the perfection of wisdom.” and the benefits conveyed using the analogy of the gods and asuras when they

div.p: and teaches the reasons for those. It is “a great knowledge-mantra” because it has all ordinary and extraordinary attributes and hence is exceedingly great; it is “an unsurpassable knowledge-mantra” because there is no other above it; and it is “a knowledge-mantra equal to the unequaled” because there is none equal to it. By giving the illustration of

other than dying due to the maturation of past actions, will not die due to poisoning, they will not die due to weapons, they will not die due to fire, and they will not die due to water. They will not die due to other causes, up to and including the one hundred and one diseases

div.p: and they are not persecuted by retainers of

q.orig: have incomplete faculties, will never have missing limbs, will never be born in
be born crippled. They will never be born

div.p: a low caste; they will have

Journeying from buddhafield to buddhafield, they will bring beings to…maturity…and they will even refine the buddhafields

ff., chapter 29.

guard, shelter

div.p:
and that those who take it up will become endowed with the finest wholesome roots. In this context, Cf. khri brgyad
, nyi khri . what emerges from the perfection of wisdom is the knowledge of all aspects.

q.p: “Issues forth from… the knowledge of all aspects”
q.orig: issues forth from this—that is, the perfection of wisdom—and the perfection of wisdom issues forth from this, that is, the knowledge of all aspects. And why? Because the knowledge of all aspects
all-aspect omniscience of the tathāgatas, arhats, completely awakened buddhas has originated from the perfection of wisdom. The perfection of wisdom has originated from all-aspect omniscience

div.p: and

q.p: “the perfection of wisdom”

div.p: teaches that they are different conventionally, and

q.p: “the knowledge of all aspects is not one thing and the perfection of wisdom another”
q.orig: the knowledge of all aspects[3]…perfection of wisdom another
Nor is all-aspect omniscience one distinct thing and the perfection of wisdom another

div.p: teaches that they are not different ultimately.

q.p: “The knowledge of all aspects issues forth from the perfection of wisdom”
q.orig: the knowledge of all aspects[1]…issues forth from this—that is, the perfection of wisdom
all-aspect omniscience of the tathāgatas, arhats, completely awakened buddhas has originated from the perfection of wisdom

div.p: is the practice level;

q.p: “the perfection of wisdom issues forth from the knowledge of all aspects”
q.orig: the perfection of wisdom issues forth from this, that is, the knowledge of all aspects
The perfection of wisdom has originated from all-aspect omniscience

div.p: is the result level.

q.p: “The knowledge of all aspects is not one thing and the perfection of wisdom another”
q.orig: the knowledge of all aspects[3]…perfection of wisdom another
Nor is all-aspect omniscience one distinct thing and the perfection of wisdom another

div.p: because both constitute the dharma body.

After that Ānanda speaks, khri brgyad
ff. and then, from le’u brgyad ma nga 74a2.

q.p: “all the buddhadharmas are preceded by the perfection of wisdom,”
q.orig: these—that is, the five perfections, connect this in the same way with each, up to the eighteen distinct attributes of a buddha—are preceded by the perfection of wisdom.
this perfection of wisdom has precedence over

div.p: up to

q.p: “Ānanda, … have been dedicated to the knowledge of all aspects in a nondual way,”
q.orig: Ānanda,” the Blessed One answered, “giving that is dedicated toward all-aspect omniscience in a nondual manner

div.p: it says that when giving has been dedicated to the knowledge of all aspects, at that time, having understood analytically that the perfection of giving and the knowledge of all aspects are not different and not two at the result level, when engaging in giving it

q.p: “gets the name ‘perfection of giving.’ ”
q.orig: get the name ‘perfection[2]
is indicative of the perfection of generosity

q.p: “Ānanda, by way of the nonduality of form, in a nonappropriating way, in a nonapprehending way” Cf. khri brgyad (kha 2a5–2b2). The Tib translators evidently read anupādānayogena (rendered len pa med pa’i tshul gyis) in place of Gilgit 465.6, PSP 2-3: 78 anutpādayogena, rendered ’bum ca 308b3, nyi khri (kha 90b3), le’u brgyad ma nga 74a6–7 m(y)i skye pa’i tshul gyis. —
q.orig: by way of the nonduality of form
owing to the nonduality of physical forms

div.p: the true dharmic nature of form is “by way of the nonduality of form”; falsely imagined form is “by way of nonapprehending”; and conceptualized form is “by way of nonappropriating.” In

q.p: “that which is nondual cannot be apprehended,”

div.p: the nondual is the thoroughly established phenomenon. It is not settled down on as something apprehended and falsely imagined.

q.p: “That which cannot be apprehended is not appropriated”

div.p: means that the absence of settling down by way of apprehending is not appropriated by the conceptualization that pays attention to it.

Then again it teaches khri brgyad
ff. infinite good qualities of the perfection of wisdom: that it serves as the cause of

q.p: “an immeasurable… morality”
q.orig: immeasurable aggregate of ethical discipline

div.p: and so on, and surpasses the

q.p: “morality… of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas”
q.orig: aggregate of ethical discipline…the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas

div.p: and so on. It teaches Śatakratu’s commitment to

q.p: “guard, protect, and keep safe”;
q.orig: guard, shelter, and nurture

div.p:
the gods connecting with confidence giving a readiness to speak; khri brgyad
“Those gods will want to connect those sons of a good family or daughters of a good family with the confidence that gives a readiness to speak about the perfection of wisdom.” not being cowed in front of retinues; not fault-finding; not feeling cowed and so on; being liked by the whole world; the seamless khri brgyad
, PSP 2-3: 82 anācchedya. true nature of dharmas; all the gods taking up the perfection of wisdom; the offering of a gift of Dharma to them; the gods guarding; the sign

q.orig: gods have come
the gods of the Caturmahā­rāja­kāyika realm and the gods [of other realms], up to and including Akaniṣṭha, will have arrived here

div.p: the inferior gods withdrawing; belief in the vast; rgya chen po la mos pa. Closest is khri brgyad (kha 7b5–6) rgya cher mos pa: “The belief of those sons of a good family or daughters of a good family becomes stronger and stronger in line with the arrival there of those extremely powerful gods.” PSP 2-3: 85 udārādhimuktika; ’bum ca 331a6, nyi khri (kha 98a7), le’u brgyad ma nga 80a5 mos pa rgya chen po. LSPW p. 243b “confirmed in their faith.” worship of the place; feeling a sense of physical pleasure and so on; having no weariness and so on; having good dreams;

q.p: bodies being infused with energy; Closest again is khri brgyad (kha 8b6) lus la gzi brjid bcug par. PSP 2-3: 86, Aṣṭa (Wogihara p. 262) kāyam ojaḥprakṣiptam; ’bum ca 336b6, nyi khri (kha 99b2), le’u brgyad ma nga 81a6 mdangs dang ldan par ’gyur.
q.orig: vitality of body

div.p: not being greedy for the four requirements; The four requirements are robes, alms, beds and seats, and medicines for sicknesses. worshiping all the buddhas in world systems all around in the ten directions with the four requirements; there being more merit merely from having respected this perfection of wisdom, even if it has not been taken up and so on, than from having stūpas made of the seven various precious stones and worshiping them; and there being more merit from taking up the perfection of wisdom than were

q.p: “Śatakratu, head of the gods”
q.orig: Śakra, mighty lord of the gods

div.p: to have

q.p: “filled this Jambudvīpa right to the top with the physical remains of the tathāgatas,”
q.orig: Jambudvīpa filled right to the top with the physical remains of the tathāgatas
Jambudvīpa, filled to the top with the bone relics of the tathāgatas

div.p: and the reasons for that.

In this context, khri brgyad
ff.

q.p: “Kauśika, the perfection of wisdom cannot be apprehended”
q.orig: Kauśika, this perfection of wisdom cannot be grasped

div.p: because it “cannot be apprehended” with thinking-mind consciousness. It

q.p: “cannot be pointed out”
q.orig: invisible

div.p: because it “cannot be pointed out” with words. It

q.p: “does not obstruct”
q.orig: unimpeded

div.p: because, since it is not an object of sense consciousness, it “does not obstruct” as an object does. It

q.p: “has only one mark—that is, no mark”
q.orig: has a single defining characteristic in that it is without defining characteristics

div.p: because it is separated from all imaginary marks.

q.p: “It is not a place to be seized or not seized”
q.orig: this perfection of wisdom is not a place to be seized or not seized,
it is not established in order that it might be grasped or rejected

div.p: because it is not suitable to be conceptualized as something that can be seized or something that cannot be seized;

q.p: “to be increased or reduced”
q.orig: nor that it might be eclipsed, nor that it might be enhanced

div.p: because it is not a place for the elimination of things on the dark side or the increase of things on the bright side; or

q.p: “to be taken away from or added to”
q.orig: nor that it might be supplemented

div.p: because it is not a place for the removal of saṃsāric dharmas or the accomplishment of nirvāṇic dharmas. And why? Because it is without all attachments to such conceptualizations. You should connect it in the same way with them all. These are the establishment and removal, respectively, of dharmas of buddhas and ordinary persons; bodhisattvas and śrāvakas; those in training and for whom there is no more training; and the uncompounded and compounded.

q.p: “A dual perfection of wisdom is not available”
q.orig: The perfection of wisdom is not known in duality

div.p: means were the perfection of wisdom to be a mode of seizing and not seizing and so on, it would be in a dual state and would be available with a diverse nature, but it is ultimately one, not broken apart, so ultimately such a proliferation of activity is absent from it.

q.p: “Similarly, a perfection of giving, a perfection of morality,”
q.orig: Similarly, a dual perfection of concentration, perfection of perseverance, perfection of patience, perfection of morality, and perfection of giving
the perfection of ethical discipline, and the perfection of generosity

div.p: and so on, in the ultimate state are essentially one, and hence

q.p: “are not two,”
q.orig: is not two
nondual[2]

div.p: because they are not broken apart. Therefore, it says,

q.p: “Kauśika… is simply to accept suchness as two,”
q.orig: Kauśika, those who hold that the perfection of wisdom is duality simply hold that the real nature, the very limit of reality, and the inconceivable realm are duality

div.p: and so on. All those perfections of wisdom and so on are one in the form of suchness; they are not there as a duality.

It gives the illustration of [the throne] khri brgyad
.

q.p: “in the Sudharmā assembly of gods”
q.orig: in the divine assembly of Sudharmā

div.p: and teaches that the physical remains of all the tathāgatas have come about from this perfection of wisdom.

q.p: “The perfection of wisdom has no causal sign”
q.orig: the perfection of wisdom is without signs

div.p: because it

q.p: “has no token, is inexpressible,”
q.orig: without indications, and inexpressible

div.p: and so on, and is therefore separated from all thought constructions. It “has no token” because it is separated from its own defining mark. It “is inexpressible” because it is not within the range of words. It

q.p: “cannot be talked about”
q.orig: cannot be spoken

div.p: because it is not in the form of language. It

q.p: “is inconceivable”
q.orig: inconceivable

div.p: because it is self-reflexive analytic knowledge.
After that it teaches that there will be none of the bad forms of life or lesser vehicle aspirations and so on; that there is more merit from taking up this perfection of wisdom than from

this great trichiliocosm, filled to the brim with the bone relics of the tathāgatas

div.p: and the reasons for that; that

q.orig: the perfection of wisdom and the tathāgatas are not two things

div.p: that for all the buddhas in the ten directions to teach the twelvefold doctrine These are the discourses, melodious narrations, predictions, verses, summaries, introductions, accounts, birth stories, expanded texts, marvels, tales, and expositions. and to read the perfection of wisdom out loud

q.p: “is equivalent”;
q.orig: there is no difference

div.p: and that worshiping all the tathāgatas of the ten directions and worshiping the perfection of wisdom

q.p: “is equivalent.”
q.orig: there is no difference

div.p:
It teaches that those who have taken up the perfection of wisdom and so on stand on the irreversible level; khri brgyad
. the analogy of

q.p: “a person fearful of rich creditors”;
q.orig: a wealthy man, out of fear

div.p: that they reach the true nature of dharmas—

q.p:
“complete nirvāṇa”; khri brgyad
.
q.orig: final nirvāṇa

div.p: the analogy of

q.p: “the large jewel”;
q.orig: large, priceless jewel
priceless gem

div.p:
again, khri brgyad
. that there is more merit from taking up this perfection of wisdom than from

q.p: “as many… world systems as there are sand particles in the Gaṅgā River filled right to the top with the physical remains of tathāgatas,”
q.orig: all the world systems of the ten directions, numerous as the grains of sand of the river Gaṅgā, filled to the brim with the bone relics of the tathāgatas

div.p: and the reason for that; and seeing

q.p:
“the dharma body, the form body, and the knowledge body.” ’bum ca 360b3 and nyi khri (kha 110a3) have ye shes kyi sku (jñānakāya) here. khri brgyad
, and also khri brgyad S kha 79b2, PSP 2-3: 96 (dharmakāyena ca rūpakāyena ca draṣṭukāmena), and le’u brgyad ma nga 89b1 omit. The dharma body and form body are the result of the jñānasaṃbhāra (“knowledge accumulation” or “equipment”) and the puṇyasaṃbhāra (“merit accumulation” or “equipment”), respectively.
q.orig: the buddha body of reality, the buddha body of form, or the buddha body of wisdom

div.p: The “knowledge body” is the knowledge accumulation.

q.p: “What the dharmas actually are when compounded” Golden 261b4 mtshan nyid.—

div.p: they have transcendental knowledge with conceptualization as their intrinsic nature.

q.p: “What dharmas actually are when they are uncompounded”—

div.p: the intrinsic nature that is the inexpressible, the ultimate is what dharmas actually are when they are uncompounded.

q.p:
“Gives detailed instruction for the three vehicles, and instruction by way of no causal sign, by way of no production, by way of no stopping,” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: the three vehicles are all extensively revealed through this perfection of wisdom, and they are indeed revealed in the manner of signlessness, in the manner of nonapprehending, in the manner of nonarising, in the manner of nonceasing

div.p: and so on—it says this intending the nirvāṇa of śrāvakas at the result stage.
Ultimately, the perfection of wisdom

q.p: “is not over there or over here, or has stayed up or sunk down,”
q.orig: is not over there or over here, nor has it stayed up or sunk down,
is neither remote nor alien

div.p: and so on. It explains it like this because, again, at the thoroughly established stage such conceptualizations and causal signs do not exist.

q.p: “Replied Śatakratu, “This—that is, the perfection of wisdom—is a great perfection.”
q.orig: Śakra replied, “Blessed Lord…this perfection of wisdom is a great transcendence

div.p: He says this having thought about the intrinsic nature of the wisdom that is perfect. The attention that does not apprehend any dharma does not see it, so it is like space because it is a greater object.

As for the analogy of the trees, khri brgyad
. the perfection of wisdom is like the trees; those other than it are like the shadows.
It teaches that giving to others has a greater result than personal worship.

q.p:
“Shatters the vajra-like body and imbues the physical remains of the tathāgata with a special power” khri brgyad
.—
q.orig: their vajra-like body dissolves. Generating great compassion in the worlds of beings for the sake of those beings who can be trained by means of the pearl relics of the tathāgatas, they consecrate the bone relics of the tathāgatas

div.p: this teaches that what has been shared has a greater result.

q.p: “Who goes to others and explicates”
q.orig: to approach others and explain

div.p: is teaching the activity of teaching.

q.p:
“ ‘What should I rely on and stay by, whom should I respect, revere, honor, and worship?’ ” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: What should I serve, respect, honor, and worship

div.p: is teaching that if even the Tathāgata worshiped this perfection of wisdom, it goes without saying those others than him should. The section of the passage that says,

q.p: “Kauśika, those sons of a good family or daughters of a good family who have entered into the Śrāvaka Vehicle or who have entered into the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle,”
q.orig: Kauśika, sons of a good family or daughters of a good family in the Great Vehicle, in the Śrāvaka Vehicle, and in the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle
noble sons or noble daughters who follow the vehicle of the śrāvakas or the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas

div.p: is teaching that the perfection of wisdom is the principal cause and therefore should be worshiped.

Then there is a section Beginning at khri brgyad
, chapter 32. teaching that the result of merit is greater

q.p: “from establishing one being in the result of stream enterer, but not so much from establishing the beings in Jambudvīpa in the ten wholesome actions.”
q.orig: established a single being in the fruit of entering the stream to nirvāṇa, their merit would increase more greatly, but by establishing the beings of Jambudvīpa in the paths of the ten virtuous actions

div.p:
Then, having taught the increase in merit in a further section, teaching that there is more merit from having khri brgyad
.

q.p: “written out this perfection of wisdom in book form and bestowed it”
q.orig: give this perfection of wisdom to others in order that they might commit it to writing in book form

div.p: than from, up to

q.p: “establishing all the beings in Jambudvīpa in the state of a worthy one and a pratyekabuddha’s awakening,”
q.orig: established beings in Jambudvīpa in . . . up to a pratyekabuddha’s awakening
establishing of the beings of Jambudvīpa in the paths of the ten virtuous actions and the establishing of them [in other goals], up to and including…individual enlightenment

div.p: and taught that the reason for that is that

q.p: “in this perfection of wisdom are taught the dharmas without outflows,”
q.orig: in this perfection of wisdom are taught in detail those dharmas without outflows
the uncontaminated attributes are extensively revealed through this perfection of wisdom

div.p:
it teaches that it serves as the cause for the appearance of all ordinary special beings and serves as the cause for the appearance of noble beings. Then there is the section khri brgyad
ff. about greater merit from having

q.p: “written out this perfection of wisdom in book form and bestowed it”
q.orig: give this book of the perfection of wisdom to others
