div.p: than from having established all the beings in this four continent world system… thousandfold… millionfold… a great billionfold world system… or in world systems in the ten directions in the state of a worthy one and a pratyekabuddha’s awakening; the section on the reason for that—that in it are taught dharmas without outflows; the section teaching that it serves as the cause for the appearance of all ordinary special beings and serves as the cause for the appearance of noble beings; and then the teaching on the greater merit, and the teaching that properly paying attention is the main thing.

q.p:
“There, properly paying attention is this: taking up… this perfection of wisdom with an understanding that operates without duality.” khri brgyad
, le’u brgyad ma, nga, 98b7; ’bum cha 27b5, nyi khri (kha 123b3–4) gnyis la spyod pa yang ma yin/ mi gnyis pa la spyod pa yang ma yin pa’i blo, Twenty-Five Thousand translation: “the mind, without engaging in duality and without engaging in nonduality.”
q.orig: There, properly paying attention is this: taking up, bearing in mind, reading aloud, mastering, and properly paying attention to this perfection of wisdom with an understanding that operates without duality; taking up, bearing in mind, reading aloud, mastering, and properly paying attention to the perfection of concentration, perfection of perseverance, perfection of patience, perfection of morality, and perfection of giving with an understanding that operates without duality;
In this regard, focussing the attention correctly entails that the mind, without engaging in duality and without engaging in nonduality

div.p: This means that engaging “with an understanding” that habitually “operates without duality” is “properly paying attention.”
Then there is the section This is explaining properly paying attention to others. on the great increase in merit and the teaching that meaning is principal.

q.p: “There the meaning of the perfection of wisdom is this:”
q.orig: the meaning of the perfection of wisdom [that they would reveal] would be as follows

div.p: first,

q.p: “not viewing the perfection of wisdom as two and not viewing it as not two.”
q.orig: The perfection of wisdom observes neither duality nor nonduality

div.p:
This means never mind a dualistic nature, there is not even the idea that because it is separated from the conceptualization of all dharmas the nature of the nonconceptual perfection of wisdom is nondual, so the perfection of wisdom is not viewed in a dual way and it is not viewed in a nondual way either. There, khri brgyad
. This is introducing the explanation of the fourteen pairs.

q.p: “not viewing the perfection of wisdom as a causal sign or as not a causal sign,”
q.orig: not viewing it as a causal sign or as not a causal sign,
It is neither with signs nor without signs

div.p: and so on, teaches the nonexistence of fourteen conceptualizations of fourteen states: being an objective support, the maturation of karma, being a differentiated object of knowledge, transformation of the basis, apprehension of the meaning of true reality, ascending from one level to another level, different levels, practice, paying attention, elimination, realization, witnessing the true nature of dharmas, meditating on suchness, and nirvāṇa.

There, it says “not as a causal sign and not as not a causal sign” because, when apprehending an objective support, it does not grasp the falsely imagined causal sign of form and so on, and the idea “there is no causal sign” does not occur. Similarly, it says not

q.p: “as brought in or as sent out,”
q.orig: It is neither to be…accepted…nor to be rejected

div.p: because it does not conceive of bringing something into existence at the time of the karmic action, and it does not conceive of being sent out in forms of life at the time of the maturation. Similarly, it says not

q.p: “as taken away or as added on,”
q.orig: It is without decrease and without increase

div.p: because, when differentiating dharmas as objects of knowledge, it does not take anything away by over-negating something that exists, and it does not add anything on by over-reifying something that does not exist. Similarly, it says not

q.p: “as defilement or as purification,”
q.orig: It is without affliction and without purification

div.p: because, when in the state of an ordinary person, the tathāgata­garbha is naturally pure, so there is no defilement, and even when there is a transformation of the basis there is no purification not already there before, like space. Similarly, it says not

q.p: “as a production or as a cessation,”
q.orig: It neither arises nor ceases

div.p: because no production or stopping is seen in the true nature of dharmas because all dharmas are not produced and do not stop. Similarly, it says not

q.p: “as grasped or as rejected,”
q.orig: It is neither grasped nor is it not grasped. It is neither adopted nor is it abandoned.

div.p: because, even when ascending from a lower level to a higher level, ultimately it does not grasp a special realization dharma at a higher level and does not reject an inferior realization dharma at a lower level. Similarly, it says not

q.p: “as stationed or as not stationed,”
q.orig: It neither dwells not does it not dwell

div.p: because it does not conceive of having to be stationed on a higher level and it does not conceive of having to be not stationed on a lower level, because both being stationed and not being stationed are simply just imaginary. Similarly, it says not

q.p: “as true or as mistaken,”
q.orig: It is neither authentic nor is it erroneous

div.p: because when engaging in the practice of calm abiding and special insight the ideas “this is correct practice” and “this is not correct practice” do not occur. Similarly, it says not

q.p: “as right or as wrong,”

div.p: because, even when zealously paying attention to true reality correctly, the ideas “this attention is produced in the right way,” and “this is produced in the wrong way” do not occur. Similarly, it says not

q.p: “as tiny or as not tiny,”

div.p: because, even though, when eliminating the afflictive obscurations and the knowledge obscurations that are the final basis of suffering, the tiny conceptualization of afflictions is eliminated in stages, such an idea does not occur. Similarly, it says not

q.p: “as a part or as not a part,”
q.orig: It is neither hybrid nor is it not hybrid

div.p: because, even when realizing the ultimate in the form of suchness in stages through parts—“in the omnipresent sense, the tip sense, the outflow sense, the neither defilement nor purification sense, the nothing is lacking and nothing added sense” and so on This is paraphrasing Madhyānta­vibhāga 2.14–16, picking and choosing from the list of ten antidotes that counteract obstacles to the ten bodhisattva levels. —such an idea does not occur. Similarly, it says not

q.p: “as a dharma or as not a dharma,”
q.orig: It is neither something nor is it nothing

div.p: because, even when making the true nature of dharmas manifest and bringing the true nature of dharmas to completion, if there is any idea of something in the form of a dharma or not a dharma the actual stable suchness is not appearing. Similarly, it says not

q.p: “as suchness or as not suchness,”
q.orig: It is neither the real nature nor is it not the real nature

div.p: because even when meditating on suchness the ideas “this is suchness” and “this is something else” do not occur. And similarly, it says not

q.p: “as the very limit of reality or as not the very limit of reality,”
q.orig: It is neither the very limit of reality nor is it not the very limit of reality

div.p: because even when in nirvāṇa “this is the very limit of reality and this is its opposite” is not grasped.
In regard to

q.p: “this is the meaning of nondual,”
q.orig: That is to say, it is without dualities

div.p: it is explained that this “meaning” is counted in one way as what is to be explained and counted in another way as apprehending; and in regard to this “nondual,” that apprehending the meaning to be explained—the perfection of wisdom that has been explained—and the nonconceptual perfection of wisdom is apprehending the meaning of the perfection of wisdom.
Then the section on

q.p: “in both the meaning and the letter”
q.orig: its meaning and its letters[1]

div.p: teaches that the merit from explaining this is greater than the merit from personally taking it up.
Then there is the section about the greater merit from explaining this than from having worshiped

q.p: “with all the requirements for happiness, all the buddhas in the ten directions”;
q.orig: with flowers, perfumes, incense, garlands, creams, powders, robes, parasols, flags, and banners, with all the requirements for happiness, infinite, countless tathāgatas, worthy ones, perfectly complete buddhas in each of the ten directions

the immeasurable, countless tathāgatas, arhats, completely awakened buddhas in each of all the ten directions with flowers, garlands, perfume, unguents, powders, robes, parasols, victory banners, ribbons, diverse musical sounds, and all comforts

div.p: then the section on the merit from explaining this

q.p: “without apprehending anything”

div.p: being greater than the merit from practicing the six perfections

q.p: “for infinite, incalculable eons by way of apprehending something”;
q.orig: over immeasurable, countless eons, practice the perfection of generosity, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of tolerance, the perfection of perseverance, the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom by way of apprehending

div.p: and the section on the perfections while apprehending something.

There are four sections The sections are khri brgyad
–,
–, and the last two at
–; cf. ’bum cha 92a5 ff. and PSP 2-3: 113. on the

q.p: “counterfeit perfection of wisdom.”
q.orig: counterfeit perfection of wisdom[1]
imitation of the perfection of wisdom

div.p: The first is the section teaching cultivation while apprehending something; the second is the section teaching the perfections with results; the third is the section about gaining

q.p: “immeasurable merit”;
q.orig: immeasurable mass of merit,
immeasurable, incalculable, inestimable mass of merit

div.p: and the fourth is the section teaching rejoicing and dedication.

The sections teaching the perfectly pure perfection of wisdom are also two. khri brgyad
–. The first is the section on the instruction that they should not apprehend anything; Cf. nyi khri (kha 130a4–5). the second is the section on not having a view of any dharma and not resting on grasping a view as absolute.

Then there are six sections This and the following sections summarize khri brgyad
–. teaching that there is more merit from explaining it to others than the merit from establishing the beings in Jambudvīpa… in the four continents… in a thousandfold… a millionfold… a billionfold world system… or in world systems in the ten directions in the result of stream enterer; similarly, the six sections teach that there is more merit from explaining it to others than the merit from establishing beings

q.p: “in the result of once-returner,”
q.orig: in the fruit of being destined for only one more rebirth

div.p: up to

q.p: “a pratyekabuddha’s awakening,”
q.orig: state of a pratyekabuddha
individual enlightenment

div.p: based on the beings in Jambudvīpa, the four continents and so on; similarly, the six sections teach that there is more merit from explaining it to others than the merit from causing beings to take up

q.p: “unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening”
q.orig: unsurpassed, complete enlightenment

div.p: based on the beings in Jambudvīpa, the four continents and so on; similarly, there are also the six sections about those established

q.p: “in the irreversible state”;
q.orig: on the level at which progress has become irreversible

div.p: and then also the six sections teaching that there is more merit from explaining

q.p: “to one”
q.orig: a single bodhisattva great being

div.p:
for the purpose of speedy clairvoyance than the merit from explaining to those who have been established in the irreversible state. khri brgyad
–; ’bum cha 110a6a–112ba2, summarized nyi khri kha -, le’u brgyad ma nga 108b7–109a7. There is then the section where Śatakratu teaches and the section where the elder Subhūti rejoices. khri brgyad
and
.
Those are the subsections of the exposition here.

div.head: Rejoicing and dedication
div.p: Then also in this context of teaching that it The admiration for, rejoicing in, and dedication to the perfection of wisdom in comparison to any other virtuous activity. is greater merit, having taught that merit from rejoicing is highest, to set the scene for the explanation it says,

q.p:
“Then the bodhisattva Maitreya said to the… venerable monk Subhūti,” khri brgyad
, nyi khri . The idea is that there is the thought of awakening (bodhicitta). Then there is rejoicing in the good works motivated by that thought and the wholesome roots planted by those good works, a rejoicing that gives energy to the motivating thought. Then there is the dedication of all the wholesome roots to awakening again—to the mindset the thought of awakening presupposes so that it grows stronger and stronger.
q.orig: Then the bodhisattva great being Maitreya said to the elder Subhūti
Then the bodhisattva great being Maitreya said to the venerable Subhūti

div.p: and so on. The meaning is this:

q.p: “in comparison to the bases of meritorious action arisen from”
q.orig: a foundation of meritorious action originating from

div.p: rejoicing in the giving, morality, and meditation of all beings, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas, the single merit from rejoicing in and dedicating when it is a bodhisattva who has set out to pay attention to not apprehending anything is

q.p: “the highest.”

div.p: Then Maitreya gives the reason for that, saying,

q.p: “Because all the bases of meritorious action arisen from giving,”
q.orig: because the foundation of meritorious action originating from the generosity

div.p: and so on,

q.p: “of those… in the Śrāvaka Vehicle and those… in the Pratyekabuddha Vehicle are made”
q.orig: of those who follow the vehicle of the śrāvakas and of those who follow the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas

div.p: available just

q.p: “for personal disciplining… a bodhisattva’s… is for disciplining all beings.”
q.orig: in order that they themselves might be disciplined…in order that all beings might be disciplined

div.p:
After he says that, the elder Subhūti takes it in his hands and says: khri brgyad
–. If all the wholesome roots of all the buddhas in the ten directions, gathering a retinue of beings, bringing them to maturity, freeing them, and so on; the five aggregates; khri brgyad
: “aggregates of morality, aggregates of meditative stabilization, aggregates of wisdom, aggregates of liberation, and aggregates of knowledge and seeing of liberation.” all the buddhadharmas; the collection K, N. of Dharma teachings; the dharma body that is reached; the wholesome roots of bodhisattvas; and perfect, complete awakening were apprehended and were to come into being, since the wholesome roots from the rejoicing of bodhisattvas has to do with an absence of

q.p: “entities and objective supports,”
q.orig: those objective supports that do not exist and those entities that do not exist
Since nonexistent foundations

div.p:
they would be like the four errors. khri brgyad
.
If anything like those “objective supports” and “entities” existed, in that case, all dharmas—form, feeling, and so on; the thought of awakening, the six perfections, the aggregates, the constituents, the sense bases, and so on; up to

q.p: “the eighteen distinct attributes of a buddha”—
q.orig: the eighteen distinct qualities of the buddhas

div.p: would also exist like them. But if they, like those objective supports and like those entities, were to be nonexistent, in that case they would all be nonexistent. He is asking how, if that is the case, since the objective supports, entities, wholesome roots, rejoicing, and bases of meritorious action would be nonexistent, would dedication be achieved. He is saying that has to be explained.

q.p: “And if, just like it is with the entities and how it is with the objective supports too, awakening is like that; if thought is like that,”
q.orig: And if, just as it is with the entities and how it is with the objective supports too, awakening is like that; if thought is like that;
just as the foundations of meritorious action and their objective referents [are nonexistent], if enlightenment is also similar, and the mind is also similar

div.p: means in that case, just as the entities and objective supports are nonexistent, the thought of awakening and so on would be nonexistent too.

After he says that, the bodhisattva Maitreya says that there is no objection that they fashion causal signs and make the dedication if they are bodhisattvas who are characterized by having a mature knowledge of emptiness, but the objection is properly directed to those bodhisattvas who are immature, not well trained, and new. Those who have a knowledge of emptiness do not fashion causal signs and make the dedication.

q.p:
“Venerable monk Subhūti, if those bodhisattva great beings again and again practice the six perfections,” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: Venerable monk Subhūti,” replied Maitreya, “if those bodhisattva great beings again and again practice the six perfections,
Bodhisattva great beings who practice the six perfections

div.p: and so on, teaches that because they are new they do not have faults like the four errors.
Then,

q.p: “Venerable monk Subhūti, you should not give an exposition of this doctrine… like this in the presence of bodhisattvas who have newly set out in the vehicle,”
q.orig: Blessed Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom that is revealed in this way should not be explained in the presence of a bodhisattva who has newly entered into the vehicle

div.p: and so on, teaches that new bodhisattvas are not receptacles for the explanation of this emptiness. If it is explained to them, because they have a

q.p: “smidgeon of faith,”
q.orig: mere faith

div.p: and so on, it teaches that there is the fault that what they have gotten will be spoiled and what they have not gotten will be spoiled too.

q.p: “The explanation… has to be given in the presence of bodhisattvas irreversible…”—
q.orig: The exposition and explanation have to be given in the presence of bodhisattvas irreversible
be explained and revealed in the presence of bodhisattva great beings who are irreversible

div.p: it is not wrong when it is explained to those who are mature.

Then, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “they will be, venerable monk Subhūti, those whose bases of meritorious action arisen from rejoicing will be dedicated in that way to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening,”
q.orig: bodhisattva great beings should dedicate the foundations of meritorious action, endowed with rejoicing, to unsurpassed, complete enlightenment

div.p: and so on, teaches the ultimate dedication.
Fashioning causal signs and making the dedication is illogical in four ways:

there is no connection between the two—the rejoicing thought and the dedicating thought; there is no connection between apprehending the basis, the wholesome root, and the basis of the meritorious action; there is no connection between the two— the dedication and to what the dedication is being made; and there is no dedication.

q.p: “The thought that does the rejoicing and dedication”
q.orig: the thoughts by which they rejoice and dedicate

div.p: of the wholesome roots to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening

q.p: “is a thought that is extinguished, stopped, nonexistent, and has run out”
q.orig: are extinct, defunct, and nonexistent

div.p: teaches that there is no connection between the two thoughts.

q.p: “And those entities and those objective supports, those wholesome roots, and those bases of meritorious action arisen from rejoicing are extinguished, stopped, nonexistent, and have run out,”
q.orig: these foundations of meritorious action, these objective referents, and these roots of virtuous action are also extinct, defunct, and nonexistent

div.p: and so on, teaches that there are no “entities” and so on.

q.p: “Does thought dedicate thought? If thought were to dedicate thought, there would be no coming together of two thoughts”
q.orig: How can the mind dedicate the mind? If the mind were to dedicate the mind in that manner, there would be two minds that would not meet

div.p: teaches that there is no connection between the two—the dedication and to what the dedication is being made.

q.p: “The intrinsic nature of thought cannot be dedicated”
q.orig: The intrinsic nature of mind cannot be dedicated

div.p: teaches that there is no thought making the dedication. It teaches that thought is a construction because of the nonexistence of its intrinsic nature, and nonexistence cannot make a dedication.

q.p: “When bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom thus know the perfection of wisdom is a nonexistent thing,”
q.orig: When bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom, if they know that the perfection of wisdom is a nonentity

div.p: and so on, teaches that it is characterized as a nonexistent thing.

q.p: “The bodhisattva Maitreya then asked the elder Subhūti, “Venerable monk Subhūti, when bodhisattva great beings who have newly set out in the vehicle,”
q.orig: Blessed Subhūti, if bodhisattva great beings who have newly entered into the vehicle

div.p: and so on. He is asking what the rejoicing and dedication of those who have newly set out are. And with

q.p: “when bodhisattvas… who have newly set out in the vehicle,”
q.orig: when bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom who have newly set out in the vehicle
if those bodhisattva great beings who have newly entered into the vehicle

div.p: and so on, Subhūti teaches Maitreya that they have to do it based on training

q.p:
“by way of not apprehending anything.” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: without apprehending anything

q.p:
“And, having heard about those works of Māra from them, no decrease happens and no increase happens,” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: once they have heard about those deeds of Māra, how those deeds are without decline or increase

div.p: because of the absence of constructing those in thought.

q.p: “Grasp the bodhisattva lineage”—
q.orig: secure the spiritual family of the bodhisattvas

div.p: pay attention to suchness.

Then, having taught one of the many explanations of rejoicing in general, it sets the scene for the ultimate explanation with, khri brgyad
. I have included some words left out of the citation to make it readable in English.

q.p: “Furthermore, Maitreya, bodhisattva great beings who have newly set out in the vehicle should compress together the merit accumulations and the wholesome roots planted by the lord buddhas whose path has come to an end, whose thought constructions and cravings for existence have been cut off,”
q.orig: Moreover, Kauśika, bodhisattva great beings who have newly entered into the vehicle…and by those whose modes of conceptual elaboration have been cut off

div.p: and so on.

Then Maitreya asks khri brgyad
ff. him how do they not go wrong and then the elder Subhūti teaches a section on dedication free of basic immorality, ninefold.
The second section is where it says

q.p: “it is a conforming dedication,”
q.orig: an authentic dedication

div.p: if they contemplate like this: ultimately there is no dedication because thinking about the thought of buddhas and so on, as well as the thought of the dedication,

q.p: “are extinguished”—
q.orig: is extinct

div.p: even awakening is nonexistent, dharmas are empty of an intrinsic nature, and dedication is nonexistent as well.

Then the third is where it says Cf. khri brgyad
. if, having rejoiced in the merits, whatever they may be, of all

q.p: “past, future, and present”

div.p: śrāvakas, bodhisattvas, buddhas, and ordinary beings,

q.p: “they rejoice in them and dedicate them, paying attention to their being”

div.p: extinguished,

q.p: “paying attention to there being no dedication, and paying attention to the”
q.orig: make this dedication, [knowing] that those attributes are extinct

div.p: emptiness of an intrinsic nature,

q.p: “by that dedication they”
q.orig: then they will have dedicated

div.p: dedicate to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening.
Then the fourth is where it says when they

q.p: “are aware that the piling up of”
q.orig: know that their accumulation of

div.p: the merit from dedication is isolated from all dharmas, and all dharmas are isolated from an intrinsic nature, they dedicate with

q.p: “the best, up to the equal to the unequaled dedication.” Cf. nyi khri ; also ’bum cha 132a2.
q.orig: the best, most authentic, supreme, perfect, foremost, most sublime, unsurpassed, and highest rejoicing that is unequaled and equal to the unequaled

div.p: Then the fifth, as before, is where it says that when they rejoice in the wholesome roots and dedicate them, they dedicate while aware that the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, wholesome roots, dedication, awakening, and the thought doing the dedication are the same in their intrinsic nature.

Then the sixth Cf. khri brgyad
–. is where it says that when they fashion a causal sign for the wholesome roots and dedicate them, and, by paying attention to past buddhas as past, fashion a causal sign for them and pay attention to them as an object, it becomes wrong, but when

q.p: “they do not form a knowledge of and do not give validity to those wholesome roots, those accumulations, or those productions of the thought,”
q.orig: they do not form a knowledge of and do not grasp at a causal sign of those lord buddhas, of those wholesome roots, of those accumulations, or of those productions of the thought
do not cognize those lord buddhas, those roots of virtuous action and their accumulations, and those settings of the mind on enlightenment

div.p: they dedicate perfectly.

Then the seventh is the section of the dedication that has not been poisoned. khri brgyad
–. This is where the bodhisattva Maitreya, thinking how is it possible that the two—not fashioning a causal sign and dedication—are not a contradiction, asks the elder Subhūti, who then teaches that it is when the dedication is made by

q.p: “bodhisattvas who are skilled.”
q.orig: bodhisattva great beings have trained in skillful means
Bodhisattva great beings should train in skillful means

div.p: Then the bodhisattva Maitreya teaches that bodhisattvas who want to make a perfect dedication

q.p: “should reflect deeply as follows: … those buddhas, those wholesome roots, those accumulations, and those… thoughts”
q.orig: should reflect deeply as follows: Those physical beings, those wholesome roots, and those accumulations have ceased, but still they conceive of them, having grasped them as causal signs—having grasped those lord buddhas, those wholesome roots, those accumulations, and those productions of the thought
should think as follows: ‘If even this body of mine has ceased, and if even those roots of virtuous action, those accumulations, and those settings of the mind on enlightenment

div.p: do not exist; nevertheless, look how having fashioned causal signs I construct them all in my mind. Tathāgatas do not permit such a dedication where, having fashioned such causal signs, they conceptualize them. It is similar to a delicacy that has been poisoned. So such a dedication should not be made, and training should not be done in that. Therefore, having taken the Buddha alone as authority, they make a dedication, thinking, “I shall dedicate those wholesome roots just as the lord buddhas understand them.”

Then the eighth is where it says khri brgyad
–. dedication while paying attention to all dharmas that do not belong to the three realms and three time periods

q.p: “has not been poisoned.”
q.orig: nonpoisonous

div.p: Dedication other than that

q.p: “has been poisoned.”
q.orig: poisonous

div.p: And then the ninth is where it says

q.p: “I too must dedicate… in this truly dharmic way,”
q.orig: I too must dedicate these wholesome roots to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening in just this truly dharmic way
I too should dedicate them on the basis of this reality

div.p: which is the domain of the transcendental knowledge of the buddhas.

Then the Lord, having rejoiced in many ways in those statements, khri brgyad
. gives a threefold teaching about greatly increasing merit.
The first is

q.p:
“this dedication… without attachment nyi khri ; khri brgyad
“untainted.” creates even more merit than”
q.orig: untainted dedication of the wholesome roots creates even more merit…than
dedicate the roots of virtuous action without attachment would increase manifold to a greater extent

div.p: the merit

q.p: “if all the beings that are in the billionfold world system were to obtain the ten wholesome actions… the concentrations, … the immeasurables, … the absorptions, and… the clairvoyances.”
q.orig: Subhūti, if all the beings that are in the great billionfold world system were to obtain the ten wholesome actions and were to obtain the four concentrations, the four immeasurables, the four formless absorptions, and the five clairvoyances,

if all beings of this great trichiliocosm were to obtain the paths of the ten virtuous actions, and if they were to obtain the four meditative concentrations, the four immeasurable attitudes, the four formless absorptions, and the five extrasensory powers

div.p:
The second khri brgyad
–. is that one has even more than the merit created from having served those beings if they

q.p: “were to become stream enterers,”
q.orig: were to become stream enterers
become those entering the stream

div.p: and so on, up to

q.p: “worthy ones and pratyekabuddhas,”
q.orig: pratyekabuddhas
pratyekabuddhas

div.p: with the four necessities for as long as they live.

And the third khri brgyad
–. is, were all those beings to have become bodhisattvas, just that same one has even more than the masses of merit such as those created by all the beings in the ten directions were they to have served each of them with the four necessities and

q.p: “with all the requirements for happiness… for as many eons as there are sand particles in the Gaṅgā River.”
q.orig: numerous as the grains of sand of the river Gaṅgā, were to serve, respect, honor, and worship a single bodhisattva great being for eons as numerous as the grains of sand of the river Gaṅgā with clothing, alms, bedding, medicines for the treatment of disease, and many resources, venerating them with all sorts of comforts

q.p: “Lord, if that basis of meritorious action had a physical form it would not fit in even as many world systems as there are sand particles in the Gaṅgā River”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, if that foundation of meritorious action were material, it could not be accommodated even in all the world systems, numerous as the grains of sand of the river Gaṅgā

div.p: means all of it would not fit there.

Then there is a section The first section is khri brgyad
–, the second
. on earlier merits being inferior because they have the perception of a causal sign and

q.p: “a perception that apprehends something,”

div.p: and masses of dedication merits being greater than them because they do not exist.

Then there are two sections The first section is khri brgyad
–, the second
. where all the chiefs of the gods and gods living in the desire realm, and all the Brahmās in the higher realms, have worshiped and raised their voices in praise, and then the section teaching that the merit of a single bodhisattva who dedicates while not apprehending anything is much greater than the merit from the dedication by way of apprehending something by

q.p: “all the beings in a billionfold world system”
q.orig: all the beings that are in a great billionfold world system
all the beings of the great trichiliocosm

div.p: who have become bodhisattvas.
The first rejoicing is

q.p:
“without grasping, without rejecting, without falsely projecting, without acquiring, and without apprehending,” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: neither accept nor reject

div.p: which teaches the sameness of those buddhas and those wholesome roots based on the fact that there is no worse or better in suchness. Similarly, because

q.p: “there is no production, cessation, defilement, purification,”
q.orig: there is no production, no cessation, no defilement, no purification
nothing at all that arises, nothing at all that ceases, nothing at all that is afflicted, nothing at all that is purified

div.p: and so on,

q.p:
“I khri brgyad
. The Lord is speaking to Subhūti. also rejoice,”
q.orig: I rejoice
I will rejoice

div.p: just like those buddhas, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and ordinary beings, and the wholesome roots, and the dedicating thought that all abide in suchness.

Then the second is also rejoicing khri brgyad
. while understanding analytically that all dharmas are comparable to

q.p: “liberation,”

div.p: which is to say, all dharmas are the same because they are comparable to that; because all dharmas are isolated from an intrinsic nature, so earlier at the stage of ordinary beings they

q.p: “are not bound, are not freed”;
q.orig: without bondage, without liberation

div.p: because all dharmas that are pure in their basic nature

q.p: “are not defiled”
q.orig: without afflictive mental states

div.p: earlier and

q.p: “are not purified”

div.p: later;
because all dharmas that are primordially calm

q.p: “are not produced”
q.orig: nonarising

div.p: through the power of earlier causes and conditions; because they have no intrinsic nature,

q.p: “do not appear,”
q.orig: unoriginated

div.p: and later

q.p: “do not stop… have not changed places, and have not been destroyed” This follows the order at nyi khri .—
q.orig: nothing has changed places and nothing has been destroyed, so too is the true dharmic nature of dharmas that are not bound, are not freed, are not defiled, and are not purified; so to is the true dharmic nature of dharmas that are not produced, do not appear, and do not stop
and unceasing, the dedication should be made to unsurpassed, complete enlightenment, because there is no change and there is no decay

div.p: thus all dharmas are the same because

q.p: “they are not bound, are not freed, are not defiled, and are not purified, … are not produced, do not appear, and do not stop, have not changed places, and have not been destroyed.”
q.orig: nothing has changed places and nothing has been destroyed, so too is the true dharmic nature of dharmas that are not bound, are not freed, are not defiled, and are not purified; so to is the true dharmic nature of dharmas that are not produced, do not appear, and do not stop

are without attachment, without bondage, without liberation, without fixation, and without afflictive mental states, and the reality in which phenomena are nonarising, uncreated, unoriginated, and unceasing, the dedication should be made to unsurpassed, complete enlightenment, because there is no change and there is no decay

div.p:
Then there is the section khri brgyad
–. teaching that the merit from dedicating the aggregates of morality from

q.p: “practicing the perfections… by way of not apprehending anything”
q.orig: practice the perfection…without apprehending anything

div.p: is greater than merit accumulated from having served all the buddhas in the ten directions with all the requirements for happiness and by practicing the six perfections together with apprehending something.
These are the sections of the text on rejoicing.

div.head: Wheel of the Dharma and the perfection of wisdom
div.p:
Then Śāriputra, feeling faith after having heard about the vast merit from rejoicing in, and dedication of, such worship and reciting of the perfection of wisdom, and from giving and so on, begins with seventeen statements khri brgyad
. The perfection of wisdom (1) makes things clear because of absolute purity; (2) makes you want to bow; (3) is bowed to by me (Subhūti and the Buddha); (4) is untainted by all three realms; (5) corrects visual distortions because of having eliminated all the darkness of afflictive emotion and views; (6) works as the highest of the dharmas on the side of awakening; (7) provides security because of having eliminated all hazards, terrors, and persecution; (8) gives light because then all beings easily appropriate the five eyes; (9) shows the ruts because beings caught in the ruts avoid the two edges; (10) works as the knowledge of all aspects because of having eliminated all residual impressions, connections, and afflictions; (11) is the mother of great bodhisattvas because she gives birth to all the buddhadharmas; (12) is unproduced and unceasing because of being empty of her own mark; (13) counteracts saṃsāra because she is not unmoved and not destroyed; (14) works as the protector of all unprotected beings because she is the giver of all dharma jewels; (15) works as the ten powers because she deals with those who are untamed; (16) works as repeating and thus turning the wheel of the Dharma; and (17) works to show the intrinsic nature of all dharmas because of the emptiness of the nonexistence of intrinsic nature. in praise of this perfection of wisdom, to generate faith in others in the retinue.

q.p: “Turning the wheel of the Dharma that has twelve aspects three times”—
q.orig: turns the wheel of the Dharma, repeating it three times and in twelve ways

div.p: the Lord turned “the wheel of the Dharma” of the four truths “that has twelve aspects three times.” There he turns it three times: One is: “These are the four truths.” It is the part of the speech stating the intrinsic nature of the four truths. The second turning is the part of the speech stating that just those four truths have to be comprehended, eliminated, realized, and cultivated. The third turning is the part of the speech stating that “I have comprehended, eliminated, realized, and cultivated” just those four truths. Those are the turning three times.

For the truth of suffering there are three aspects: the intrinsic nature of suffering, that it has to be comprehended, and that “I have comprehended.” For the truth of origination there are three aspects: the intrinsic nature of origination, that it has to be eliminated, and that “I have eliminated it.” For the truth of cessation there are three aspects: the intrinsic nature of cessation, that it has to be realized, and that “I have realized it.” And for the truth of the path there are three aspects: the intrinsic nature of the path, that it has to be cultivated, and that “I have cultivated it.” Thus, there are twelve aspects.

q.p: “Lord, how does one stand in the perfection of wisdom?” This question by Śāriputra comes at the end of his seventeen statements praising the perfection of wisdom.
q.orig: Blessed Lord, how can bodhisattvas or those in the vehicle of the bodhisattvas, śrāvakas or those in the vehicle of the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas or those in the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas dwell in the perfection of wisdom

div.p:
Śatakratu has already asked earlier khri brgyad
ff. about the way to stand in the perfection of wisdom, and it has already been explained, so this is not a question about the way to stand in the perfection of wisdom. Here “how does one stand” means this: how, by respecting and serving it, does one stand? ’jar is apparently a form of the modern colloquial honorific gcar, “to approach,” with honor to the place or person being approached. Bṭ1 pa 28a6–7 gus shing rim gro bya ba’i thabs ji lta bur bgyi, “how do you feel respect for and serve.”

q.p: “The perfection of wisdom is itself the Teacher and the Teacher is himself the perfection of wisdom.”
q.orig: The perfection of wisdom is itself the Teacher and the Teacher is himself the perfection of wisdom,
the Teacher himself is indeed the perfection of wisdom and the nature of the perfection of wisdom is indeed the Teacher

div.p: Because it does the work of the Buddha it is envisioned and taught to be not different.
Śatakratu wonders,

q.p: “What occasioned this inquiry by the venerable monk Śāriputra? What was the catalyst?”
q.orig: What is the basis of this question that the venerable Śāradvatīputra has asked? What is the reason for it

div.p: because he is not satisfied with just those reasons Śāriputra has given. So then Śāriputra says

q.p: “assisted by the perfection of wisdom”
q.orig: acquired the perfection of wisdom

div.p: and so on. It teaches that this perfection of wisdom is principal. It teaches that even though all the perfections other than that are causes of unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening, they are governed by it, so it should be greatly respected.

q.p: “Dedicate”
q.orig: dedicated

div.p:
them all khri brgyad
: “dedicate those wholesome roots of the past, future, and present lord buddhas, as many as there are, starting from when they first produced the thought, up to for as long as their good Dharma lasts…”

q.p: “to the knowledge of all aspects”

div.p: by rejoicing in them.

q.p:
“When the five perfections are assisted by the perfection of giving, they do not get the name perfection.” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: When the five perfections are assisted by the perfection of giving, they do not get the name perfection.
These five perfections are not designated as perfections because they are acquired by means of the perfection of generosity

div.p: It says this because it taught earlier that all six are lodged one in the other and work as a single cause.

q.p: “It is not so, Kauśika, it is not so”
q.orig: Kauśika,” he replied, “that is not so! That is not so

div.p: is teaching that when you complete one of the six perfections, all six are completed, so they are reciprocally one and just simply one cause, but, unlike the perfection of wisdom that is the nature of them all, they are not therefore the cause in all respects.

q.p: “Lord, how should [they]… find and produce within themselves the perfection of wisdom?” khri brgyad (kha 54a2) “find and produce within themselves” renders mngon par sgrub (abhinirhṛ); LSPW “consummate.”
q.orig: Lord, how should bodhisattva great beings find and produce within themselves the perfection of wisdom?
Blessed Lord, how should the perfection of wisdom be brought into being

div.p: Here too it is not asking how they find and produce the perfection of wisdom within themselves, it is asking what the result of finding and producing the perfection of wisdom within themselves is.

q.p: “So they do not find and produce within themselves form”
q.orig: so that there is no bringing into being of physical forms

div.p: means: so form is a nonexistent thing.

q.p:
“Lord, how do they find and produce within themselves the perfection of wisdom so that they do not find and produce within themselves form?” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: Lord, how do they find and produce within themselves the perfection of wisdom so that they do not find and produce within themselves form?
Blessed Lord, how is the perfection of wisdom to be brought into being…so that there is no bringing into being of physical forms

div.p: This is the second question Śāriputra asks the Lord. It means: in what form within themselves should the perfection of wisdom be found and produced so that the nonexistence of form and so on is feasible?

q.p: “Śāriputra, they should find and produce within themselves the perfection of wisdom as the nonenactment, the nonproduction, the noncessation, the nonappearance, the nondestruction, and the nonapprehension of form.”
q.orig: “Śāriputra,” replied the Lord, “they should find and produce within themselves the perfection of wisdom as the nonenactment, the nonproduction, the noncessation, the nonappearance, the nondestruction, and the nonapprehension of form.”

The perfection of wisdom should be brought into being by physical forms not being conditioned, by physical forms not arising, by physical forms not ceasing, by physical forms not being apprehensible, and by physical forms not disintegrating

div.p: In the context of a thoroughly established phenomenon there is no “enactment” of falsely imagined form. There is neither “production nor cessation” from the perspective of a continuum. In each instant there is neither “appearance nor nondestruction.” And there is no “apprehension” because in all respects there is no production. It

q.p: “does not cause any dharma to be gained.”
q.orig: in that manner attains nothing at all

div.p: At that time there are not any dharmas at all.

q.p: “It is counted as the perfection of wisdom.”
q.orig: is counted the perfection of wisdom.
it may be styled ‘the perfection of wisdom

div.p: The nonconceptual effortless wisdom that has gone to the other side of the nonexistence of all dharmas is the “perfection of wisdom.”

q.p:
“The perfection of wisdom… does not cause even the knowledge of all aspects to be gained. It does not apprehend it.” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: This perfection of wisdom does not attain and does not apprehend even all-aspect omniscience

div.p:
In the context of the dharma body, just that is the perfection of wisdom, just that is the knowledge of all aspects. It does not apprehend that “the knowledge of all aspects is one thing and the perfection of wisdom another.” khri brgyad
: “Those sons of a good family or daughters of a good family who take up, up to properly pay attention to this perfection of wisdom will have attended on many buddhas and will have been looked after by spiritual friends. And why? Because the knowledge of all aspects issues forth from this—that is, the perfection of wisdom—and the perfection of wisdom issues forth from this, that is, the knowledge of all aspects. And why? Because the knowledge of all aspects is not one thing and the perfection of wisdom another. Therefore, the knowledge of all aspects and the perfection of wisdom are not two and cannot be divided into two; they have not been broken apart and have not been cut apart.”

q.p: “Kauśika… it is because the perfection of wisdom does not cause it to be gained as a name, as a causal sign, or as something to be enacted.”
q.orig: Kauśika,” replied the Blessed One, “the perfection of wisdom, just as if it were a designation, a distinguishing mark, or a conditioning

div.p: The true nature of dharmas is nonconceptual. The perfection of wisdom does not grasp any dharma at all through a name, causal sign, or enactment, so the knowledge of all aspects cannot be apprehended through that name, that causal sign, or that enactment.

q.p: “Well then, Lord, how does this perfection of wisdom cause it to be gained?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, how then does it bring about attainment

div.p: Insofar as the perfection of wisdom does cause the knowledge of all aspects to be gained conventionally, how does it cause it to be gained?

q.p: “The perfection of wisdom causes it to be gained without apprehending, without asserting, without being stationed on, without forsaking, without settling down on, without grasping, and without rejecting anything at all, but it does not cause any dharma to be gained.”
q.orig: It brings about attainment insofar as it does not apprehend, accept, dwell in, abandon, or adhere to anything…Nothing at all is attained. Kauśika, so it is that the perfection of wisdom does not attain any phenomena

div.p: When apprehended and apprehender have become the same thing in the same form, this wisdom does not “apprehend” that this is a dharma I have to grasp; does not “assert” that I myself am the grasper; does not see, as does the eye and so on, as something “stationed”; does not see any defiling conceptualization that has to be “forsaken”; does not “settle down” even slightly on “this is true” as being in the nature of truth; and does not “grasp or reject” because it does not see what is grasped and has to be joined with in the form of bright and dark sides. At that time, because it itself is the entity of the knowledge of all aspects, it is also said that “it causes the knowledge of all aspects to be gained.”

q.p:
“It is amazing, Lord, … this perfection of wisdom…” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: Blessed Lord, how wonderful that this perfection of wisdom

div.p: Because all dharmas do not exist, they are not produced, do not cease, do not occasion anything, are not apprehended, and are not destroyed in that context, it is explained with the names

q.p: “nonproduction”
q.orig: neither arise

div.p: and so on.
It says if they

q.p: “have such ideas as ‘the perfection of wisdom causes all dharmas to be gained’ or ‘the perfection of wisdom does not cause all dharmas to be gained,’… the perfection of wisdom is forsaken,”
q.orig: wonder whether the perfection of wisdom brings about the attainment of all phenomena, but perceive to the contrary that the perfection of wisdom does not bring about the attainment of all phenomena, in that case, Blessed Lord, those bodhisattvas would undervalue the perfection of wisdom

div.p: because both an existent thing and a nonexistent thing are thought constructions.

q.p:
“I do not have confidence in form.” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: I do not have confidence in form
one will not have conviction in physical forms

div.p: This means the Lord has confidence in and comprehends form that is marked as a nonexistent thing. Construe the others similarly.

q.p:
“Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom gives me confidence because form cannot be apprehended,” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom gives me confidence because form cannot be apprehended.
Subhūti,” replied the Blessed One, “they will have conviction in the perfection of wisdom because physical forms are nonapprehensible

div.p: and so on, means that having comprehended all dharmas, form and so on, as the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature, the Lord has “confidence in”—that is, has a directly realization of—the perfection of wisdom.

q.p:
“Does not make form bigger nor does not make it smaller” khri brgyad
—
q.orig: does not enhance physical forms, nor does it diminish them

div.p: it The perfection of wisdom. does not make the form of the true nature of dharmas that is thoroughly established bigger and it does not make falsely imagined form smaller. Construe them all similarly.

q.p:
“Those bodhisattva great beings with such notions, Lord, are not practicing the the perfection of wisdom.” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: those bodhisattva great beings with such notions, Lord, are not practicing the perfection of wisdom.
Blessed Lord, those bodhisattva great beings who perceive in such a way do not practice the perfection of wisdom

div.p: Were this perfection of wisdom to do anything, in that case it might be right to say ‘this perfection of wisdom does not do anything,’ but because this perfection of wisdom is beyond every false imagination it does not do anything at all. Therefore it is not right to say that “the perfection of wisdom does not make form bigger and does not make form smaller” and so on.

q.p:
“Lord… because… they are not in harmony with the perfection of wisdom as cause” khri brgyad
. ’bum cha 239b4, nyi khri (kha 168a1), le’u brgyad ma nga 134a1 render niṣyanda by dang mthun pa’i ’bras bu, “not a result in accord with the perfection of wisdom.”
q.orig: is not in harmony with the perfection of wisdom as cause
is not an outcome compatible with the perfection of wisdom

div.p: means that because all dharmas remain in their intrinsic nature, in their own basic nature as it really is, there is nothing there in harmony with the perfection of wisdom as cause.
Now it again teaches that even the perfection of wisdom is like form and so on, in twelve rounds of teaching beginning with

q.p: “because beings are not produced.”
q.orig: Owing to the fact that beings are nonarising

div.p: You should view the perfection of wisdom as marked by nonproduction because a being is marked by not arising.
There, “because beings are not produced,” up to

q.p: “because one who sees is not produced,” Our author’s version of the Sūtra has the synonyms of “a being” at this point. Other versions omit.

div.p: intends the selflessness of persons. From

q.p: “because form is not produced, up to… because a buddha is not produced,”
q.orig: because[2]…is not produced, up to you should know that the nonproduction of the perfection of wisdom is because a buddha is not produced.

Owing to the fact that physical forms are nonarising…you should see that the perfection of wisdom is nonarising. Owing to the fact that feelings, perceptions, formative predispositions, and consciousness are nonarising, and that [all those other phenomena, attributes, and attainments], up to and including enlightenment, buddhas, and the attributes of the buddhas, are nonarising

div.p: intends the selflessness of dharmas.

q.p:
“There is no full awakening” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: does not attain consummate buddhahood

div.p: of form and so on. There is no realization of them.

q.p: “Because beings are not endowed with the powers,”
q.orig: Owing to the fact that beings are not endowed with the consummate powers

div.p: they are weak or do not have the power of wisdom.

div.head: Not bound and not freed

q.p:
“Because dharmas are in an inanimate material state” khri brgyad
ff. This is misplaced here, probably early in the transmission of the text by a scribe. It should come after the following summary, not before it.
q.orig: Owing to the inanimate nature of phenomena

div.p: means because all dharmas are the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature.

The elder Śāriputra, khri brgyad
–. having heard that this perfection is thus in its nature big and vast, feels faith, and for the bodhisattvas poses four questions about the death and birth of bodhisattvas, the amount of time since they have set out, the number of tathāgatas they have attended on, and the amount of time they have been practitioners of the perfections. That same part of the text sets the scene for an account of what happens to those forsaking the good Dharma, and that same part of the text also sets the scene for it being

q.p:
“hard… to believe in this perfection of wisdom.” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: It is difficult for those who lack perseverance, who are without the roots of virtuous action, and who have fallen into in the clutches of evil associates to have devotion to this profound perfection of wisdom

div.p: Then, because it has taught it is hard to believe in, Subhūti asks the question,

q.p: “Just how deep, Lord, is this perfection of wisdom in which it is so hard for them to believe?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, how profound is that perfection of wisdom, for which it is difficult to have devotion in that manner

div.p: The Lord explains that it

q.p: “is not bound and it is not freed,”
q.orig: is not bound and is not freed
are neither fettered nor liberated

div.p: explains about

q.p: “purity,”

div.p: explains about

q.p: “the unlimited,”
q.orig: unlimited
the limitlessness

div.p: and explains about

q.p: “those who are attached and not attached.”
q.orig: they are neither attached nor unattached

div.p: Thus, it sets the scene for a fourfold explanation.
Among these,

q.p:
“Subhūti… form is not bound and it is not freed.” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: “Subhūti,” said the Lord, “form is not bound and is not freed.
Subhūti,” replied the Blessed One, “physical forms are neither fettered nor liberated

div.p: During the period of the cycle of existences, that which is the appearance of the thoroughly established true dharmic nature of form “is not bound,” because, for the entire duration it is not bound by all the bonds of affliction, karma, and maturation, and later during the period of the thoroughly established phenomenon it “is not freed” because freedom does not exist, so being “bound and freed” is said of just a falsely imagined state, not of the true dharmic nature of form that, like space, is not tainted by anything at all. Therefore, it says

q.p: “because the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature in form is form.”
q.orig: Because the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature in form is form
in physical forms the absence of inherent existence is still physical forms

div.p: This means falsely imagined form, the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature, is the true dharmic nature of form. You should construe all dharmas, up to the knowledge of all aspects, like this as well.
Again, to elucidate just that, that it is not bound and is not freed, there is an explanation in tandem with the three time periods:

q.p:
“Subhūti, the prior limit of form is not bound and is not freed.” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: Subhūti, the prior limit of form is not bound and is not freed.
the past limits of physical forms are neither fettered nor liberated

div.p: The “prior limit” is the true dharmic nature of form in the cycle of existences during the period when there are stains and impurity. The

q.p: “present”

div.p: describes the present period during which there is purity and impurity.

q.p: “The later limit”
q.orig: future limits

div.p: describes the future period when there is purity.

q.p: “Because the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature in the prior limit is form”
q.orig: Because the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature in the prior limit is…form
the inherent existence of their past limits, though without entity, is still physical forms

div.p: teaches that what is marked as abiding without change in all three time periods is suchness, indicating that the true nature of dharmas does not have the mark of being freed over time.

div.head: Purity
div.p: Having thus taught, through the explanation of not being bound and not being freed, that saṃsāra and nirvāṇa are nonexistent things, again, to teach that defilement and purification do not exist it begins the explanation of purity with

q.p:
“that purity of form is the purity of the result.” khri brgyad
ff., nyi khri
ff., ’bum cha 345b1 ff.
q.orig: that purity of[1]…result[1]
the purity of physical forms is the purity of fruition

div.p: There the dharmas from form, up to, finally, the knowledge of all aspects, have no bonds so there is no defilement. Because there is no defilement they are pure in their intrinsic nature, and because they are pure in their intrinsic nature there are no purification dharmas either. Ultimately purification dharmas do not do anything at all to natural purity. So, even though defilement and purification are impossible, foolish beings construct them. They are not thoroughly established.

Thus, having taught in one way that it is hard to believe, khri brgyad
: “Subhūti, it is hard for those who do not work hard, up to are without introspection to believe in this perfection of wisdom.” it again teaches it is hard to believe because of purity. There, “just that purity of form is the purity of the result” means there is nothing other than purity that results from the purification dharmas—the perfections, the dharmas on the side of awakening, and so on. The true dharmic nature of form, the constantly abiding purity in the form of the thoroughly established nature, just that is purity in the form of the result.
You should construe all the dharmas like this as well.
Having thus taught the intrinsic nature of purity, then it teaches that the purity of all dharmas is also one, not broken apart:

q.p: “That purity of form is the purity of the result. That purity of the result is the purity of the perfection of wisdom. That purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of form.”
q.orig: that purity of form is the purity of the result. That purity of the result is the purity of the perfection of wisdom. That purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of form.
The purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of physical forms

div.p: There, the true dharmic nature of the form state is called “the purity of form.” The very limit of reality called the “nirvāṇa” state is called “the purity of the result.” The dharma body state is called “the purity of the perfection of wisdom.” The meaning there is that the suchness that is the purity of form is the purity of the result, that is, is freed; just that freedom is the purity of the perfection of wisdom, that is, is the dharma body; and just that dharma body is the purity of form, that is, is suchness. Hence suchness, freedom, and the dharma body are ultimately not broken apart.
You should construe up to the purity of the knowledge of all aspects like this as well.

Summing up in conclusion it teaches that the purity of all dharmas is one. Therefore, those purities from the purity of form, the purity of the result, and the purity of the perfection of wisdom, up to the knowledge of all aspects, are

q.p: “not two, not divided, not separate, and not broken apart.” ’bum cha 348b3 so so ma yin, also nyi khri (kha 182a2); khri brgyad (kha 64b5–6), S kha 147b1 tha mi dad de gcad du med.
q.orig: are not two, are not divided, are not broken apart, and are not cut apart.
are not two things, they cannot be divided into two, and they cannot be differentiated or distinguished

div.p: They are “not two” because they are the same; they are “not divided” because you cannot divide them into different things; they are “not separate” because a particular one does not exist; they are “not broken apart” because nothing obstructs them, or, because they are constant.

Thus, it has taught the purity of the result shared in common with śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas. Now, to teach the uncommon purity of bodhisattvas it leaves out the result, and it teaches having taken up only the purity of the perfection of wisdom. khri brgyad
ff., ’bum cha 348a2 ff., nyi khri
ff.

Thus, these two passages The two passages (khri brgyad
–, ’bum cha 345b1–259b3, nyi khri -) are the one that includes the purity of the result and the one that leaves it out. teach that the purity of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and the purity of the tathāgata, are “one.”

Now it teaches the purity in a sequence of three connected sections: the purity that is the nonexistence of a self of persons, khri brgyad
, nyi khri -. The passage is truly spelled out in full from ’bum cha 259b3 to ’bum ja 208a7! the purity that is the nonexistence of secondary afflictions, khri brgyad
, nyi khri -, ’bum ja 208a7–265a3. and the purity that is the nonexistence of a self in dharmas.

q.p: “Because of the purity of self, there is the purity of form.”
q.orig: that purity of self is the purity of…form
the purity of the self is the purity of physical forms

div.p: The knowledge that a self is a nonexistent thing is the purity of self. There it should be taught in the order of the sections of the text. It teaches that

q.p: “because of the purity of self, there is the purity of form.”
q.orig: that purity of self is the purity of…form
the purity of the self is the purity of physical forms

div.p: Because of the purity of form there is the purity of self. Thus, this purity of self and purity of form are not two, are not divided, are not separate, and are not broken apart.
Similarly,

q.p: “because of the purity of self, there is the purity of feeling… perception… volitional factors… and consciousness. Because of the purity of consciousness, there is the purity of self,”
q.orig: The purity of the self is the purity of feelings, perceptions, formative predispositions, and consciousness. The purity of consciousness [and so forth] is the purity of the self

div.p: and so on, and that

q.p: “the purity of self and purity of”
q.orig: The purity of the self is the purity of[2]

div.p: all dharmas, up to, finally,

q.p: “the purity of the knowledge of all aspects”
q.orig: The purity of all-aspect omniscience

div.p: is not two.
Then, in the section on the purity that is the nonexistence of secondary afflictions,

q.p: “because of the purity of greed there is the purity of form; because of the purity of form there is the purity of greed. Thus, this purity of greed and the purity of form is not two,”
q.orig: because of the purity of greed there is the purity of form, the purity of . . . up to the knowledge of all aspects. Thus, this purity of greed, purity of form, purity of . . . up to the knowledge of all aspects is not two, is not divided, is not broken apart, and is not cut apart. Similarly, because of the purity of hatred and confusion there is the purity of form, the purity of . . . up to the knowledge of all aspects. Thus, this purity of hatred and confusion, purity of form, purity of . . . up to the knowledge of all aspects is not two,
physical forms are pure owing to the purity of…is pure owing to the purity of physical forms. So it is that the purity of…and this purity of physical forms are not two things

div.p: and so on, again explains that the purity of dharmas, up to, finally, the knowledge of all aspects, and the purity of greed

q.p: “is not two.”
q.orig: not two things

div.p: Similarly connect this with

q.p: “hatred, and confusion.”
q.orig: hatred

div.p: Then, in the section on the purity that is the nonexistence of a self of dharmas, having taken up the purity of dharmas, the dependent originations, and so on, up to, finally, the knowledge of all aspects, there is the section explaining that the purity of two dharmas is not two:

q.p:
“Because of the purity of ignorance there is the purity of volitional factors; because of the purity of volitional factors there is the purity of ignorance. Thus, this purity of ignorance and the purity of volitional factors is not two,” nyi khri , ’bum ja 265a3–4; cf. khri brgyad
ff.
q.orig: because of the purity of ignorance there is the purity of volitional factors;

formative predispositions are pure owing to the purity of ignorance, and ignorance is pure owing to the purity of formative predispositions. So it is that the purity of ignorance and this purity of formative predispositions are not two things

div.p: and so on. So too with the perfections as well, it says,

q.p: “Because of the purity of the perfection of giving there is the purity of the perfection of morality; because of the purity of the perfection of morality there is the purity of the perfection of giving. Thus, this purity of the perfection of giving and the purity of the perfection of morality is not two,” Closest is nyi khri . Our author’s version differs slightly. Cf. khri brgyad , ’bum ja 266a–b5.
q.orig: because of the purity of the perfection of giving there is the purity of the perfection of morality

The perfection of generosity is pure owing to the purity of the perfection of ethical discipline. [And in reverse], the perfection of ethical discipline is pure owing to the purity of the perfection of generosity [and so forth]. So it is that the purity of the perfection of generosity [and so forth] and this purity of the perfection of ethical discipline [and so forth] are not two things

div.p: and so on. All have to be construed in the same way as well. Thus, you should construe

q.p:
“because of the purity of the knowledge of the path aspects there is the purity of the knowledge of all aspects, because of the purity of the knowledge of all aspects there is the purity of the knowledge of all path aspects. Thus, this purity of the knowledge of the path aspects and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects is not two,” This citation suggests our author is following a version giving even more detail. Cf. nyi khri , and ’bum ja 271a5–7, where the purity of each earlier dharma is the reason for the purity of the next in the series, ending with the purity of the knowledge of the path aspects being the reason for the purity of the knowledge of all aspects. khri brgyad
is an abbreviation.
q.orig: All-aspect omniscience is pure owing to the purity of knowledge of the path. [And in reverse], knowledge of the path is pure owing to the purity of all-aspect omniscience. So it is that the purity of knowledge of the path and this purity of all-aspect omniscience are not two things

div.p: and so on.

Then, also in the section gathering the purity of all dharmas together, first, having taken up among the six perfections the purity of the perfection of wisdom, and the purity of the aggregates and so on, up to, finally, the six collections of feelings, The collections are the collecting together of a form, the eyes, eye consciousness, eye contact, and pleasurable, suffering, and neither pleasurable nor suffering feelings that arise from the condition of contact with the eyes and so on. and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects, there is the section teaching that it is not two:

q.p:
“Furthermore, Subhūti, that purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of form. That purity of form is the purity of the knowledge of all aspects. Thus, this purity of the perfection of wisdom, purity of form, and purity of the knowledge of all aspects is not two, not divided, not separate, and not broken apart.” Cf. nyi khri , ’bum ja 271a7–b2. khri brgyad
is an abbreviation.
q.orig: Furthermore, Subhūti, that purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of form. That purity of form is the purity of…the knowledge of all aspects is not two, is not divided, is not broken apart, and is not cut apart.

Moreover, Subhūti, physical forms are pure owing to the purity of the perfection of wisdom. [All phenomena, attributes, and attainments], up to and including all-aspect omniscience, are pure owing to the purity of physical forms. So it is that the purity of the perfection of wisdom, the purity of physical forms, and this purity [of all phenomena, attributes, and attainments], up to and including all-aspect omniscience, are not two things, they cannot be divided into two, and they cannot be differentiated or distinguished

div.p: Similarly connect this with

q.p: “feeling, perception, volitional factors, and consciousness,”
q.orig: Feelings, perceptions, formative predispositions, and consciousness

div.p: up to

q.p:
“that purity of the perfection of wisdom is the purity of the feeling that arises from the condition of contact with the thinking mind. The purity of the feeling that arises from the condition of contact with the thinking mind is the purity of the knowledge of all aspects. Thus, this purity of the perfection of wisdom, purity of the feeling that arises from the condition of contact with the thinking mind, and purity of the knowledge of all aspects is not two,” Cf. nyi khri ,
, and ’bum nya 101a5–7.
q.orig: feelings conditioned by mentally compounded sensory contact, are pure owing to the purity of all-aspect omniscience. The perfection of wisdom is pure owing to the purity of feelings conditioned by mentally compounded sensory contact [and so forth]. So it is that the purity of all-aspect omniscience, the purity of feelings conditioned by mentally compounded sensory contact [and so forth], and this purity of the perfection of wisdom are not two things

div.p:
and so on. Then also, ’bum nya 101a7–121a7; cf. khri brgyad
. The operative factor is the similarity with the purity of the knowledge of all aspects. having taken up the purity of the dharmas—from the perfection of concentration up to the aggregates and so on, and finally the feelings—and

q.p: “the purity of the knowledge of all aspects,”
q.orig: the purity of all-aspect omniscience

div.p: it teaches that it is not two; and similarly it teaches that the purity of the dharmas—all the perfections, all the emptinesses, up to, finally, the feelings—and

q.p: “the purity of the knowledge of all aspects is not two”;
q.orig: are not two things

div.p: and, similarly, it explains that (1) the purity of the dharmas, the applications of mindfulness, and so on, up to, finally, all-knowledge; and (2) the purity of the dharmas form and so on, up to, finally, the six collections of feelings; and (3) the purity of the knowledge of all aspects is one.
Then it teaches the section on

q.p: “the purity of the compounded”
q.orig: the purity of conditioned phenomena

div.p: and

q.p: “the uncompounded,”
q.orig: unconditioned phenomena[3]

div.p:
and the section on the purity of the three time periods. khri brgyad
–, ’bum nya 121a7–122b4.

The elder Śāriputra, having listened to the exposition of purity up to here, because a retinue is gathered together, musters the confidence to speak and says, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “Lord, this purity is deep,”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, this purity is profound

div.p: and so on. With this begins a sequence of thirteen statements about purity.

q.p: “Śāriputra, it is deep because it is extremely pure”
q.orig: It is deep, Śāriputra, because it is extremely pure
That is due to absolute purity

div.p: says that the true nature of dharmas that is not broken apart from those saṃsāric dharmas, composed of the stains of the many afflictions, secondary afflictions, and conceptualizations, does not become stained by those stains. It is extremely pure at all times, so it is hard for fools to feel confidence in it. Hence it is called “deep because it is extremely pure.”

q.p: “Śāriputra, purity is light because it is extremely pure,”
q.orig: Purity is light, Śāriputra, because it is extremely pure,
That is due to absolute purity

div.p: To illustrate, the sun and moon and so on are extremely pure, that is, they shine brightly where there are no clouds, fog, haze and so on. Similarly, the true dharmic nature of form and so on is called “light because it is extremely pure,” so it says “purity is light because form is extremely pure.” purity is light because form is extremely pure

q.p: “Lord, purity does not link up.”
q.orig: Purity is not having rebirth

div.p: Because the stains of the proliferation of afflictions and conceptualizations have stopped there is no further linking up, so, because it is stainless and pure, it is said that it “does not link up.”

q.p: “Śāriputra, form does not link up because it does not change places, so it is pure” In the cyclic of existences, a stream of deaths and rebirths, death both precedes rebirth, and follows it.
q.orig: “Śāriputra,” replied the Lord, “form does not link up because it does not change places, so it is pure,
Śāradvatīputra,” replied the Blessed One, “due to physical forms not passing away and not having rebirth this is purity

div.p: means because falsely imagined form and so on that have been abandoned do not change places again, they have stopped.

q.p: “Lord, purity is without defilement”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, purity is not having affliction

div.p: is saying that even though there have been clouds, fog, haze and so on, like space, in its basic nature it is thoroughly clean.

q.p: “Lord, there is no obtaining and no clear realization of purity.”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, purity is neither attained nor is it manifestly realized

div.p: Were the two dharmas—something obtained and a cause of obtaining—to exist, there would be an “obtaining”; were the two dharmas—something clearly realized and a cause of clear realization—to exist, there would be a “clear realization.” But because the mere nonexistence of false imagining and conceptualizing is posited as the “purity” that is the thoroughly established true nature of dharmas, “obtaining” and “clear realization” do not exist in that purity at all.

q.p: “Lord, purity does not come into being.”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, purity has not been brought into being

div.p: “Purity” is posited as the dharmas, falsely imagined and conceptualized form and so on, not coming into being, so it is “marked by not coming into being.”

q.p: “Lord, purity does not arise in the desire realm… the form realm… [or] the formless realm.”
q.orig: Lord, purity does not arise in the desire realm,
Blessed Lord, purity is not subject to rebirth in the realm of desire

div.p: The desire, form, and formless realms are falsely imagined. When not arising and appearing in them it is called “purity,” so it says

q.p: “because you cannot apprehend the desire realm’s intrinsic nature.”
q.orig: because the realm of desire is naturally nonapprehensible

q.p: “Lord, purity does not know”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, purity is not cognizant

div.p: means the self is not the intrinsic nature self-awareness.

q.p: “Because dharmas are inanimate material”—
q.orig: due to the inanimate nature of phenomena

div.p: it is saying “dharmas are inanimate material” because they are free from conceptual consciousness.

q.p: “Lord, purity does not know form.”
q.orig: Lord, purity does not know form,
Blessed Lord, purity is not cognizant of physical forms

div.p: This means it also does not see all dharmas, form and so on.

q.p: “Because it is empty of its own mark”
q.orig: owing to the emptiness of intrinsic defining characteristics

div.p: means things like form and so on are without defining marks. This “does not know” teaches that purity is the mark of the absence of conceptualization. This “purity does not know form” teaches that dharmas are the mark of nonexistence. The two teach the mark of the nonexistence of apprehended object and apprehending subject.

q.p: “Lord, the perfection of wisdom does not help nor does it hinder the knowledge of all aspects,”
q.orig: Blessed Lord! The perfection of wisdom neither helps nor hinders all-aspect omniscience

div.p: because both, marked by suchness, are

q.p: “extremely pure.”
q.orig: absolute purity

div.p: Suchness does not help and does not hinder suchness, just like space does not help and does not hinder space. Therefore, it says

q.p: “because of the establishment of the dharma-constituent.” nyi khri (kha 192a3–4); ’bum nya 151b7, and khri brgyad (kha 69b1) have chos kyi dbyings gnas pa nyid (*dharma­dhātu­sthititā). PSP 2-3: 1562 dharmasthititā, le’u brgyad ma nga 147b2 ch[o]s gnas pa nyid.
q.orig: owing to the presence of reality’s expanse

div.p: This is teaching that nobody helps or hinders the dharma body, given that at all times it is marked by staying in the same state.

q.p: “Lord, the purity that is the perfection of wisdom does not assist any dharma,”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, the purity of the perfection of wisdom does not appropriate anything at all

div.p: because the extremely pure perfection of wisdom is the mark of not taking hold of anything. Were it to take hold of any dharma it would not be pure. “Assist” renders yongs su ’dzin (parigrah), “take hold of.” Cf. Aṣṭa (Wogihara p. 411) prajñāpāramitā na kaṃcid dharmaṃ na parigṛhṇāti na parityajati, glossed by Haribhara (Sparham 2006–11, vol. 2, p. 287) with pratipakṣa (“antidote”) and vipakṣa (“opposing side”) (the words in single quotation marks are words from the Eight Thousand): “ ‘neither gains’ an antidote that counteracts ‘nor abandons’ an opposing side ‘any dharma.’ ” Bṭ1 pa 44a3–7 says help and harm is irrelevant to the dharma-constituent, which has an unchangeable nature and is intrinsically complete. It says “the ultimate, nonconceptual perfection of wisdom is not an existent thing and is purity, therefore it does not conceive of any dharma at all and is not in its intrinsic nature something that apprehends a causal sign.” LSPW p. 282: “How is it that the purity of the perfection of wisdom does not take hold of any dharma? The Lord: Because the Dharma-element has been taken hold of.”

Then the statements by the elder Subhūti, khri brgyad
ff.

q.p: “Lord, form is pure because self is pure”
q.orig: “Lord[2]…is pure because self is pure
Blessed Lord, the purity of physical forms is due to the purity of the self

div.p: and so on, mean that because the self is something that is nonexistent, form and so on are things that do not exist either, because here you have to take “purity” as something that does not exist. Hence, it says

q.p: “because it is extremely pure, Subhūti.”
q.orig: Because it is extremely pure, Subhūti,
