q.p: “Venerable Śāriputra, what do you think, does form turn back from unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening?”
q.orig: Venerable Śāriputra, what do you think, does form turn back from unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening?
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, do you think that physical forms regress from unsurpassed, complete enlightenment

div.p:
and so on. Here again it teaches six ways it could happen: khri brgyad
–. You can suppose that a dharma, form and so on, turns back; or a dharma other than form turns back; or some dharma that is the suchness of the dharmas, form and so on with stains, turns back; or some dharma other than the suchness of form and so on turns back; or absolutely pure, stainless suchness turns back; or some dharma other than that turns back. Given that it could not happen in those six ways, what truly established dharma is there that will turn back? This is teaching that ultimately, therefore, there is nothing at all that turns back.
With

q.p:
“according to the way things are in the elder Subhūti’s teaching,” khri brgyad
; LSPW pp. 371–72: “When one adopts the method of considering dharmas in their ultimate reality, which Subhuti the elder uses in his exposition.”
q.orig: According to this exposition of the elder Subhūti, which accords with the principle of [ultimate] reality and its aspects

div.p:
and so on, the elder Śāriputra is saying that if there are no bodhisattvas who turn back from progress toward awakening, in that case all bodhisattvas will become buddhas; they will not turn back to become śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, having in mind that were that to be the case there would not be the three types of bodhisattvas where it says “the bodhisattva is threefold.” He questions Subhūti with the elder Pūrṇa’s words, khri brgyad
. and then the elder Subhūti, impatient with the words “the bodhisattva is threefold” says,

q.p: “Venerable Śāriputra, do you accept in suchness there are three bodhisattvas?”
q.orig: Venerable Śāriputra, do you accept that in suchness there are three bodhisattvas
Venerable Śāradvatīputra, do you hold that according to the real nature there are three sorts of bodhisattvas

div.p:
and so on. As already explained before,
– . from the perspective of suchness all childish ordinary persons, all noble persons, those with a pratyekabuddha’s awakening, bodhisattvas, and even buddhas are just simply one, there is no difference among them. This is explaining that if, even while all are thus just simply one, you accept that bodhisattvas are of three types, then how, given that suchness is totally without difference, can it be feasible to divide it into

q.p: “one… or two… or three”
q.orig: one mode, two modes, or three modes

div.p: subdivisions?

Then the Lord says to the elder Subhūti that he should know that those bodhisattvas will go forth to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening, and in that context, for the sake of those in the retinue who want to know the defining marks of those who will succeed in going forth, Subhūti asks,

q.p: “Lord, how should bodhisattva great beings who want to go forth to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening stand?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, how should bodhisattva great beings who seek emancipation in unsurpassed, complete enlightenment dwell

div.p:
After that there is the explanation that they stand with a fully complete aspiration and a fully complete practice. The fully complete aspiration is from khri brgyad
.

q.p: “I must produce a balanced thought toward all beings,”
q.orig: Their minds should dwell in a state of equanimity with respect to all beings

div.p: up to

q.p: “I must focus on all beings with the thought they are kinsmen, and blood relatives.”
q.orig: I must focus on all beings with the thought they are brothers, sisters, friends, kinsmen, up to blood relatives.
an attitude that regards all beings as their parents, brothers, sisters, friends, allies, and kinsmen

div.p:
And the fully complete practice is from khri brgyad
.

q.p: “I must also stop killing,”
q.orig: I must stop killing
They should praise abstention from the killing

div.p: up to

q.p: “the good doctrine lasts, welcoming it.”
q.orig: the good doctrine lasts as well, welcoming it.
praise and take empathetic delight in other beings acquiring the stability of the Dharma

div.p: Then there are the two results from the practice: the absence of obscuration and the absence of seizing.
The “I must produce a balanced thought toward all beings” is from the perspective of the suchness of all dharmas.

q.p:
“Form will be without obscuration” khri brgyad
, nyi khri : “That is how bodhisattva great beings should train in the perfection of wisdom and skillful means. Training like that, standing like that, their form will be without obscuration.”
q.orig: form will be without obscuration
The physical forms of those who do so will be unobscured

div.p: means they do not obscure or conceptualize form.

q.p: “Even in the past… did not seize form.”
q.orig: even in the past those bodhisattva great beings did not seize form
those bodhisattva great beings of the past have not grasped physical forms

div.p: Even in times past there was no obscuration of form and so on and they did not seize it. Having said “it is because they did not seize,” and so on, it then says,

q.p: “and why?”
q.orig: If you ask why[2]

div.p: asking, for the sake of those who are uncertain, how they “did not seize form” and so on. Bṭ1 pa 160b2–7: “It teaches that they gain the obscuration-free knowledge of all dharmas, form and so on. Why? Because they did not seize form in the past. This teaches the reason why obscuration is absent relative to all dharmas. They have seen that all dharmas were nonexistent things in the past and hence have not seized on an existent thing or a causal sign. That is why obscuration is absent. That is the meaning. What is the reason for that? ‘Even that absence of seizing form is not form,’ up to ‘… knowledge of all aspects.’ That absence of seizing all dharmas, form and so on, is not an absence of seizing something that exists, because ultimately all dharmas are empty of an intrinsic nature, therefore the dharmas, form and so on, are not existent things and hence are not seized.”

q.p: “Because even that form that has not been seized, Subhūti, is not form.”
q.orig: Because even that form that has not been seized is not form
because those physical forms that have not been grasped are not physical forms

div.p: Bodhisattvas cause just not seizing on all dharmas to get stronger, not seizing. But even that which bodhisattvas do not seize is not the intrinsic nature of form and so on. Therefore, when not seizing has gotten stronger, form and so on will not be seized on by bodhisattvas.

div.head: Signs of bodhisattvas irreversible from progress toward awakening
div.p:
Then, because the elder Subhūti has earlier said At khri brgyad
it says, “Sixty bodhisattvas lacking in what is necessary stopped appropriating anything and their minds were freed from contamination.” This leads to an exchange between Śāriputra and the Lord ( –) and a discussion in which śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas feature. “Why, Lord, even though they have similarly cultivated just those dharmas—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—did those separated from skillful means actualize the very limit of reality and become śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, while those other bodhisattvas, Lord, will, thanks to skillful means, by cultivating just those dharmas—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening?” This leads to Subhūti ( ) saying it is not hard to awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening. Śāriputra ( ) says this leads to an absurdity: “If bodhisattva great beings do not believe that dharmas are like space, but still it is easy to fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening, full awakening would not be hard, and bodhisattvas, as many of them as there are sand particles in the Gaṅgā River, would not turn back from unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening.” that ultimately even turning back does not exist, and the three types of bodhisattva The three types are with the śrāvaka, pratyekabuddha, and bodhisattva dispositions. do not exist either, here, in this part of the text, he asks about the signs that they are irreversible from progress toward awakening. Then the Lord gives an explanation of thirty-five signs: because irreversible bodhisattvas khri brgyad
–.

item.p: see without duality in suchness;
have turned away from all;
do not honor and so on other teachers or have a doctrine that is not inferior;
are not born in a place that precludes a perfect human birth;
stop the ten unwholesome actions;
complete the ten wholesome actions;

complete all the perfections for the sake of all beings; khri brgyad
. K, N omit.
study the doctrine—the twelve branches of the sacred word—for the sake of all beings;
are not unsure about the deep dharmas;
are endowed with gentle and loving physical, verbal, and thinking-mind actions;

do not put up with the five obscurations; The five are desire for sense gratification, malice, drowsiness and dozing, gross mental excitement and uneasiness, and doubt, where the pair drowsiness and dozing are counted as one, as are the pair gross mental excitement and uneasiness.

do not have the seven bad proclivities; The seven bad proclivities (anuśaya) according to Abhidharmakośa 5.1–2 are attachment (rāga), of which there are two based on the desire realm and two upper realms, anger (pratigha), pride (māna), ignorance (avidyā), view (dṛṣṭi), and doubt (vicikitsā).
act with mindfulness and a clear awareness of what they are doing;
are habitually clean and so on;
are those bodhisattvas in whom the thousands of maggot families do not arise;
have a pure body, pure speech, and a pure mind;
are not needy, are content, and rely on the qualities of the ascetic;
are not miserly and so on;
have a steady, profound intellect and so on;

do not repose their confidence in others; khri brgyad
–.
comprehend the works of Māra;

have gained forbearance for the nonproduction of dharmas; khri brgyad
: They have gained the forbearance because they have entered “into the secure state of a bodhisattva.”

have turned back and are irreversible from progress toward awakening; khri brgyad
: “Lord, do you call an irreversible bodhisattva great being ‘irreversible,’ or do you call a bodhisattva who turns back ‘irreversible’?”
do not focus on all dharmas, form and so on;

have the perfect four khri brgyad
. The four are: “They personally practice the perfection of giving, and they inspire others to practice the perfection of giving, speak in praise of practicing the perfection of giving, and speak in praise of others practicing the perfection of giving as well, welcoming it.” practices of the perfections;

do not hope the result of giving is that others become distressed and so on; khri brgyad
: “without oppressing anyone by unleashing the oppression that causes others mental distress.”

have the faculties such that the five vajra families are always shadowing them and so on; This supports the reading at khri brgyad
. ’bum tha 137a3, nyi khri (kha 366a4–5) have lag na rdo rje’i rigs rnams, “Vajrapāṇi families”; khri pa (nga 361b4) rdo rje’i rigs lnga brgya, “five hundred Vajra families.”
do not resort to spells and base arts;

stop being preoccupied with base stories and engage in perfect deeds and aspirations; khri brgyad
–.

will give up even their life to look after the doctrine; khri brgyad
. and
do not lose the doctrines they have taken up.

div.p: Among them,

q.p:
“in regard to those suchnesses, they have no doubt at all that they are not each separate and both.” Our author (or the translator) reads nominative plurals, as at PSP 1: 141 hi tās tathatā yā. Cp. khri brgyad
de bzhin nyid las de dag, where the translator reads an ablative (tathatāyā): “have no doubt at all that they are not each separate from suchness”; cp. nyi khri , Twenty-Five Thousand translation: “they are not in the slightest consumed by doubt, thinking that the real nature is individual, dual, or neither.”
q.orig: have no doubt at all that they are not each separate from suchness,
they are not in the slightest consumed by doubt, thinking that the real nature is individual, dual, or neither

div.p: This is explaining, based on the suchness of all persons, that the tathāgatas are exactly the same. It means the intrinsic nature, or the intrinsic nature of both, is not the intrinsic nature of suchness. The different noble persons, from śrāvakas to buddhas, are ultimately “suchness, unchanging, undifferentiated, not two, and not divided.” The sign that the bodhisattvas are irreversible is their understanding that does not reify a “suchness” over and above each of their individual suchnesses. Their suchnesses are both unique to each of them separately and yet make them ultimately the same.

q.p:
“All dharmas are without attributes, without tokens, and without signs” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: all phenomena are without attributes, without indications, and without signs

div.p: because suchness has no attributes.

q.p: “Lord, if all dharmas are without attributes,”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, if all phenomena are without attributes

div.p: and so on, means that if you say there are no attributes and no signs how have you explained the attributes and signs of those who are irreversible from progress toward awakening?

q.p: “Subhūti… bodhisattva great beings who have turned away from form,”
q.orig: Subhūti,” replied the Lord, “you should know that bodhisattva great beings who have turned away from form
Subhūti…replied the Blessed One, “when bodhisattva great beings have turned away from physical forms

div.p: and so on, is teaching that just the knowledge, in the absence of the attribute, is the reason they are irreversible from progress toward awakening. They have “turned away from” an attribute of form, from what is a token of form.

q.p:
“Know what needs to be known” khri brgyad
. —
q.orig: know what should be known

div.p: know the knowable;

q.p: “see what needs to be seen”—
q.orig: see what should be seen

div.p: see what needs to be looked at.

q.p: “They do not hold that a spectacle or an auspicious sign makes for cleanliness.”
q.orig: They do not conceive of purity [merely] on the basis of auspicious ceremonies and omens

div.p: An auspicious spectacle or auspicious sign means that just because they think so, [purification] has been done by bathing, fasting, chanting, visiting holy places, ceremonial offerings, and so on.
The explanation of all the tokens of irreversibility is easy.

It is true that not turning back from progress toward full awakening happens just by reaching the first level, but it also teaches a second not turning back from progress toward full awakening that happens at the eighth level.

As for those who “turn back” and are “irreversible,” khri brgyad
: “Subhūti, irreversible bodhisattvas are said to ‘turn back,’ and bodhisattvas who turn back are said to be ‘irreversible.’ ” those who turn back from the śrāvaka and pratyekabuddha levels “turn back”; those who do not turn back from the Buddha level are “irreversible from progress toward full awakening.”

div.head: Subhūti’s Two Hundred and Seventy-Seven Questions
div.p: Having thus heard about the good qualities of irreversible bodhisattvas not turning back, the elder Subhūti asks about the deep places for the benefit of bodhisattvas who want to be irreversible from progress toward full awakening and says

q.p: “would that you might also well expound those deep places.” khri brgyad ; nyi khri , ’bum tha 145b: “please reveal the profound states…”
q.orig: please reveal the profound states

div.p: From here on the elder Subhūti asks two hundred and seventy-seven questions about the deep places and the Lord provides the responses.
The first is “would that you might also well expound those deep places.”
The second is,

q.p: “Lord, are they words only for nirvāṇa or are they words for all dharmas?”
q.orig: Lord, are they words only for nirvāṇa or are they, Lord, words for all dharmas
Is it a designation of nirvāṇa but not of all phenomena

div.p: and so on.
The third is,

q.p: “Lord, what is the suchness of form like?”
q.orig: Lord, what is the suchness of form like,
Blessed Lord, how is the real nature of physical forms

div.p: and so on.
The fourth is,

q.p: “The Lord has said, ‘Whatever merit has been accumulated it is all imaginary,’ so how will a son of a good family or daughter of a good family make a lot of merit?”
q.orig: the Lord has said, ‘Whatever merit has been accumulated, it is all imaginary,’ so how will a son of a good family or daughter of a good family create a lot of merit?

Blessed Lord, since the Blessed One has said that phenomena that are not subject to conditioning are imaginary, how…could the merit of those noble sons or noble daughters increase manifold, more than the former

div.p: and so on.
The fifth is,

q.p: “Lord, what are the specific features of incalculable, infinite, and immeasurable?”
q.orig: What are the specific features of…immeasurable
Blessed Lord, what are the distinctions and what are the differences between the incalculable, the inestimable, and the immeasurable

div.p: and so on.
The sixth is,

q.p: “Lord, would there also be a way such that form would also be incalculable?”
q.orig: Lord, would there also be a way such that form would also be incalculable
Blessed Lord, is there a reason why physical forms are incalculable

div.p: and so on.
The seventh is,

q.p: “Lord, is it just that form is empty?”
q.orig: Lord, is it that just that form is empty,
Blessed Lord, is it only physical forms that are empty

div.p: and so on.
The eighth is,

q.p: “Lord, does an inexpressible reality know increase or decrease?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, can an object that is inexpressible increase or decrease

div.p: and so on.
The ninth is,

q.p: “Lord, if an inexpressible reality does not increase or decrease, will the perfection of giving, Lord, not increase or decrease?”
q.orig: if an inexpressible reality does not increase or decrease, the perfection of giving, Lord, will not increase or decrease.
Blessed Lord, if an object that is inexpressible neither increases nor decreases, then, Blessed Lord, the perfection of generosity would neither increase nor decrease

div.p: and so on.
The tenth is,

q.p: “Lord, what is unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, what is the nature of unsurpassed, complete enlightenment

div.p: The eleventh is,

q.p: “What is the suchness of all phenomena?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, of what is the real nature

div.p: The twelfth is,

q.p: “Lord, do bodhisattva great beings fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening because of the first production of the thought?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, do bodhisattva great beings…attain consummate buddhahood in unsurpassed, complete enlightenment through their initial setting of the mind on enlightenment

div.p: and so on.
The thirteenth is,

q.p: “Lord, do bodhisattva great beings, having completed all the ten levels, fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening?”
q.orig: Lord, bodhisattva great beings, having completed all the ten levels, fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening?
Blessed Lord, what are the ten levels by perfecting which bodhisattva great beings attain consummate buddhahood in unsurpassed, complete enlightenment

div.p: and so on.
The fourteenth is,

q.p: “How, Lord, when they do so, will bodhisattva great beings become absorbed for the sake of beings in the three meditative stabilizations?”
q.orig: how, Blessed Lord, do those bodhisattva great beings become absorbed in the three meditative stabilities and bring beings to maturity through those meditative stabilities

div.p: The fifteenth is,

q.p: “How do bodhisattva great beings complete the perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: how do bodhisattva great beings complete the six perfections

div.p: The sixteenth is,

q.p: “How do bodhisattva great beings fully master emptiness?”
q.orig: Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom fully master emptiness
Blessed Lord, how should bodhisattva great beings who practice the perfection of wisdom investigate…emptiness[1]

div.p: The seventeenth is,

q.p: “How do bodhisattva great beings stand in emptiness but not actualize emptiness?” PSP 4: 193 kathaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ śūnyatāyāṃ sthitaḥ śūnyatāṃ na sākṣātkaroti; ’bum tha 199b4, nyi khri ga 7b3 mngon sum du m(y)i bgyid pa lags; ŚsPN4 9817v7 kathaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ śūnyatāyāṃ sthitaḥ śūnyatāṃ sākṣātkaroti; LSPW p. 406 “how then does [he] who has stood in emptiness, realize emptiness?”
q.orig: how then, Blessed Lord, do bodhisattva great beings dwell in emptiness and not actualize emptiness

div.p: The eighteenth is,

q.p: “Lord, what is the mark of the perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, what are the defining characteristics of the perfection of wisdom

div.p: The nineteenth is,

q.p: “Lord, if all phenomena are isolated from all phenomena and if all phenomena are empty of all phenomena, Lord, how could there be the defilement and purification of beings?”
q.orig: Lord, if all phenomena are isolated from all phenomena, and if all phenomena are empty of all phenomena, Lord, how could there be the defilement and purification of beings?
Blessed Lord, if all phenomena are void of all phenomena and if all phenomena are empty of all phenomena, how could there be affliction and purification of beings

div.p: The twentieth is,

q.p: “Lord, given that all attention is separated from an intrinsic nature, that all attention is empty of an intrinsic nature, how, Lord, are bodhisattva great beings never separated from attention connected to the knowledge of all aspects?”
q.orig: Lord, given that all attention is separated from an intrinsic nature, that all attention is empty of an intrinsic nature, how, Lord, are bodhisattva great beings never separated from attention connected to the knowledge of all aspects?

Blessed Lord, if all such acts of attention are indeed without inherent existence‍—that is to say, if all acts of attention are indeed empty of inherent existence‍—how could bodhisattva great beings not part from focusing their attention with all-aspect omniscience in mind

div.p: The twenty-first is,

q.p: “Lord, given that the perfection of wisdom is separated from an intrinsic nature, how will bodhisattva great beings succeed at the perfection of wisdom and fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening?”
q.orig: Lord, given that the perfection of wisdom is separated from an intrinsic nature and empty of an intrinsic nature, how will bodhisattva great beings succeed at the perfection of wisdom and fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening?

Blessed Lord, if the perfection of wisdom is devoid of inherent existence and it is empty of inherent existence, then, Blessed Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings genuinely bring forth the perfection of wisdom and attain consummate buddhahood in unsurpassed, complete enlightenment

div.p: The twenty-second is,

q.p: “Lord, is it the emptiness of the perfection of wisdom, its state of ringing hollow, being in vain [that practices the perfection of wisdom]?”
q.orig: Lord, is it the emptiness of the perfection of wisdom, its state of ringing hollow, being in vain, being a fraud, and being pointless, that practices the perfection of wisdom?
Blessed Lord, is it this [very] perfection of wisdom, which is emptiness, voidness, vacuity, hollowness, and essencelessness, that engages in the perfection of wisdom

div.p: At this point there is a subsection with ten questions. 1. Is it the emptiness of the perfection of wisdom that practices the perfection of wisdom? 2. Can you apprehend any dharma other than the perfection of wisdom that is practicing the perfection of wisdom? 3. Does the perfection of wisdom practice the perfection of wisdom? 4. Does emptiness practice emptiness? 5. Does something other than emptiness practice emptiness? 6. Does form and so on practice the perfection of wisdom? 7. Do the six perfections and so on practice the perfection of wisdom? 8. Is it the emptiness of form and so on that practices the perfection of wisdom? 9. Is it the emptiness of the four fearlessnesses that practices the perfection of wisdom? 10. If those dharmas do not practice the perfection of wisdom, how does a bodhisattva great being practice when one practices the perfection of wisdom?
The twenty-third is,

q.p: “Lord, is the bodhisattvas’ unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening prophesied because there will be the production of all the dharmas?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, is it through this nonarising nature of all phenomena that bodhisattva great beings are prophesied to attain unsurpassed, complete enlightenment

div.p: The twenty-fourth is,

q.p: “Lord, what is the sameness of bodhisattva great beings?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, what is the sameness of the bodhisattva great beings

div.p: The twenty-fifth is,

q.p: “Lord, when bodhisattva great beings train to put an end to form do they train in the knowledge of all aspects?”
q.orig: Lord, when bodhisattva great beings train to put an end to form do they train in the knowledge of all aspects
Blessed Lord, when bodhisattva great beings undertake training in order that physical forms may be terminated, do they train in all-aspect omniscience

div.p: The twenty-sixth is,

q.p: “Lord, if all dharmas are in their basic nature perfectly pure, what dharma’s perfect purity do bodhisattva great beings attain?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, inasmuch as all phenomena are naturally pure, what are the attributes of the bodhisattva great beings through which this refinement is acquired

div.p: The twenty-seventh is,

q.p: “Lord, do they even have to obtain a śrāvaka’s and a pratyekabuddha’s perfect state?”
q.orig: Do they even have to obtain a śrāvaka’s perfect state, and do they even have to obtain a pratyekabuddha’s perfect state?
Blessed Lord, will they also attain the excellence of the śrāvakas? Will they also attain the excellence of the pratyekabuddhas

div.p: The twenty-eighth is,

q.p: “Lord, in what way will a thought that is like an illusion fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening?” This is placed later by Haribhadra at PSP 5: 44.
q.orig: Blessed Lord, how does the illusion-like mind attain consummate buddhahood in unsurpassed, complete enlightenment

div.p: The twenty-ninth is,

q.p: “How will there be a realization of the isolated by the isolated?”
q.orig: how can voidness attain buddhahood through voidness

div.p: The thirtieth is,

q.p: “Lord, do those lord buddhas teach the Dharma in the form of a proclamation of the names K, N; D adds here, and below, “and by way of being delighted by” (dga’i ba’i tshul gyis), probably an accidental addition by a block-cutter. of those bodhisattva great beings who turn back or those who do not turn back?”
q.orig: Lord, do those lord buddhas teach the Dharma in the form of a proclamation of the names of, and by way of being delighted by, those bodhisattva great beings who turn back or those who do not turn back?
Blessed Lord, while teaching the Dharma, do those lord buddhas proclaim the names of bodhisattva great beings who may regress, or of those whose progress is irreversible

div.p: The thirty-first is,

q.p: “Lord, given that no phenomenon is apprehended when they have stood in suchness and practiced for suchness, how will they stand in the knowledge of all aspects?”
q.orig: Lord,” Subhūti then inquired, “given that no phenomenon is apprehended when they have stood in suchness and practiced for suchness, how will they stand in the knowledge of all aspects?
Blessed Lord, when they dwell in the real nature, earnestly intent on the real nature, if they do not apprehend anything at all, how then will they dwell in all-aspect omniscience

div.p: The thirty-second is,

q.p: “Lord, given that no dharma called ‘a tathāgata’s magical creation’ is apprehended at all, who will stand in suchness?”
q.orig: Lord, given that no phenomenon called ‘a tathāgata’s magical creation’ is apprehended at all, who will stand in suchness
Blessed Lord, when, apart from the real nature, there is nothing apprehensible at all, who will dwell in this real nature

div.p: The thirty-third is,

q.p: “Lord, how are they to accomplish the perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: Lord, how are bodhisattva great beings to accomplish the perfection of wisdom
Blessed Lord, how should the perfection of wisdom be brought into being

div.p: The thirty-fourth is,

q.p: “Lord, how does the perfection of giving reach completion in bodhisattva great beings practicing this perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: Lord, how does the cultivation of the perfection of giving reach completion in bodhisattva great beings practicing this perfection of wisdom?
Blessed Lord, how will bodhisattva great beings who engage by dwelling in the perfection of wisdom complete the cultivation of the perfection of generosity

div.p: The thirty-fifth is,

q.p: “How do bodhisattva great beings standing in the perfection of giving incorporate the perfection of morality?”
q.orig: how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of generosity, acquire the perfection of ethical discipline

div.p: The thirty-sixth is,

q.p: “How do they, standing in the perfection of giving, incorporate the perfection of patience?”
q.orig: Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings standing in the perfection of giving incorporate the perfection of patience
how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of generosity, acquire the perfection of tolerance

div.p: The thirty-seventh is,

q.p: “How the perfection of perseverance?”
q.orig: how do bodhisattva great beings standing in the perfection of giving incorporate the perfection of perseverance?
how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of generosity, acquire the perfection of perseverance

div.p: The thirty-eighth is,

q.p: “How the perfection of concentration?”
q.orig: how do bodhisattva great beings standing in the perfection of giving incorporate the perfection of concentration?
how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of generosity, acquire the perfection of meditative concentration

div.p: The thirty-ninth is,

q.p: “How the perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: how do bodhisattva great beings standing in the perfection of giving incorporate the perfection of wisdom?
how will bodhisattva great beings, while dispensing generosity with skill in means, acquire the perfection of wisdom

div.p: The fortieth is,

q.p: “How do they, standing in the perfection of morality, incorporate the perfection of giving?”
q.orig: Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings standing in the perfection of morality incorporate the perfection of giving
how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of ethical discipline, acquire the perfection of generosity

how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of ethical discipline, acquire the perfection of perseverance

q.orig: how do bodhisattva great beings standing in the perfection of morality incorporate the perfection of concentration?
how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of ethical discipline, acquire the perfection of meditative concentration

div.p: The forty-fourth is,

q.p: “How the perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: how do bodhisattva great being standing in the perfection of morality incorporate the perfection of wisdom?
how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of ethical discipline, acquire the perfection of wisdom

div.p: The forty-fifth is,

q.p: “How do they, standing in the perfection of patience, incorporate the perfection of giving?”
q.orig: Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings standing in the perfection of patience incorporate the perfection of giving
how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of tolerance, acquire the perfection of generosity

div.p: The forty-sixth is,

q.p: “How the perfection of morality?”
q.orig: how do bodhisattva great beings standing in the perfection of patience incorporate the perfection of morality?
how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of tolerance, acquire the perfection of ethical discipline

q.p: “How the perfection of perseverance?”
q.orig: how do bodhisattva great beings standing in the perfection of patience incorporate the perfection of perseverance?
how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of tolerance, acquire the perfection of perseverance

div.p: The forty-eighth is,

q.p: “How the perfection of concentration?”
q.orig: how do bodhisattva great beings standing in the perfection of patience incorporate the perfection of concentration?
how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of tolerance, acquire the perfection of meditative concentration

div.p: The forty-ninth is,

q.p: “How the perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: how do bodhisattva great beings standing in the perfection of patience incorporate the perfection of wisdom?
how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of tolerance…acquire the perfection of wisdom

div.p: The fiftieth is,

q.p: “How do they, standing in the perfection of perseverance, incorporate the perfection of giving?”
q.orig: Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings standing in the perfection of perseverance incorporate the perfection of giving
how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of perseverance, acquire the perfection of generosity

div.p: The fifty-first is,

q.p: “How the perfection of morality?”
q.orig: how do bodhisattva great beings standing in the perfection of perseverance incorporate the perfection of morality?
how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of perseverance, acquire the perfection of ethical discipline

how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of perseverance, acquire the perfection of tolerance

div.p: The fifty-third is,

q.p: “How the perfection of concentration?”
q.orig: how do bodhisattva great beings standing in the perfection of perseverance incorporate the perfection of concentration?
how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of perseverance, acquire the perfection of meditative concentration

div.p: The fifty-fourth is,

q.p: “How the perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: how do bodhisattva great beings standing in the perfection of perseverance incorporate the perfection of wisdom?
how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of perseverance, acquire the perfection of wisdom

div.p: The fifty-fifth is,

q.p: “How do they, standing in the perfection of concentration, incorporate the perfection of giving?”
q.orig: Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings standing in the perfection of concentration incorporate the perfection of giving
how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of meditative concentration, acquire the perfection of generosity

div.p: The fifty-sixth is,

q.p: “How the perfection of morality?”
q.orig: how do bodhisattva great beings standing in the perfection of concentration incorporate the perfection of morality?
how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of meditative concentration, acquire the perfection of ethical discipline

div.p: The fifty-seventh is,

q.p: “How the perfection of patience?”
q.orig: how do bodhisattva great beings standing in the perfection of concentration incorporate the perfection of patience?
how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of meditative concentration, acquire the perfection of tolerance

div.p: The fifty-eighth is,

q.p: “How the perfection of perseverance?”
q.orig: how do bodhisattva great beings standing in the perfection of concentration incorporate the perfection of perseverance?
how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of meditative concentration, acquire the perfection of perseverance

q.p: “How the perfection of wisdom?”

how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of meditative concentration, acquire the perfection of wisdom

div.p: The sixtieth is,

q.p: “How do they, standing in the perfection of wisdom, incorporate the perfection of giving?”
q.orig: how do bodhisattva great beings standing in the perfection of wisdom incorporate the perfection of giving
how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of wisdom, acquire the perfection of generosity

q.p: “How the perfection of morality?”
q.orig: how do bodhisattva great beings standing in the perfection of wisdom incorporate the perfection of morality?
how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of wisdom, acquire the perfection of ethical discipline

q.p: “How the perfection of patience?”
q.orig: how do bodhisattva great beings standing in the perfection of wisdom incorporate the perfection of patience?
how will bodhisattva great beings…abiding in the perfection of wisdom, acquire the perfection of tolerance

div.p: The sixty-third is,

q.p: “How the perfection of perseverance?”
q.orig: how do a bodhisattva great beings standing in the perfection of wisdom incorporate the perfection of perseverance?
how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of wisdom, acquire the perfection of perseverance

div.p: The sixty-fourth is,

q.p: “How the perfection of concentration?”
q.orig: how do bodhisattva great beings standing in the perfection of wisdom incorporate the perfection of concentration?
how will bodhisattva great beings, abiding in the perfection of wisdom, acquire the perfection of meditative concentration

div.p: The sixty-fifth is,

q.p: “How long a time has it been since bodhisattva great beings with such skillful means set out?” In Haribhadra’s version (PSP 5: 50, le’u brgyad ma, ca, 74a7) this is located in a different part of the Sūtra.
q.orig: Blessed Lord, for how long have bodhisattva great beings who possess such skill in means set out [on this path

div.p: The sixty-sixth is,

q.p: “Lord, how many lord buddhas have the bodhisattva great beings with such skillful means attended on?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, how many buddhas have those bodhisattva great beings who possess such skill in means revered

div.p: The sixty-seventh is,

q.p: “How large is the wholesome root they have planted?”
q.orig: Lord, how large is the wholesome root the bodhisattva great beings with such skillful means have planted?
Blessed Lord, what are the roots of virtuous action that those bodhisattva great beings who possess such skill in means have cultivated

div.p: The sixty-eighth is,

q.p: “Lord, if all phenomena are empty of an intrinsic nature how will bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of giving and so on fully awaken?”
q.orig: Lord, if all phenomena are empty of an intrinsic nature, how will bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of giving, the perfection of morality, the perfection of patience, the perfection of perseverance, the perfection of concentration, and the perfection of wisdom fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening?

Blessed Lord, if all phenomena are naturally empty, in that case, Blessed Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings who practice the perfection of generosity, and who practice the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of tolerance, the perfection of perseverance, the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom attain consummate buddhahood in unsurpassed, complete enlightenment

div.p: The sixty-ninth is,

q.p: “Lord, given there is no specific feature or variation of any phenomenon for someone who has entered into reality, why is the perfection of wisdom said to be the highest… when it comes to the five perfections?”
q.orig: Lord, given that there is no specific feature or variation in any phenomenon for someone who has entered into reality, why is the perfection of wisdom said to be the highest, and is said to be…foremost, best, superb, sublime, unsurpassed, unrivaled, and equal to the unequaled, when it comes to the five perfections?

Blessed Lord, if in that way there are no distinctions and no particulars with respect to anything at all that is to be objectively established, why then is the perfection of wisdom, in relation to the five other perfections, said to be the best

div.p: The seventieth is,

q.p: “Lord, does the perfection of wisdom not fully take hold of or release any dharma?”
q.orig: Lord, does the perfection of wisdom take hold of or release any dharma?
Blessed Lord, with respect to what does the perfection of wisdom neither acquire nor relinquish anything

div.p: The seventy-first is,

q.p: “Lord, how is form not taken hold of and not released?”
q.orig: Lord, how is form, up to awakening not taken hold of and not released?
Blessed Lord, how are physical forms neither acquired nor relinquished

div.p: The seventy-second is,

q.p: “Lord, if there is no attention being paid to form, how will the wholesome roots flourish?”
q.orig: Lord, if there is no attention being paid to form, up to there is no attention being paid to the knowledge of all aspects, how, Lord, without attention to form, up to without attention to the knowledge of all aspects will the wholesome roots flourish?
Blessed Lord, if one does not focus attention on physical forms;

div.p: The seventy-third is,

q.p: “Lord, why, when they thus do not pay attention to form, do they reach the knowledge of all aspects?”
q.orig: Lord, why, when they thus do not pay attention to form, up to do not pay attention to awakening do they reach the knowledge of all aspects?
Why is it that by not focusing attention on physical forms

div.p: The seventy-fourth is,

q.p: “Lord, where will bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom stand?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, in what do those bodhisattva great beings who accordingly practice the perfection of wisdom dwell

div.p: The seventy-fifth is,

q.p: “Lord, how will they not stand in form?”
q.orig: Lord, how will they not stand in form,

div.p: The seventy-sixth is,

q.p: “Lord, how will these faults of bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom not occur?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings who practice the perfection of wisdom avoid these faults

div.p: The seventy-seventh is,

q.p: “Lord, is the perfection of wisdom not separated from the perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, is the perfection of wisdom not bereft of the perfection of wisdom

div.p: The seventy-eighth is,

q.p: “Lord, what is the path of bodhisattva great beings, and what is not the path?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, what is the path of bodhisattva great beings? What is not their path

div.p: The seventy-ninth is,

q.p: “Lord, if the perfection of wisdom does not produce and does not stop any phenomenon, how do bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom give gifts?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, if this perfection of wisdom does not produce or stop anything at all, in that case, Blessed Lord, how should bodhisattva great beings who practice the perfection of wisdom dispense gifts

div.p: The eightieth is,

q.p: “Lord, how should bodhisattva great beings make an effort at the six perfections?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, how should bodhisattva great beings persevere in the six perfections

div.p: The eighty-first is,

q.p: “Lord, have you said that they have to train in the perfection of wisdom with the perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: Lord, are you saying they have to train in the perfection of wisdom with the perfection of wisdom?
Blessed Lord, do you say that they should train in the perfection of wisdom by means of the perfection of wisdom

div.p: The eighty-second is,

q.p: “Lord, how do the lord buddhas watch over those practicing the perfection of giving?”
q.orig: How do the lord buddhas turn their enlightened intention toward bodhisattva great beings who practice the perfection of generosity

div.p: The eighty-third is,

q.p: “Lord, how will bodhisattva great beings come to know all dharmas in brief and in detail?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, how will bodhisattva great beings understand all phenomena in brief and in detail

div.p: The eighty-fourth is,

q.p: “Lord, what is the suchness of form?”
q.orig: Lord, what is the suchness of form?
Blessed Lord, what is the real nature of physical forms

div.p: The eighty-fifth is,

q.p: “Lord, what is the very limit of reality?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, what is the very limit of reality

div.p: The eighty-sixth is,

q.p: “Lord, how should all dharmas be known in brief and in detail?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, how should they understand all phenomena in brief and in detail

div.p: The eighty-seventh is,

q.p: “Lord, what are the dharmas that are not conjoined and are not disjoined?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, what are those phenomena that are not conjoined and that are not disjoined

div.p: The eighty-eighth is,

q.p: “Lord, how should bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, how should they practice the perfection of wisdom

div.p: The eighty-ninth is,

q.p: “Lord, for bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom, how long is it?”
q.orig: Lord, for bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom, how long is the practice of the perfection of wisdom?
Blessed Lord, when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom, for how long will they practice it

div.p: The ninetieth is,

q.p: “Lord, should they practice connected with an unbroken, unseparated thought?” K, N yon tan la in place of rje su ’brel ba (anuśaṃsā in place of anubandha); ’bum da 132b3, nyi khri ga 119a7 just sems kyi rgyun ma chad pa dang / ma bral bar spyad par bgyi. PSP 5: 111 kiṃ punar bhagavaṃś cittāntarānām avakāśan dadatā prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caritavyam; le’u brgyad ma ca 133b1 sems gzhan gyi go skabs mi ’byed par, “not giving an occasion for other thoughts.”
q.orig: Lord, should they practice…with an unbroken, unseparated stream of thoughts
Blessed Lord, how should they practice without interruption and without separation from the mind set on enlightenment

div.p: The ninety-first is,

q.p: “Lord, will bodhisattva great beings who have practiced the perfection of wisdom, accomplished the perfection of wisdom, and meditated on the perfection of wisdom reach the knowledge of all aspects?”
q.orig: Lord, will bodhisattva great beings who have practiced the perfection of wisdom, accomplished the perfection of wisdom, and meditated on the perfection of wisdom reach the knowledge of all aspects?
Blessed Lord, will those who have practiced the perfection of wisdom, activated the perfection of wisdom, and cultivated the perfection of wisdom attain all-aspect omniscience

div.p: In this “Lord, how will bodhisattvas reach the knowledge of all aspects?” part of the text, there are four questions in a subsection. The four questions are: “How will (1) suchness, how will (2) the very limit of reality, how will (3) the dharma-constituent, and how will (4) the self element, up to the person element, reach the knowledge of all aspects?” Alternatively, it intends these four questions: “Will they reach the knowledge of all aspects (1) having meditated, (2) without having meditated, (3) having meditated when they meditated and without having meditated when they did not meditate, or (4) without having meditated and without having not meditated?”
The ninety-second is,

q.p: “Lord, is the perfection of wisdom something that cannot be labeled?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, is the perfection of wisdom inconceivable

div.p: The ninety-third is,

q.p: “Why, Lord, does hell have a label?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, why are the hells conceived

div.p: The ninety-fourth is,

q.p: “Well then, Lord, do bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom train in form?”
q.orig: In that case, Blessed Lord, should bodhisattva great beings who practice the perfection of wisdom train in physical forms

div.p: The ninety-fifth is, Noteworthy here is the omission of the question, “Lord, how will one train in, up to the knowledge of all aspects, without taking anything away and without adding anything?”

q.p: “Lord, how should they train in form as not produced and not stopping?”
q.orig: Lord, how should they train in form as not produced and not stopping
Blessed Lord, how should they train in nonarising and nonceasing

div.p: The ninety-sixth is,

q.p: “Lord, how should they train in all dharmas empty of their own marks?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, how should they see that all phenomena are empty of their own defining characteristics

div.p: The ninety-seventh is,

q.p: “Lord, if form is empty of form, how will bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: Lord, if form is empty of form, up to even awakening is empty of awakening, well then, Lord, how will bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom?

Blessed Lord, if in this way physical forms are empty of physical forms; and feelings, perceptions, formative predispositions, and consciousness are empty of consciousness [and so forth]; and [all the attributes and goals], up to and including all-aspect omniscience, are empty of unsurpassed enlightenment [and so forth], in that case, Blessed Lord, how will bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom

div.p: The ninety-eighth is,

q.p: “Lord, why is not practicing the practice of the perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, why is the practice of the perfection of wisdom without practice

div.p: The ninety-ninth is,

q.p: “Lord, if not practicing is the practice of the perfection of wisdom, how then will bodhisattva great beings who are beginning the work practice the perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, if they practice the perfection of wisdom in that manner, without practicing, how should bodhisattva great beings who are beginners practice the perfection of wisdom

div.p: The one hundredth is,

q.p: “Lord, to what extent does not apprehending come about?”
q.orig: To what extent is there nonapprehension

div.p: From here on down are the second hundred.
The first is,

q.p: “Lord, what is duality?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, what is duality

div.p: The second is,

q.p: “Lord, what is nonduality?”

div.p: The third is,

q.p:
“Lord, is what cannot be apprehended not apprehended?” khri brgyad, K, N, ’bum da 152a7, nyi khri
.
q.orig: is it the nonapprehensible that is not apprehended

div.p: The fourth is,

q.p: “Lord, if bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom are not attached to apprehending and are not attached to not apprehending, how, Lord, will bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom complete level after level, and how, having completed level after level, will they reach the knowledge of all aspects?”
q.orig: Lord, if bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom are not attached to apprehending and are not attached to not apprehending, how, Lord, will bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom complete level after level, and how, having completed level after level, will they reach the knowledge of all aspects?

Blessed Lord, when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom in that manner, if they are not attached to apprehending and they are not attached to nonapprehension, how then will bodhisattva great beings who practice the perfection of wisdom perfect the levels, from one to the next, and, after perfecting the levels from one to the next, how will they attain all-aspect omniscience

div.p: The fifth is,

q.p: “Lord, if a perfection of wisdom cannot be apprehended, how will bodhisattvas… make an investigation?”
q.orig: Lord, if a perfection of wisdom cannot be apprehended, awakening cannot be apprehended, and someone practicing the perfection of wisdom cannot be apprehended either, well then, how will bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom make an investigation

Blessed Lord, if in that way the perfection of wisdom is nonapprehensible, and those who engage in enlightenment are also nonapprehensible, in that case, how do bodhisattva great beings who practice the perfection of wisdom understand all phenomena

div.p: The sixth is,

q.p: “Lord, if bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom do not apprehend form, … how will they complete the perfection of giving… and having done the work of a buddha free all beings from saṃsāra?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom in that manner, if they do not apprehend even physical forms…And having accomplished the enlightened activity of the buddhas…how will they liberate beings from cyclic existence

div.p: The seventh is,

q.p: “Well then, Lord, for whose sake do bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: Well then, Lord, for the sake of what do bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom?
Blessed Lord, why then do bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom

div.p: The eighth is,

q.p: “Lord, if all dharmas are unmade and are unchanging, how is there an arrangement of three vehicles?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, if in that way all phenomena are uncreated and unconditioned, how then will these three vehicles

div.p: The ninth is,

q.p: “Lord, if a tathāgata, worthy one, perfectly complete buddha were not to apprehend with the five eyes those beings they free from saṃsāra, how then would the Lord… have predicted beings in the three groups…?”
q.orig: Lord, if a tathāgata, worthy one, perfectly complete buddha were not to apprehend with the five eyes those beings they free from saṃsāra, how then would the Lord, having fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening, have prophesied beings in the three groups?

Blessed Lord, if even with their five kinds of eye the tathāgatas, arhats, completely awakened buddhas do not see those beings whom they would liberate from cyclic existence, how then, Blessed Lord, does the Blessed One, having attained consummate buddhahood in unsurpassed, complete enlightenment, then prophesy which beings belong to the three categories

div.p: The tenth is, This question perhaps includes a second rhetorical question, PSP 5: 120: “Well then, Lord, the tathāgatas stood in miraculous powers in a succession / (GilgitC 142) in error”? Alternatively, the absence of the second question here suggests that the rhetorical question at PSP 5: 120 is an unsupported addition to the Sūtra.

q.p: “But Lord, the tathāgatas stood in the ultimate and fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect complete awakening.”
q.orig: But Lord, the tathāgatas stood in the ultimate and fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening.
Did the Blessed One then attain consummate buddhahood in unsurpassed, complete enlightenment after entering into ultimate reality

div.p: The eleventh is,

q.p: “Lord, if all dharmas are like magical creations, then what distinction and what differentiation, Lord, is there between a tathāgata and a magical creation?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, if all phenomena are like an emanation, what is the distinction and the difference between the tathāgatas and their emanations

div.p: The twelfth is,

q.p: “Lord, when there is no tathāgata, does the tathāgata’s magical creation do the work?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, is it when the tathāgatas are not present that their emanations perform those activities

div.p: The thirteenth is,

q.p: “Lord, if there is no distinction at all between a magical creation and a tathāgata, how will there be a pure gift?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, if there is no distinction between such an emanation and the tathāgatas, how will donations be purified when they are offered

div.p: The fourteenth is,

q.p: “Lord, the true dharmic nature of all dharmas should not be made complicated, but has the Lord not complicated the true dharmic nature of all dharmas?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, if the reality of all phenomena should not become disturbed, has the reality of all phenomena not been purposefully disturbed by the Blessed One

div.p: The fifteenth is,

q.p: “Lord, if the Lord has taught the true dharmic nature of dharmas and explained dharmas with words and signs in order that others will comprehend, why, Lord, have you given an explanation in words and signs of dharmas that have no names and have no signs?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, if the Blessed One has revealed the reality of all phenomena and expressed [the nature of] all phenomena through names and signs so that others might comprehend it, how then, Blessed Lord, are all phenomena without names and without signs expressed through names and signs

div.p: The sixteenth is,

q.p: “Lord, if all dharmas finish as a mere name and sign, well then, for what do bodhisattva great beings produce the thought to be awakened?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, if all these conditioned phenomena are merely names and signs, for what purpose do bodhisattva great beings set their minds on enlightenment

div.p: The seventeenth is,

q.p: “Lord, you say ‘knowledge of all aspects’ again and again?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, you speak of ‘all-aspect omniscience, all-aspect omniscience

div.p: The eighteenth is,

q.p: “Lord, what distinction is there between these three types of omniscience?”
q.orig: What distinction and what differentiation, Lord, is there between these three types of omniscience
Blessed Lord, is the distinction among these three sorts of all-knowing

div.p: The nineteenth is,

q.p: “Lord, why does the knowledge of all aspects belong to tathāgatas?”

div.p: The twentieth is,

q.p: “Lord, why does the knowledge of path aspects belong to bodhisattva great beings?”
q.orig: why the knowledge of path aspects to bodhisattva great beings
Why does knowledge of the path pertain to bodhisattva great beings

div.p: The twenty-first is,

q.p: “Why does all-knowledge belong to śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas?”
q.orig: why all-knowledge to śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas
Blessed Lord, why does knowledge of all the dharmas pertain to śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas

div.p: The twenty-second is,

q.p: “Lord, from among the three types of omniscience, is there a difference in the elimination of afflictions by them such that it is said, ‘with its abandonment there is something left over,’ but ‘with its abandonment there is nothing left over.’?”
q.orig: “Lord,” he asked further, “from among the three types of omniscience—all-knowledge, knowledge of path aspects, and knowledge of all aspects—is there a difference in the abandonment of affliction such that it is said, ‘with its abandonment there is something left over,’ but ‘with its abandonment there is nothing left over’?

Blessed Lord, among these three sorts of all-knowing‍—knowledge of all the dharmas, knowledge of the path, and all-aspect omniscience‍—is there a difference in the aspects of afflicted mental states that are abandoned, one through which they are abandoned without residue, and one through which they are not abandoned without residue

div.p:
The twenty-third is, ’bum da 175a4, ŚsPN4 9965v10. khri brgyad
, PSP 5: 126 have “Before reaching the knowledge of all aspects, is there an uncompounded elimination of afflictions?”

q.p: “Lord, before these śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas have reached the uncompounded, have they eliminated afflictions?”
q.orig: Lord, before reaching the knowledge of all aspects is there an uncompounded abandonment of afflictions?
Blessed Lord, have all those śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas abandoned afflicted mental states without attaining the unconditioned state

div.p: The twenty-fourth is,

q.p: “Lord, are differences apprehended in the uncompounded?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, are differences in the unconditioned state apprehensible

div.p: The twenty-fifth is,

q.p: “Lord, if differences are not apprehended in the uncompounded, why does the Lord say, ‘This is an abandonment of residual impressions and connections. This is not an abandonment of residual impressions and connections?”
q.orig: Lord, if differences are not apprehended in the uncompounded, why does the Lord say, ‘This is an abandonment of residual impression connections. This is not an abandonment of residual impression connections’?

Blessed Lord, if such [differences] are not apprehensible, why then did the Blessed One say that these have abandoned reincarnation through the continuity of propensities, but those have not abandoned reincarnation through the continuity of propensities

div.p: The twenty-sixth is, This question in four parts is placed in a different order here and below ( ) than in the presently extant versions of the Sūtra. The four questions are: “Do they actualize the very limit of reality (1) having stood on the path, (2) having stood on what is not the path, (3) having stood on both the path and what is not the path, or (4) having stood on neither the path nor what is not the path? And, have they “stopped appropriating anything and become freed in their hearts from outflows having stood on a path?” and so on (four alternatives).

q.p: “Lord, does a bodhisattva great being having stood on the path…?”
q.orig: Lord, do bodhisattva great beings actualize the very limit of reality having stood on the path?
Blessed Lord, should bodhisattva great beings, having been established on the path, then actualize the very limit of reality

div.p: In this part of the text, in a sub-section, there are four questions.
The twenty-seventh is,

q.p: “Lord, if the path is not an existent thing and nirvāṇa is not an existent thing, why is it taught that ‘this is a stream enterer’?”
q.orig: Lord, if the path is not an existent thing and nirvāṇa is not an existent thing, why is it taught that ‘this is a stream enterer;
Blessed Lord, if the path is indeed nonexistent, and nirvāṇa is also nonexistent, in that case, why is it explained that this one is entering the stream to nirvāṇa

div.p: The twenty-eighth is,

q.p: “Lord, does something uncompounded make the category ‘this is a stream enterer’?”
q.orig: Lord, does something uncompounded make the categories ‘this is a stream enterer,
Blessed Lord, is it the unconditioned [reality] that makes distinctions to the effect that this one is entering the stream to nirvāṇa

div.p:
The twenty-ninth is, khri brgyad
: “Lord, how will a later limit be designated?”

q.p: “Lord, how will there be a later limit to saṃsāra?”
q.orig: Lord, how will a later limit be designated?

div.p: The thirtieth is,

q.p: “Lord, if in all phenomena empty of their own marks a prior limit is not apprehended, what need is there to say more about a later limit?”

div.p: The thirty-first is,

q.p: “Lord, you say ‘perfection of wisdom’ again and again. Why, Lord, is it called ‘perfection of wisdom’?”
q.orig: Lord, you say ‘perfection of wisdom’ again and again. Why, Lord, is it called ‘perfection of wisdom’?
Blessed Lord, when you speak of ‘the perfection of wisdom, the perfection of wisdom,’ for what purpose do you speak of the perfection of wisdom?

div.p: The thirty-second is,

q.p: “Lord, if a meaning and a method don dang tshul gyis (PSP 2-3:149 arthataś ca nayataś), absent from other versions. The translation is from LSPW. are not found in this perfection of wisdom, how can bodhisattva great beings practice this deep perfection of wisdom’s meaning?”
q.orig: Lord, if good and bad are not found in this deep perfection of wisdom, how can bodhisattva great beings practice this deep perfection of wisdom’s reality?

Blessed Lord, if meaning and nonmeaning are not apprehended in this profound perfection of wisdom, in that case how should bodhisattva great beings engage in the meaning of this profound perfection of wisdom

div.p: The thirty-third is,

q.p: “Lord, why does the perfection of wisdom not do good and not do bad?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, why does the perfection of wisdom not render anything at all meaningful? Why does it not render anything at all meaningless

div.p: The thirty-fourth is,

q.p: “But Lord, the uncompounded is good for all noble ones, is it not?”
q.orig: But Lord, the uncompounded is good for all noble buddhas and a buddha’s śrāvakas, is it not?
Blessed Lord, in that case is the unconditioned [reality] not meaningful for the buddhas and all noble śrāvakas of the buddhas

div.p: The thirty-fifth is,

q.p: “Lord, having trained in the uncompounded perfection of wisdom, do bodhisattva great beings not reach the knowledge of all aspects?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, do bodhisattva great beings, having trained in the unconditioned perfection of wisdom, not attain all-aspect omniscience

div.p: The thirty-sixth is,

q.p: “Lord, does a nondual dharma…?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, is it that something nondual attains something nondual

div.p: In this part of the text, in a subsection, there are three questions. The three questions are: “Does a dual dharma reach a nondual dharma? Does a nondual dharma reach a nondual dharma? Does a nondual dharma reach a dual dharma?”
The thirty-seventh is,

q.p: “Lord, how much merit do bodhisattva great beings make, who have produced the first thought, and who want to fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening for the sake of all beings?”
q.orig: Lord, how much merit do bodhisattva great beings create, who have produced the first thought, and who want to fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening for the sake of all beings?

Blessed Lord, to what extent will the merit increase of those bodhisattva great beings who have initially set their minds on enlightenment and who seek to attain consummate buddhahood in unsurpassed, complete enlightenment for the sake of all beings

div.p: The thirty-eighth is,

q.p: “Lord, what should bodhisattva great beings who have produced the first thought pay attention to?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, on what should bodhisattva great beings who have initially set their minds on enlightenment focus their attention?

div.p: The thirty-ninth is,

q.p: “Lord, what is the objective support of the knowledge of all aspects?”
q.orig: Lord, what sort of thing is the knowledge of all aspects—what is the objective support,
Blessed Lord, what is the entity of all-aspect omniscience? What is its reference

div.p: The fortieth is,

q.p: “Lord, is only the knowledge of all aspects a nonexistent thing?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, is all-aspect omniscience exclusively a nonentity or is it not

div.p: The forty-first is,

q.p: “Lord, why does the knowledge of all aspects have no intrinsic nature?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, why is all-aspect omniscience without essential nature

div.p: The forty-second is,

q.p: “Lord, if all dharmas are the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature, with what skillful means do bodhisattva great beings, who have produced the first thought of awakening, practice the perfection of giving?”
q.orig: Lord, if all dharmas are the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature, with what skillful means do bodhisattva great beings who have produced the first thought of awakening practice the perfection of giving

Blessed Lord, if all phenomena are of the essential nature of nonentity, in that case, with what skill in means do bodhisattva great beings who have initially set their minds on enlightenment refine the buddhafields and bring beings to maturity while practicing the perfection of generosity

div.p: The forty-third is,

q.p: “Lord, are phenomena separated from the phenomena themselves?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, in that case are all phenomena themselves devoid of all phenomena

div.p: The forty-fourth is,

q.p: “Lord, is ordinary convention one thing and the ultimate another?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, are mundane relative [appearances] one thing and ultimate [truth] another

div.p: The forty-fifth is,

q.p: “Lord, you say ‘bodhisattva’s practice’ again and again, what are the words bodhisattva’s practice for?”
q.orig: Lord, you say ‘bodhisattva’s practice’ again and again. Lord, what are the words bodhisattva’s practice for?
Venerable Lord, when one speaks of the conduct of a bodhisattva, of what is the expression bodhisattva conduct a designation

div.p: The forty-sixth is,

q.p: “Lord, you say ‘buddha’ again and again…?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, when one speaks of a buddha

div.p: The forty-seventh is,

q.p: “Lord, you say ‘awakening’ again and again…?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, when one speaks of ‘enlightenment

div.p: The forty-eighth is,

q.p: “Lord, if bodhisattva great beings who practice for this awakening practice the six perfections… what wholesome root of theirs will be accumulated or diminished, decreased or increased, produced or stopped, or defiled or purified?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, with regard to the roots of virtuous action of those bodhisattva great beings who conduct themselves in this enlightenment, and who practice the six perfections…do they accumulate or do they decline? Do they decrease or do they increase? Do they arise or do they cease? Are they afflicted or are they purified

div.p: The forty-ninth is,

q.p: “Lord, if the awakening of bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom is not available as any dharma in the manner of an objective support, how will bodhisattvas… fully grasp the perfection of giving?”
q.orig: Lord, if the awakening of bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom is not available as any dharma in the manner of an objective support, how will bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom fully grasp the perfection of giving,

“Blessed Lord, if, with regard to the enlightenment of bodhisattva great beings who practice the perfection of wisdom…nothing is established by way of apprehending, so that nothing at all will accumulate or decline, decrease or increase, arise or cease, or be defiled or purified‍—in that case, Blessed Lord, when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom, how will they acquire the perfection of generosity

div.p: The fiftieth is,

q.p:
“If… in a dualistic way…?” khri brgyad
: “Lord, if they do not practice the perfection of giving in a dualistic way, and similarly, up to do not practice the knowledge of all aspects in a dualistic way, how will the bodhisattva great beings, starting from the production of the first thought, grow and flourish on wholesome roots, and how will they grow and flourish on wholesome roots up to the production of the last thought?”
q.orig: if they do not practice the perfection of giving in a dualistic way
if it is not with duality

div.p: The fifty-first is,

q.p: “Lord, do bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of wholesome roots?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, should bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom for the sake of the roots of virtuous action

div.p: The fifty-second is,

q.p: “Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings who have attended on the lord buddhas… gain the knowledge of all aspects?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings who have revered the lord buddhas, who have been favored by the roots of virtuous action, and who have been accepted by spiritual mentors attain all-aspect omniscience

div.p: The fifty-third is,

q.p: “Lord, those bodhisattva great beings would not gain the knowledge of all aspects, would they?”
q.orig: those bodhisattva great beings would not gain the knowledge of all aspects, would they?

Blessed Lord, if there are bodhisattva great beings who have not revered the lord buddhas, have not even perfected the roots of virtuous action, and have not even been favored by spiritual mentors, would they not attain all-aspect omniscience

div.p: The fifty-fourth is,

q.p: “Lord, why would even bodhisattva great beings who attend on the lord buddhas… not gain the knowledge of all aspects?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, why do bodhisattva great beings not attain all-aspect omniscience, even though they have revered the lord buddhas

div.p: The fifty-fifth is,

q.p: “Lord, what are those skillful means, in possession of which bodhisattva great beings gain the knowledge of all aspects?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, what is the skill in means that bodhisattva great beings have, through which they would attain all-aspect omniscience

div.p: The fifty-sixth is,

q.p: “Lord, does a nonexistent thing fully awaken to a nonexistent thing?”
q.orig: Lord, can a nonexistent thing fully awaken to a nonexistent thing
In that case, can nonentities attain consummate buddhahood through nonentities

div.p: In this part of the text, in a subsection, there are four questions. The four questions are: (1) “Can a nonexistent thing fully awaken to an existent thing, (2) can an existent thing fully awaken to a nonexistent thing, (3) can a nonexistent thing fully awaken to a nonexistent thing, and (4) and an existent thing fully awaken to an existent thing?”
The fifty-seventh is,

q.p: “Lord, what is the bodhisattva great beings’ thought construction?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, what are the conceptual elaborations that bodhisattva great beings might have

div.p: The fifty-eighth is,

q.p: “Lord, if no phenomenon at all can be apprehended as having an intrinsic nature, on what path do bodhisattva great beings enter into the secure state of a bodhisattva?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, if the essential nature is not apprehended with respect to anything at all, by what do bodhisattva great beings enter a bodhisattva’s full maturity

div.p: The fifty-ninth is,

q.p: “Lord, if bodhisattva great beings enter into the secure state of a bodhisattva having completed all paths, in that case, Lord, given that the Aṣṭamaka path is different… how will bodhisattva great beings enter into the secure state of a bodhisattva having completed all paths?”
q.orig: Lord, if bodhisattva great beings enter into the secure state of a bodhisattva having completed all paths, in that case, Lord, given that the Aṣṭamaka path is different, the stream enterer path is different, the path of the candidate for once-returner is different, the once-returner path is different, the path of the candidate for non-returner is different, the non-returner path is different, the path of the candidate for worthy one is different, the worthy one path is different, the pratyekabuddha path is different, and the path of the tathāgata, worthy one, perfectly complete Buddha is different, well then, Lord, if all those paths are different from each other, how will bodhisattva great beings enter into the secure state of a bodhisattva…having completed all paths[2]

Blessed Lord, if bodhisattva great beings enter a bodhisattva’s full maturity after perfecting all pathways, is it the case, Blessed Lord, that the pathway of arhats on the eighth level is indeed one distinct path, that the pathway of those destined for only one more rebirth is another, that the pathway of those no longer subject to rebirth is another, that the pathway of those entering arhatship is another, that the pathway of arhats is another, that the pathway of pratyekabuddhas is another, and that the pathway of the tathāgatas, arhats, completely awakened buddhas is another? Blessed Lord, if these pathways are distinct from one another, how do bodhisattva great beings perfect all pathways and enter a bodhisattva’s full maturity

div.p:
The sixtieth is, K, N. Emend D bdag gi to dag gis? (PSP 5: 154, GilgitC 183, ŚsPN4/2 3r4 jānīyāma). Cf. khri brgyad
; ’bum da 257a7–b2: “Given that it would be impossible for a bodhisattva great being to enter into the fixed state of a bodhisattva and reach the knowledge of all aspects, how, Lord, am I to understand a bodhisattva great being entering into the fixed state of a bodhisattva having completed all paths, and having entered into the fixed state of a bodhisattva reaching the knowledge of all aspects and eliminating all residual impression connections?” le’u brgyad ma ca 173b4 lam de snyed ma thob par rnam pa thams cad mkhyen pa nyid thob bar ji ltar mi ’gyur lags, “How, if one does not attain all the paths, as many as there are, would one not not attain the knowledge of all aspects?” The psychological dimension of “complete” (a path) includes (1) unbroken bodhicitta, (2) knowing that paths ultimately go nowhere, (3) knowing a path has temporary value for the beings attracted to it, and (4) knowledge of each path after having learned and practiced it.

q.p: “Lord, how will bodhisattva great beings reach the knowledge of all aspects without having produced these paths?”
q.orig: how, Lord, are we to understand bodhisattva great beings entering into the secure state of a bodhisattva having completed all paths, and having entered into the secure state of a bodhisattva reaching the knowledge of all aspects

Blessed Lord, how should one understand that bodhisattva great beings…perfect all pathways and enter a bodhisattva’s full maturity? How do they attain all-aspect omniscience, having entered into the maturity of the bodhisattvas, and how do they abandon all afflicted mental states associated with reincarnation through the continuity of propensities

div.p: The sixty-first is,

q.p: “Lord, which is the bodhisattvas’ path of a knower of path aspects?”
q.orig: Lord, which of these paths—the śrāvaka path, the pratyekabuddha path, and the buddha path—that the Lord has spoken about is this path of a knower of path aspects?
Blessed Lord, what is the pathway of knowledge of the path, distinct from the pathway of the śrāvakas, the pathway of the pratyekabuddhas, and the pathway of the buddhas

div.p: The sixty-second is,

q.p: “Lord, if those dharmas—the dharmas on the side of awakening and the awakening—[are not conjoined and not disjoined… how, Lord, will the dharmas on the side of awakening be those that bring about awakening]?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, if the factors that are conducive to enlightenment and all those attributes that constitute enlightenment are neither conjoined nor disjoined, immaterial, invisible, unimpeded, and their sole defining characteristic is that they are without defining characteristics, how do bodhisattva great beings nurture enlightenment

div.p: The sixty-third is,

q.p: “Lord, what are the dharmas bodhisattva great beings should realize, having trained in them by knowing and seeing?”

div.p: The sixty-fourth is,

q.p: “Lord, you say ‘noble Dharma and Vinaya’ [again and again. Lord, what is the noble Dharma and Vinaya]?”
q.orig: The Blessed One speaks of the ‘Dharma and Vinaya of the noble ones…What is the extent of the Dharma and Vinaya of the noble ones

div.p: The sixty-fifth is,

q.p: “Lord, should they not train in the mark of form?”
q.orig: Lord, they should not train in the mark of form,
Blessed Lord, if they do not train in the defining characteristics of physical forms

div.p: The sixty-sixth is, ’bum da 265b3.

q.p: “If they should not train in the marks of those dharmas how, Lord, will bodhisattva great beings transcend the śrāvaka and pratyekabuddha levels?”
q.orig: Lord, without having trained in the mark of dharmas and the mark of volitional factors will a bodhisattva great being transcend the śrāvaka and pratyekabuddha levels?
Blessed Lord, if they do not train in the defining characteristics of all these phenomena, how then, Blessed Lord, do bodhisattva great beings transcend the levels of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas

div.p: The sixty-seventh is,

q.p: “Lord, if all dharmas are unmarked, do not have various marks, and do not have even one mark, how, Lord, will bodhisattva great beings meditate on the perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, if all phenomena are in that manner without defining characteristics, and there is neither difference nor identity with respect to defining characteristics, how could the perfection of wisdom that bodhisattva great beings have be cultivated

div.p: The sixty-eighth is,
