q.p: “Lord, in what way is meditation on the unmarked, meditation on the perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: How is the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom a cultivation without defining characteristics

div.p:
The sixty-ninth is, Earlier khri brgyad
, in response to the question, “Lord, how is the disintegration of meditation on all dharmas meditation on the perfection of wisdom?” “The Lord said, ‘The disintegration of meditation on form is meditation on the perfection of wisdom.’ ” Cf. ’bum da 272b7.

q.p: “Lord, how is the disintegration of meditation on form, meditation on the perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: Lord, how is the disintegration of meditation on all dharmas, meditation on the perfection of wisdom?
Blessed Lord, how does the cultivation of the breaking down of all phenomena constitute the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom

div.p: The seventieth is, ’bum da 294a3.

q.p: “If, for someone with dualistic perception, there is not even the patience that arises in a natural order, how could there ever be the comprehension of form?” This question is ungrammatical. The order of the questions here is problematic.

div.p: The seventy-first is, ’bum da 295a1.

q.p: “When bodhisattva great beings are practicing the perfection of wisdom, is there the notion of an existent thing or a nonexistent thing?”

div.p: The seventy-second is,

q.p: “Lord, what is an existent thing? What is a nonexistent thing?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord what are entities? What are nonentities

div.p: The seventy-third is,

q.p: “Lord, what is duality? What is nonduality?”
q.orig: Lord, what is duality?
Blessed Lord, with respect to what are entities dualistic

div.p:
The seventy-fourth is, nyi khri
.

q.p: “Lord, if all phenomena are the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature…?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, if in that manner all phenomena are of the essential nature of nonentity

div.p: The seventy-fifth is,

q.p: “Lord, how has a tathāgata, worthy one, perfect complete buddha produced the four concentrations that are the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature?”
q.orig: Lord, how has a tathāgata, worthy one, perfectly complete buddha produced the four concentrations that are the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature?
Blessed Lord, how did the tathāgata, arhat, completely awakened Buddha develop the four meditative concentrations, which are of the essential nature of nonentity

div.p: The seventy-sixth is,

q.p: “How, even while all dharmas are the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature, will there be serial action?”
q.orig: how, even while all phenomena are the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature, will there be serial action,
although all phenomena have the essential nature of nonentity, why is it, Blessed Lord, that bodhisattva great beings undertake the serial practice

div.p: The seventy-seventh is,

q.p: “Lord, if all phenomena are the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature, well then, there is no form…?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, if in that manner all phenomena are of the essential nature of nonentity, in that case, there are indeed no physical forms

div.p: The seventy-eighth is,

q.p: “Lord, if all dharmas are the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature, what reality do bodhisattva great beings who have set out for unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening for the welfare of beings see?”
q.orig: Lord, if all phenomena are the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature, Lord, what reality do bodhisattva great beings who have set out for unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening for the welfare of beings see?
Blessed Lord, if all phenomena have the essential nature of nonentity, what is the goal that bodhisattva great beings see in embarking on unsurpassed, complete enlightenment for the sake of beings

div.p: The seventy-ninth is,

q.p: “Lord, without an apprehended object is there attainment, is there clear realization?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, with regard to nonapprehension, is there attainment, clear realization

div.p:
The eightieth is, This formulation of the question makes better sense than the version at khri brgyad
, which begins, “If in the absence of an apprehended object there is no attainment, there is no clear realization, and there is no unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening…” LSPW p. 508, n. 3, says, “The last clause of this sentence puzzles me, and the translation is only approximately right.”

q.p: “If just the absence of an apprehended object is attainment, just the absence of an apprehended object is clear realization… in that case, Lord, how will there be the bodhisattva great beings’ first level?”
q.orig: but nonetheless nonapprehension is attainment, nonapprehension is clear realization, and nonapprehension is unsurpassed, complete enlightenment, how then, Blessed Lord, could there possibly be bodhisattva great beings of the first level

div.p: The eighty-first is,

q.p: “Lord, what distinction and what differentiation is there between the absence of an apprehended object, and giving, morality…?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, what is the distinction and what is the difference between nonapprehension on the one hand and generosity, ethical discipline

div.p: The eighty-second is,

q.p: “Lord, how is an exposition made that differentiates between unapprehended giving, morality, patience, perseverance, concentration, wisdom, and the clairvoyances?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, how are immaculate generosity, ethical discipline, tolerance, perseverance, meditative concentration, wisdom, and extrasensory powers revealed to be different

div.p: The eighty-third is,

q.p: “How do they incorporate the six perfections in a single production of the thought?”
q.orig: how do they acquire the six perfections through a single setting of their minds on enlightenment

div.p: The eighty-fourth is, nyi khri .

q.p: “How do they not, when giving a gift, have a dualistic notion?”
q.orig: how do they dispense gifts, and in this be without dualistic perception

div.p: The eighty-fifth is, ’bum da 345a4.

q.p: “Lord, given that all dharmas are without causal signs and do not occasion anything, how do bodhisattvas complete the perfection of giving and so on.”
q.orig: Lord, given that all dharmas are without causal signs and do not occasion anything, how is the perfection of giving completed;
Blessed Lord, since all phenomena are without concepts, uneffected, unapprehended, and unconditioned, how do bodhisattva great beings complete the perfection of generosity

div.p:
The eighty-sixth is, nyi khri ; cf. khri brgyad
.

q.p: “Lord, given that dharmas are without causal signs, how is it that bodhisattvas complete the cultivation of the six perfections?”
q.orig: Lord, given that dharmas are without causal signs, without effort, unadulterated, and empty of their own mark, how is it that bodhisattvas complete the cultivation of the six perfections
Blessed Lord, since all phenomena are indivisible, signless, and empty of their own defining characteristics, how could the cultivation of the six perfections

div.p: The eighty-seventh is,

q.p: “Lord, what is forbearance for dharmas that are not produced?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, what is the acceptance that phenomena are nonarising

div.p: The eighty-eighth is, The complete question is: “Lord, what is the difference between these two types of patience: the forbearance for dharmas that are not produced of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas and the forbearance for dharmas of bodhisattva great beings?”

q.p: “Lord, … of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas?”
q.orig: Lord[2]…of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas?
Blessed Lord, what are the distinctions between the acceptance that śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas

div.p: The eighty-ninth is,

q.p: “Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings, having completed the perfection of meditative stabilization that has no mark, pass beyond the śrāvaka and pratyekabuddha levels?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings complete the perfection of meditative stability and transcend the levels of the śrāvakas and the pratyekabuddhas

div.p: The ninetieth is,

q.p:
“Lord, what is a… flaw and what is flawlessness?” khri brgyad
. This derives nyāma (PSP niyāma) (“fixed state”) from āma (“hardheadedness”) (Conze “rawness,” Twenty-Five Thousand “immaturity”). The Tib translators render āma with skyon (“flaw”) and nyāma with skyon med (“flawlessness”).
q.orig: Lord, what is a bodhisattva’s flaw and what is a bodhisattva’s flawlessness?
Blessed Lord, what is the immaturity of bodhisattva great beings, and what is the maturity of the bodhisattvas

div.p: The ninety-first is,

q.p: “Lord, what is apprehending?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, what is apprehending

div.p: The ninety-second is,

q.p: “Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom comprehend that all phenomena are like a dream?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom, how do they definitively comprehend that all phenomena are like a dream

div.p: The ninety-third is,

q.p: “Lord, if all dharmas are an unbroken unity, why is there an exposition of wholesome dharmas?”
q.orig: Lord, if all dharmas are unadulterated, how are wholesome and unwholesome dharmas taught
Blessed Lord, since all phenomena are indivisible, how are phenomena revealed to be virtuous or nonvirtuous

div.p: The ninety-fourth is,

q.p: “Lord, how, when all dharmas are like a dream… can you present these as wholesome…?”
q.orig: Lord, how, when all dharmas are like a dream, have no basis, are the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature, and are empty of their own marks, can you present these as wholesome

Blessed Lord, since all phenomena are dreamlike nonentities, with the essential nature of nonentity and empty of intrinsic defining characteristics, how then can it be established that these are virtuous phenomena

div.p: The ninety-fifth is,

q.p: “Lord, what is that amazing, marvelous dharma of bodhisattva great beings that śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas do not have?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, what are the wonderful and marvelous attributes of bodhisattva great beings who practice the perfection of wisdom, which are unknown to all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas

div.p: The ninety-sixth is,

q.p:
“Subhūti, how do bodhisattva great beings practicing this perfection of wisdom gather a retinue of beings by giving?” ’bum na 38b7; cf. khri brgyad
. This question is not in fact asked by Subhūti but is one of a series of rhetorical questions posed by the Lord in response to Subhūti.
q.orig: How, Subhūti, do bodhisattva great beings gather a retinue of beings by giving?
Subhūti, if you ask how bodhisattva great beings attract beings through generosity

div.p: The ninety-seventh is,

q.p: “Lord, do bodhisattva great beings gain the knowledge of all aspects?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, will bodhisattva great beings also attain all-aspect omniscience

div.p:
The ninety-eighth is, ’bum na 41b3–4; cf. khri brgyad
, “Well then, Lord, is there a distinction to be made between a bodhisattva great being and a tathāgata?”

q.p: “If a bodhisattva great being gains the knowledge of all aspects, what is the distinction to be made between a bodhisattva great being and a tathāgata?”
q.orig: Well then, Lord, is there a distinction to be made between a bodhisattva great being and a tathāgata?
Blessed Lord, if bodhisattva great beings will also attain all-aspect omniscience, what then is the distinction between bodhisattva great beings and the tathāgatas

div.p: The ninety-ninth is,

q.p: “Lord, if, because of the emptinesses of what transcends limits and no beginning and no end, a being absolutely cannot be apprehended… how, Lord, do bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom arisen from maturation… teach the Dharma to beings?”
q.orig: Lord, if, because of the emptinesses of what transcends limits and no beginning and no end, a being absolutely cannot be apprehended, a dharma also cannot be apprehended, and a dharma’s intrinsic nature cannot be apprehended, well then, Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom arisen from maturation…teach the Dharma to beings?
Blessed Lord, if, owing to the emptiness of the unlimited and the emptiness of that which has neither beginning nor end…and teach the Dharma to beings

div.p: The one hundredth is,

q.p: “Lord, if, in that case, in the dharma-constituent, there is no going beyond, and in suchness and at the very limit of reality there is no going beyond, well then, is form one thing and the dharma-constituent another?”
q.orig: Lord, if, in the dharma-constituent, there is no going beyond, and in suchness and at the very limit of reality there is no going beyond, well then, Lord, is form one thing and the dharma-constituent another

Blessed Lord, if in that manner the realm of phenomena is not transcended, and the real nature and the very limit of reality are also not transcended, then are physical forms not one thing and the realm of phenomena another

div.p: From here on down are the third hundred.

The first is, khri brgyad
: “Lord, when one has become habituated to the path does the result appear and does one attain the result?” ’bum na 86a3, nyi khri : “Lord, when one has become habituated to the path does one attain the result or does one not attain the result?” le’u brgyad ma ca 251a3 bcom ldan ’das ci lags/ lam bsgoms pas ’bras bu ’thob pa’am/ ’bras bu ’thob par bgyi pa ma mchis sam: “Lord, when one has become habituated to the path does one attain or does one cause the result to be attained?”

q.p: “Lord, when they have become habituated to the path does the result appear, and do they attain the result or not attain the result?”
q.orig: Lord, when they have become habituated to the path, does the result appear and do they attain the result?
Blessed Lord, will the fruit then be attained by those who have cultivated the path, or is the fruit attainable

div.p: The second is,

q.p: “Lord, if the results have not been presented in detail by curbing Emend both D rigs su tshar bcad and K, N rigs su bcad to ris su bcad? khri brgyad (ga 87a1) tshar bcad pa’i tshul kyis, “by curbing.” Cf. below Bṭ3 (F.272a7) char bcad pa’i tshul gyis. khri brgyad ga 86a7 gal te ’dus byas kyi khams sam/ ’dus ma byas kyi khams la tshar bcad pas. LSPW pp. 538–39: “without having cut off the share of either the conditioned or the unconditioned element.” Gilgit 628.4–5 na ca bhāgacchedena saṃskṛtadhātau asaṃskṛtadhātau vā vyavasthānam; AAVN 103b6 phala­bhāgacchedābhāva­praśnena; ’bum na 86a5–6, nyi khri (ga 245b1), le’u brgyad ma ca 251a5–6 ’dus byas kyi khams sam/ ’dus ma byas kyi khams ris su bcad cing; khri pa nga 337b ’dus byas kyi khams la’am/ ’dus ma byas kyi khams la tshar bcad pa’i tshul kyis, Twenty-Five Thousand translation: “eradicating (bhāgacchedena, tshar gcad pas).” the compounded element and uncompounded element… Lord, how am I to understand what you have said, Lord, that ‘the results have not been presented in detail by curbing the compounded and uncompounded dharmas’?”
q.orig: Lord, if the results have not been presented in detail by curbing the compounded element and the uncompounded element, given that you, Lord, have said, ‘This is the result of stream enterer because three fetters have been eliminated; this is the result of once-returner because of a weakening of attachment to sense objects and malice; this is the result of non-returner because the fetters that are associated with living in the desire realm have been eliminated; this is the state of a worthy one because the five fetters that are associated with the upper realms have been eliminated; a pratyekabuddha’s awakening is to “every dharma qualified by origination, all of them, are subject to cessation”; and the elimination of all residual impression connections is perfect, complete awakening,’ then, Lord, how am I to understand what you have said, Lord, that ‘the results have not been presented in detail by curbing the compounded and uncompounded dharmas’?”

Blessed Lord, if the fruit is not established by eradicating conditioned or unconditioned elements…I understand the Blessed One’s statement that the fruit of conditioned and unconditioned phenomena is not established by eradicating them

div.p: The third is,

q.p: “Lord, how have bodhisattva great beings realized well what marks dharmas as dharmas?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings realize the defining characteristic of phenomena, of which all phenomena partake

div.p: The fourth is,

q.p: “Lord, how does a magical creation meditate on the path?”
q.orig: Lord, how do they meditate on the path of a magical creation?
Blessed Lord, what is the cultivation of the path on which the Blessed One depends

div.p: The fifth is,

q.p: “Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings realize all dharmas that are not real things?”
q.orig: Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings realize all dharmas that are nonexistent things

div.p: The sixth is,

q.p: “Lord, is all form like a tathāgata’s magical creation?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, are all physical forms like a phantom emanation

div.p: The seventh is,

q.p: “Lord, if bodhisattva great beings know… all phenomena are like an illusion, then for whose sake do they practice the six perfections?”
q.orig: Lord, if bodhisattva great beings know, see, and are aware that all phenomena are like an illusion and are like a magical creation, then for whose sake do they practice the six perfections,

Blessed Lord, if bodhisattva great beings have known, seen, and realized that all phenomena are like a magical display, and known, seen, and realized that they are like a phantom emanation, for what purpose do bodhisattva great beings…practice the six perfections

div.p: The eighth is,

q.p: “Lord, if all phenomena are like a dream, where are beings such that by practicing the perfection of wisdom bodhisattva great beings cause them to advance beyond that location?”
q.orig: Lord, if all phenomena are like a dream, like an apparition, like an illusion, like a mirage, and like a magical creation, where are beings such that by practicing the perfection of wisdom bodhisattva great beings cause them to advance beyond that location?

Blessed Lord, if all phenomena are like a dream, like an echo, like a mirage, like an optical aberration, like a magical display, and like a phantom emanation, what is it, Blessed Lord, on which beings are fixed, and for which bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom and cause beings to escape

div.p: The ninth is,

q.p: “Lord, what is a name, and what is a causal sign?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, what are names and what are signs

div.p: The tenth is,

q.p: “Lord, if all dharmas end up as simply that, how will bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom become personally special on account of wholesome dharmas?”
q.orig: Lord, if all dharmas end up as simply that—end up as simply the absence of a causal sign like that—then, Lord, how will bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom become personally special on account of wholesome dharmas,

If all these phenomena are merely like that, which is to say, they are merely names and signs‍—mere imputations that originate from imagination‍—then when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom, how do they attain particular virtuous attributes

div.p: The eleventh is,

q.p: “Lord, if all dharmas are without signs, without mindfulness… how do you enumerate ‘these are dharmas with outflows’?”
q.orig: Lord, if all dharmas are without signs, without mindfulness, and without attention, well then, Lord, how do you enumerate ‘these are dharmas with outflows,

Blessed Lord, if all phenomena are signless, free from recollection, and free from attention, in that case, Blessed Lord, how are designations applied, such as, ‘These are virtuous attributes. These are nonvirtuous attributes. These are mundane attributes. These are supramundane attributes. These are contaminated attributes

div.p:
The twelfth is, ’bum na 97a2. Gilgit 631.14 yathā kathaṃ punar. khri brgyad
, corroborated by PSP 6-8: 80: “Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom train in the five appropriating aggregates?”

q.p: “Lord, how, in what sort of way, do bodhisattva great beings train in the five appropriating aggregates?”
q.orig: Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom train in the five appropriating aggregates?
Blessed Lord, when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom, how do they train in that [aforementioned] manner in the five acquisitive aggregates

div.p: The thirteenth is,

q.p: “Lord, if bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom are aware in that way of those dharmas that are different from each other, well then, Lord, does that not complicate the dharma-constituent?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom, if they were to investigate phenomena that are so different from one another in this manner, would the realm of phenomena not be disrupted

div.p: The fourteenth is,

q.p: “Lord, in what are bodhisattva great beings training in the dharma-constituent trained?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, in what will bodhisattva great beings who train in the realm of phenomena become trained

div.p: The fifteenth is,

q.p: “Lord, if all dharmas are the dharma-constituent, how should bodhisattva great beings train in the perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: Lord, if all dharmas are the dharma-constituent, well then, Lord, how should bodhisattva great beings train in the perfection of wisdom?
Blessed Lord, if all phenomena constitute the realm of phenomena, in that case, how should bodhisattva great beings who practice the perfection of wisdom train in physical forms

div.p: The sixteenth is,

q.p: “Lord, if a being is absolutely not apprehended… for whose sake do bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, if beings are absolutely not apprehended and indeed not apprehensible as beings, for whose sake do bodhisattva great beings cultivate the perfection of wisdom

div.p:
The seventeenth is, ’bum a 123b5–7 is: “Lord, if the very limit of reality limit is thus not one thing and the limit of beings is not another, well then, does the very limit of reality rest at the very limit of reality? Lord, if the very limit of reality rests at the very limit of reality, an intrinsic nature will rest in intrinsic nature. Lord, given that an intrinsic nature does not rest in intrinsic nature, how, Lord, is a bodhisattva great being practicing the perfection of wisdom going to establish the limit of beings at the very limit of reality?” At khri brgyad
, the beginning of the question differs, “Lord, if the very limit of reality is also the limit of beings…?” The remainder of the question is the same.

q.p: “Lord, if the very limit of reality is thus not one thing and the limit of beings is not another…?”
q.orig: Lord, if the very limit of reality is also the limit of beings,
Blessed Lord, if the very limit of reality is not one thing and the very limit of beings not another

div.p:
The eighteenth is, khri brgyad
. The part left out is: “establish beings at the very limit of reality without complicating the very limit of reality?”

q.p: “Lord, what are the skillful means in possession of which bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom with skillful means…?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom, what is the skill in means

div.p:
The nineteenth is, khri brgyad
. The part left out is: “and if in the emptiness of a basic nature a being is not apprehended, nor are a dharma and a path apprehended, Lord, how will bodhisattva great beings stand in the knowledge of all aspects?”

q.p: “Lord, if all dharmas are empty of a basic nature…?”
q.orig: Lord, if all phenomena are empty of a basic nature
Blessed Lord, if in that manner all phenomena are empty of inherent existence

div.p: The twentieth is,

q.p: “Lord, if all dharmas are not different things, well then, for what will bodhisattva great beings, thinking, ‘I will fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening,’ set out?”
q.orig: Lord, if all phenomena are not different things, well then, Lord, for what will bodhisattva great beings, thinking, ‘I will full awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening,’ set out?
Blessed Lord, if all phenomena are indivisible, why do bodhisattva great beings think, ‘Having set out for unsurpassed, complete enlightenment, I should attain consummate buddhahood

div.p: The twenty-first is, ’bum na 191a6–7.

q.p: “Lord, if a bodhisattva great being’s awakening is not a practice of taking anything up K, N. and is not a practice of not taking anything up, well then, of what is a bodhisattva great being’s awakening a practice?”
q.orig: Lord, if a bodhisattva great being’s awakening is not a practice of taking anything up and is not a practice of not taking anything up, well then, of what is a bodhisattva great being’s awakening the practice?
Blessed Lord, if the enlightenment of bodhisattva great beings does not engage in grasping and does not engage in nongrasping, in what does the enlightenment of bodhisattva great beings engage

div.p:
The twenty-second is, khri brgyad
; nyi khri , ’bum na 191a4 sems dpa’ chen po’i byang chub, “If a bodhisattva great being’s awakening is not practiced…”

q.p: “Lord, if bodhisattva great beings do not practice taking anything up or not taking anything up, do not practice form… how will bodhisattva great beings… fully awaken to the knowledge of all aspects?”
q.orig: Lord, if a bodhisattva great being’s awakening is not a practice of taking anything up or not taking anything up, is not a practice of form, up to and is not a practice of the knowledge of all aspects, well then, Lord, having practiced the six perfections, having accomplished the ten levels, the thirty-seven dharmas on the side of awakening, the fourteen emptinesses, the three gateways to liberation, the concentrations, the deliverances, the absorptions, up to the ten tathāgata powers, and eighty minor signs, and having stood in the clairvoyances, completed the ten levels, entered into the secure state of a bodhisattva, purified a buddhafield, and brought beings to maturity, how will bodhisattva great beings fully awaken to the knowledge of all aspects?
Blessed Lord, if the enlightenment of bodhisattva great beings does not engage in grasping or nongrasping…and the eighteen distinct qualities of the buddhas

div.p:
The twenty-third is, nyi khri
: “Lord, if a bodhisattva great being’s awakening is not practiced by taking anything up or not taking anything up, is not a practice of form, up to is not a practice of the knowledge of all aspects, well then, Lord, how will a bodhisattva great being practice the six perfections… practice the eighteen distinct attributes of a buddha?” This is followed by the question
“how will one complete the ten bodhisattva levels?” khri brgyad
, does not demarcate the two separate questions, twenty-two and twenty-three.

q.p: “The ten bodhisattva levels…?”
q.orig: How would they perfect the ten bodhisattva levels

div.p: The twenty-fourth is,

q.p: “Lord, what is the bodhisattva great beings’ path on which bodhisattva great beings who have to purify a buddhafield and bring beings to maturity practice?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, what path of enlightenment do bodhisattva great beings practice? What is the path of enlightenment of bodhisattva great beings who bring beings to maturation and refine the buddhafields

div.p: The twenty-fifth is,

q.p: “Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of giving bring beings to maturity?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings bring beings to maturation, while practicing the perfection of generosity

div.p: The twenty-sixth is,

q.p: “What is the path of a bodhisattva?”

div.p: The twenty-seventh is,

q.p: “Lord, if all dharmas are empty, how will bodhisattva great beings train in all dharmas?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, if all phenomena are empty, in what manner should bodhisattva great beings train

div.p: The twenty-eighth is,

q.p: “Lord, why are they not located?”
q.orig: Why do they not dwell in them

div.p: The twenty-ninth is,

q.p: “Lord, if all dharmas are unproduced, how will bodhisattva great beings produce a path to awakening?”
q.orig: Lord, if all dharmas are unproduced, well then, Lord, how will bodhisattva great beings produce a path to awakening?
Blessed Lord, if all phenomena are nonarising, how will bodhisattva great beings achieve the path of enlightenment

div.p: The thirtieth is,

q.p: “Lord, whether the tathāgatas arise or whether the tathāgatas do not arise, does the true dharmic nature of dharmas not remain?”
q.orig: On the other hand, Blessed Lord, is it not the case that, whether the tathāgatas have appeared or whether the tathāgatas have not appeared, the reality of phenomena dwells in that manner

div.p: The thirty-first is,

q.p: “Lord, do they reach awakening on that path that has been produced?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, is enlightenment then attained by a path that arises

div.p: Here, in a subsection, there are five questions. The five questions are: (1) do they reach awakening on that path that has been produced, (2) on that path that has not been produced, (3) on that path that has not been produced when it is not produced and is produced when it is produced, or (4) on that path that has neither been produced nor not produced, and (5) how do they reach awakening?
The thirty-second is,

q.p: “Lord, if just awakening is the path, would not bodhisattva great beings already have reached awakening?”
q.orig: Lord, if just awakening is the path, and just the path is awakening, well then, would not bodhisattva great beings already have reached awakening?
Blessed Lord, if enlightenment itself is the path and the path itself is enlightenment, then bodhisattva great beings will have already attained enlightenment

div.p: The thirty-third is,

q.p: “Lord, if all dharmas are isolated from their own intrinsic nature, well then, Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings purify a buddhafield?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, if all phenomena are devoid of inherent existence, how do bodhisattva great beings refine the buddhafields

div.p: The thirty-fourth is,

q.p: “Lord, what is the bodhisattva great beings’ final physical basis of suffering?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, what are the factors of the body that take on negative states

div.p: The thirty-fifth is,

q.p: “Lord, are bodhisattva great beings ‘destined’?” Emend D des shes to nges zhes.
q.orig: Lord, are bodhisattva great beings ‘destined’
Blessed Lord, are bodhisattva great beings certain to progress

div.p: The thirty-sixth is,

q.p: “Lord, to which group is one destined?”
q.orig: Lord, which group, the śrāvaka group or the pratyekabuddha group, are they destined to be in?
Are they certain to progress in the category of the śrāvakas, in the category of the pratyekabuddhas, in the category of the buddhas, or in what category

div.p: The thirty-seventh is,

q.p: “Lord, are bodhisattva great beings who have produced the first thought destined, or are those who are irreversible destined, or are those who are in a last existence destined?”
q.orig: Lord, are bodhisattva great beings who have produced the first thought destined [to be in the buddha group], or are those who are irreversible from awakening destined, or are those who are in a last existence destined?
Blessed Lord, are bodhisattva great beings who have first begun to set their mind on enlightenment certain to progress,…or else are irreversible bodhisattvas certain to progress

div.p: The thirty-eighth is,

q.p: “Lord, do bodhisattva great beings who have become destined take birth in terrible forms of life?”
q.orig: Lord, do bodhisattva great beings who have become destined take birth in terrible forms of life?
Blessed Lord, will bodhisattva great beings who are certain to progress be reborn in the inferior realms

div.p:
The thirty-ninth is, ’bum na 309a5, nyi khri (ga 305b7), le’u brgyad ma ca 302b2 de ltar nges pa, “a bodhisattva destined like that”; khri brgyad
, “a bodhisattva great being with such wholesome roots.”

q.p: “Lord, if destined bodhisattva great beings do not take birth in those places—namely, the negative ones—then where were those wholesome roots when the Tathāgata took birth in the animal world, as you personally have taught in your birth stories?”
q.orig: Lord, if bodhisattva great beings with such wholesome roots do not take birth in those places—namely, the negative ones—then where were those wholesome roots when the Tathāgata took birth in the animal world, as you personally have taught in your birth stories?

Blessed Lord, if bodhisattva great beings are endowed with the roots of such virtuous actions and they are not reborn in incomparably inferior places…why did the Tathāgata disclose his own past lives in the animal realm? Where did those roots of virtuous action go on such occasions

div.p: The fortieth is,

q.p: “Lord, in which wholesome dharmas do bodhisattva great beings stand when they appropriate such a body?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, maintaining which virtuous attributes do bodhisattva great beings acquire such corporeal forms

div.p: The forty-first is,

q.p: “Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings endowed with the bright dharmas take birth in terrible forms of life or in the animal world?”
q.orig: Lord, how, through a noble action without outflows, do bodhisattva great beings endowed with bright dharmas take birth in terrible forms of life or in the animal world?
Blessed Lord, how are bodhisattva great beings who possess such positive attributes of sublime beings, free from contaminants, born in the inferior realms or in the animal realm

div.p:
The forty-second is, The question is put in the mouth of the Lord at khri brgyad
, and also at ’bum na 310a2–3 and nyi khri .

q.p: “Lord, is a tathāgata a noble being without outflows?”
q.orig: Subhūti, are tathāgatas noble beings without outflows?
Subhūti, are the tathāgatas sublime and without contaminants

div.p: The forty-third is,

q.p: “Lord, standing in those bright dharmas, do bodhisattva great beings utilize such skillful means but still are not affected by those actions?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, in which pure attributes do bodhisattva great beings dwell when they employ such skill in means, but act without being tainted by such actions

div.p: The forty-fourth is,

q.p: “Lord, do bodhisattva great beings stand only in the perfection of wisdom but not in other dharmas?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, why do bodhisattva great beings, without abiding in other attributes, dwell in the perfection of wisdom alone when they employ such skill in means

div.p: The forty-fifth is,

q.p: “Lord, if the perfection of wisdom is empty of an intrinsic nature, how could all dharmas be included in the perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, if the perfection of wisdom is empty of inherent existence, in what way are all phenomena gathered within the perfection of wisdom

div.p: The forty-sixth is,

q.p: “Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings… find and produce within themselves the perfection of clairvoyance?”
q.orig: Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom, standing in the emptiness of all dharmas, find and produce within themselves the perfection of clairvoyance
Blessed Lord, when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom and dwell in the emptiness of all phenomena, in what extrasensory powers are they certain to progress

div.p:
The forty-seventh is, The question as it is found here is closest to a paraphrase of ’bum na 334b, nyi khri (ga 314a7), le’u brgyad ma ca 309b4–5: bcom ldan ’das byang chub sems dpa’i sems dpa’ chen po lam gyi yan lag yongs su rdzogs par bgyis shing / bla na myed pa yang dag par rdzogs pa’i byang chub tu mngon par rdzogs par ’tshang rgya bar ’gyur ba’i lam de dag gang lags. “Lord, what are the paths, when the branches of those paths have been completed, through which a bodhisattva great being will fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening?” The question at khri brgyad
, is: “Lord, what are the branches of the bodhisattva great beings’ awakening, having completed which the bodhisattva great beings will fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening?”

q.p: “Lord, what are the paths for fully awakening to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening?”
q.orig: Lord, what are the branches of the bodhisattva great beings’ awakening, having completed which the bodhisattva great beings will fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening?
Blessed Lord, what are those aspects of the path that bodhisattva great beings should perfect, and through which they will attain consummate buddhahood in unsurpassed, complete enlightenment

div.p: The forty-eighth is,

q.p: “Lord, if all dharmas are empty of their own marks, how can you apprehend specific features in all dharmas that are empty of their own marks and make the distinctions, ‘This is a being in hell’…?”
q.orig: Lord, if all dharmas are empty of their own marks, how can you apprehend specific features in all dharmas that are empty of their own marks and make the distinctions, ‘This is a being in hell

Blessed Lord, if all phenomena are empty of intrinsic defining characteristics, how can one make distinctions and differentiate between these phenomena that are empty of intrinsic defining characteristics, saying, ‘This is a denizen of the hells

div.p: The forty-ninth is,

q.p: “Does the Lord, having fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening, apprehend the five forms of life in saṃsāra?”
q.orig: does the Blessed Lord see cyclic existence with its five classes of living beings, having attained consummate buddhahood in unsurpassed, complete enlightenment

div.p: The fiftieth is,

q.p: “Lord, does a tathāgata apprehend bright, or dark, or bright and dark, or neither bright nor dark dharmas?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, do the tathāgatas apprehend phenomena that are negative, phenomena that are positive, phenomena that may be negative or positive, and phenomena that are neither negative nor positive

div.p: The fifty-first is,

q.p: “Lord, if all phenomena are empty of their own marks, well then, how do bodhisattva great beings fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening and free beings from the five forms of life in saṃsāra?”
q.orig: If all phenomena are empty of intrinsic defining characteristics, how do bodhisattva great beings, having attained consummate buddhahood in unsurpassed, complete enlightenment, liberate beings from cyclic existence with its five classes of beings

div.p: The fifty-second is,

q.p: “Lord, will beings pass into complete nirvāṇa on account of knowing suffering or will they pass into complete nirvāṇa on account of suffering?”
q.orig: Lord, will beings pass into complete nirvāṇa on account of knowing suffering or will they pass into complete nirvāṇa on account of suffering?
Blessed Lord, do they pass into final nirvāṇa through the cognition of suffering or do they pass into final nirvāṇa through suffering

div.p: The fifty-third is,

q.p: “Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom practice in order to awaken to the truths?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom, how do they practice so as to realize the truths

div.p: The fifty-fourth is,

q.p: “Lord, what are ‘all dharmas as they really are’?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, what is the definitive nature of all phenomena, just as they are

div.p: The fifty-fifth is,

q.p: “In that case, Lord, is awakening not a real thing?”
q.orig: In that case, Lord, is awakening a nonexistent thing
Indeed, enlightenment is a nonentity

div.p: The fifty-sixth is,

q.p: “Lord, if all dharmas are in their nature not real things, if they have not been made by buddhas… why in these dharmas is there a distinction made between ‘these are beings in hell, these in the animal world’?”
q.orig: Lord, if all dharmas are the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature, if they have not been made by buddhas, have not been made by pratyekabuddhas, have not been made by worthy ones, have not been made by non-returners, have not been made by once-returners, have not been made by stream enterers, and have not been made by those bodhisattva great beings who are practicing for this awakening, well then, Lord, why in these dharmas is there a distinction made between them, or a presentation of them thus: ‘These are beings in hell, these in the animal world

Blessed Lord, if all phenomena are nonentities‍—that is to say, if they have not been created by the buddhas…how, with respect to all phenomena, could one differentiate and establish, ‘These are denizens of the hells. These belong to the animal realm

div.p: The fifty-seventh is,

q.p: “Lord, is there some real basis called suchness and unmistaken suchness that foolish, ordinary people stand on and settle down on as ‘a real basis’?”
q.orig: Lord, is there some real basis called…that was or is, that foolish, ordinary people stand on and settle down on as ‘a real basis’
Blessed Lord, is there an entity that is said to be the real nature or the unmistaken real nature, such as that to which ordinary, simple people become attached and fixated

div.p: The fifty-eighth is,

q.p: “Lord, for someone who sees reality, defilement does not happen… well then, what purification has the Lord been speaking about?”
q.orig: Lord, for someone who sees reality, defilement does not happen and purification does not happen, and even for someone who does not see reality, defilement does not happen and purification does not happen. This is because, Lord, all dharmas are the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature. So, there is no defilement and there is no purification for something that does not exist, and there is no defilement and there is no purification even for something that does exist. Lord, if there is no defilement and there is no purification even for something that exists in itself, and if there is no defilement and there is no purification even for something that is the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature, well then, what is that purification the Lord has been speaking about?”
Blessed Lord, just as those who see authentically are neither afflicted nor purified…what is that which the Blessed Lord has described as purification

div.p: The fifty-ninth is,

q.p: “Lord, what is the sameness of all dharmas?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, what is the sameness of all phenomena

div.p: The sixtieth is,

q.p: “Lord, if all dharmas are like an illusion… how do bodhisattvas… produce the thought of unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening?”
q.orig: Lord, if all dharmas are like an illusion, like a dream, like an echo, like an apparition, like a reflection in the mirror, like a mirage, like a city of the gandharvas, and like a magical creation, well then, how, given that dharmas are like an illusion, up to like a magical creation, are nonexistent things and are not materially existent, do bodhisattva great beings produce the thought of unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening

Blessed Lord, if all phenomena are like a dream, like an echo, like an optical aberration, like a mirage, like a magical display, and like a phantom emanation, how do bodhisattva great beings, with respect to all phenomena that are nonentities and insubstantial, like a dream, like an echo, like an optical aberration, like a mirage, like a magical display, and like a phantom emanation…themselves set their minds on unsurpassed, complete enlightenment

div.p: The sixty-first is,

q.p: “Lord, is the dharma a tathāgata has fully awakened to, fully awakened to as an ordinary convention or as an ultimate?”
q.orig: Lord, is the dharma a tathāgata has fully awakened to, fully awakened to as an ordinary convention or as an ultimate?
Blessed Lord, regarding this attainment of consummate buddhahood by the tathāgatas, is consummate buddhahood attained by way of mundane convention or, otherwise, by way of ultimate reality

div.p: The sixty-second is,

q.p: “Lord, given that dharmas are in their nature nonexistent, what is this ‘sameness of dharmas’?”
q.orig: Lord, given that dharmas are the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature, what is this ‘sameness of dharmas’?
Blessed Lord, how are phenomena that have the nature of nonentity not entities if it is said that all phenomena have the nature of sameness

div.p: The sixty-third is,

q.p: “Lord, is that sameness of dharmas not within the range even of a tathāgata?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, is the sameness of phenomena not even an object for the tathāgatas

div.p: The sixty-fourth is,

q.p: “Lord, is a tathāgata, worthy one, perfectly complete buddha not in control of the entire range of dharmas?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, do the tathāgatas, arhats, completely awakened buddhas not have mastery over of all phenomenal objects

div.p:
The sixty-fifth is, The question at khri brgyad
, is: “Lord, if in the sameness of all dharmas ‘this is an ordinary person, this is a stream enterer,’ up to ‘this is a pratyekabuddha, this is a bodhisattva,’ up to ‘this is a tathāgata, worthy one, perfectly complete buddha’ all cannot be apprehended, in that case would foolish ordinary people, faith-followers and dharma-followers, stream enterers, once-returners, non-returners, worthy ones, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and even tathāgatas, worthy ones, perfectly complete buddhas not have specific features?”

q.p: “Lord, if, in the sameness of all dharmas, ‘this is an ordinary person…’ all cannot be apprehended, in that case would foolish ordinary people… not have specific features?”
q.orig: Lord, if, in the sameness of all dharmas, ‘this is an ordinary person, this is a stream enterer,’ up to ‘this is a pratyekabuddha, this is a bodhisattva,’ up to ‘this is a tathāgata, worthy one, perfectly complete buddha’ all cannot be apprehended, in that case foolish, ordinary people, faith followers and Dharma followers, stream enterers, once-returners, non-returners, worthy ones, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and even tathāgatas, worthy ones, perfectly complete buddhas would not have specific features.

Blessed Lord, if in the sameness of all phenomena there is no apprehending of the conceptual thoughts enabling one to say, ‘This is an ordinary person. This one is entering the stream to nirvāṇa. These ones are destined for only one more rebirth, no longer subject to rebirth, an arhat, a pratyekabuddha, and a bodhisattva. This one is a tathāgata, arhat, completely awakened buddha,’ in that case there would be no distinction between ordinary people

div.p: The sixty-sixth is,

q.p: “Lord, if, in the sameness of dharmas, foolish ordinary people… do not have specific features, well then, Lord, from where do the Three Jewels—the Buddha Jewel, Dharma Jewel, and Saṅgha Jewel—appear in the world?”
q.orig: Lord, if, in the sameness of dharmas, foolish, ordinary people, faith followers, up to tathāgatas, worthy ones, perfectly complete buddhas do not have specific features, well then, Lord, from where do the Three Jewels—the Buddha Jewel, Dharma Jewel, and Saṅgha Jewel—appear in the world?

Blessed Lord, if in the sameness of all phenomena there is no distinction between ordinary people, those entering the stream to nirvāṇa, those destined for only one more rebirth, those no longer subject to rebirth, arhats, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and tathāgatas, arhats, completely awakened buddhas, why, Blessed Lord, do the Three Precious Jewels‍—the precious jewel of the Buddha, the precious jewel of the Dharma, and the precious jewel of the Saṅgha‍—emerge in the world

div.p: The sixty-seventh is,

q.p: “Lord, is the way in which a tathāgata does not move from the sameness of dharmas…?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, just as the tathāgatas do not stir from the sameness of phenomena

div.p: The sixty-eighth is,

q.p: “Lord, if just that true dharmic nature of dharmas is just that true dharmic nature of ordinary people… given that those—namely, form…—have different marks… how do those dharmas with different marks come to have one mark?”
q.orig: Lord, if just that true dharmic nature of all dharmas is just that true dharmic nature of ordinary people…how do those dharmas with different marks come to have one mark?

Blessed Lord, if the sameness of phenomena that ordinary people have is itself the sameness of phenomena that followers on account of faith have, and that followers of the Dharma, those of the eighth level, those entering the stream to nirvāṇa, those destined for only one more rebirth, those no longer subject to rebirth, arhats, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas have, and if it is itself the sameness of phenomena that tathāgatas, arhats, completely awakened buddhas have, in that case, Blessed Lord, how would all those phenomena with dissimilar defining characteristics‍…Blessed Lord, have unique defining characteristics that are different from one another

div.p: The sixty-ninth is,

q.p: “Lord, is that true nature of dharmas a compounded phenomenon or is it an uncompounded phenomenon?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, is that reality conditioned, or is it unconditioned

div.p: The seventieth is,

q.p: “Lord, if the sameness of all dharmas is empty of a basic nature, then no dharma does anything, so how, while dharmas are not doing anything and are not anything at all, do bodhisattvas not move from the ultimate but still work for the welfare of beings?”
q.orig: Lord, if the sameness of all dharmas is empty of a basic nature, then no dharma does anything, so how, while dharmas are not doing anything and are not anything at all, do bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom not move from the ultimate but still work for the welfare of beings

Blessed Lord, the sameness of all phenomena is empty of inherent existence‍—there is nothing at all that does anything to anything. Since all phenomena do nothing whatsoever and are nothing whatsoever, how is it that, when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not stir from ultimate truth…but still act for the sake of all beings

div.p:
The seventy-first is, khri brgyad
. I have supplied the referent “emptiness” from the context.

q.p: “Lord, of what is emptiness empty?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, of what is that [unconditioned expanse] empty

div.p: The seventy-second is,

q.p: “Lord, if those ordinary dharmas are magical creations, are these extraordinary dharmas… magical creations as well?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, if mundane phenomena are phantom emanations, are supramundane phenomena…‍not also similar to a phantom emanation

div.p:
The seventy-third is, khri brgyad
. The part left out is: “and those other dharmas—the result of stream enterer, result of once-returner, result of non-returner, and state of a worthy one—also magical creations? And are those other dharmas—the Pratyekabuddha level, the Buddha level, and the elimination of all residual impressions, connections, and afflictions—are those dharmas…”

q.p: “Lord, are this ‘abandonment’… also magical creations as well?”
q.orig: Lord, are this ‘abandonment,’ and those other dharmas—the result of stream enterer, result of once-returner, result of non-returner, and state of a worthy one—also magical creations? And are those other dharmas—the pratyekabuddha level, the buddha level, and the elimination of all residual impressions, connections, and afflictions—also magical creations?
Blessed Lord, are the attributes of ‘abandonment…also phantom emanations

div.p: The seventy-fourth is,

q.p: “Lord, what is the dharma that is not a magical creation?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, what is not a phantom emanation

div.p: The seventy-fifth is,

q.p: “And what, Lord, is that?”
q.orig: What is that

div.p: The seventy-sixth is,

q.p: “Lord, according to what you have said…”
q.orig: Lord…according to what you have said
The Blessed One has said

div.p: And the seventy-seventh is,

q.p: “Lord, if a person who is beginning the work is going to understand the emptiness of an intrinsic nature, how should they be advised and instructed?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, how should an individual who is a beginner be instructed and advised, so as to understand the emptiness of inherent existence

div.p: You should know that all these questions have been asked for the sake of irreversible bodhisattvas seated in the retinue and for the benefit of persons in the future.

div.head: The deep places
div.p: Among these, in regard to

q.p:
“Subhūti, form is deep,” nyi khri
; khri brgyad
zab pa.
q.orig: Subhūti, it is because form is deep
Subhūti, physical forms are profound

div.p: here form is being used as a word for the suchness of form. Therefore, it asks

q.p: “why is form deep?”
q.orig: why, Subhūti, is…deep[8]
how physical forms are profound

div.p: and says,

q.p: “Subhūti… just as the suchness of form is deep, so too is form deep,”
q.orig: Just as the suchness of…deep[10]
physical forms are as profound as the real nature of physical forms

div.p: indicating that it is just suchness. This means that form is deep in the way that suchness is deep.
What is intended by the question,

q.p: “Lord, what is the suchness of form like?”
q.orig: Lord, what is the suchness of…like[1]
Blessed Lord, how is the real nature of physical forms

div.p: It is asking how, given that “suchness” is without attributes and hence is not the mark of form and is not contingent on form either, can you use the word form and so on in “the suchness of form, suchness of feeling”?

q.p: “Subhūti, there is no form in the suchness of form, and there is no suchness of form other than form. The suchness of form is like that.”
q.orig: “Subhūti,” replied the Lord, “there is no form in the suchness of form, and there is no suchness of form other than form. The suchness of form is like that.

Subhūti,” replied the Blessed One, “in the real nature of physical forms there are indeed no physical forms…nor is there any real nature other than physical forms‍—such is the real nature of physical forms

div.p: Having eliminated falsely imagined phenomena, that thoroughly established suchness that is other than falsely imagined phenomena is separated from all mental images so it is not suitable to express it with the word “form” and so on. This is teaching that the name form and so on is superimposed onto suchness when it has stains, that it is not expressible as just that form and so on that foolish ordinary persons imagine, or other than that, in order to designate it during that period.

q.p: “Made to turn back from form, and nirvāṇa has been pointed out”—
q.orig: have indeed turned away from physical forms, and have also pointed toward nirvāṇa!

div.p: with that “form is deep” they are made to turn back from falsely imagined form. “Nirvāṇa,” the true dharmic nature of form, “has been pointed out.”

The illustration of the man with a strong libido is easy to understand. khri brgyad
–.

q.p: “fill up as many world systems as there are sand particles in the Gaṅgā River with the wholesome roots appropriated in a single day … it still would not approach what remains of those wholesome roots even by one hundredth part”
q.orig: fill up as many world systems as there are sand particles in the Gaṅgā River with the wholesome roots appropriated in a single day by a bodhisattva great being thus preoccupied with and dwelling in the dwelling of this deep perfection of wisdom as it has been taught, it still would not approach what remains of those wholesome roots even by a hundredth part,

in a single day acquire roots of virtuous action such that those accrued by having filled world systems numerous as the grains of sand of the river Gaṅgā [with gifts] could not come anywhere near even a hundredth part of their residue of the roots of virtuous action

div.p: means that even if you were to fill up as many world systems as there are sand particles in the Gaṅgā River with those wholesome roots accumulated in a single day, there would be many parts left over from the one part of the wholesome roots that filled up as many world systems as the sand particles in the Gaṅgā River. That part of the wholesome roots that filled up the world systems would not approach even a hundredth part of what remains of those wholesome roots. The wholesome roots of an irreversible bodhisattva are so vast that an immense amount of them would be left over even after using them to fill up that many world systems.

q.p:
“If… separated from the perfection of wisdom [that bodhisattva] were to… cultivate wisdom” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: if a bodhisattva great being separated from the perfection of wisdom remaining for as many eons as there are sand particles in the Gaṅgā River were to give gifts, guard morality, cultivate patience, make an effort at perseverance, become absorbed in concentration, and cultivate wisdom,

“Subhūti, when certain bodhisattva great beings, lacking the perfection of wisdom, and living for eons equal in number to the grains of sand of the river Gaṅgā, offer generosity, maintain ethical discipline, practice tolerance, undertake perseverance, become absorbed in meditative concentration, and cultivate wisdom, do you think that their merits would increase manifold on that basis?”

div.p: means if, without the wisdom of the knowledge of path aspects that sees what cannot be apprehended, they were to cultivate just ordinary wisdom.
Take

q.p:
“this perfection of wisdom is the mother of the bodhisattvas” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: this perfection of wisdom is the mother of the bodhisattva great beings
this perfection of wisdom is the mother of bodhisattva great beings

div.p: as the knowledge of path aspects.

q.p:
“Lord, the Lord has said, ‘Whatever merit has been accumulated, it is all imaginary,’ so how will a son of a good family or daughter of a good family make a lot of merit?” khri brgyad
. This is Subhūti’s fourth question.
q.orig: Lord, the Lord has said, ‘Whatever merit has been accumulated, it is all imaginary,’ so how will a son of a good family or daughter of a good family create a lot of merit?
Blessed Lord, since the Blessed One has said that phenomena that are not subject to conditioning are imaginary, how…could the merit of those noble sons or noble daughters increase manifold

div.p: Whatever the composition of the merit bodhisattvas separated from the perfection of wisdom accumulated it is falsely imagined, so the merit will not increase a lot.

q.p: “What has been accumulated does not exist,”

div.p: is a nonexistent thing. Since it is a nonexistent thing,

q.p: “they will not be able to enter into the right view and the secure state of a bodhisattva,”
q.orig: cannot generate the authentic view or even enter into the maturity [of the bodhisattvas]

div.p: and so on. He is asking how if they are not able to do anything could that be correct.

q.p:
“What [they]… have accumulated appears as just empty, appears as just in vain,” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: what the bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom have accumulated appears as just empty, appears as just in vain,
those gifts of bodhisattva great beings who practice the perfection of wisdom are not subject to conditioning‍—they are declared to be just empty

div.p: and so on. This is saying, “I do not say that they increase merit by accumulating it,” and “I do not say that they increase merit by not accumulating it” either. How then? How should whatever the merit that bodhisattvas have to accumulate that has been obtained always in all respects be understood analytically as “just empty, in vain,” and as

q.p: “just ringing hollow?”
q.orig: just ring hollow
to be just hollow

div.p: When they understand analytically like that, because they

q.p: “are inseparable from the perfection of wisdom… to that extent they make infinite, incalculable merit.”
q.orig: are inseparable from the perfection of wisdom. Subhūti, to the extent that bodhisattva great beings are inseparable from the perfection of wisdom, to that extent they create incalculable, infinite, immeasurable merit.
Insofar as bodhisattva great beings do not lack the perfection of wisdom, their incalculable, inestimable, and immeasurable merits will increase

q.p:
“What are the specific features…?” khri brgyad
. This is Subhūti’s fifth question.
q.orig: what are the distinctions

div.p: He asks this as an aside because it is contextually appropriate.

q.p: “Subhūti, the incalculable is that which has no enumeration.”
q.orig: The incalculable is that which has no enumeration,
the term incalculable suggests that the number of conditioned elements and unconditioned elements cannot be approximated

div.p: That which cannot be enumerated by a word is incalculable;

q.p: “the infinite”
q.orig: inestimable[2]

div.p: cannot be measured; and

q.p: “the immeasurable”
q.orig: immeasurable[2]

div.p: cannot be delimited as just this, even by the force of a calculation. Its measure cannot be apprehended. All three, furthermore, are particulars of counting.

q.p: “A calculable element or an incalculable element”

div.p: means

q.p:
“the compounded element and the uncompounded element.” nyi khri
; Gilgit 575.12–13 asaṃkhyeyam api [emend to iti] subhūte yat saṃkhyām nopeti saṃskṛte vā dhātā ca [delete ca] asaṃskrte vā dhatau.
q.orig: conditioned elements and unconditioned elements

q.p:
“Form is also empty so it is infinite, incalculable, and immeasurable.” nyi khri
; cf. khri brgyad
. This is the response to Subhūti’s sixth question.
q.orig: form is empty, it is incalculable, infinite, and immeasurable;
physical forms are empty, they are incalculable, inestimable, and immeasurable

div.p: A number, measure, and so on exist for falsely imagined phenomena, but in the emptiness element they do not exist. They are included in synonyms of emptiness. Therefore, there is the word “also,” in “form is also empty,” in order to make it into a particular. On account of great compassion, it is

q.p:
“an exposition in harmony with what causes a tathāgata’s teaching.” khri brgyad
. The “great compassion” is part of the extract according to le’u brgyad ma ca 6a2 thugs rje chen po’i rgyu mthun gyis bstan pa; cf. Abhi­samayālaṃkāra 4.55c (Wogihara p. 710) kṛpāniṣyandabhūtās te.
q.orig: make manifest the teaching of the tathāgatas

div.p: This means that it is conventionally an “exposition” in harmony with the cause, compassion.

q.p: “Lord, all phenomena are simply inexpressible?”
q.orig: what you, Lord, have said is that all phenomena are simply inexpressible.
all phenomena, Blessed Lord, are inexpressible

div.p: Earlier it explained that just the true nature of dharmas is inexpressible. Now it teaches that all dharmas, not different from the true nature of dharmas, are simply inexpressible too.

q.p:
“Lord, does an inexpressible reality know increase or decrease?” khri brgyad
. This is Subhūti’s eighth question.
q.orig: “Lord, does an inexpressible reality know increase or decrease?”
Blessed Lord, can an object that is inexpressible increase or decrease

div.p: This teaches the following: it asks, if inexpressible is an expression for emptiness, and emptiness does not increase because of bright dharmas and does not decrease because of dark dharmas, and if the perfections and so on also have no increase or decrease, well then, on account of what cause will

q.p: “the knowledge of all aspects come with the good fortune of fully awakening to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening?”
q.orig: the knowledge of all aspects will not come with the good fortune of fully awakening to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening either
If all-aspect omniscience were nonexistent, who would attain consummate buddhahood in unsurpassed, complete enlightenment

div.p:
Having asked that, the final part of the passage, khri brgyad
.

q.p: “they will make a dedication just like unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening,”
q.orig: they make this dedication definitively, in accordance with unsurpassed, complete enlightenment

div.p: teaches that it will happen because of the power of dedication with skillful means.

q.p: “Lord, what is unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening?” This is Subhūti’s tenth question.
q.orig: Blessed Lord, what is the nature of unsurpassed, complete enlightenment

div.p: It has as its essential nature the emptiness not different from form and so on. The inquiry is made so there will be a further explanation.

q.p: “[They] should practice the perfection of wisdom like that, by way of no increase or decrease”
q.orig: bodhisattva great beings should practice the perfection of wisdom like that, by way of no increase or decrease.
bodhisattva great beings should practice the perfection of wisdom by way of nonincrease and nondecrease

div.p: teaches that just this alone is the practice of the perfection of wisdom.

div.head: Which moment of thought causes awakening?

q.p: “Lord, do bodhisattva great beings fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening because of the first production of the thought, or do they fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening because of a later production of the thought?”
q.orig: Lord, do bodhisattva great beings fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening because of the first production of the thought, or do they fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening because of a later production of the thought?

Blessed Lord, do bodhisattva great beings…attain consummate buddhahood in unsurpassed, complete enlightenment through their initial setting of the mind on enlightenment, or else do bodhisattva great beings attain consummate buddhahood in unsurpassed, complete enlightenment through their final setting of the mind on enlightenment

div.p: This inquiry is in the part of the text to do with the deep places. Given that those who have accumulated wholesome roots will fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening, how will the wholesome roots for that come to be accumulated? Here, do bodhisattvas fully awaken through the power of the initial production of the thought—produced prior to the first of three incalculable eons—or do they fully awaken through the power of the second, or the third, or the last of all the productions of the thought when they are seated at the site of awakening? In regard to those, they do not fully awaken because of a single thought, because it does not have such power and the rest of the accumulation of merit would be meaningless. It is also not because of all the thoughts either, because they are not suited to accumulation, since they are destined to perish instant by instant. That is what it teaches, so there the Lord gives

q.p: “the illustration of an oil lamp”
q.orig: I will furnish an illustration. What do you think, Subhūti? When a wick is being lit up by the flame of an oil lamp,
in the case of a burning oil lamp

div.p: saying that when the wick of an oil lamp is burned up, it has been burned up through the power of all the instants of flame, even though each is destined to perish instant by instant. Similarly, it teaches that full awakening too is through the power of all the thoughts, intending that even though they are momentary it is by way of accumulated habit formation. Literally, “by way of the accumulation of residual impressions left by volitional factors.”

q.p: “The Śuklavipaśyanā level
q.orig: the level of bright insight

div.p: is when there is special insight;

q.p: “the Gotra level”
q.orig: the level of the spiritual family

div.p: is the highest ordinary dharma;

q.p: “the Aṣṭamaka level”
q.orig: Aṣṭamaka level
the eighth-lowest level

div.p: is the path of the stream enterers;

q.p: “the Darśana level”
q.orig: Darśana level
the level of insight

div.p: is their result, the level of seeing;

q.p: “the Tanū level”
q.orig: Tanū level
the level of attenuated refinement

div.p: is the once-returner level because it has attenuated attachment to sense objects and malice;

q.p: “the Vītarāga level”
q.orig: Vītarāga level
the level of no attachment

div.p: is the non-returner level because attachment and malice have been stopped;

q.p: “the Kṛtāvin level”
q.orig: Kṛtāvin level
the level of [an arhat’s] spiritual achievement

div.p: is the state of a worthy one because the work has been done;

q.p: “the Pratyekabuddha level”
q.orig: the level of the pratyekabuddhas

div.p: is a pratyekabuddha’s awakening;

q.p: “the Bodhisattva level”
q.orig: the level of the bodhisattvas

div.p: is the knowledge of path aspects; and

q.p: “the Buddha level”
q.orig: the level of the buddhas

div.p: is the knowledge of all aspects. K, N omit.

q.p:
“Will that thought which has stopped be produced again?” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: do you think that thoughts that have ceased will arise again

div.p: and so on, again teaches the deep state.

q.p:
“What has stopped will not be produced. What has been produced is subject to stopping. What is subject to stopping will not stop. It will remain just as suchness does. It will not be unmoved.” This is a paraphrase of khri brgyad
–.
q.orig: will that thought which has stopped be produced again?
do you think that thoughts that have ceased will arise again

div.p: That is a deep place. Take “that which has stopped will not be produced again” as stopped in its intrinsic nature—the uncompounded. Śrījagattalanivāsin’s Āmnayānusāriṇī, man ngag gi rjes su brang ba Degé Tengyur (shes phyin, ba), 231a–b provides helpful glosses for this part of the text. Take “that which has been produced is not Perhaps emend chos can ma yin to chos can yin, “that which has been produced is subject to stopping.” subject to stopping” as the compounded. It says “that which is subject to stopping will not stop” because there is not a second stopping. Take “it will remain just as suchness does” as suchness. As for “it will not be unmoved,” it says that because it has no intrinsic nature.

q.p:
“Subhūti, what do you think, is that thought also suchness?” nyi khri
; khri brgyad
omits yang.
q.orig: Subhūti, what do you think, is that thought suchness?
Subhūti, do you think that the mind is also the real nature

div.p: is asking, “Is compounded thought the intrinsic nature of suchness?”

q.p: “It is not, Lord,”
q.orig: No, Blessed Lord

div.p: again says, “Because it is together with stains it is not the intrinsic nature of suchness.”

q.p: “Is that thought other than suchness?”
q.orig: mind is other than the real nature

div.p: is asking, “Is compounded thought other than suchness?” Subhūti again says,

q.p: “It is not, Lord,”
q.orig: No, Blessed Lord

div.p: because a falsely imagined phenomenon is not suitable to be described as just exactly a thoroughly established phenomenon or as different from it.

q.p: “Is thought in suchness?”
q.orig: Is the real nature present in the mind

div.p: and

q.p: “is suchness in thought?”
q.orig: Is the mind present in the real nature

div.p: are asking if they are a real basis and what is based on that relative to each other.

q.p: “They are not, Lord,”
q.orig: it is not, Lord
No, Blessed Lord

div.p: again says that the two—a falsely imagined phenomenon and a thoroughly established phenomenon—do not exist as a real basis and what is based on that.

q.p: “Does suchness see suchness?”
q.orig: Does the real nature observe the real nature

div.p: This question intends: “Does that thought see all phenomena?” He again says,

q.p: “It does not, Lord,”
q.orig: No, Blessed Lord

div.p: because in the state of suchness an apprehended and apprehender do not exist.

q.p:
“Lord, someone practicing like that is not practicing anything at all” Golden 335a3, citing nyi khri , khri brgyad
.
q.orig: Blessed Lord, those who practice in that manner do not practice anything at all

div.p: teaches that they have not practiced anything at all.

q.p: “They practice in the ultimate where there are no habitual dualistic ideas.”
q.orig: They engage in ultimate reality where dualistic habitual thoughts are nonexistent

div.p: There is “they practice” and a second, “they do not.”

q.p: “Has the perception of a causal sign disintegrated because of them?”
q.orig: do you think that they have annihilated the perception of conceptual images

div.p: This means do they make the perception of a causal sign nonexistent? He again says,

q.p: “They do not, Lord,”
q.orig: It has not, Lord,
No, Blessed Lord

div.p: because an idea like “I will make the perception of a causal sign disintegrate” does not arise. This teaches that the habitual idea, such a conceptualization, is nonexistent. through the power of cultivating the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness meditative stabilizations they also cure themselves of their habit of perceiving a causal sign.

q.p:
“[They] bring beings to maturity with those… meditative stabilizations,” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom thus bring beings to maturity with those three meditative stabilizations.
bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom, dwell in the three meditative stabilities, and bring beings to maturity

div.p: through the power of skillful means. That they will personally behold emptiness and so on, and bring beings to maturity as well, is the power of skillful means.

div.head: Karma in a dream and the waking state

q.p: “When [they]… have become absorbed in the three meditative stabilizations on emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness in a dream, do they improve on account of the perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: when bodhisattva great beings have become absorbed in the three meditative stabilizations on emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness in a dream, do they improve on account of the perfection of wisdom?”
when certain bodhisattva great beings are absorbed in the three meditative stabilities of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness in their dreams, are they enhanced by the perfection of wisdom

div.p: Having set the scene for the deep places, the two elders expound on just those meditative stabilizations that have gone before. The two elders, Śāriputra and Subhūti, discussed how a bodhisattva, for the sake of those who benefit from such a model, models the meditations on emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness that deliver a śrāvaka to nirvāṇa, while employing the skillful means to avoid actually entering nirvāṇa. Śāriputra asks intending this: If all phenomena cannot be apprehended, then, when bodhisattvas are absorbed in the three meditative stabilizations in a dream, it makes sense that they should improve on account of the perfection of wisdom. But if the perfection of wisdom does not increase in a dream and does when they have stopped sleeping, in that case there is a certain distinction between phenomena that exist and that do not exist in a dream, and when they have not fallen asleep.

q.p: “Venerable Śāriputra, if they improve on account of having meditated during the day, they improve in a dream like that as well?”
q.orig: Venerable Śāradvatīputra,” replied Subhūti, “if they are enhanced by cultivating it during the day, they would also be enhanced by cultivating it in their dreams

div.p: He is asking a question. Then the elder Subhūti teaches that here, when bodhisattvas are dreaming and also when they have stopped sleeping phenomena cannot be apprehended—they are similar in a dream and also when sleep has stopped. “A dream” and “the day” also are just merely constructed in thought. Both a dream and not being asleep are similar. Therefore, given that the two—the day and the dream—are similar, it explains that if the meditative stabilization when they have not fallen asleep increases wisdom, then the meditative stabilization in a dream increases wisdom as well.

q.p: “Venerable Subhūti, when bodhisattva great beings have made some karma in a dream is there an accumulation or diminution in their karma?”
q.orig: when bodhisattva great beings perform an action in their dreams, will that action accumulate or diminish

div.p: What is the elder Śāriputra’s intention? He is asking: if phenomena are similar when not asleep and in a dream, well then, in regard to the giving that is the giving and so on in a dream, and also the result of stream enterer that is reached in a dream, with the earlier of the two is there or is there not the accumulation of good karma and with the later the finishing of the karma?
Then the elder Subhūti says,

q.p: “The Lord has said that all phenomena are like a dream, so there is no accumulation or diminution there,”
q.orig: the Blessed One has said, all phenomena are like dreams, then there would be no accumulation or diminution

div.p: and so on. He is saying that when “accumulation and diminution” are other than something real, all phenomena are thus dream-like, so both in a dream and when not asleep that karma and that agent are totally nonexistent. And in that case, why would you say there is an accumulation or a diminution from them? It says

q.p: “you cannot apprehend any phenomenon in a dream that is accumulated or diminished.”
q.orig: there is no accumulation or diminution of anything at all that is apprehended in dreams

div.p: It is teaching this: If somebody in a dream sees something filled up with river water, or sees a dried-up lake, is there an accumulation or a diminution from that? Or is it the case that just as there is both no accumulation or diminution there in a dream, similarly even during the day when they have not fallen asleep there is no accumulation or a diminution at all, either.
Then the elder Śāriputra says,

q.p: “If it is thought about in a certain way, on waking there is an accumulation or reduction in one’s karma.”
q.orig: if it is thought about in a certain way, on waking there is also an accumulation or reduction in one’s karma,

div.p: “I am not speaking based on bodhisattvas who view things as not findable, who are free from falsely imagining things, but rather based on present-day novices caught up in falsely imagining things. If, when they wake up and think intentionally about an act that they have done in their dream and rejoice in it, is there accumulation of or diminution in that karma done at night?” That is what Śāriputra is asking. He therefore intends a distinction between when they are in a dream and when they have has not fallen asleep.
Then the elder Subhūti says,

q.p: “Venerable Śāriputra, what would you say about the karma of someone who committed a murder during the day, and someone who dreamed about committing the murder and on waking thought, ‘I killed him. It is excellent that I killed him’?”
q.orig: If one who has committed an act of killing by day and one who has committed an act of killing in a dream were to think, ‘I have killed. It is right that I have killed,’ in that case, Venerable Śāradvatīputra, what would you say about that action

div.p: This is saying that it is wrong, but what is intended? A certain man during the day or in a dream murders someone. When the murder has been committed, if he rejoices in those two actions intentionally with his thinking mind is there more maturation from rejoicing in the action of murder during the day or is there more maturation from rejoicing in the action done in a dream?
Then Śāriputra says,

q.p: “Venerable Subhūti, karma does not happen without an objective support; intention does not happen without an objective support.”
q.orig: no action will occur without an objective support. No volition will occur without an objective support

div.p: It intends to say that a murder in a dream is in its nature a nonexistent thing, so a thought apprehending that is apprehending something that is a nonexistent thing. It therefore has no additional maturation.
Then the elder Subhūti says

q.p: “exactly so!”
q.orig: it is so
