div.p: rejoicing in Śāriputra’s words. So, what is this teaching? It is teaching that if karma does not happen without an objective support, well then, what Śāriputra said before, “If it is thought about in a certain way, on waking there is an accumulation or reduction from that karma,” is not correct. Here the rest of the argument is this: Were karma not to happen without an objective support, in that case, because what is done in a dream has no objective support but what is done when one has not fallen asleep does have an objective support, there would therefore be a distinction between the two—a dream and when one has not fallen asleep—so the statement “all dharmas are dream-like” gets damaged. So, to deal with that argument the elder Subhūti says,

q.p: “The intellect engages with the seen, the heard, the thought—something one has been aware of; the intellect does not engage with the unseen, the unheard, the unthought—a thing of which one has not been conscious. There, one intellectual act gets hold of defilement. Another intellectual act gets hold of purification.”
q.orig: The mind engages with phenomena that are seen, heard, thought of, and appraised…The mind does not engage with phenomena that are unseen, unheard, not thought of, and not appraised. On that basis some minds grasp afflicted mental states, and some minds grasp purified mental states

div.p: He is saying that novices caught up in apprehending things when dreaming and awake become intellectually engaged because of following after the seen, the heard, and the thought—the thing of which they have been aware—without investigating whether ultimately things exist or do not exist. When the intellect is engaged like that, some intellectual acts have no result, some have a great result, some have a small result, some are caught up in and some are not caught up in defilement, and some are caught up in and some are not caught up in purification. What is this teaching? It is teaching that you should know that these intellectual acts come about through the force of perfect and deficient life forms, time periods, practices, bodies, sleep, and so on, and from the lack of necessary conditions.
What is Śāriputra thinking where he says,

q.p: “Venerable Subhūti, the Lord has said ‘all karma is isolated and all intention is isolated.’ ”
q.orig: Venerable Subhūti, the Lord has said ‘all karma is isolated and all intention is isolated,
Venerable Subhūti, if, as the Blessed One has said, all actions and all volitions are void

div.p: He is thinking that scripture says “all dharmas are isolated from an intrinsic nature,” so karmas and intentions are isolated from an intrinsic nature. How then is it possible to investigate whether they have an objective support or do not have an objective support?
Then the elder Subhūti says,

q.p:
“Venerable Śāriputra, ordinary beings, having made a causal sign, pile up karmas.” Cf. khri brgyad
: “ordinary beings, having made each separate one into a causal sign”; nyi khri , ’bum tha 182b5 omit “ordinary beings” and “each separate one.”
q.orig: Venerable Śāriputra,” replied Subhūti, “ordinary beings, having made each separate one into a causal sign, pile up karmas,
Venerable Śāradvatīputra,” replied Subhūti, “following the creation of a conceptual image, actions occur

div.p: What he intends here is this: From the context, take this not with bodhisattva great beings who view things as not findable, who are free from thought construction, but rather with those caught up in apprehending things. Therefore, it teaches that having an objective support and not having an objective support is based on what is constructed by their intellects.
Then again, from,

q.p: “Venerable Subhūti, if bodhisattva great beings in a dream give gifts,”
q.orig: Venerable Subhūti, if bodhisattva great beings in their dreams have dispensed generosity

div.p: up to

q.p: “cultivate wisdom,”
q.orig: cultivated wisdom

div.p: the elder Śāriputra again voices other arguments. Set aside for the moment the novice bodhisattvas—if bodhisattvas whose continuums have matured give gifts in a dream, for them, since both dreaming and not having fallen asleep are similar, does the rejoicing in and dedication of the giving and so on become as excellent as when not having fallen asleep? This is what he is saying.

q.p: “Venerable Śāriputra, you should ask this of Maitreya the bodhisattva, the great being,”
q.orig: Venerable Śāriputra,” said Subhūti, “you should ask this of Maitreya, the bodhisattva great being

Venerable Śāradvatīputra,” replied Subhūti, “since the bodhisattva great being Maitreya is destined for only one more rebirth and has been manifestly prophesied by the Blessed One as irreversible, you should ask him

div.p: and so on. Maitreya has given the response to that argument because it is beneficial to the persons to be trained gathered there at that time, or to show that their intentions match his own.

q.p: “Venerable monk Śāriputra, what do you think, will this—the designation ‘Maitreya the bodhisattva great being’—respond with the answer; or will form respond with the answer,”
q.orig: “Venerable monk Śāriputra, what do you think, will this…respond with the answer[2]
Will this one named the bodhisattva great being Maitreya answer? Or will physical forms answer

div.p: and so on. Maitreya has responded to the argument that the elder Śāriputra, with an apprehension of things, voiced before. For bodhisattvas who view without apprehending things and whose continuums have been matured, giving and so on, and rejoicing and dedication and so on, in both a dream and when not having fallen asleep, are nonexistent like unreal things in a dream, so Śāriputra has asked his question arguing like somebody who does not understand that they are unreal. It is a teaching from the perspective of emptiness.

If persons and dharmas do not exist, what is Subhūti thinking when he says that Maitreya “will respond with the answer” to this? He is saying that he will speak based on words plucked out of thin air, or form and so on, or their emptiness will respond with the answer. It means here that when

q.p: “all dharmas are not two and cannot be divided into two,”
q.orig: All those dharmas are not two and cannot be divided into two,
All these phenomena are not two things and are not to be divided into two

div.p: are standing as one, who responds with what answer to whom? Which is to say, nobody responds with any answer.

q.p: “Son of a good family, have you had direct witness of those dharmas in the way you have explained them to be?”
q.orig: Have you realized those phenomena, just as you have explained them

div.p: The elder Śāriputra has said: if you have had such direct witness of those dharmas, in that case you would apprehend separately a witness, something being witnessed, and a witnessing.
Therefore, the noble Maitreya again says,

q.p: “I do not directly witness those dharmas in the way I have explained them to be.”
q.orig: I have not realized those phenomena, just as I have explained them

div.p: This is teaching that when he directly witnesses those dharmas, they cannot be apprehended and are also inexpressible, so how is he going to speak about them?
The Lord says,

q.p: “Do you see that dharma on account of which you come to be known as a worthy one?”
q.orig: do you think you can observe anything by which you are declared to be an arhat

div.p: Having in mind that apart from the transformation of the basis, a dharma that is a “worthy one” does not exist, Śāriputra again says,

q.p: “Lord, I do not.”
q.orig: No, Blessed Lord!

div.p: What is the intention where Subhūti asks,

q.p: “Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings complete the perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, how do bodhisattva great beings complete the six perfections

div.p: He is asking: “If all dharmas cannot be apprehended, who completes the perfection of wisdom in which way and for whose sake?”

Then the Lord, having taught that when assisting beings they become, governed by compassion, conventionally, those who have a perception with an objective support, delineates their methods to bring the six perfections to completion and teaches the purifications of a buddhafield. khri brgyad
–. I will not go into these because the meaning of them all is clear.

It is not that all bodhisattvas make all these prayers that are vows. Golden 339b3 thams cad la don yod pa, “are not all fully answered.” The bodhisattvas make the prayers that are vows to complete the six perfections and purify a buddhafield as explained at length at this point in the Sūtra. The prayers that are vows come about in harmony with each of their individual different aspirations. It could be that some have fully made a prayer that is a vow but later, because of the force of the beings’ karma, a bit of it might not be accomplished.

The prophesy Emend lus to lung. khri brgyad
–. of Gaṅgadevī is also easy to understand.

div.head: Fully mastering emptiness
div.p: Then the elder Subhūti asks Earlier ( ), it said “the sixteenth question is, ‘How do bodhisattva great beings fully master emptiness?’ ” The question has not been repeated here. how a bodhisattva cultivates the three gateways to liberation and cultivates the thirty-seven dharmas on the side of awakening while rejecting the freedom of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas. The explanatory section following that says they

q.p:
“should understand analytically ‘…empty.’ ” Cf. khri brgyad
.
q.orig: should determine that physical forms are empty

div.p: At the time special insight into emptiness is increasing,

q.p:
“one way or the other, when they understand this analytically, such an analytical understanding should be without mental distraction.” Cf. khri brgyad
; nyi khri .
q.orig: By whatever means they make such determinations, they should do so with an unwavering mind

div.p: At the time of the meditative stabilization on emptiness,

q.p: “without mental distraction they do not see the phenomenon that is the phenomenon to be actualized, and,”
q.orig: One whose mind is unwavering does not observe those phenomena

div.p: as for the time when they reach suchness,

q.p: “not seeing that phenomenon they do not actualize it,”
q.orig: not seeing that phenomenon they do not actualize it.
One who does not observe those phenomena, does not actualize them

div.p: and so on, up to

q.p:
“they see [they]… are not joined and are not disjoined.” khri brgyad
: “Because they are well trained in phenomena that are empty of their own marks, so they see that all those phenomena—an actualizer, something to be actualized, and something through which there is actualization—are not joined and are not disjoined.”
q.orig: they see that all those phenomena—an actualizer, something to be actualized, and something through which there is actualization—are not joined and are not disjoined.

div.p: That is what that the text teaches, that something apprehended and something that apprehends are equally the same and cannot be conceived of.

Hence, “not seeing that phenomenon they do not actualize it.” Just not seeing a phenomenon is the cause of not actualizing it. Were they to see it they would actualize it. And what would the fault be were they to have actualized it? They would have actualized the very limit of reality just like a śrāvaka does. And in that case they would connect with their liberation.

q.p: “How do bodhisattva great beings stand in emptiness but not actualize emptiness?”
q.orig: how then, Blessed Lord, do bodhisattva great beings dwell in emptiness and not actualize emptiness

div.p: This teaches that emptiness, “the phenomenon that is… to be actualized” that “they do not see,” is where they stand. Again, “not seeing that phenomenon they do not actualize it” teaches they do not actualize emptiness. This “stand… but not actualize” is asking “how could it be known?”
The Lord, based on the prior intention, teaches a modification:

q.p: “Subhūti, when bodhisattva great beings contemplate emptiness furnished with the best of all aspects, they do not contemplate that they should actualize it.”
q.orig: When bodhisattva great beings contemplate emptiness furnished with the best of all aspects, they do not contemplate that they should actualize it
when bodhisattva great beings determine the emptiness endowed with all its finest aspects, they do not think, ‘I actualize it! I will actualize it

div.p: With just the earlier intention, “I should meditate on emptiness,” those bodhisattvas do not have the intention “I will actualize emptiness,” like śrāvakas thinking “I will actualize the cessation.” A “cessation” (nirodha, ’gog pa) is a nirvāṇa. The thought “I will meditate on emptiness” is just the intention “I will totally harmonize with it.” Therefore, this means that even later on it is only a meditation, it is not an actualization. Therefore, it says

q.p: “they contemplate that it is not the time it should be actualized, but rather it is the time it should be mastered.”
q.orig: they think, ‘This is the time for investigation, but this is not the time for actualization

div.p: The mastering of emptiness without also actualizing it is the power of knowledge of mastery.

q.p: “When not in actual meditative equipoise… [they] attach their minds to an objective support”
q.orig: When not in actual…meditative equipoise, bodhisattva great beings attach their minds to an objective support
Bodhisattva great beings, when not in a state of absorption, focus their minds on perceptual objects

div.p: is teaching that “knowledge of mastery” is mind in its ordinary state, In the absence of the Skt it is hard to be certain of the meaning of rang bzhin gyi sems (*prakṛtacitta) (“mind in its ordinary state”). Alternatively, “a thought of the intrinsic nature.” it is not meditative equipoise. Therefore, in that instant there is no calm abiding, and because there is no calm abiding the extraordinary path does not arise.
Now, teaching that knowledge of mastery is the knowledge of when is and is not the time, it says

q.p: “it is the time for the perfection of giving,”
q.orig: This is the time for the perfection of generosity

div.p: and so on.

Understand the heroic person illustration, bird illustration, and master archer illustration from the text. khri brgyad
–.

q.p: “Lord, it is amazing! Sugata, it is amazing!”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, how wonderful it is, Blessed Lord…Sugata, this is most amazing

div.p: is saying “it is amazing” that those seeing all dharmas as emptiness have not, in the interim, Read bar ma dor in place of par ma dor. feeling intimidated, fallen to a śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha awakening that is caused by meditation on the three meditative stabilizations.
Here the Lord, with,

q.p: “Subhūti, it is because the bodhisattva great beings do not forsake all beings,”
q.orig: “Subhūti,” said the Lord, “it is because the bodhisattva great beings do not forsake all beings
Subhūti,” replied the Blessed One, “this is because such bodhisattva great beings do not forsake any beings

div.p: and so on, teaches the cause of not feeling intimidated. Here there are a further seven subsections to the passage: the section about engaging with doctrines that are not good; the section about views with a false apprehension of facts; the section about distorted minds; the section about the conceptualization of a self and dharmas; the section about causal signs; the section about the fault of making wishes; and the section on questioning bodhisattvas.

Among these, the first section is Cf. nyi khri , Twenty-Five Thousand translation: “I should release all these sentient beings who maintain inauthentic doctrines”; khri brgyad
: “these beings who are deceived because they perceive nonexistent phenomena as existing.”

q.p: “I will not forsake these ignorant beings, these beings who are deceived because they perceive doctrines that are not good as good.”
q.orig: I will not forsake these ignorant beings, these beings who are deceived because they perceive nonexistent phenomena as existing.
I will not forsake any beings. I should release all these beings who maintain inauthentic doctrines

div.p: Bodhisattvas generate compassion and are attentive to not forsaking beings, and that causes them, in the interim, not to feel cowed and not to actualize the very limit of reality.

The second subsection is where they do not feel cowed based on the power of generating the thought, khri brgyad
–. “These beings have… for a long time been practicing a practice with a false apprehension of facts while viewing… a self… a being and so on, so I will fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening and teach them the doctrines in order to eliminate their views.”

The third subsection khri brgyad
. is where bodhisattvas think, “The minds of these beings have been distorted for a long time by the fourfold erroneous perception of permanence… happiness… pleasant… and self, so I will turn them back from that.”

The fourth khri brgyad
. is where they think, “For a long time these beings have been practicing a practice while falsely imagining a being, and while falsely imagining the dharmas, form and so on, so, having fully awakened, I will explain the doctrine of emptiness for their sake.”

The fifth khri brgyad
. is, “For a long time these beings have been practicing a practice with causal signs—the causal sign for a woman, for a man, and so on—so, having fully awakened, I will explain the doctrine of signlessness for their sake.”
Similarly, the sixth is, “For a long time these beings have been practicing a practice while making wishes, and making prayers so it will lead to the dharmas of wealth and the beautiful body of

q.p:
“Śatakratu, Brahmā, a world protector,” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: status of Śakra, the status of Brahmā, the status of a guardian of the world

div.p: and so on, so, having fully awakened, I will explain the doctrine of wishlessness for their sake.”

Also, in regard to asking bodhisattvas, khri brgyad
: “Subhūti, you should ask bodhisattva great beings thus practicing mastery of those thirty-seven dharmas on the side of awakening, ‘How do bodhisattva great beings who want to fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening cultivate the perfection of wisdom?’ ” if when asked they respond, “They must meditate well on

q.p: emptiness… signlessness… wishlessness… not occasioning anything, nonproduction, and the absence of an existent thing,”
q.orig: emptiness, must pay attention to signlessness, must pay attention to wishlessness, and must pay attention to not occasioning anything, to nonproduction, and to the absence of an existing thing
they should focus their attention on signlessness, wishlessness, nonconditioning, nonarising, noncessation, and nonentity

div.p: taking just those as their point of departure, they should know they will have been prophesied because they will have realized well This renders rab tu rtogs pa literally, “realized well”; cf. khri brgyad (kha 224b1), nyi khri (ga 13b6) rab tu ’byed, “sort out,” “distinguish.” the mark of the knowledge of mastery. But if, when asked, they respond, “They should reject the meditation on emptiness, and so on, they should not meditate on them, they should cast them away and cultivate impermanence and so on instead,” up to they should know they have not been prophesied. They

q.p: “are not like irreversible bodhisattvas who… have stepped onto the irreversible level.”
q.orig: are not like irreversible bodhisattva great beings who, having achieved mastery, have stepped onto the irreversible level,
in the manner in which irreversible bodhisattva great beings have investigated and transcended the level at which progress has become irreversible

div.p: Those without mastery do not, like those who have reached the eighth level,

q.p: “having achieved mastery”
q.orig: having achieved mastery[1]

div.p: of them,

q.p: “passing beyond the Tanū level,”
q.orig: transcend the level of the attenuated refinement

div.p: become irreversible. This means that they are not fully matured just through that. This means through the lack of skillful means that leads a bodhisattva to say to another bodhisattva that it is necessary to reject a śrāvaka’s meditation on emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessnes. The “Tanū level” is from the second up to the seventh level.

q.p: “Would there then, Lord, be ways in which [they] would be irreversible from awakening?”
q.orig: Would there then, Lord, be ways in which the bodhisattva great beings would be irreversible from awakening?
Blessed Lord, is there a reason why bodhisattvas may be styled ‘irreversible

div.p: It is teaching this: if they, even without having reached the eighth level where they are irreversible from awakening, having excellently achieved mastery, deliver the response of an irreversible bodhisattva, would they become irreversible because of meeting the definition of those irreversible from awakening?

q.p:
“Levels that they have cleansed or levels that they are cleansing do not appear” Cf. khri brgyad
; nyi khri , ’bum tha 212a1.
q.orig: levels that have been cleansed or levels that have not been cleansed do not appear
dwell on the purificatory levels or the nonpurificatory levels

div.p: teaches the lower levels.

q.p: “Those bodhisattva great beings… are few”
q.orig: bodhisattva great beings of whom the level of irreversible wisdom has been prophesied are few in number

div.p: means that even though

q.p: “bodhisattvas who practice for awakening are many,”
q.orig: bodhisattva great beings who practice for awakening are many
there are many who are engaged in [the pursuit of] enlightenment

div.p: those who will give the answer of an irreversible bodhisattva who has excellently developed mastery, even without having reached the eighth level, “are few.”

q.p: “Whether they are levels that have been cleansed or whether they are levels that have not been cleansed”
q.orig: levels that have been cleansed or levels that have not been cleansed
the purificatory levels or the nonpurificatory levels

div.p: teaches the lower levels. I have translated this without emendation even though it is a repetition.

Then, the marks of irreversibility, the works of Māra, and spiritual friends occurring in this section of the text are again easy to understand. khri brgyad
–.

div.head: Questions 18 to 27

q.p:
“Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom is like space, unimpeded.” khri brgyad
. This is the response to Subhūti’s eighteenth question, “Lord, what is the mark of the perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: “Subhūti,” replied the Lord, “the perfection of wisdom is like space, unimpeded.
Subhūti, like space, the perfection of wisdom has the defining characteristic of nonattachment

div.p:
This means it is characterized as unimpeded like space. Earlier the explanation was of the perfection of wisdom impeded by the works of Māra and so on. khri brgyad
ff. The “and so on” brings in the impediment to the perfection of wisdom posed by the false projection of superiority over other bodhisattvas because of living in physical isolation, engaging in austerities, and mistaking Māra for a spiritual friend. Now,

q.p: “Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom is without a mark. The perfection of wisdom’s mark does not exist at all”
q.orig: Subhūti, the defining characteristic of the perfection of wisdom is nonexistent. The perfection of wisdom has no defining characteristics at all

div.p: says that it is marked as unimpeded. The perfection of wisdom is not the mark of anything else, and the mark of the perfection of wisdom is also not anything at all. This is teaching that it is not an entity that is a nonexistent thing. N, K, Golden 343a2; D: “it is not the nonexistence of an intrinsic nature.”

q.p: “Subhūti… all phenomena are isolated from an intrinsic nature, all phenomena are empty of an intrinsic nature.”
q.orig: Subhūti[3]…all phenomena are isolated from an intrinsic nature, all phenomena are empty of an intrinsic nature.
Subhūti, all phenomena are naturally void. All phenomena are devoid of all phenomena. All phenomena are empty of all phenomena

div.p: The thoroughly established—the intrinsic nature of all phenomena—is isolated from and separated from all falsely imagined phenomena. Therefore, it means they “all are empty of the intrinsic nature.”

q.p: “Lord, if all phenomena are isolated from all phenomena, and if all phenomena are empty of all phenomena, Lord, how could there be the defilement and purification of beings?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, if all phenomena are void of all phenomena and if all phenomena are empty of all phenomena, how could there be affliction and purification of beings

div.p: and so on is asking: “Lord, if all phenomena are isolated from and empty of an intrinsic nature, later there will be nothing to be isolated from and nothing to be empty of, and if that is the case how will those—the isolated and empty—be defiled, and how will they be purified?”
Having asked that,

q.p: “What do you think, Subhūti, do beings go on grasping at ‘I’ and grasping at ‘mine’ for a long time?”
q.orig: Subhūti, do you think that beings engage in notions of ‘I’ and ‘mine’ for a long time

div.p: and so on, teaches the following: Even though all phenomena are already isolated from an intrinsic nature and empty of an intrinsic nature, simple folk do not know that they are just isolated and empty. On account of the fault of not knowing, they become attached to phenomena—the aggregates and so on—through grasping at them as “I” and grasping at them as “mine,” and because of that attachment they undertake actions that are good and bad and so on. Governed by that, beings link up with and pass through cycles of existence, becoming defiled by afflictive defilement and karmic defilement. Thus, there is defilement on account of the fault of not knowing. Later, when they have again found spiritual friends, based on having listened and reflected and so on they realize the mark of the isolated and the mark of the empty. Then the aforementioned defilement does not arise and gradually, through putting a stop to the imaginary dharmas, there is purification.
Then to eliminate the doubts of those who think that because it has said they

q.p:
“do not practice” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: do not engage

div.p: in all dharmas,

q.p: “in form”
q.orig: form[1]
in physical forms

div.p: and so on, therefore nothing of benefit comes from the practice explained here, it then says there is a lot of merit and explains its cause. You can understand the great increase in merit, and the cause for that as well, from the illustration of

q.p: “a precious jewel”
q.orig: a precious gem

div.p:
in the text itself. khri brgyad
–.

q.p:
“Lord, given that all attention is separated from an intrinsic nature, that all attention is empty of an intrinsic nature” khri brgyad
. This is Subhūti’s twentieth question.
q.orig: Lord, given that all attention is separated from an intrinsic nature, that all attention is empty of an intrinsic nature
Blessed Lord, if all such acts of attention are indeed without inherent existence‍—that is to say, if all acts of attention are indeed empty of inherent existence

div.p: is asking: if all attentions are isolated and separated from an intrinsic nature, how can they know they are

q.p: “never separated from attention to the knowledge of all aspects,”
q.orig: never separated from attention connected to the knowledge of all aspects
not part from focusing their attention with all-aspect omniscience in mind

div.p: because when they are separated from and empty of an intrinsic nature, you cannot apprehend any

q.p: “knowledge of all aspects, or attention, or bodhisattva.”
q.orig: a bodhisattva, attention, or the knowledge of all aspects
a bodhisattva is not apprehended, focusing of the attention is not apprehended, and all-aspect omniscience is not apprehended

div.p: Then, with

q.p: “Subhūti, if bodhisattva great beings know this,”
q.orig: bodhisattva great beings know

div.p: and so on, the Lord, not speaking while having falsely imagined a knowledge of all aspects, a bodhisattva, and attention as some other phenomena, without there being any ultimate difference between them, still simply designates bodhisattvas as “not separated from attention connected to the knowledge of all aspects,” just on account of their knowing all phenomena are isolated from an intrinsic nature.

q.p: “The perfection of wisdom is empty of an intrinsic nature”—
q.orig: It is empty of inherent existence

div.p: naturally pure and stainless wisdom is isolated from all dharmas, is empty of all dharmas.

q.p: “It has no increase and it has no decline.”
q.orig: It is empty of inherent existence

div.p: This means there is neither increase, plucked out of thin air, on account of striving, nor is there decline on account of not striving.

q.p: “Lord, given that the perfection of wisdom is separated from an intrinsic nature and empty of an intrinsic nature”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, if the perfection of wisdom is devoid of inherent existence and it is empty of inherent existence

div.p: is the second question. This is Subhūti’s twenty-first question. It is asking how, if the perfection of wisdom is separated from an intrinsic nature, will an isolated, empty perfection of wisdom bring about full awakening to perfect, complete awakening.

Then the Lord explains that bodhisattvas are the intrinsic nature of the dharma body so they are a separated state, an empty state. Furthermore, he is teaching that it is not as if dharma body bodhisattvas fully awaken to perfect, complete awakening on account of the power of the perfection of wisdom. They do not become more of what they are thanks to the perfection of wisdom, and they do not become less when they do not rely on the perfection of wisdom either, because they are marked by staying as what they are. He says,

q.p: “Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom is not one and it is not two either.”
q.orig: the perfection of wisdom is not one and it is not two either.
the perfection of wisdom is neither one nor two

div.p: He means “the knowledge of all aspects,” “bodhisattva,” “perfection of wisdom,” and “suchness” are not one, they cannot be divided, and they are not different in terms of a particular enumeration.
The third question is, This is Subhūti’s twenty-second question.

q.p: “Lord, is it the emptiness of the perfection of wisdom, its state of ringing hollow, being in vain, being a fraud, and being pointless, that practices the perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, is it this [very] perfection of wisdom, which is emptiness, voidness, vacuity, hollowness, and essencelessness, that engages in the perfection of wisdom

div.p: He is asking about five possibilities: “Is it the emptiness of the perfection of wisdom” that practices the perfection of wisdom; or does something other than the perfection of wisdom practice; or does the perfection of wisdom practice; or does emptiness practice; or does something other than emptiness practice? And, similarly, about two other possibilities: is it form and so on that practices or is it the emptiness of form and so on that practices? He has asked based on seven possibilities like that. Then, because those same possibilities are in fact impossible, the Lord does not apprehend the practice, the perfection of wisdom, or a way of practicing; and then does not apprehended even nonappearances; and does not apprehend

q.p:
“production or stopping” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: arises…or ceases

div.p: either.
Taking that as his point of departure, the Lord gives an explanation of those bodhisattva great beings endowed with the forbearance for the nonproduction of dharmas who have been prophesied.

q.p:
“Lord, is the bodhisattvas’ unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening prophesied because there will be a production of all the dharmas?” khri brgyad
. This is Subhūti’s twenty-third question.
q.orig: Lord, is the bodhisattvas’ unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening prophesied because there will be the production of all the dharmas?

div.p: Is it on account of the production of all the buddhadharmas? Is it because of

q.p: “the nonproduction of all the dharmas?”
q.orig: nonarising nature of all phenomena

div.p: Is it on account of the nonproduction of any of the dharmas—form and so on—or the defilement dharmas?

q.p: “What do you think, Subhūti, do you see that dharma, the dharma of which unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening is being prophesied?”
q.orig: Subhūti, do you think that you can observe such phenomena that are prophesied to attain unsurpassed, complete enlightenment

div.p: means something being prophesied and something causing full awakening are nonexistent things, so there is no such thing as a prophesy of this or that type of state.

q.p: “Lord, this perfection of wisdom is deep,”
q.orig: this perfection of wisdom is deep
the perfection of wisdom, owing to its extreme voidness, is profound

div.p: and so on.

div.head: Explanation of Chapters 56 to 63
div.p:
Then it goes on to give an explanation of great merit again in order to generate faith. This is a general characterization of khri brgyad
–: glorification ( ), good qualities (ends ), Śatakratu and Ānanda (ends ), the description of Māra and the work of Māra ( ), the description of what happens because of that work ( ), how one should behave in the presence of persons in the Bodhisattva Vehicle ( ), sameness ( ), ending, detachment, and cessation ( ), the benefits of training ( ), surpassing nonbeings ( ), the Śatakratu passage ( ), and the immeasurable merit ( ). All the glorification passages; the explanation of the good qualities; the exchange between Śatakratu and Ānanda; the description of Māra and the work of Māra; the description of what happens because of it; how one should behave in the presence of persons in the Bodhisattva Vehicle; the explanation of sameness; the conversation about ending, detachment, and cessation and so on; the explanation of the benefits of training; surpassing nonperfect beings; Here sems can ma yin pa rnams means those for whom life is not the perfect moment for the practice of the perfection of wisdom—those without “the perfect human rebirth.” the Śatakratu passage; immeasurable merit; and then again the Śatakratu passage are easy to understand from the scripture itself, so I have not explained them.

div.head: No duality and no nonduality

q.p:
“One way or the other they should turn it over… in such a way that there is no notion of duality and no notion of nonduality.” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: they should dedicate [the merit] to unsurpassed, complete enlightenment. This dedication should be made in such a way that there is no notion of duality and no notion of nonduality

div.p: This is saying that ultimately their thought-productions and those unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakenings, whatever they are, are not different so, because their suchness is categorized as purity, there is therefore “no notion of duality.” The dual is when there are stains and when there are no stains. The two exist as different particulars so there is also a notion of duality. Therefore it says “there is no notion of duality” because they are the same. There is the notion of duality because they are different. Alternatively, as explained clearly in the part of the text that comes below, the notion of duality is of “existent and nonexistent,” and the notion of nonduality is of “nonexistent and not nonexistent.”

Then also after that it says, khri brgyad
. I have added the word “awakening” based on the following gloss.

q.p: “And one way or the other they should turn it over in such a way that awakening will not be in that thought, nor in another thought either.”
q.orig: they should then dedicate this [merit] toward unsurpassed, complete enlightenment, doing so free of a mindset and free of anything else other than a mindset.

div.p: Based on the fact that there has been a transformation of the basis, it Based on the fact that there has been a transformation of the basis, awakening will not be in that thought, which is to say, awakening will not be the same as the state of mind during the first moment of bodhicitta. Ultimately, they are not different, so it will not be in another moment of bodhicitta, which is to say awakening will not be other than the state of mind during the first moment of bodhicitta. “will not be in that thought.” Ultimately they are not different so it will not be “in another thought either.”

q.p:
“Subhūti, what do you think, do you see that thought that is like an illusion?” This is the response to Subhūti’s twenty-eighth question (nyi khri
), “Lord, in what way will a thought that is like an illusion fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening?” Its presence here perhaps buttresses the argument that Haribhadra changed the order of his version (PSP 5: 37, le’u brgyad ma ca 63a7).
q.orig: do you think that you can observe the illusion-like mind

div.p: What does this intend? If a thought is like an illusion but awakening is not like an illusion, then there would be a fault. A thought and awakening are both like an illusion, however, therefore the fault is not there.

q.p: “The dharma that is extremely isolated “Extremely isolated” means totally isolated from the aspirations of śrāvakas or from its own hypothetical intrinsic nature. will not be existent or nonexistent.”
q.orig: Anything that is absolutely void is neither existent nor nonexistent

div.p: A falsely imagined phenomenon is like an illusion, so, as with an illusion, it is not suitable to say “it is existent” or “it is nonexistent,” and it is also not suitable to say “it is not existent and it is not nonexistent” either. A thoroughly established phenomenon is isolated from all aspects of a thing, so it is also not suitable to say “it is existent.” It is not suitable to say “it is nonexistent,” because its inexpressible isolated nature exists. The convention “it is existent” also exists, so it is not suitable to say “it is nonexistent.” And the convention “it is nonexistent” also exists, so it is not suitable to say “it is not nonexistent.” Therefore, the notion of duality and the notion of nonduality are not tenable.

q.p: “Lord, it is because all those dharmas that are defiled or purified do not exist and are not apprehended.”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, it is because this applies to all phenomena, defiled or purified, which are nonexistent and utterly nonexistent

div.p: Phenomena that become defiled and become purified do not exist because the defiled does not exist even when there are stains, because it is isolated from an intrinsic nature, like space. And because that is just nonexistent, something not there before that has been purified is nonexistent too. This is the explanation of “it Unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening. will not be in that thought, nor in another thought either.”

q.p: “And a dharma that is extremely isolated is not something you cultivate and not something you analyze.” khri brgyad kha 254a2 rnam par gzhig pa; cf. nyi khri ga 48a5 rnam par bsgom pa.
q.orig: There is nothing at all that is absolutely void that is to be cultivated, and nothing that is to be uncultivated

div.p: To “cultivate” is to become habituated; that is untenable because it Here “it” means a dharma that is cultivated or eliminated. is isolated. To “analyze” is to eliminate stains; that too is untenable because it is isolated.

q.p:
“There is not any dharma that is bringing anything about.” Cf. khri brgyad
; nyi khri .
q.orig: it does not bring about any dharma,
there is nothing at all that is to be attained

div.p: Because it is extremely isolated it is not something that causes the attainment of awakening.

q.p:
“Given that it is extremely isolated, how will there be a realization of the isolated by the isolated?” khri brgyad
. This is Subhūti’s twenty-ninth question.
q.orig: Given that unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening is extremely isolated, how will there be a realization of the isolated by the isolated?
Since unsurpassed, complete enlightenment, too, is absolutely void, how can voidness attain buddhahood through voidness

div.p: Given that the perfection of wisdom and perfect, complete awakening are extremely isolated how will an isolated perfection of wisdom come to realize an isolated perfect complete awakening?
With

q.p: “exactly so, Subhūti, exactly so!”
q.orig: Subhūti, it is so! It is so

div.p: the Lord teaches that were one to be isolated but the other not isolated, in that case it would not be tenable. But both are isolated like that, so there is therefore no fault. When the true reality that all dharmas are marked as isolated is understood, then there is complete, full awakening.

q.p: “The way I understand the meaning of what you, Lord, have said, is that bodhisattva great beings are not those who do what is difficult”
q.orig: as I understand the meaning spoken by the Blessed One, if they do not incur the slightest difficulty, how do bodhisattva great beings do what is difficult

div.p: means that when one thing is apprehended and another thing is not apprehended, it is difficult because they do not conform, but since all dharmas do not exist—that is, are nonexistent things—they are not apprehended. It is not difficult to understand that you cannot apprehend something that does not exist.

q.p: “Lord this course of action where nothing is apprehended is the course of action of bodhisattvas.”
q.orig: “Lord, this course of action where nothing is apprehended is the course of action of bodhisattvas.
they engage in nonapprehension with respect to all phenomena that can be realized‍

div.p: There is no course of action except a course of action where nothing is apprehended.

Then it teaches that the perfection of wisdom is a state without thought construction. That is easy to understand. The section specifically dealing with the absence of vikalpa (“conceptualization,” “thought construction”) is khri brgyad
–. Cf. nyi khri , PSP 5: 37, le’u brgyad ma ca 63a7 ff.

div.head: Cyclic existence and nirvāṇa

q.p: “How has this division of cyclic existence into the five forms of life… come about, and how do the categorizations of stream enterer,”
q.orig: how has this differentiation come about with regard to the cycle of existence with its five realms of living beings, namely the denizens of the hells, the animal domain, the world of Yama, the world of the gods, and the world of humankind? How are those who have entered the stream to nirvāṇa

div.p: and so on, come about? This is asking how, if all phenomena are without thought construction, the cycles of existence and purification dharmas come about.

Then the Lord states khri brgyad
. This is not said by the Lord, but is an exchange between Subhūti and Śāriputra. that these thought constructions are in error; they are marked by grasping at the nonexistent and by obscuring the existent. Because they are mixed up with them, thought constructions that are greedy, hating, and so on obscure the existent. They grasp at the nonexistent. Because they give rise to them, intentions to perform karmic action that is meritorious, demeritorious, and so on also grasp at error. Because those actions and those thought constructions give rise to the maturation consciousnesses, they do not grasp true reality either. Therefore

q.p: “the desire-to-do”

div.p: and greed and so on have what is not true reality as their object, so all origination is not a true intrinsic nature. The “five forms of life”

q.p: “in the hells, animal world, and world of Yama, and as a human and god”
q.orig: in the hells, animal world, world of Yama, and as a human and god.
the hells, and the beings of the animal domain, the world of Yama, and the realms of gods and humans

div.p: are explained as the intrinsic nature of true reality. Therefore, even though all phenomena are not thought construction, cyclic existence is still presented like that.

Also, for purification dharmas it presents all the stream enterers and so on as simply not constructed in thought, teaching that in their intrinsic there is no difference in nature between stream enterers and so on, up to tathāgatas, because all phenomena do not pass beyond the dharma body.
Having thus heard about the true dharmic nature of the perfection of wisdom, Śāriputra’s understanding greatly increases and he says,

q.p: “Ah! Those bodhisattva great beings who are practicing this perfection of wisdom make a practice of something really worthwhile.”
q.orig: Ah! Venerable Subhūti, those bodhisattva great beings who are practicing this perfection of wisdom make a practice of something really worthwhile.
Indeed, Venerable Subhūti, bodhisattva great beings who practice the perfection of wisdom practice that which is the essence

div.p: Subhūti then says that they

q.p: “make a practice of something that is not worthwhile!”
q.orig: practice that which is essenceless

div.p: It is not worthwhile because it is not a real thing and is not something that exists. With that in mind, using ordinary reasoning it says they

q.p: “do not apprehend even something not worthwhile, so however could they apprehend something really worthwhile?”
q.orig: not apprehend and do not see even something not worthwhile, so however could they apprehend something really worthwhile

div.p: It makes the conventional statement that even ordinarily it is easy to get something worthless, but it is hard to get something worth a lot.

q.p:
“It is right to bow down to those bodhisattva great beings… who do not actualize these dharmas as being the same” I have added “It is right to bow down to those bodhisattva great beings,” which comes at the beginning of the sentence at khri brgyad
.—
q.orig: bodhisattva great beings who do not actualize the sameness of all phenomena are worthy of homage

div.p: to stream enterers and so on and tathāgatas as being the same, and to the dharma body and the very limit of reality as being the same.

q.p:
“Because space is isolated” khri brgyad
. The first aspect is just as space is isolated, utterly other than the material objects within it, so too is a being in their inner absolute nature utterly other than the falsely imagined being the person projects. The second aspect is as follows: to buckle on armor to fight the hard fight is to do what is difficult, but seeing the space-like emptiness of all things is the armor that makes the difficult practice of the six perfections, which is done in order to bring about the welfare of infinite beings, doable. Third, just as beings are empty and isolated, like space, so are all the dharmas that locate them.—
q.orig: because space itself is void

div.p: because space is isolated from its mental image. This passage, furthermore, is in three subsections: the passage on space and beings being alike; the passage on the armor of space-like beings; and the passage on form and so on, and beings, being alike.

The explanation of isolation and the benefits of the perfection of wisdom are easy to understand. khri brgyad
–.

div.head: Standing in the knowledge of all aspects
div.p: Subhūti asks,

q.p:
“Lord, given that no phenomenon is apprehended when they have stood in suchness and practiced for suchness, how will they stand in the knowledge of all aspects?” nyi khri , le’u brgyad ma ca 69b4–5, and in a slightly different translation khri brgyad
. This is Subhūti’s thirty-first question.
q.orig: “Lord,” Subhūti then inquired, “given that no phenomenon is apprehended when they have stood in suchness and practiced for suchness, how will they stand in the knowledge of all aspects?
Blessed Lord, when they dwell in the real nature, earnestly intent on the real nature, if they do not apprehend anything at all, how then will they dwell in all-aspect omniscience

div.p: Standing in reality and progress would be viable were any phenomenon to exist, but if all phenomena are not apprehended, how will they stand?

q.p: “Subhūti, they stand as things really are, like a tathāgata’s magical creation.” This reading, a good one not attested in the present versions of the Sūtra, does not support Conze’s conjecture (GilgitC, 265 n. 10) that GilgitC 66 tathāgata­nirmito (le’u brgyad ma ca 70a2 gang de bzhin gshegs pa’i sprul pa) is a corruption of Aṣṭa (Wogihara p. 858, Mitra p. 453) tathatā­vinirmukto nānyaḥ kaścid dharmam upalabhyate; cf. ŚsPN4 9869v10.

div.p: This means that just as a tathāgata’s magical creation does all that has to be done and stands, so too bodhisattvas stand as well.

q.p: “Lord, given that no phenomenon called ‘a tathāgata’s magical creation’ is apprehended at all,”
q.orig: Lord, given that no phenomenon called “a tathāgata’s magical creation” is apprehended at all

div.p: and so on, is teaching that there is no phenomenon at all called “a tathāgata’s magical creation,” and because it is just nonexistent there is no standing and practicing in suchness, no full awakening, and no demonstration of the Dharma, so how can it be tenable that “a bodhisattva exists”?

q.p: “Given that even suchness is not apprehended, what need is there to say more about someone who will stand in suchness.”
q.orig: When the real nature is itself nonapprehensible, how could one speak of anyone abiding in the real nature

div.p: This teaches other things that are not tenable. It is saying this because during the period it has stains even suchness is comparable to a falsely imagined phenomenon. At that time even suchness cannot be apprehended as what suchness really is.
The Lord’s intention when it says

q.p: “exactly so, Subhūti, exactly so!”
q.orig: That is so, Subhūti! That is so

div.p: is this: He is saying there would be a fault if something were to be apprehended and something else were not to be apprehended. But given that a bodhisattva, the perfection of wisdom, awakening, standing, and progressing all do not exist what fault is there in this?

q.p: “And why? Subhūti, it is because whether the tathāgatas arise or whether the tathāgatas do not arise,”
q.orig: And why? Subhūti, it is because whether the tathāgatas arise or whether the tathāgatas do not arise,
If you ask why, Subhūti, whether the tathāgatas have appeared or not

div.p: unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening remains, so it is there at all times. Therefore, “standing” and “progress” do not exist at all. This is teaching that standing, progress, and full awakening do not exist at all in suchness.

Then there is the praise of Subhūti, the praise of dwelling in the perfection of wisdom, the worship of the gods, the account of the six thousand monks, the benefits of the perfection of wisdom, the entrusting it to Ānanda, the enactment of a magical performance, the training in the perfections, the glorification of the perfection of wisdom, and the account of it being inexhaustible. khri brgyad
–.

q.p:
“Ānanda, this deep perfection of wisdom is the entrance into all letters, and the entrance into all for which there are no letters. Ānanda, this deep perfection of wisdom is the gateway to all the dhāraṇīs—the dhāraṇī gateways in which bodhisattva great beings should train.” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: Ānanda, this profound perfection of wisdom is an entrance to all syllables. Ānanda, this profound perfection of wisdom is the gateway of all dhāraṇīs in which bodhisattva great beings should train

div.p: It is the entrance into those recollections, wisdoms, and meditative stabilizations related with speech sounds; it is the entrance into those recollections, wisdoms, and meditative stabilizations related with that for which there are no speech sounds; and it is the gateway to those doctrine dhāraṇīs, meaning dhāraṇīs, forbearance dhāraṇīs, and secret mantra dhāraṇīs.

q.p:
“Subhūti, because form is inexhaustible they will accomplish the perfection of wisdom,” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: “Subhūti,” he replied, “because form is inexhaustible they will accomplish the perfection of wisdom.
“Subhūti,” replied the Blessed One, “the perfection of wisdom should be brought into being through the inexhaustibility of physical forms.

div.p: and so on, means they should generate wisdom having taken the inexhaustibility of dharmas—form and so on—as their objective support.

q.p: “Through form and space being inexhaustible, Subhūti”—
q.orig: Through form and space being inexhaustible, Subhūti,
inexhaustible space-like nature of physical forms. Subhūti

div.p: even while taking the suchness of form and so on, and space, as an objective support, they should generate the wisdom that they are inexhaustible. This is in response to the question, “Lord, how are bodhisattva great beings to accomplish the perfection of wisdom?” The response is that everything is akṣaya (“inexhaustible,” a word similar in sound to ākāśa, “space”), so all dharmas are indivisible as thoroughly established phenomena, so seeing them as dharmas, and seeing them as the inexhaustible ultimate reality of things, produces wisdom.

Then the benefits of the space-like inexhaustible meditation connecting it with each of the six perfections is easy to understand. I am unsure exactly which part of the Sūtra our author is referring to, whether it includes the section of dependent origination or whether it begins from khri brgyad
and goes up to . Just below our author will reference “each of the six perfections being connected one with the other,” a section that perhaps begins at .

q.p:
“[They] do not apprehend inner emptiness as ‘inner emptiness’ ” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom do not apprehend inner emptiness as ‘inner emptiness,
they do not apprehend the emptiness of internal phenomena as the emptiness of internal phenomena
bodhisattva great beings do not apprehend the notion that physical forms are empty, or the notion that they are not empty

div.p: means they do not construct it in thought as “inner emptiness.”

q.p: “[They] do not apprehend ‘form is empty’ or ‘is not empty,’ ”
q.orig: bodhisattva great beings do not apprehend…is empty’ or ‘is not empty[1]
Blessed Lord, if the perfections are not different, how is it that this perfection of wisdom is, with respect to the five other perfections, said to be the best

div.p: because they do not construct it in thought as being either.

Each of the six perfections being connected one with the other, then skillful means and the account of the completion of the accumulations, the wheel-turning emperor illustration, This omits the analogy of the sun and moon. the woman illustration, the heroic person who heads into battle illustration, the local ruler illustration, the river illustration, the right hand illustration, the taste in the ocean illustration, the precious wheel illustration, and then the explanation of the six perfections are easy to understand. The six perfections are khri brgyad
–; skillful means and the account of the completion of the accumulations, the illustrations, and the six perfections go up to
.

q.p:
“Lord, if the perfections are not different why is the perfection of wisdom said to be the highest… when it comes to the five perfections?” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: Lord, if the perfections are not different, why is the perfection of wisdom said to be the highest, and is said to be the most excellent, foremost, best, superb, sublime, unsurpassed, unrivaled, and equal to the unequaled when it comes to the five perfections?

div.p: The idea is that they have no specific feature because they are not different, and a highest is not tenable when they are the same.

q.p: “Exactly so, Subhūti, exactly so!”
q.orig: Subhūti, it is so! It is so!

div.p: The idea is that the five perfections are not different when they are informed by it—namely, the perfection of wisdom—so, because based on it they are just not different, it is highest among them. The

q.p: “Sumeru”

div.p: illustration teaches this too.

q.p:
“Lord, given that there is no specific feature or variation in any phenomenon for someone who has entered into reality” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: “Blessed Lord, if in that way there are no distinctions and no particulars with respect to anything at all that is to be objectively established

div.p: is saying that a phenomenon does not appear with a specific feature to a person who has entered into reality. Similarly, because of the force of reality, phenomena have no specific features. You should not, therefore, say just the perfection of wisdom is

q.p: “the most excellent.”
q.orig: the most excellent
supreme

q.p: “Exactly so, Subhūti, exactly so!”
q.orig: Subhūti, it is so! It is so

div.p: teaches that based on the perfection of wisdom they become those who have entered into reality, so it is

q.p: “best.”

div.p: Thus, even though they are not different, following the conventional terms in use in the world, one says “this is on account of giving,” “this is moral,” “this is patience,” and the cause of saying that, furthermore, is the perfection of wisdom, not anything else. The

q.p: “precious lady”
q.orig: precious queen consort

div.p: illustration teaches this too.

q.p: “The perfection of wisdom does not take hold of or release any dharma.”
q.orig: The perfection of wisdom does not acquire or relinquish anything at all

div.p: If a bodhisattva’s wisdom takes hold of any dharma just that is the fault of settling down on it, and even if it releases any, the knowledge of a knower of all aspects is not achieved, hence it “does not take hold of or release.” Alternatively, based on a falsely imagined phenomenon it does not take hold, and based on a true dharmic nature it does not release.

q.p:
“Subhūti, those who do not pay attention to form… do not take hold of form.” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: Subhūti, those who do not pay attention to form, up to do not pay attention to awakening do not take hold of form.
it is through nonattention to physical forms that physical forms are neither acquired nor relinquished

div.p: There is no “do not take hold” at all. The unreal is something that does not exist, so it says just those who do not pay attention “do not take hold.”

q.p:
“Subhūti, when bodhisattva great beings do not pay attention to form, up to do not pay attention to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening, then those bodhisattva great beings’ wholesome roots flourish.” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: Subhūti, when bodhisattva great beings do not pay attention to form, connect this in the same way with each, up to do not pay attention to awakening, then those bodhisattva great beings’ wholesome roots flourish
Subhūti,” replied the Blessed One, “when bodhisattva great beings do not focus attention on physical forms…the roots of virtuous action will increase

div.p: Phenomena that do not exist are nonexistent, so it teaches that having comprehended that they are nonexistent things and just not paying attention to them is the flourishing of wholesome roots.

q.p:
“Those bodhisattva great beings fall back from the perfection of wisdom.” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: those bodhisattva great beings would degenerate from the perfection of wisdom

div.p: On account of the fault of focusing on the causal sign they have attachment.

q.p:
“All phenomena… have not been taken hold of.” khri brgyad
: “All phenomena are without attachment and have not been taken hold of”; nyi khri (ga 104b5) med pa (asattāḥ in place of GilgitC 120, note c asaktāḥ): “All phenomena do not exist and have not been taken hold of.”
q.orig: All phenomena are nonexistent and cannot be acquired

div.p: They have not been taken hold of because they are not attached to the perfection of wisdom. The wisdom of the bodhisattvas is not attached to anything and does not take hold of anything. Thus,

q.p: “the perfection of wisdom is not separated from the perfection of wisdom”
q.orig: the perfection of wisdom is not bereft of the perfection of wisdom

div.p: means that at all times the perfection of wisdom is not separated from the intrinsic nature of the perfection of wisdom.
If all dharmas, whatever they are, are thus not separated from their intrinsic nature,

q.p: “how, then, is the perfection of wisdom to be accomplished?”
q.orig: how then would the perfection of wisdom be brought into being

div.p: This is asking: if all dharmas are not separated from their intrinsic nature, how then, through the wholesome roots and so on, are they to be appropriated?

q.p: “[They] do not settle down on form, nor do they settle down on ‘this is form, this is its form,’ ”
q.orig: bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom do not settle down on form, nor do they settle down on ‘this is…form[3]
they are not fixated on the notions of ‘physical forms,’ ‘these physical forms,’ or ‘their physical forms

div.p:
and so on, is teaching that nothing accomplishes anything, because they khri brgyad
: “ ‘Subhūti,’ replied the Lord, ‘here bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom do not settle down on form.’ ” do not settle down on anything. By properly not seeing, just the realization of things as they really are, marked by remaining just as they are, is said to be accomplishing, not something else. This should also be understood from the

q.p: “wheel-turning emperor”
q.orig: imperial monarch

div.p: analogy and the

q.p: “driver”
q.orig: riding

div.p:
analogy. khri brgyad
.

q.p: “Lord, if the perfection of wisdom does not produce and does not stop any phenomenon,”
q.orig: Blessed Lord, if this perfection of wisdom does not produce or stop anything at all

div.p:
and so on, khri brgyad
. is asking: If the bodhisattvas’ wisdom does not produce any dharma and does not stop anything bad, what do the six perfections do? How will the six perfections be completed? With

q.p: “Subhūti, having turned the knowledge of all aspects into an objective support,”
q.orig: Subhūti, having turned the knowledge of all aspects into an objective support
while referring to all-aspect omniscience

div.p: and so on, the Lord is saying: they do not complete the equipment, having thought ‘I have to produce something. I have to stop something.’ It is teaching that they dedicate them over to the knowledge of all aspects and complete them.

q.p:
“Form is not conjoined and not disjoined.” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: form is not conjoined and not disjoined;
physical forms are neither conjoined nor disjoined

div.p:
When they practice the six perfections they should not have it in mind that they have to separate from, and have to produce a disjunction from, the fetters The nine kun tu sbyor ba/ kun sbyor (samyojana) were given earlier at
. “Conjoin” renders samyuj, “fetter” renders samyojana. to form. It means because something with such an essence is in its intrinsic nature pure it “is not conjoined and not disjoined.”

q.p: “[They] should not work with the idea ‘I will stand in form,’ ”
q.orig: bodhisattva great beings should not work with the idea, ‘I will stand in form’
bodhisattva great beings should not persevere with the notion, ‘I will be established in physical forms

div.p: and so on. They should not work with the idea, “In my future lives I will be someone with a great body and mind,” Literally this says, “I will stand in a maturation of charming aggregates and so on.” or “I will stand, in result mode, in the knowledge of all aspects.”

q.p: “Form is not situated anywhere.”
q.orig: physical forms are not established anywhere

div.p: Take this as the true dharmic nature of form. There is the fruit tree analogy, and

q.p: “the door of all,”
q.orig: gateway to all
gateway to all

div.p: and

q.p: “the master archer”
q.orig: master archer
master of archery

div.p:
analogies. khri brgyad
–; “the ocean is the door of all rivers.” Then,

q.p:
“the buddhas… watch over… but they do not apprehend giving, do not apprehend morality, patience… at all.” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: the lord buddhas watch over the bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom, but they do not apprehend giving, morality, patience, perseverance, concentration, or wisdom at all.

the lord buddhas turn their enlightened intention toward bodhisattva great beings…They turn their enlightened intention toward those who practice the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of tolerance, the perfection of perseverance, the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom, and by whatever means they turn their enlightened intention in such a way that wisdom [and so forth] are not apprehended

div.p: Just as they watch by way of not apprehending, by not apprehending giving and so on, so too they watch over bodhisattvas as well, by way of not apprehending them.

q.p:
“When they know the suchness… they will come to know all dharmas in brief and in detail.” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: If they understand the real nature of physical forms, they will understand all phenomena, in brief and in detail

div.p: When they know the thoroughly established phenomenon as just “suchness,” they come to know in brief; and when they know the suchness of form, the suchness of feeling, and so on as uncleaned thoroughly unestablished phenomena, they come to know in detail.

q.p:
“Subhūti, the very limit of reality is the limitless.” khri brgyad
; “limit,” “summit,” “edge” (mtha’) render koṭi.
q.orig: Without finite limits is the very limit of reality

div.p: The word “limit” means summit, as in, for instance, “the summit of a mountain.” In some cases it is taken as an end, as in, for instance, “the edge of an ocean.” It is without both of those limits. Limitless in the sense of summit is saying it is not truncated; endless is saying it is “not delimited.” Therefore, it means “the very limit of reality” is “unchangeable reality.”

q.p: “Subhūti, all dharmas should be known as not conjoined and not disjoined.”
q.orig: they should understand that all phenomena are neither conjoined nor disjoined

div.p: They are nonexistent things, so they are neither.

q.p:
“Skilled in singular words” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: singular designations

div.p: shows they know number;

q.p: “skilled in feminine words”
q.orig: feminine designations

div.p: shows they know gender;

q.p: “skilled in the path that has been cut” lam gyi rgyun bcad pa is probably an archaic translation (based on the original meaning of the root śrambh) that escaped the eye of an editor. Mvy attests rgyun bcad pa as rendering pratiprasrabdha (PSP 5: 110). Cf. GilgitC 134 prasrabdhi­mārga­kuśalo; khri brgyad kha 303a7–b1, le’u brgyad ma ca 132a3 shin tu sbyang ba; ’bum da 125b6, nyi khri ga 118a5 rab tu sbyang ba, “skilled in the path with pliancy,” which is to say, a path that has incorporated calm abiding (śamatha).
q.orig: skilled in the path with pliancy
expert in the path of refinement

div.p: shows they are skilled in the ordinary path;

q.p: “skilled in the path that has not been cut”
q.orig: skilled in the path without pliancy
the path of nonrefinement

div.p: shows they are skilled in the extraordinary path.

q.p:
“Subhūti… they should practice the perfection of wisdom through the calmness of form.” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: “Subhūti,” replied the Lord, “they should practice the perfection of wisdom through the calmness of form
They should practice the perfection of wisdom through the peace of physical forms

div.p: Having taken hold of the defining marks of calmness and so on they should generate wisdom.

q.p: “They should accomplish the perfection of wisdom by accomplishing a space-like emptiness.”
q.orig: They should accomplish the perfection of wisdom by accomplishing a space-like emptiness.
they should actualize the perfection of wisdom through the actualization of the emptiness of space

div.p: They should comprehend it as a space-like emptiness.

q.p:
“They should meditate on the perfection of wisdom by meditating on a space-like emptiness.” PSP 5: 110 ākāśa­śūnyatā­bhāvanayā prajñāpāramitā bhāvayitavyā. GilgitC 135, nyi khri
, LSPW pp. 468–69 differ.
q.orig: They should meditate on the perfection of wisdom by meditating on a space-like emptiness.
they should cultivate the perfection of wisdom through the breaking down of cultivation

div.p: They should meditate on emptiness by just meditating on space.

Wanting to give a specific explanation for each of these, “These” are the practice of, the accomplishment of, and the meditation on the perfection of wisdom. it teaches that the first is practice during the period when there is effort and there are causal signs; the accomplishing is from the first level on up during the period when there is effort but there are no causal signs; and the meditation is from the eighth level when it is spontaneous and there are no causal signs.

q.p: “With an unbroken, unseparated stream of connected thoughts one after the other”
q.orig: with an unbroken, unseparated stream of thoughts connected one after the other?
should they practice without interruption and without separation from the mind set on enlightenment

div.p: means they should make that unbroken and unseparated stream of thoughts, which is to say ones that are connected one after the other in a continuum, uninterrupted, undivided into separate ones, and connected together. They

q.p: “should meditate… in such a way that mind and mental factor dharmas are not set in motion at all”
q.orig: should meditate on the perfection of wisdom in such a way that mind and mental factor dharmas are not set in motion at all.
they should practice it in such a way that the phenomena constituting mind and mental states are unmoved

div.p: means until the transformation of the basis.
Subhūti asks: will those

q.p: “who have meditated reach the knowledge of all aspects?”
q.orig: meditated on the perfection of wisdom reach the knowledge of all aspects?
cultivated the perfection of wisdom attain all-aspect omniscience

div.p: and the Lord negates that with

q.p: “no.”
q.orig: No, Subhūti.
No,” replied the Blessed One

div.p: Take this with the period when there is effort and thought construction. Subhūti asks,

q.p: “Will they without having meditated?”
q.orig: will those who have not cultivated it do so

div.p: and the Lord is silent, and then negates that with

q.p: “no.”
q.orig: No, Subhūti.
No,” replied the Blessed One

div.p: Subhūti asks,

q.p: “Will they, having meditated when they meditated, and without having meditated when they did not meditate?”
q.orig: “Well then, Lord, will they having meditated when they meditated, and without having mediated when they did not meditate?”
will those who have both cultivated and not cultivated it do so

div.p: Because the two faults have already been explained, the answer is no. The response to,

q.p: “Will they without having meditated and without having not meditated?”
q.orig: will they without having meditated and without having…meditated?
will those who have neither cultivated nor not cultivated it do so

div.p: eliminates that because the passages propounding the two main options could have raised a doubt, D gal; Golden 357b3, K, N gal te, “because of worrying about whether they have been disturbed by the passage propounding a duality.” so it teaches that it is a totally inexpressible and inconceivable state.

q.p: “Just as suchness will, Subhūti” This is in response to the question, “Well then, Lord, how will they reach the knowledge of all aspects?”—
q.orig: In accordance with the real nature

div.p: teaching all dharmas later in a state that cannot be apprehended—

q.p: “just as the self element,”
q.orig: accords with the elements constituting the self

div.p: and so on, will.

q.p: “Subhūti, the perfection of wisdom cannot be labeled”
q.orig: Subhūti,” replied the Lord, “the perfection of wisdom cannot be labeled
the perfection of wisdom is inconceivable

div.p: means it is inexpressible.

q.p: “Subhūti, what do you think, can a being that is a label be apprehended?”
q.orig: Subhūti,” asked the Lord in return, “what do you think, can a being that is a label be apprehended?
Subhūti, do you think that the concept of beings is apprehensible

div.p: and so on is teaching that hell and so on do not exist because they are falsely imagined phenomena, but they are labeled conventionally for the benefit of ordinary fools.

q.p: “Without taking anything away and without adding anything”—
q.orig: without subtraction or addition

div.p: over-negation of what exists is “taking away”; over-reification of what does not exist is “adding something.”

q.p: “Subhūti, they should train in those as not produced and not stopping.”
q.orig: They should train in nonarising and nonceasing

div.p: Training “as not produced” is without over-reification; training “as not stopping” is without over-negation.

q.p: “Without meditating on and without investigating” Cf. khri brgyad (ga 3b4), which has gzhig pa in place of rnam par gzhig pa; nyi khri ga 121b2 bsgom pa’am rnam par bsgom pa.
q.orig: the cultivation or breaking down of the nonconditioning of formative predispositions,

div.p: is training in not occasioning anything. It is training that is not produced, because of not occasioning anything by thinking, “I should meditate, I should produce something”; and it is training that does not stop because of not occasioning anything by thinking, “I should destroy,” The gloss suggests the translators understood gzhig pa (vibhāvana) here, at least, as a future form of ’jig, “to destroy,” not as “investigate.” should make something nonexistent.

q.p: “Form as empty of form”—
q.orig: form as empty of form
physical forms are empty of physical forms

div.p: falsely imagined form does not exist in form itself because it is empty of the defining mark of form.

q.p:
“Not practicing is the bodhisattvas’ practice of the perfection of wisdom” khri brgyad
.—
q.orig: the practice of the perfection of wisdom that bodhisattva great beings have is without practice

div.p: not practicing anything is the practice, because nothing can be apprehended.

q.p: “If not practicing is the practice of the perfection of wisdom, how then will bodhisattva great beings who are beginning the work practice the perfection of wisdom?”
q.orig: if they practice the perfection of wisdom in that manner, without practicing, how should bodhisattva great beings who are beginners practice the perfection of wisdom

div.p:
This is the question, khri brgyad
. This is Subhūti’s ninety-ninth question. and

q.p: “bodhisattva great beings beginning the work,”
q.orig: bodhisattva great beings who are beginners

div.p: and so on,

q.p: “starting from the first production of the thought… train in all phenomena as providing no basis for apprehension”
q.orig: commencing from their initial setting of the mind on enlightenment, should train in all phenomena as being nonapprehensible

div.p: teaches that those beginning the work do not have a practice of the ultimate, but still they should train for it, so just that training is the practice. Bṭ1 pa 245a5: “Even though bodhisattvas beginning the work are not able to complete the ultimate practice of not apprehending all dharmas, they should train to the extent they are able.”

q.p:
“Lord… does the findable provide a basis for not apprehending?” This is the reading at ’bum da 152a7, nyi khri
, Bṭ1 pa 245b3, GilgitC 139, ŚsPN4 9956r8 and PSP 5: 116. An alternative translation: “Lord, does apprehending not apprehend or does the absence of apprehending not apprehend?” khri brgyad
differs.
q.orig: does the findable provide a basis for not apprehending?
is it the nonapprehensible that is not apprehended

div.p: This is asking, “Is a basis for not apprehending findable?” An unfindable intrinsic nature is unfindable so it cannot be said that “it provides a basis for apprehending,” therefore it says that it does not, with

q.p:
“neither does the findable provide a basis for not apprehending.” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: it is not the apprehensible that is not apprehended

div.p: This means there is a sameness to all dharmas that are marked as being unfindable, so the absence of a basis for apprehending is not unfindable.

q.p:
“The sameness of the findable and the unfindable is the unfindable.” khri brgyad
. Alternative translation: “the sameness of providing a basis for apprehending and not providing a basis for apprehending is the absence of a basis for apprehending.”
q.orig: it is the sameness of the apprehensible and the nonapprehensible that is not apprehended

div.p: The existent thing when all dharmas are findable and the nonexistent thing when all dharmas are unfindable are both comparable. Why? Because they are without an intrinsic nature. The findable is falsely imagined and hence without an intrinsic nature, and the unfindable is in the form of a nonexistent thing and hence without an intrinsic nature too, so both are comparable as being without an intrinsic nature. This means the sameness of both the findable and unfindable, that absence of an intrinsic nature, is the unfindable. To paraphrase Bṭ1 pa 245b3–6: Someone thinks that when bodhisattvas do not apprehend something it means there is something intrinsically real left as an object when not apprehending occurs. With that in mind the person asks if the object is something real that can be apprehended or something real that cannot be apprehended. The Lord responds that it is neither of those two.

q.p: “How… will… [they] complete level after level, and how… will they reach the knowledge of all aspects?”
q.orig: how, Lord, will bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom complete level after level, and how, having completed level after level, will they reach the knowledge of all aspects?

how then will bodhisattva great beings who practice the perfection of wisdom perfect the levels, from one to the next, and, after perfecting the levels from one to the next, how will they attain all-aspect omniscience

div.p: This intends to say that if they are not attached to what provides a basis for apprehending, how will they work hard at level after level and the knowledge of all aspects?

q.p:
“Subhūti… a perfection of wisdom cannot be apprehended,” khri brgyad
.
q.orig: Subhūti[2]… a perfection of wisdom cannot be apprehended,
the perfection of wisdom is indeed nonapprehensible

div.p: and so on, teaches that with a findable intrinsic nature a higher level or the knowledge of all aspects would not be reached, but because the perfection of wisdom, awakening, and a bodhisattva are in their nature unfindable, as the absence of apprehending gets stronger and stronger there is an ascent from one level to the other and they reach the knowledge of all aspects.

q.p: “How will [they]… make an investigation into… all these dharmas that are without an intrinsic nature?”
q.orig: how will bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom make an investigation—‘this is form, this is feeling, this is perception, these are volitional factors, this is consciousness,’ up to ‘this is awakening’—into all these dharmas that are without an intrinsic nature?
how do bodhisattva great beings who practice the perfection of wisdom understand all phenomena

div.p: If all dharmas are without an intrinsic nature, how will they make an investigation into

q.p: “ ‘this is form, this is feeling,’ ”
q.orig: this is form, this is feeling
these are physical forms; that these are feelings

div.p: and so on?

q.p: “Subhūti… bodhisattvas… who do it in such a way that they apprehend form… do not make an investigation into dharmas,”
q.orig: Subhūti, bodhisattva great beings practicing the perfection of wisdom who do it in such a way that they apprehend form, up to apprehend consciousness, up to apprehend awakening do not make an investigation into dharmas.
Subhūti,” replied the Blessed One, “when bodhisattva great beings practice the perfection of wisdom, they do not understand anything in such a way that they would apprehend physical forms
